title: Songs of Grace, Book VI, Volume 3

intro.title: Introduction: Thiru Arutpa
paras: Thiru Arutpa, which means Divine Songs of Grace, is a collection of poems written by Ramalinga Adigal, lovingly known as Vallalar.

The entire poetic work is divided into 6 volumes or Thirumurais. The poems narrate the spiritual journey of Vallalar. From his early days of worship into the Saiva Siddhanta doctrine, the suffering from separation from the divine, to the final realization of the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light) in his late stage of Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam Sathya Sangam philosophy and way of life. The core philosophical pillars of the Thiru Arutpa include:
Active Compassion: The foundation is Jeeva Karunyam, or active compassion for all living beings as basis to spiritual life
Unity of All Beings: The Arutpa teaches Anma Neya Orumaipadu, or the Unity of Souls, asserting that every creature shares the exact same spiritual essence.
Rejection of Division: Vallalar wholly rejected caste systems, religious divisions, and sectarian hierarchies.
The Divine Light: The ultimate recognition is that ArutPerunJothi, the supreme divine light, dwells within every single soul without exception.
Ultimately, the Thiru Arutpa is a spiritual guide toward boundless compassion to all life, self-realization, and what Vallalar taught as the physical body's ability to reach a deathless state.

intro.title: Introduction: Thiru Arutpa Sixth Thirumurai
paras: The Thiru Arutpa is the collected poetry of Ramalinga Adigal, and it is arranged in six parts called Thirumurai. This is the sixth and last.

The first five volumes were written by a younger Ramalinga inside a tradition. They are temple hymns. They name places, they address deities by their local names, and they follow forms Tamil devotional poetry had used for a thousand years.

The Sixth is what came after. These are the works of his final years, written at Vadalur and at Mettukuppam, in the same period when he opened a kitchen that fed anyone who came and built a hall with no god in it.

In the earlier volumes he is a devotee. Here he is teaching something, and it has a name: Suddha Sanmarkkam, the pure true path. He describes it, he sets out what it asks, and he tells people to enter it.

He says caste, creed and sect are false. Not incomplete. False. He uses the word poy, a lie, and he says he was told so from the beginning. The man writing the Sixth Thirumurai has stopped working within the religions and has begun speaking past them.

He says the body does not have to die. The teaching on deathlessness, on the body remade by grace, appears here and nowhere earlier. It is the hardest part of his work and the part most often argued over.

He puts compassion at the gate. Jeeva Karunyam, mercy toward every living thing, is not presented as one virtue among many. It is the condition. Without it, he says, nothing else opens. This is why the free kitchen and these poems belong to the same act.
The form changes too. The temple hymn gives way to direct address. He is no longer singing about the divine from a shrine. He is speaking to it, and reporting what it said back.

A note on the arrangement. Ramalinga did not publish these works himself. He wrote as occasion demanded and left the ordering to others. His disciple Thozhuvur Velayutha Mudaliar, who had edited the earlier volumes during his lifetime, gathered the late writings after 1874 and arranged them. The six-part division is the work of the disciples, not of Ramalinga. Later editors, chiefly Ooran Adigal, reordered the volumes by date of composition, which is why some poems sit in different Thirumurai in different editions.

A note on this volume. The Sixth Thirumurai is published in three volumes, and the ArutPerunJothi Agaval, at 1,596 lines a book in itself, has a book of its own: The Hymn of the Vast Grace-Light. This is Volume Three of three, with pathigams 108 to 150. All of them are free to read at sanmarkkamlife.org.
The Tamil text follows the arrangement of Ooran Adigal, as given at thiruarutpa.org, checked against the printed editions of 1885 and 1932 where it was damaged.

works.title: The Hymn of the Vast Grace-light

blocks.html: The ArutPerunJothi Agaval, the Hymn of the Vast Grace-Light, is the greatest work of Ramalinga Adigal, the Tamil saint lovingly known as Vallalar. He wrote it in his last and most mature years, at Mettukuppam in south India. It is said that he wrote it in one unbroken session, in a single night.

It has 1,596 lines. Its subject is the ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light. The poem describes what that Light is, how everything that exists came out of it and is still held by it, and what happens inside a person when it is let in.

It begins by naming it. For 437 couplets, every second line ends in the same word. Then the naming stops, and the poem calls the same thing mother, father, friend, medicine, gold, mountain, ocean, lamp. At the end the first name returns, and the poem closes on the line it opened with.
Three things are said clearly. Caste, creed and sect are false. The path of non-violence is the path of grace. Every living thing is to be seen as your own.
More than a century later, devotees all over the world still wake up before dawn to sing these blissful lines.

translit: āyuraitta aruṭjōti varukiṉṟa taruṇamitē aṟimiṉ eṉṟē vāyuraitta vārttaieṉṟaṉ vārttaikaḷeṉ kiṉṟārim maṉitarantō tāyuraitta tiruppotuvil naṭampurinteṉ uḷaṅkalanta talaivā iṅkē nīuraitta tiruvārttai eṉaaṟiyār ivaraṟiviṉ nikaḻcci eṉṉē.
translation: Alas! These people claim that the words I spoke, "Know this! This is the moment the well-researched Grace-Jothi is arriving", are my own words. O Leader who dances in the sacred common space spoken of by the Mother and has merged with my being, they do not know that these are Your sacred words spoken here. What a state their intelligence is in!
commentary: Vallalar expresses his frustration that people attribute his prophecies to him personally. He insists that his announcements, like the news that the Grace-Jothi is arriving now, are direct communications from God. He sees the failure to recognize this as a sign of a deep spiritual blindness.

translit: iṟantavarkaḷ palarumiṅkē eḻukiṉṟa taruṇamitē eṉṟu vāymai aṟantaḻaiya uraikkiṉṟa vārttaikaḷeṉ vārttaikaḷeṉ ṟaṟaikiṉ ṟārāl maṟantaciṟi yēṉuraikka vallēṉō ellāñcey vallōy uṉṟaṉ ciṟantatiru vārttaieṉat terintilarim maṉitarmatit tiṟamai eṉṉē.
translation: They proclaim the words I speak so that truth and righteousness may flourish, "This is the moment when many of the dead will rise up here", as my own words. Can I, a forgetful, lowly one, have the power to speak them? O All-powerful one who does everything, they have not realized that these are Your own excellent, sacred words. What is the caliber of these people's intellect?
commentary: Here, Vallalar gives another example of his divine message being misunderstood. His incredible claim that the dead will rise again is taken as his own invention. He asks, how could a lowly, forgetful person like him invent something so momentous? He argues that the sheer audacity of the prophecy proves it can only come from God.

translit: cōṟṟācai yoṭukāmac cēṟṟācaip paṭuvārait tuṇintu kollak kūṟṟācaip paṭumeṉanāṉ kūṟukiṉṟa tuṇmaiyiṉil koṇṭu nīvīr nēṟṟācaip paṭṭavaruk kiṉṟaruḷvār pōlumaṉṟi niṉaitta vāṅkē pēṟṟācaik karuḷpuriyum ñāṉacapā patippukaḻaip pēcu vīrē.
translation: Take what I say as truth: Death desires to boldly kill those who fall for the lure of food and the mire of lust. You people, rather than thinking of him as one who might grant grace today to those who desired yesterday, should speak the praise of the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom, who grants the desired state the very moment you think of it.
commentary: Vallalar issues a blunt warning: being obsessed with sensual pleasures like food and lust is to make oneself a target for death. Instead of living under this threat, he urges people to praise the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom (Jnana Sabai), who offers a much better deal: a state of being granted the very instant it is sincerely desired.

translit: toṇṭāḷap paṇantēṭun tuṟaiyāḷa ulakāḷac cūḻnta kāmap peṇṭāḷat tirikiṉṟa pēymaṉattīr nummuyiraip piṭikka nāḷaic caṇṭāḷak kūṟṟuvaril eṉpukalvīr ñāṉacapait talaivaṉ ummaik koṇṭāḷak karutumiṉō āṇṭapiṉṉar ivvulakil kulāvu vīrē.
translation: O you with demonic minds, who wander about scheming to rule the world, to possess women caught in lust, to enslave devotees, and to control money-seeking monasteries! When cruel Death comes tomorrow to seize your life, what will you say? Intend for the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom to rule you. After he has ruled you, you can then live splendidly in this world.
commentary: Speaking to those who chase power, wealth, and sensual pleasure, Vallalar asks them to consider their mortality. What good will their schemes be when Death arrives? He presents a surprising alternative to mere renunciation: first, you must surrender completely to the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom (Jnana Sabai). Only after this total inner surrender, he says, can you truly begin to live a splendid and meaningful life in the world.

translit: piṟantavarai nīrāṭṭip perukavaḷart tiṭukiṉṟīr pēya rēnīr iṟantavaraic cuṭukiṉṟīr evvaṇañcam matittīrō iravil tūṅki maṟantavarait tīmūṭṭa vallīrāl nummaṉattai vayiram āṉa ciṟantavarai eṉappukaḻac ceytukoṇṭīr ēṉpiṟantu tirikiṉ ṟīrē.
translation: O you demons! You bathe and lavishly raise those who are born, yet you burn those who have died. How have you come to accept this? You are capable of setting fire to someone who has forgotten himself in sleep at night. You have arranged to be praised as excellent people whose minds are as hard as diamond. Why were you even born, and why do you wander about?
commentary: This verse begins Vallalar's fierce critique of cremation, which he sees as a deep spiritual hypocrisy. He finds it unthinkable that people lovingly raise a person from birth, only to violently destroy their body after death. He compares this to setting fire to a sleeping person, arguing that the practice reveals a heart that has become hard and unfeeling.

translit: aṇaṅkeḻupē rōcaiyoṭum paṟaiyōcai poṅkakkō raṇikoṇ ṭantō piṇaṅkaḻuvi eṭuttuppōyc cuṭukiṉṟīr iṉiccākum piṇaṅka ḷēnīr kaṇaṅkaḻukuṇ ṭālumoru payaṉuṇṭē eṉṉapayaṉ kaṇṭīr cuṭṭē eṇaṅkeḻucām palaikkaṇṭīr atupuṉcey eruvukkum iyalā taṉṟē.
translation: With a great, awesome sound and the booming of drums, you hold a grand procession, alas! You wash the corpse, carry it away, and burn it. You yourselves are just corpses waiting to die. If a flock of vultures eats the body, there is at least some use. What use have you found in burning it? You have found only magnificent ash, which is not even fit to be manure for dry fields.
commentary: The elaborate rituals of a funeral mean nothing if the final act is the pointless destruction of the body. Vallalar makes a pragmatic argument against cremation: if the body were left to be eaten by vultures, it would at least nourish other living beings. Burning it, however, produces nothing but sterile ash. He sees the whole affair as a wasteful spectacle performed by people who fail to see the cycle of life.

translit: kuṇamputaikka uyiraṭakkam koṇṭatucuṭ ṭālatutāṉ kolaiyām eṉṟē vaṇamputaikka vēṇṭumeṉa vāytaṭikkac colkiṉṟēṉ vārttai kēṭṭum piṇamputaikkac cammatiyīr paṇamputaikkac cammatikkum pēya rēnīr eṇamputaikkat tuyilvārnum pāṟṟuyilaṟ kañcuvarē iḻutai yīrē.
translation: I tell you until my mouth swells that to burn the body in which the life lies withdrawn and held is murder, and that it must be buried with care. Yet, even after hearing my words, you do not agree to bury the corpse. You ghouls, you who agree to bury money! Those who sleep, their thoughts put to rest, will be afraid to rest near you, you fools.
commentary: Vallalar states it plainly: cremation is murder. The dead body still holds the life withdrawn within it, like one asleep, and to burn it is murder. He is exasperated with people who will gladly bury their money but refuse to bury a human body, and who are so hard that even the sleeping would fear to rest near them.

translit: kaṭṭālum kaṉattālum kaḷikkiṉṟa pēyulakīr kalaicōrn tāraip poṭṭālum tukilālum puṉaivittuc cuṭukiṉṟīr putaikka nērīr cuṭṭālum cuṭumatukaṇ ṭumatuṭampu tuṭiyāteṉ collīr nummait toṭṭālum tōṣamuṟum viṭṭālum katiyilaimēl cūḻvīr aṉṟē.
translation: O ghoulish worldlings who delight in physique and weight, you adorn those whose life-force has faded with a pottu (a decorative dot on the forehead) and clothes, and then you burn them. You do not agree to bury them. Even as you burn a body, your own body does not tremble at the sight. What can I say? Touching you incurs a spiritual flaw, yet if I abandon you, you have no path to salvation. Think about what is to come!
commentary: The final verse in this sequence highlights a disturbing contradiction: people who value the physical body in life can watch one burn without flinching. This emotional numbness is a sign of deep spiritual corruption. Vallalar ends with a cry of personal anguish: to engage with such people is spiritually risky, but to abandon them is to leave them without hope. He urges them to think about the ultimate consequences of their heartless actions.

translit: paraṉaḷikkum tēkamitu cuṭuvatapa rātameṉap pakarkiṉ ṟēṉnīr ciramneḷikkac cuṭukiṉṟīr cettavarkaḷ paṟpalarum citta cāmi uraṉaḷikka eḻukiṉṟa tirunāḷvan taṭuttaṉaī tuṇarntu nallōr varaṉaḷikkap putaittanilai kārō kaṇkeṭṭa māṭṭi ṉīrē.
translation: This body is a gift from the Supreme One. I declare that burning it is a transgression. Yet you shake your heads in disagreement and burn it. The sacred day is fast approaching when the Siddha Lord will grant strength and the many who have died will rise. Understanding this, the good people adopted the practice of burial as a boon. Do you not see this, you blind cattle?
commentary: The body is a gift from God, and burning it is a sin. Vallalar gives a weighty reason for this: he foretells a coming day of grace when the dead will be resurrected. Burial preserves the body for this miraculous event, while cremation destroys that possibility. He calls those who cremate "blind" for failing to understand this future potential.

translit: pulaittoḻilē purikiṉṟīr puṇṇiyattaik karuṅkaṭalil pōka viṭṭīr kolaittoḻilil koṭiyīrnīr cettāraic cuṭukiṉṟa koṭumai nōkkik kalaittoḻilil periyaruḷam kalaṅkiṉarak kalakkamelām kaṭavuḷnīkkit talaittoḻilcey caṉmārkkam talaieṭukkap purikuvatit taruṇam tāṉē.
translation: You perform only debased work. You have thrown your spiritual merit into the deep ocean. You are cruel in this work of killing. Seeing your cruelty in burning the dead, the hearts of the great masters of knowledge are shaken. God will remove all their distress. This very moment is when He will make the supreme path, Sanmarkkam, emerge and prevail.
commentary: The practice of cremation is a cruel act that destroys spiritual merit and causes despair even in great souls. But Vallalar offers hope, declaring that this very moment is the dawn of a new age. God is about to establish Sanmarkkam, the universal True Path, which will replace such cruelty with compassion.

translit: iṉpāl ulakaṅkaḷ yāvum viḷaṅkiṉa tuṉpāl iṟantavar tuṉpaṟṟut tōṉṟiṉar aṉpāl aṭiyavar āṭiṉar pāṭiṉar eṉpāl aruṭperuñ cōtiyār eytavē.
translation: All the worlds shine with joy. Those who died in suffering have appeared, free of sorrow. With love, the devotees dance and sing, all because the Vast Grace-Light has reached me.
commentary: The descent of the Vast Grace-Light into Vallalar is an event of cosmic significance. It does more than affect him; it radiates outward, filling all worlds with joy, freeing the souls of the dead from their suffering, and causing his followers to erupt in celebration. His attainment is a blessing for all of existence.

translit: pāmpelām ōṭiṉa paṟavaiyuṭ cārntaṉa tīmpalā vāḻaimāt teṉṉai ciṟantaṉa āmpalaṉ meṉmēlum āyiṉa eṉṉuḷat tōmpaleṉ aruṭperuñ cōtiyār ōṅkavē.
translation: All the snakes fled; the birds drew near and gathered. Sweet jackfruit, plantain, mango, and coconut trees flourished, and their good yield grew more and more, all because my Vast Grace-Light, cherished in my heart, rose high.
commentary: The divine transformation reaches the natural world: what harms departs and what is gentle draws near. The snakes, bearers of venom, flee, while the birds gather close, and the fruit-bearing trees flourish and yield ever more. Grace renews the soul and creation itself.

translit: malaṅkaḻin tulakavar vāṉavar āyiṉar valampeṟu cuttacaṉ mārkkam ciṟantatu palampeṟu maṉitarkaḷ paṇpuḷar āyiṉar nalampeṟum aruṭperuñ cōtiyār naṇṇavē.
translation: Having shed their impurities, the people of the world became celestials. The victorious Suddha Sanmarkkam flourished. Humans who received strength became people of fine character, all as the Vast Grace-Light, who brings well-being, drew near.
commentary: The coming of the Vast Grace-Light elevates humanity itself, purifying people until they become like divine beings. This transformation allows the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Purity) to thrive, as people gain the inner strength and moral character to live by its principles. Divine grace does more than save individuals; it refines all of society.

translit: muṉṉuḷa mārkkaṅkaḷ yāvum muṭintaṉa maṉṉuḷa cuttacaṉ mārkkam ciṟantatu paṉṉuḷan teḷintaṉa patinaṭam ōṅkiṉa eṉṉuḷat taruṭperuñ cōtiyār eytavē.
translation: All previous paths have come to an end. The enduring Suddha Sanmarkkam has flourished. The minds of many have become clear and the dance of the Lord has risen high, all because the Vast Grace-Light has reached my heart.
commentary: Vallalar makes a bold declaration: with the arrival of the Vast Grace-Light, all previous religions and spiritual paths are now obsolete. The one true and lasting path, Suddha Sanmarkkam, now flourishes in their place. This new way clears people's minds and makes them aware of the cosmic dance of Pati (the supreme Lord), revealing a direct and universal truth.

translit: iṭampeṟṟa uyirelām viṭamaṟṟu vāḻntaṉa maṭampeṟṟa maṉitarkaḷ matipeṟṟu vāḻkiṉṟār tiṭampeṟṟē eḻukiṉṟār cettavar tiṉantiṉam naṭampeṟṟa aruṭperuñ cōtiyār naṇṇavē.
translation: All beings that exist now live without venom. Ignorant people have gained wisdom and now thrive. Day after day, the dead are rising up, having gained strength, all as the Vast Grace-Light of the cosmic dance draws near.
commentary: The influence of the Vast Grace-Light removes all forms of poison from the world, both the literal venom of creatures and the metaphorical venom of ignorance in humans. People who were once foolish now find wisdom and prosper. In a stunning vision of renewal, Vallalar repeats that even the dead are being resurrected, showing this divine power overcomes the ultimate limitation of life.

translit: aṇṭamum akilamum aruḷara cāṭciyaik koṇṭaṉa ōṅkiṉa kuṟaielām tīrntaṉa paṇṭaṅkaḷ palittaṉa parinteṉa tuḷḷattil eṇṭakum aruṭperuñ cōtiyār eytavē.
translation: As the praiseworthy Vast Grace-Light compassionately reached my heart, the universe and the entire world accepted the reign of grace and flourished. All deficiencies vanished, and all things came to fruition.
commentary: This verse presents a vision of a world completely transformed. When the Vast Grace-Light enters the speaker's heart, the entire universe accepts the "reign of grace" as its new reality. Under this divine rule, all problems, shortages, and imperfections are eliminated, and everything reaches its perfect fulfillment.

translit: kuṇaṅkaḷ ciṟantaṉa kuṟṟaṅkaḷ aṟṟaṉa maṇaṅkaḷ viḷaṅkiṉa vāḻvukaḷ ōṅkiṉa piṇaṅkaḷ elāmuyir peṟṟeḻun tōṅkiṉa iṇaṅka aruṭperuñ cōtiyār eytavē.
translation: As the Vast Grace-Light harmoniously arrived, virtues became excellent and faults ceased. Fragrances shone forth, and lives flourished. All the corpses received life, rose up, and thrived.
commentary: Grace brings about a complete perfection of reality. It operates on every level: morally, by replacing faults with virtues; physically, by making life flourish; and even supernaturally, by bringing the dead back to life. Vallalar consistently presents the raising of the dead as a present reality initiated by the arrival of the Vast Grace-Light.

translit: pattarkaḷ pāṭiṉar paṇintuniṉ ṟāṭiṉar muttarkaḷ meypporuḷ muṉṉi makiḻntaṉar cittarkaḷ āṉantat teḷḷamu tuṇṭaṉar cutta aruṭperuñ cōtiyār tōṉṟavē.
translation: When the Pure Vast Grace-Light appeared, devotees sang, bowed, and danced. The liberated ones contemplated the True Reality and rejoiced. The Siddhas drank the clear nectar of bliss.
commentary: The appearance of the Pure Vast Grace-Light evokes different responses from different kinds of spiritual seekers. Devotees respond with joyful worship, the liberated contemplate reality, and the Siddhas (perfected masters) directly experience divine bliss. This shows that grace is accessible to all, meeting each person at their own level of spiritual evolution.

translit: ēḻula kavattaiviṭ ṭēṟiṉaṉ mēṉilai ūḻitō ṟūḻiyum uyirtaḻait tōṅkiṉaṉ āḻiyāṉ ayaṉmutal aticayit tiṭaeṉuḷ vāḻia ruṭperuñ cōtiyār maṉṉavē.
translation: As the blessed Vast Grace-Light reigns within me, I have left behind the seven worldly states and ascended to the higher plane. To the amazement of Vishnu, Brahma, and the others, my life has sprouted and will flourish through eon after eon.
commentary: The indwelling of the Vast Grace-Light has elevated Vallalar beyond ordinary human existence. He declares he has transcended the typical planes of consciousness and achieved an immortal life that will last for ages. This transformation is so great that it astonishes even the great gods of creation and preservation, Brahma and Vishnu, signifying a spiritual attainment beyond the known cosmic order.

translit: iruṭperu malamuḻu tuntavirn tiṟṟatu maruṭperum kaṉmamum māyaiyum nīṅkiṉa teruṭperuñ cittikaḷ cērntaṉa eṉṉuḷat taruṭperuñ cōtieṉ aṉpiṟ kalantatē.
translation: Because the Vast Grace-Light has mingled with my love within my heart, the great darkness of primal impurity is entirely destroyed. The great deluding karma and Maya have departed. The great siddhis of clarity have joined me.
commentary: The cause of liberation is the union of divine light with the soul's own love. This inner event is what purges the fundamental impurities (malam), dissolves the effects of past actions (karma), and clears away illusion (Maya). Spiritual powers (siddhis) are a natural consequence of this inner purity.

translit: evvuyirum potueṉakkaṇ ṭiraṅkiupa karikkiṉṟār yāvar antac cevviyartam ceyalaṉaittum tiruvaruḷiṉ ceyaleṉavē terintēṉ iṅkē kavvaiilāt tiruneṟiat tiruvāḷar tamakkēval kaḷippāl ceyya ovviyateṉ karuttavarcīr ōtiṭaeṉ vāymikavum ūrva tālō.
translation: I have understood here that all the actions of those noble ones, whoever they may be, who see all lives as equal, feel compassion, and offer help, are indeed the actions of sacred grace. My mind has consented to joyfully serve those blessed ones on the flawless, sacred path, and oh, my mouth is so eager to speak of their glory.
commentary: Holiness is found in people who treat all lives as equal and act with compassion. Vallalar states that the actions of such people are not merely good deeds; they are direct expressions of divine grace itself. For him, serving these living saints is the highest path.

translit: ettuṇaiyum pētamuṟā tevvuyirum tamuyirpōl eṇṇi uḷḷē otturimai uṭaiyavarāy uvakkiṉṟār yāvaravar uḷantāṉ cutta citturuvāy emperumāṉ naṭampuriyum iṭameṉanāṉ terintēṉ anta vittakartam aṭikkēval purintiṭaeṉ cintaimika viḻainta tālō.
translation: I have realized that the heart of those who rejoice with a sense of inner oneness, considering every life as their own without any distinction whatsoever, is the very place where our great Lord, as the form of pure consciousness, performs His dance. Oh, my mind greatly yearns to serve at the feet of those wise masters.
commentary: The true temple where God dwells is the heart of a compassionate person. Vallalar realizes that the divine dance of pure consciousness happens within those who feel a sense of oneness with all living beings. His deepest desire is to serve these masters.

translit: karuṇaioṉṟē vaṭivāki evvuyirum tamuyirpōl kaṇṭu ñāṉat teruḷneṟiyil cuttaciva caṉmārkkap perunīti celuttā niṉṟa poruḷneṟicaṟ kuṇacāntap puṇṇiyartam tiruvāyāl pukaṉṟa vārttai aruḷneṟivē tākamattiṉ aṭimuṭicol vārttaikaḷeṉ ṟaṟaiva rālō.
translation: The words spoken from the sacred mouths of those virtuous and peaceful saints, who embody compassion itself, see every life as their own, and establish the great principle of the Pure Siva Sanmarkkam on the clear path of wisdom, oh, people declare those words to be the very essence that defines the beginning and the end of the gracious Vedas and Agamas.
commentary: The words of a truly compassionate person are the highest scripture. Vallalar places the living speech of a saint above even the Vedas and Agamas (traditional Hindu scriptures), declaring them to be the essence of all sacred texts. This living truth is the core principle of the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Goodness).

translit: maṉṉappā maṉṟiṭattē mānaṭañcey appāeṉ taṉṉappā caṇmukaṅkoḷ cāmiyappā evvuyirkkum muṉṉappā piṉṉappā mūrttiyappā mūvāta poṉṉappā ñāṉap poruḷappā tantaruḷē.
translation: O enduring Father! O Father who performs the great dance in the hall! My very own Father! O Father, Lord with six faces! O Father before and after all lives! O Father, the divine form! O Father of undecaying gold! O Father, the substance of wisdom! Please grant me your grace.
commentary: This verse is a litany of loving praise, calling on God with the intimate term "Father" (Appa). Each title, from the cosmic dancer to the six-faced Lord, expresses a different facet of the divine. The prayer is an intensely personal and emotional cry for grace, like a child calling out to a beloved parent.

translit: ātiap pānam aṉātiyap pānaṅkaḷ ammaioru pātiap pāniru pātiap pāciva pattaraṉu pūtiap pānal vipūtiap pāpoṟ potunaṭañcey cōtiap pācuyañ cōtiap pāeṉaic cūḻntaruḷē.
translation: O primal Father! Our eternal Father! O Father who has our Mother as one half of your form! O Father without affliction! O Father who is the direct experience of Siva's devotees! O Father who is the good sacred ash! O Father, the Jothi who dances in the golden hall! O Father, the self-effulgent Jothi! Surround me and bestow your grace.
commentary: The prayer continues by addressing God as the source of everything: the primal beginning, the eternal presence, and the union of masculine and feminine principles ("Mother as one half"). God is also the direct, felt experience of devotees and, above all, the self-luminous divine light, or Jothi. The plea to be "surrounded" is a desire to be completely enveloped and protected by this all-encompassing divine reality.

translit: aṇṭaap pāpaki raṇṭaap pānañ caṇintamaṇi kaṇṭaap pāmuṟṟum kaṇṭaap pāciva kāmieṉum oṇtavap pāvaiyaik koṇṭaap pācaṭai ōṅkupiṟait tuṇṭaap pāmaṟai viṇṭaap pāeṉaic cūḻntaruḷē.
translation: O Father of the universe, Father of the cosmos beyond! O Father with the gem-like throat adorned with poison, Father who perceives all! O Father who wed the radiant, ascetic woman Sivakami! O Father with the sliver of the crescent moon rising from your matted locks, Father revealed by the Vedas! Surround me and grant your grace.
commentary: Here, Vallalar invokes classic stories and images associated with the god Siva to illustrate God's nature. Mentioning the poison-adorned throat, for instance, recalls the myth of Siva saving the universe, portraying God as a compassionate protector who absorbs suffering for the sake of others. By using these powerful symbols, the prayer grounds its plea for protection in a God of cosmic power and saving grace.

translit: vēlaiap pāpaṭai vēlaiap pāpava veyyilukkōr cōlaiap pāparañ cōtiap pācaṭait tuṉṟukoṉṟai mālaiap pānaṟ camaraca vētacaṉ mārkkacaṅkac cālaiap pāeṉait tantaap pāvantu tāṅkikkoḷḷē.
translation: O Father who is an ocean of grace, Father with the spear as your weapon! Father who is a shady grove for the harsh sun of worldly existence! O Father, the Supreme Jothi! Father with the dense konrai garland on your matted locks! Father of the hall of the assembly for the good Samarasa Veda Sanmarkkam! Father who gave me to myself, come and take me into your care.
commentary: This concluding prayer brings together traditional images of God with Vallalar's own central teaching. He calls God the father of his own spiritual movement, the Samarasa Veda Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Harmonious Truth), and a refuge from worldly suffering. The final lines, "Father who gave me to myself, come and take me into your care," express the height of devotion: a recognition that our very selfhood is a gift from God, and a deep yearning to surrender that self back to its divine source.

translit: mecciap pāvalar pōṟṟap potuvil viḷaṅkiyaeṉ ucciap pāeṉ ṉuṭaiyaap pāeṉṉai uṟṟuppeṟṟa acciap pāmukkaṇ appāeṉ āruyirk kāṉaappā kacciap pātaṅkak kaṭṭiap pāeṉṉaik kaṇṭukoḷḷē.
translation: My supreme Father, who shines in the Common Hall, praised and cherished by poets! My very own Father! The mother who mindfully bore me! Three-eyed Father! Father who is my precious life! Father who is a bar of pure gold from Kachi! Look upon me and take me in.
commentary: The relationship with the divine becomes intensely personal, like that of a child to both father and mother. Calling God "the mother who mindfully bore me" is an especially powerful expression of God as the direct source of one's being. This divine parent is also the highest reality, shining in the "Common Hall" (Chitrambalam, the inner space of consciousness) and is as pure and precious as a bar of gold.

translit: ekkarai yummiṉṟi ōṅkum aruṭkaṭal eṉṟuraikkō cekkarai veṉṟapoṉ eṉkō paṭikat tiraḷateṉkō tikkarai amparaṉ eṉkōeṉ uḷḷattil tittikkiṉṟa cakkaraik kaṭṭieṉ kōniṉait tāṉmaṉṟil tāṇṭavaṉē.
translation: O you who dance in the Hall of Consciousness! Shall I call you the shoreless, swelling ocean of grace? Shall I call you gold that surpasses the red sunset sky? Shall I call you a mass of crystal? Shall I call you the one who wears the directions as your garment? Or shall I call you the lump of sugar candy that sweetens my heart?
commentary: This verse expresses the difficulty of capturing the divine in words. Vallalar offers a series of grand metaphors: a boundless ocean, brilliant gold, pure crystal. He then contrasts these with a simple, personal experience: God is like "the lump of sugar candy that sweetens my heart." This shows that the same God who is vast and absolute is also an immediate, sweet presence felt within.

translit: oṭṭieṉ kōtaṟut tāṭkoṇ ṭaṉainiṉai ōṅkaṟivām tiṭṭieṉ kōuyar ciṟṟam palantaṉil cērkkumnalla veṭṭieṉ kōaruṭ peṭṭiyil ōṅki viḷaṅkumtaṅkak kaṭṭieṉ kōpoṟ potunaṭañ ceyyumuk kaṇṇavaṉē.
translation: O three-eyed one who dances in the Golden Hall! You came close, cut away my flaws, and made me your own. Shall I call you the divine vision that is supreme knowledge? Shall I call you the good path that leads to the high Chitrambalam? Or shall I call you the bar of gold shining brightly in the casket of grace?
commentary: The focus here is on God's active role in spiritual transformation. God is the one who "cut away my flaws," purifying the soul. The metaphors reflect this active grace: God is the "divine vision" of truth, the very "path" that leads to the goal, and the "treasure" of grace one receives. The destination is the high Chitrambalam (Hall of Consciousness), and God is both the way to it and the reality found there.

tamil: அருட்பெருங் கடலே என்னை ஆண்டசற் குருவே ஞானப்
பொருட்பெருஞ் சபையில் ஆடும் பூரண வாழ்வே நாயேன்
மருட்பெரு மாயை முற்றும் மடிந்தன வினைக ளோடே
இருட்பெருந் தடையை நீக்கி இரவியும் எழுந்த தன்றே.
translit: aruṭperuṅ kaṭalē eṉṉai āṇṭacaṟ kuruvē ñāṉap poruṭperuñ capaiyil āṭum pūraṇa vāḻvē nāyēṉ maruṭperu māyai muṟṟum maṭintaṉa viṉaika ḷōṭē iruṭperun taṭaiyai nīkki iraviyum eḻunta taṉṟē.
translation: O great ocean of Grace! O Satguru who took me as your own! O perfect life that dances in the great hall of Gnosis! My vast, bewildering māyai, along with my karmas, has been completely destroyed. Removing the great obstacle of darkness, the sun has risen indeed.
commentary: This is a declaration of liberation. Through the grace of the Satguru (True Master), the soul's deepest burdens have been lifted. Māyai, the bewildering illusion of a separate self, has vanished along with its accumulated karmas (the binding consequences of past actions). The "sun" that rises is the light of gnosis (true spiritual knowledge), dispelling the darkness of ignorance and revealing the perfect, non-dual reality that dances in the great hall.

tamil: மாணவ நிலைக்கு மேலே வயங்கிய ஒளியே மன்றில்
தாணவ நடஞ்செய் கின்ற தனிப்பெருந் தலைவ னேஎன்
கோணவ மாயை எல்லாம் குலைந்தன வினைக ளோடே
ஆணவ இருளை நீக்கி அலரியும் எழுந்த தன்றே.
translit: māṇava nilaikku mēlē vayaṅkiya oḷiyē maṉṟil tāṇava naṭañcey kiṉṟa taṉipperun talaiva ṉēeṉ kōṇava māyai ellām kulaintaṉa viṉaika ḷōṭē āṇava iruḷai nīkki alariyum eḻunta taṉṟē.
translation: O light that shines above the state of ego-conceit! O singular, great Lord who performs the cosmic dance in the sacred hall! All my perverse māyai, along with my karmas, has been shattered. Removing the darkness of āṇava, the sun has risen indeed.
commentary: The divine light utterly shatters the self-centered ego and all its delusions. This light shines from a state beyond our ordinary, limited self. When it dawns, it removes the distortions of māyai (illusion) and the root of separation itself, the deep-seated ignorance called āṇava (the principle of 'I'-ness).

tamil: தற்பரம் பொருளே வேதத் தலைநின்ற ஒளியே மோனச்
சிற்பர சுகமே மன்றில் திருநடம் புரியுந் தேவே
வற்புறு மாயை எல்லாம் மடிந்தன வினைக ளோடே
இற்படும் இருளை நீக்கி இரவியும் எழுந்த தன்றே.
translit: taṟparam poruḷē vētat talainiṉṟa oḷiyē mōṉac ciṟpara cukamē maṉṟil tirunaṭam puriyun tēvē vaṟpuṟu māyai ellām maṭintaṉa viṉaika ḷōṭē iṟpaṭum iruḷai nīkki iraviyum eḻunta taṉṟē.
translation: O supreme reality! O light that stands at the head of the Vedas! O bliss of silent, transcendent consciousness! O Deva who performs the sacred dance in the sacred hall! All insistent māyai, along with my karmas, has perished. Removing the darkness that filled this house, the sun has risen indeed.
commentary: The direct experience of God dissolves all illusion and suffering, like light filling a dark house. Vallalar addresses God as the supreme reality and the silent bliss of pure consciousness. When this divine presence is felt, the darkness of māyai (illusion) and the consequences of past actions simply cease to exist.

translit: ciṟṟaṟi vuṭaiyanāṉ ceyta tīmaikaḷ muṟṟavum poṟuttaruḷ muṉintiṭēl iṉṟē teṟṟeṉa aruṭperuñ cōtic celvamum maṟṟavum vaḻaṅkuka varataṉē eṉṟēṉ.
translation: I said: "O Bestower of boons, completely forgive the evil deeds I have done with my meager wisdom. Do not be angry. Today, grant me clearly the wealth of the Vast Grace-Light and all other boons as well."
commentary: A simple, humble request is the way to receive divine grace. Acknowledging his own imperfect understanding, Vallalar asks for forgiveness and for the supreme gift of the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi). The prayer is a direct and honest appeal from the heart.

translit: eṉṟacol cevimaṭut tiṟaiyum añciṭēl iṉṟuṉak karuṭperuñ cōti īntaṉam naṉṟuṟa makiḻkaen nāḷuñ cāvuṟā veṉṟiyum aḷittaṉam eṉṟu mēviṉāṉ.
translation: Hearing the words I spoke, he drew near and said: "Do not fear in the least. Today I have given you the Vast Grace-Light. Rejoice fully. I have also granted you the victory of never dying, for all time."
commentary: God's response to a sincere plea is immediate, total, and removes all fear. The divine voice promises that the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi) is a gift given today. With this grace comes the final assurance: victory over death itself.

translit: mēvieṉ uḷḷakat tiruntu mēlumeṉ āviyiṟ kalantivaṉ avaṉeṉ ṟōtumōr pūviyaṟ pētamum pōkki oṉṟatāyt tēviyaṟ purintaṉaṉ citampa rēcaṉē.
translation: The Lord of Chidambaram entered and stayed within my heart, mingled with my very life, and erased the worldly distinction that speaks of 'this one' and 'that one'. Becoming one with me, he made my nature divine.
commentary: The Lord enters Vallalar's heart and dissolves the very distinction between 'I' and 'He'. Becoming one with him, God confers on him a divine nature. This is the union Vallalar describes throughout these verses, where the soul and the divine are no longer two.

translit: pōṟṟi niṉaruḷ pōṟṟi niṉpotu pōṟṟi niṉpukaḻ pōṟṟi niṉuru pōṟṟi niṉiyal pōṟṟi niṉnilai pōṟṟi niṉneṟi pōṟṟi niṉcukam pōṟṟi niṉuḷam pōṟṟi niṉmoḻi pōṟṟi niṉceyal pōṟṟi niṉkuṇam pōṟṟi niṉmuṭi pōṟṟi niṉnaṭu pōṟṟi niṉaṭi pōṟṟi pōṟṟiyē.
translation: Praise to your grace, praise to your universal space, praise to your glory, praise to your form. Praise to your nature, praise to your state, praise to your path, praise to your bliss. Praise to your heart, praise to your word, praise to your action, praise to your quality. Praise to your crown, praise to your waist, praise to your feet. Praise, praise!
commentary: In an outpouring of pure devotion, Vallalar praises every aspect of the divine. The praise moves from abstract qualities like grace and bliss to the symbolic form of God, from crown to feet. This is the language of a soul completely saturated with gratitude and awe.

translit: pōṟṟi niṉiṭam pōṟṟi niṉvalam pōṟṟi niṉnaṭam pōṟṟi niṉnalam pōṟṟi niṉtiṟam pōṟṟi niṉtaram pōṟṟi niṉvaram pōṟṟi niṉkati pōṟṟi niṉkalai pōṟṟi niṉporuḷ pōṟṟi niṉoḷi pōṟṟi niṉveḷi pōṟṟi niṉtayai pōṟṟi niṉkoṭai pōṟṟi niṉpatam pōṟṟi pōṟṟiyē.
translation: Praise to your left side, praise to your right side, praise to your dance, praise to your goodness. Praise to your power, praise to your stature, praise to your boons, praise to your refuge. Praise to your arts, praise to your substance, praise to your light, praise to your expanse. Praise to your compassion, praise to your generosity, praise to your divine feet. Praise, praise!
commentary: The hymn of praise continues, celebrating God's every dimension. It honors God's dynamic cosmic dance, his protective power, and his fundamental nature as light, compassion, and generosity. Praising the "left" and "right" sides acknowledges the divine as a perfect union of all principles.

translit: pōṟṟu kiṉṟaeṉ puṉmai yāvaiyum poṟutta niṉperum poṟumai pōṟṟieṉ āṟṟu vēṉuṉak kaṟiki lēṉeṉak kaṟivu tantapē raṟiva pōṟṟivāṉ kāṟṟu nīṭaḻal āti aintunāṉ kāṇak kāṭṭiya karutta pōṟṟivaṉ kūṟṟu taittunīt taḻivi lāuruk koḷḷa vaittaniṉ koḷkai pōṟṟiyē.
translation: Praise to your great forbearance that has forgiven all my baseness. I do not know what I can do for you. Praise to you, O Great Wisdom who gave me wisdom! Praise to the primal Intent who showed me the five elements: sky, air, vast fire, and the rest, so I could see them! Praise to your principle that struck down and removed harsh Kūṟṟu, enabling me to take on an indestructible form!
commentary: Vallalar gives thanks for the specific gifts he has received: forgiveness for his flaws, the wisdom he now possesses, and a true vision of the universe. Above all, he praises the divine principle that defeated Kūṟṟu (the god of death) and gave him an indestructible body. His feeling that he can do nothing in return highlights the purely gratuitous nature of grace.

translit: ampalam cērntēṉ empalam ārntēṉ appaṉaik kaṇṭēṉ ceppamuṭ koṇṭēṉ umpar viyappa impar iruntēṉ ōtā tuṇarntēṉ mītāṉam uṟṟēṉ nampiṭil aṇaikkum emperu māṉai nāyakaṉ taṉṉait tāyavaṉ taṉṉaip pampuṟap pāṭip paṭikkiṉṟēṉ mēlum paṭippēṉ eṉakkup paṭippitta vāṟē.
translation: I reached the sacred hall and was filled with my own strength. I saw the Father and took perfection into my being. I remained here in this world, to the astonishment of the celestials. I understood without being taught and reached the supreme place. I am abundantly singing and reciting about our great Lord who embraces those who trust him: the Master, who is also a mother. I will continue to recite, just as he has taught me.
commentary: This is a song of arrival, a declaration of having reached the highest spiritual state. The Ambalam (sacred hall) represents the inner space of consciousness where he directly experienced God. It was a total transformation, filling him with a new strength and perfection. He now understands truth directly, "without being taught," and his purpose is to share this experience by singing about the God who is both a father and a nurturing mother.

translit: kaḷḷattai aṟṟa uḷḷattaip peṟṟēṉ kaṉṟik kaṉintē maṉṟil pukuntēṉ teḷḷat teḷinta veḷḷattai uṇṭēṉ ceyvakai kaṟṟēṉ uyvakai uṟṟēṉ aḷḷak kuṟaiyā vaḷḷaṟ poruḷai ampalac cōtiyai emperu vāḻvai paḷḷikkuṭ pāṭip paṭikkiṉṟēṉ mēlum paṭippēṉ eṉakkup paṭippitta vāṟē.
translation: I gained a heart free of deceit. Ripening in love, I entered the Hall. I drank the utterly clear flood. I learned the right way to act and attained the way of salvation. I sing and study in the school about the inexhaustible, generous treasure, the Jothi of the Ambalam, my great life, and I will study further, just as I am taught.
commentary: Reaching the sacred space (Ambalam) requires deep inner work: purifying the heart and letting love ripen. The spiritual realization itself is like drinking a "clear flood," an image of being filled with pure grace. This experience begins a new way of living. Life becomes a "school" where the only subject is the divine Jothi (Light), the inexhaustible treasure found within.

translit: kāṭṭaik kaṭantēṉ nāṭṭai aṭaintēṉ kavalai tavirntēṉ uvakai mikuntēṉ vīṭṭaip pukuntēṉ tēṭṭamu tuṇṭēṉ vētāka mattiṉ viḷaivelām peṟṟēṉ āṭṭaip purintē ampalat tōṅkum aiyar tiruvaṭik kāṉanta mākap pāṭṭaip paṭittēṉ paṭikkiṉṟēṉ mēlum paṭippēṉ eṉakkup paṭippitta vāṟē.
translation: I crossed the wilderness and reached the homeland. My worries ceased, my joy abounded. I entered the House of liberation and consumed the sought-after nectar. I received all the fruits of the Vedas and Agamas. With bliss, I have recited a song to the sacred feet of the Master who performs the dance and soars in the Ambalam. I am reciting, and I will recite further, just as I am taught.
commentary: The spiritual path is described here with classic metaphors: a difficult crossing of a "wilderness" (worldly confusion) to finally arrive at the "homeland" (spiritual peace). Reaching this state of liberation puts an end to all anxiety. By experiencing God directly, he has gained the essential wisdom of all scriptures, the Vedas and Agamas (sacred Hindu texts), without needing to study them externally. His life now is a joyful song of gratitude for this highest attainment.

tamil: தேன்பாடல் அன்புடையார் செயப்பொதுவில் நடிக்கின்ற சிவமே ஞானக்
கான்பாடிச் சிவகாம வல்லிமகிழ் கின்றதிருக் கணவா நல்ல
வான்பாட மறைபாட என்னுளத்தே வயங்குகின்ற மன்னா நின்னை
யான்பாட நீதிருத்த என்னதவஞ் செய்தேனோ எந்தாய் எந்தாய்.
translit: tēṉpāṭal aṉpuṭaiyār ceyappotuvil naṭikkiṉṟa civamē ñāṉak kāṉpāṭic civakāma vallimakiḻ kiṉṟatiruk kaṇavā nalla vāṉpāṭa maṟaipāṭa eṉṉuḷattē vayaṅkukiṉṟa maṉṉā niṉṉai yāṉpāṭa nītirutta eṉṉatavañ ceytēṉō entāy entāy.
translation: O Sivam, who dances in the Common Hall as loving devotees sing honeyed songs! O sacred Husband, who makes Sivakama Valli rejoice as she sings in the forest of wisdom! O King, shining in my heart as the good heavens and the Vedas sing! For me to sing of you, and for you to correct my song, what penance did I perform, O my Father, my Father!
commentary: The devotee is filled with overwhelming gratitude and wonder. He is amazed that the Supreme Being (Sivam), who is praised by the heavens and whose dance delights divine wisdom (Sivakama Valli), would listen to his humble, human song. The deepest mystery is that God does listen and personally helps to perfect the devotee's praise, turning worship into an intimate collaboration.

tamil: ஆன்பாலும் நறுந்தேனும் சர்க்கரையும் கூட்டியதெள் ளமுதே என்றன்
ஊன்பாலும் உளப்பாலும் உயிர்ப்பாலும் ஒளிர்கின்ற ஒளியே வேதம்
பூம்பாடல் புனைந்தேத்த என்னுளத்தே ஆடுகின்ற பொன்னே நின்னை
யான்பாட நீதிருத்த என்னதவஞ் செய்தேனோ எந்தாய் எந்தாய்.
translit: āṉpālum naṟuntēṉum carkkaraiyum kūṭṭiyateḷ ḷamutē eṉṟaṉ ūṉpālum uḷappālum uyirppālum oḷirkiṉṟa oḷiyē vētam pūmpāṭal puṉaintētta eṉṉuḷattē āṭukiṉṟa poṉṉē niṉṉai yāṉpāṭa nītirutta eṉṉatavañ ceytēṉō entāy entāy.
translation: O clear nectar, blended with cow's milk, fragrant honey, and sugar! O Light that shines in my flesh, in my mind, and in my soul! O Gold, dancing in my heart as the Vedas compose and praise you with flower-like songs! For me to sing of you, and for you to correct my song, what penance did I perform, O my Father, my Father!
commentary: God is experienced as an intimate, sensory reality. He is the nourishing sweetness of nectar, the radiant light that shines within the devotee's own flesh, mind, and soul. Knowing God in this deeply personal way makes the ability to even speak His name feel like an astonishing, unearned privilege.

translit: poruṭperun taṉimeyp pōkamē eṉṉaip puṟattiṉum akattiṉum puṇarnta teruṭperuñ civamē cuttacaṉ mārkkac celvamē nāṉpeṟṟa ciṟappē maruṭperuṅ kaṭalaik kaṭattieṉ taṉṉai vāḻvitta eṉperu vāḻvē aruṭperuñ cōti ampalat taracē ammaiyē appaṉē apayam.
translation: O unique, true bliss of the great reality! O great Sivam of clarity, who united with me outside and within! O wealth of the Suddha Sanmarkkam, the excellence I have received! O my great life, who made me cross the vast sea of delusion and brought me to life! O great Jothi of grace, King of the Ambalam! O Mother, O Father, grant me refuge!
commentary: This is a cry for refuge made from a place of deep trust, not fear. God, the great bliss, has already saved the devotee by uniting with him both inwardly and outwardly, guiding him across the "sea of delusion." He is the very wealth of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure Path). The appeal to God as both Mother and Father recognizes the divine as the complete and ultimate source of protection and life.

translit: poruṭperu maṟaikaḷ aṉantamā kamaṅkaḷ pukalumōr aṉantammēṟ pōnta teruṭperu veḷimaṭ ṭaḷavilāk kālam tēṭiyum kāṇkilāc civamē maruṭperum pakaitīrt teṉṉaiāṭ koṇṭa vaḷḷalē teḷḷiya amutē aruṭperuñ cōti ampalat taracē ammaiyē appaṉē apayam.
translation: O Sivam, whom countless great, meaningful Vedas and countless proclaimed Agamas cannot find, even after searching for immeasurable time up to the vast expanse of clear wisdom! O benefactor who dispelled the great enemy of delusion and made me your own! O clear ambrosia! O King of the Hall of Vast Grace-Light! O my Mother, O my Father, refuge!
commentary: There is a truth beyond the limits of scripture and intellect. Even the sacred Vedas and Agamas cannot fully grasp God through endless searching. Yet, this same unknowable God (Sivam) can reveal Himself directly to a sincere soul, dispelling delusion through pure grace. This personal experience of being "made His own" is more real and potent than any knowledge gained from books.

translit: poruṭperuñ cuṭarcey kalāntayō kāntam pukaṉṟapō tānta nātāntam teruṭperu vētān tamtikaḻ cittān tattiṉum tittikkum tēṉē maruṭperu iruḷait tīrtteṉai vaḷarkkum māperuṅ karuṇaiyā ramutē aruṭperuñ cōti ampalat taracē ammaiyē appaṉē apayam.
translation: O honey, sweeter than Kalānta and Yogānta, which are made of great, substantial light; sweeter than the proclaimed Bodhānta (the end of knowing) and Nādānta; sweeter even than the great, clear Vedānta and the radiant Siddhānta! O ambrosia of immense compassion who dispels the great darkness of delusion and nurtures me! O King of the Hall of Vast Grace-Light! O my Mother, O my Father, refuge!
commentary: The direct experience of God's grace surpasses even the highest states described in traditional philosophy and mysticism. Vallalar lists several "final states" from various paths: Kalānta (transcending the mind's limits), Yogānta (the goal of yoga), Nādānta (going beyond cosmic sound), and the great philosophical systems of Vedānta and Siddhānta. He says the sweetness of God's presence is greater than all these combined, a nurturing compassion that personally dispels darkness.

translit: aruṭperuñ cōti apayam apayam aruṭperuñ cōti apayam - aruṭperuñ cōti apayamciṟ cōti apayampoṟ cōti apayam tuṇai.
translation: Vast Grace-Light, refuge, refuge! Vast Grace-Light, refuge! Vast Grace-Light, refuge! Refuge in the Light of Consciousness! Refuge in the Golden Light, my support!
commentary: This verse is a powerful, repetitive chant of surrender. By calling for refuge in the "Vast Grace-Light," the "Light of Consciousness," and the "Golden Light," Vallalar emphasizes that the divine is fundamentally a reality of pure, conscious light. The repetition expresses a total and urgent turning to God as the only true support and protection.

translit: tuṇaivā apayam tuyarakala eṉpāl aṇaivā apayam apayam - paṇaivāy vaṭalā apayam varatā apayam naṭanāya kāapayam nāṉ.
translation: O my companion, refuge! You who draw near to me to dispel my sorrow, refuge, refuge! O Lord of flourishing Vadalur, refuge! O giver of boons, refuge! O Lord of the Dance, refuge for me!
commentary: God is a remote power and an intimate companion who actively draws near to end suffering. Vallalar grounds this universal presence in a specific place, Vadalur (the town where he founded his community), showing that the divine can be experienced right here and now. He addresses God as a "giver of boons" and the "Lord of the Dance," acknowledging both the personal and cosmic aspects of the divine.

translit: nāṉākit tāṉāy naṭittaruḷkiṉ ṟāyapayam tēṉāy iṉikkum civaapayam - vāṉāṭu meyyā apayam vimalā apayameṉṟaṉ aiyā apayamapa yam.
translation: You who graciously enact the play of being both myself and yourself, refuge! O Sivam, sweet as honey, refuge! O Truth sought by the heavens, refuge! O immaculate one, refuge! O my master, refuge, refuge!
commentary: The relationship between the individual soul and God is a divine play. Vallalar points to the mystery of God "being both myself and yourself," suggesting a deep unity where the distinction between the worshipper and the worshipped dissolves. This experience is "sweet as honey," a deeply personal and loving relationship with the final truth, his master, Sivam.

translit: apayam patiyē apayam paramē apayam civamē apayam - upaya patattiṟ kapayam parinteṉuḷat tēnal vitattil karuṇai viḷai.
translation: Sanctuary, O Master! Sanctuary, O Supreme One! Sanctuary, O Sivam! Sanctuary! To your twin feet, sanctuary! With compassion, make grace flourish well within my heart.
commentary: Surrendering at the "twin feet" of God is a traditional act of humility. Here, the request is for an inner change. The prayer asks God, the supreme Master (Pati), to make compassion and grace flourish within the heart, turning the act of seeking refuge into a path of spiritual growth.

translit: karuṇā nitiyē apayam kaṉinta aruṇā ṭakaṉē apayam - maruṇāṭum uḷḷak kavalai oḻippāyeṉ vaṉmaṉattup poḷḷaṟ piḻaikaḷ poṟuttu.
translation: Sanctuary, O Treasure of Compassion! Sanctuary, O Performer of the ripe Dance of Grace! Banish the anxieties of a mind that seeks delusion, and forgive the gaping faults of my hard heart.
commentary: This prayer acknowledges the reality of inner struggle: a mind drawn to delusion, a heart hardened by its own faults. By appealing to God as a "Treasure of Compassion," the speaker admits they cannot fix themselves. The only hope is for a grace that can overcome anxiety and a mercy that can forgive even deep-seated flaws.

translit: iṇakkaṟiyīr itamaṟiyīr iruntanilai aṟiyīr iṭamaṟiyīr taṭamaṟiyīr ivvuṭampai eṭutta kaṇakkaṟiyīr vaḻakkaṟiyīr ampalattē māyaik kalakkamaṟa naṭikkiṉṟa tulakkamaṟi vīrō piṇakkaṟivīr puraṭṭaṟivīrpiḻaiceyavē aṟivīr pēruṇavaip peruvayiṟṟup pilattiliṭa aṟivīr maṇakkaṟiyē piṇakkaṟiyē vaṟuppēpērp porippē vaṭaikkuḻampē cāṟēeṉ ṟaṭaikka aṟivīrē.
translation: You do not know harmony, you do not know what is good for you. You do not know your own state, the right place, or the true path. You do not know the purpose for which you took this body, nor the proper way to live. Do you even know the splendor of the One who dances in the Hall, dispelling the confusion of māyā? You know conflict, you know deception; you only know how to do wrong. You know how to shove huge meals into the cave of your giant stomach. You know how to cram it all in, calling out for "fragrant curry," "corpse curry," "sautés," "fries," "lentil-cake stew," and "broth"!
commentary: The tone shifts sharply to a direct and startling critique of ordinary human life. People are experts in conflict and deception and masters of filling their stomachs, yet they know nothing of their own state or of the purpose of this body. Among the dishes they cry out for, Vallalar names 'corpse curry': he calls flesh-food what it is, the body of a slain being. Such people remain unaware of the divine reality that dances in the Hall and dispels māyā.

translit: uḻakkaṟiyīr aḷappataṟkōr uḷavaṟiyīr ulakīr ūraṟiyīr pēraṟiyīr uṇmaioṉṟum aṟiyīr kiḻakkaṟiyīr mēṟkaṟiyīr ampalattē māyaik kētamaṟa naṭikkiṉṟa pātamaṟi vīrō vaḻakkaṟivīr caṇṭaiyiṭṭē vampaḷakka aṟivīr vaṭikkummuṉṉē cōṟeṭuttu vayiṟṟaṭaikka aṟivīr kuḻakkaṟiyēpaḻakkaṟiyē kūṭṭuvarkkak kaṟiyē kuḻampēcā ṟēeṉavum kūṟaaṟi vīrē.
translation: O people of the world, you do not know the proper measure, nor the secret of measurement. You do not know your true place or your true name; you do not know a single thing about truth. You do not know east from west. Do you even know the Feet of the One who dances in the Hall, ending the sorrow of māyā? You know how to argue, start fights, and spread gossip. You know how to grab rice and stuff your stomach before it is even finished cooking. You know how to call out for "mashed curries," "fruit curries," "mixed vegetable dishes," "thick stews," and "broths"!
commentary: Continuing his fierce wake-up call, Vallalar points out the absurdity of a life spent on gossip and gluttony. People may know how to start a fight or how to grab food before it is even ready, but they do not know their "true place or true name." They are spiritually lost, like someone who does not know east from west, yet they are preoccupied with demanding a variety of curries. This is the tragic comedy of a life lived without self-knowledge.

tamil: உணிக்கும் மூட்டுக்கும் கொதுகுக்கும் பேனுக்கும் உவப்புறப் பசிக்கின்றீர்
துணிக்கும் காசுக்கும் சோற்றுக்கும் ஊர்தொறும் சுற்றிப்போய் அலைகின்றீர்
பிணிக்கும் பீடைக்கும் உடலுளம் கொடுக்கின்றீர் பேதையீர் நல்லோர்கள்
பணிக்கும் வேலைசெய் துண்டுடுத் தம்பலம் பரவுதற் கிசையீரே.
translit: uṇikkum mūṭṭukkum kotukukkum pēṉukkum uvappuṟap pacikkiṉṟīr tuṇikkum kācukkum cōṟṟukkum ūrtoṟum cuṟṟippōy alaikiṉṟīr piṇikkum pīṭaikkum uṭaluḷam koṭukkiṉṟīr pētaiyīr nallōrkaḷ paṇikkum vēlaicey tuṇṭuṭut tampalam paravutaṟ kicaiyīrē.
translation: You feel hunger just to please the bedbugs, woodworms, mosquitoes, and lice. For cloth, for cash, and for rice, you roam and wander from town to town. You surrender your body and mind to sickness and affliction. O fools! Why will you not consent to do the work the virtuous ask, eat and dress simply, and praise the Hall?
commentary: Living only to feed the body and acquire possessions is a path to sickness and despair. Vallalar describes this as a life spent feeding insects and wandering aimlessly. He offers a clear alternative: perform service for good people, live simply, and direct your heart towards God, symbolized by praising the divine "Hall."

tamil: மழவுக்கும் ஒருபிடிசோ றளிப்பதன்றி இருபிடிஊண் வழங்கில் இங்கே
உழவுக்கு முதல்குறையும் எனவளர்த்தங் கவற்றைஎலாம் ஓகோ பேயின்
விழவுக்கும் புலால்உண்ணும் விருந்துக்கும் மருந்துக்கும் மெலிந்து மாண்டார்
இழவுக்கும் இடர்க்கொடுங்கோல் இறைவரிக்கும் கொடுத்திழப்பர் என்னே என்னே.
translit: maḻavukkum orupiṭicō ṟaḷippataṉṟi irupiṭiūṇ vaḻaṅkil iṅkē uḻavukku mutalkuṟaiyum eṉavaḷarttaṅ kavaṟṟaielām ōkō pēyiṉ viḻavukkum pulāluṇṇum viruntukkum maruntukkum melintu māṇṭār iḻavukkum iṭarkkoṭuṅkōl iṟaivarikkum koṭuttiḻappar eṉṉē eṉṉē.
translation: They will not give even one handful of rice to a child; if asked for two, they say, "The capital for farming will be reduced." Yet, oh! They give away all they hoarded and lose it to festivals for demons, to flesh-eating feasts, to medicine, to funerals for those who wasted away and died, and to the taxes of a cruel, oppressive government. How astonishing! How astonishing!
commentary: This verse exposes a bitter hypocrisy. People refuse even a handful of rice to a hungry child, fearing it will reduce their capital, yet they lose all they have hoarded to demon-festivals, to feasts where flesh is eaten, to medicine, to funerals, and to the taxes of cruel rulers. Vallalar is astonished that wealth denied to the hungry is poured into what harms and destroys.

tamil: கடுகாட்டுக் கறிக்கிடுக தாளிக்க எனக்கழறிக் களிக்கா நின்ற
முடுகாட்டுக் கூற்றுவரும் சாவீரால் சாவதற்கு முன்னே நீவீர்
translit: kaṭukāṭṭuk kaṟikkiṭuka tāḷikka eṉakkaḻaṟik kaḷikkā niṉṟa cuṭukāṭṭup piṇaṅkāḷic cukamaṉaittum kaṇaccukamēcollak kēṇmiṉ muṭukāṭṭuk kūṟṟuvarum cāvīrāl cāvataṟku muṉṉē nīvīr iṭukāṭṭuppiṇaṅkaṇṭāl ēttumiṉō emaiyumivvā ṟiṭukaeṉṟē.
translation: “Add mustard! Temper the curry!” you shout and rejoice, O you corpses destined for the cremation ground! Listen to what I tell you: all this pleasure lasts only for a moment. The hastening god of death will come, and you will die. Before you die, when you see a corpse in the burial ground, you should praise it, saying, “Place me here just like this too.”
commentary: All worldly pleasures are fleeting, because death is inevitable. Vallalar's harsh tone is a deliberate shock, meant to awaken us from our distractions. The strange instruction to see a corpse and wish for the same is not a death wish. It is a call to accept mortality and, in line with his other teachings, to choose burial over cremation, returning the body respectfully to the earth rather than destroying it.

tamil: மதிப்பாலை அருட்பாலை ஆனந்தப் பாலைஉண்ண மறந்தார் சில்லோர்
விதிப்பாலை அறியேம்தாய்ப் பாலைஉண்டு கிடந்தழுது விளைவிற் கேற்பக்
துதிப்பாலை அருள்தருநம் தேவசிகா மணித்தேவைத் துதியார் அன்றே.
translit: matippālai aruṭpālai āṉantap pālaiuṇṇa maṟantār cillōr vitippālai aṟiyēmtāyp pālaiuṇṭu kiṭantaḻutu viḷaiviṟ kēṟpak kotippālai uṇarvaḻikkum kuṭippālai maṭippālaik kuṭippārantō tutippālai aruḷtarunam tēvacikā maṇittēvait tutiyār aṉṟē.
translation: Some people have forgotten to drink the milk of wisdom, the milk of grace, and the milk of bliss. Saying, "We do not know the decree of fate," they, who once drank only mother's milk as they lay crying, now, according to their actions, drink boiling toddy, the liquor that destroys consciousness, and the milk of laziness. Alas! They will not praise our Deva Sikamani Devan, the gem-like God who grants the very grace of praise.
commentary: Vallalar uses the metaphor of "milk" to contrast spiritual nourishment with worldly intoxication. Instead of drinking the "milk of wisdom" and the "milk of grace," people choose cheap substitutes like alcohol ("boiling toddy") and laziness that dull the mind. This is a willful act of forgetting their divine potential and ignoring the very God, "Deva Sikamani Devan" (a name for the supreme Lord), who offers true and lasting bliss.

translit: cirippilē poḻutu kaḻikkumiv vāḻkkaic ciṟiyavar cintaimāt tiramō poruppilē tavañcey periyartam maṉamum puḷippilē tuvarppilē uvarppuk karippilē koṭiya kayappilē kaṭiya kārppilē kārppoṭu kalanta erippilē pukuva taṉṟieḷ aḷavum iṉippilē pukukiṉṟa tilaiyē.
translation: Is it only the minds of the small-minded people of this world, who spend their time in laughter? No, even the minds of great ones who perform penance on mountains delve into sourness, astringency, saltiness, terrible bitterness, harsh pungency, and the burning heat mixed with pungency. Not even for the measure of a sesame seed do their minds enter into sweetness.
commentary: The human mind has a natural tendency toward negative states. Using the metaphor of taste, this verse points out that even great spiritual seekers often get stuck in "sour" and "bitter" thoughts and feelings. Without divine grace, the mind rarely enters the "sweetness" of peace and bliss.

translit: pūvār koṉṟaic ceñcaṭai yāḷar pukaḻāḷar īvār pōlvan teṉmaṉai pukkār eḻilkāṭṭi tēvār tillaic ciṟcapai mēvum tiruvāḷar āvā eṉṟār eṉṉaṭi ammā avarcūtē.
translation: The praiseworthy one with red, matted hair adorned with konrai flowers came like a great benefactor and entered my house. The glorious Lord who presides over the Chit Sabhai in Tillai, revered by the gods, showed me his beauty, then simply exclaimed, “Alas!” What a trick of his this is, my dear friend.
commentary: Speaking as a devotee, Vallalar describes a mystifying encounter with God. The Lord appears, shows his glorious form, and then withdraws, leaving the soul in a state of longing and confusion. This "trick" is a common theme in devotional poetry, representing the divine play that deepens the devotee's love and yearning for union. The Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness) is both the temple at Chidambaram and the inner space of the heart where God reveals himself.

translit: nalviṉai ciṟitum nayantilēṉ eṉpāḷ nāṉceyat takkatē teṉpāḷ celviṉai oṉṟun terintilaṉ aiyō teyvamē teyvamē eṉpāḷ velviṉai maṉṟil naṭampuri kiṉṟār viruppilar eṉmicai eṉpāḷ valviṉai uṭaiyēṉ eṉṟuḷam pataippāḷ varuntuvāḷ nāṉpeṟṟa makaḷē.
translation: She says, "I have not desired even a little good karma." She asks, "What is there for me to do?" "Alas, I know nothing of the way forward," she cries, "O God, O God!" She says, "He who performs the victorious dance in the hall has no desire for me." Her heart trembles, saying, "I am one with powerful karma." She suffers so, the daughter I bore.
commentary: A mother observes her daughter, who represents the soul in a state of spiritual crisis. The soul feels trapped by her past actions (karma) and utterly abandoned by God. This verse powerfully conveys the "dark night of the soul," a painful period of despair and helplessness that can precede a spiritual breakthrough.

translit: nātararuṭ peruñcōti nāyakareṉ taṉaiyē nayantukoṇṭa taṉittalaivar ñāṉacapā patiyār vātanaṭam purikaruṇai mānitiyār varatar vaḷḷalelām vallavarmā nallavareṉ iṭattē kātaluṭaṉ varukiṉṟār eṉṟupara nātam kaḷippuṟavē toṉikkiṉṟa tantaratun tupitāṉ ētamaṟa muḻaṅkukiṉṟa teṉṟucollik koṇṭē eḻukiṉṟāḷ toḻukiṉṟāḷ eṉṉuṭaiya makaḷē.
translation: "The Lord, the Master of the vast grace-light, the singular Chief who desired me for Himself, the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom, the great treasure of compassion who performs the sublime dance, the bestower of boons, the benefactor, the all-powerful, the greatly good one, He is coming to me with love!" she says. She says, "The supreme sound joyfully resonates, the celestial drum thunders flawlessly." Saying this, my daughter rises and worships.
commentary: Following the previous verse's despair, this is the moment of ecstatic breakthrough. The soul now has a direct experience of God, whom she calls the Lord of the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), coming to unite with her. She hears the supreme celestial sound (para nādam) announcing his arrival. Desolation is replaced by joyous worship, showing that grace can arrive when one feels most lost.

tamil: என்பாடென் றிலைஎன்னால் துரும்பும் அசைத் திடமுடியா திதுகால் தொட்டுப்
பொன்பாடெவ் விதத்தானும் புரிந்துகொண்டு நீதானே புரத்தல் வேண்டும்
உன்பாடு நான்உரைத்தேன் நீஇனிச்சும் மாஇருக்க ஒண்ணா தண்ணா.
translit: aṉpāṭu tiruppotuvil āṭukiṉṟa aṭimēl āṇai eṉpāṭeṉ ṟilaieṉṉāl turumpum acait tiṭamuṭiyā titukāl toṭṭup poṉpāṭev vitattāṉum purintukoṇṭu nītāṉē purattal vēṇṭum uṉpāṭu nāṉuraittēṉ nīiṉiccum māirukka oṇṇā taṇṇā.
translation: I swear on the feet that dance in the sacred common hall filled with love: my own efforts are no more. I cannot move even a blade of grass. From this moment on, you yourself must understand my plight in every way and protect me. I have done my part by telling you. O great one, you can no longer just remain still.
commentary: Here, the devotee makes a radical declaration of surrender. Swearing an oath, they renounce all personal effort, claiming they are so helpless they "cannot move even a blade of grass." It is an act of turning over complete responsibility to God. It is a bold statement: having realized their own powerlessness, they insist that God must now step in and take charge of their protection.

tamil: முன்பாடு பின்பயன்தந் திடும்எனவே உரைக்கின்றோர் மொழிகள் எல்லாம்
இன்பாடும் இவ்வுலகில் என்னறிவில் இலைஅதனால் எல்லாம் வல்லோய்
அன்பாடு திருப்பொதுவில் ஆடுகின்றோய் அருட்சோதி அளித்துக் காத்தல்
உன்பாடு நான்உரைத்தேன் எனக்கொருபா டுண்டோநீ உரைப்பாய் அப்பா.
translit: muṉpāṭu piṉpayaṉtan tiṭumeṉavē uraikkiṉṟōr moḻikaḷ ellām iṉpāṭum ivvulakil eṉṉaṟivil ilaiataṉāl ellām vallōy aṉpāṭu tiruppotuvil āṭukiṉṟōy aruṭcōti aḷittuk kāttal uṉpāṭu nāṉuraittēṉ eṉakkorupā ṭuṇṭōnī uraippāy appā.
translation: The words of those who say that past actions yield future results do not exist in my consciousness in this pleasant world. Therefore, O All-Powerful One, O You who dance in the sacred common hall filled with love, it is your responsibility to grant the grace-light and protect me. I have stated this. Is there any responsibility left for me? You tell me, Father.
commentary: The devotee takes the previous verse's surrender a step further. People say that earlier effort brings later fruit, but he finds no such effort of his own to rely on. Therefore, he says, granting the Grace-Light and protecting him is wholly God's task, and he asks whether any burden is left for him at all.

tamil: உன்ஆணை உன்னைவிட உற்றதுணை வேறிலைஎன் உடையாய் அந்தோ
என்நாணைக் காத்தருளி இத்தினமே அருட்சோதி ஈதல் வேண்டும்
அந்நாள்நை யாதபடி அருள்புரிந்த பெருங்கருணை அரசே என்னை
முன்னாள்நின் அடியவன்என் றுலகறிந்த இந்நாள்என் மொழிந்தி டாதே.
translit: uṉāṇai uṉṉaiviṭa uṟṟatuṇai vēṟilaieṉ uṭaiyāy antō eṉnāṇaik kāttaruḷi ittiṉamē aruṭcōti ītal vēṇṭum annāḷnai yātapaṭi aruḷpurinta peruṅkaruṇai aracē eṉṉai muṉṉāḷniṉ aṭiyavaṉeṉ ṟulakaṟinta innāḷeṉ moḻinti ṭātē.
translation: I swear on you, there is no closer support than you, O my Master. Alas, you must protect my honor and grant the grace-light this very day. O King of great compassion who showed grace so I would not suffer back then, do not now disown me, on this day when the world knows I have long been your devotee.
commentary: This is a deeply personal and urgent appeal. The devotee reminds God of their long relationship, framing salvation as a matter of honor: since the world knows them as God's devotee, to be abandoned now would be a public shame. The plea for grace "this very day" shows that the spiritual struggle has reached a breaking point where a future promise is not enough. The argument rests on the intimacy and history of their connection to God.

tamil: தூங்காதே விழித்திருக்கும் சூதறிவித் தெனைஆண்ட துரையே என்னை
நீங்காதே என்னுயிரில் கலந்துகொண்ட பதியேகால் நீட்டிப் பின்னே
வாங்காதே விரைந்திவண்நீ வரல்வேண்டும் தாழ்த்திடில்என் மனந்தான் சற்றும்
தாங்காதே இதுநினது தனித்ததிரு வுளமறிந்த சரிதம் தானே.
translit: tūṅkātē viḻittirukkum cūtaṟivit teṉaiāṇṭa turaiyē eṉṉai nīṅkātē eṉṉuyiril kalantukoṇṭa patiyēkāl nīṭṭip piṉṉē vāṅkātē viraintivaṇnī varalvēṇṭum tāḻttiṭileṉ maṉantāṉ caṟṟum tāṅkātē ituniṉatu taṉittatiru vuḷamaṟinta caritam tāṉē.
translation: O Lord who ruled me by teaching me the secret of staying awake without sleeping! O Master who never leaves me, who has mingled with my very life! You must come here swiftly; do not start to come and then pull back. If you delay, my mind cannot bear it in the least. This is a fact known to your own singular, sacred will, is it not?
commentary: Having experienced a deep connection with the divine, the soul finds any separation unbearable. Vallalar speaks of being taught the secret of "staying awake without sleeping," a state of continuous spiritual consciousness. Now, he warns God that his mind cannot endure any delay in God's full and final presence, capturing the intense fragility and longing of a soul on the verge of union.

tamil: இயங்காளி புலிகரடி எனப்பெயர்கேட் டுளம்நடுங்கி இருந்தேன் ஊரில்
சயங்காளிக் கோயிலைக்கண் டஞ்சிமனம் தழுதழுத்துத் தளர்ந்தேன் இந்தப்
பயங்காளிப் பயல்போலப் பயந்தவர்கள் எங்குளர்காண் பதியே என்னை
வயங்காளில் ஒருவன்என நினையேல்கைப் பிள்ளைஎன மதித்தி டாயே.
translit: iyaṅkāḷi pulikaraṭi eṉappeyarkēṭ ṭuḷamnaṭuṅki iruntēṉ ūril cayaṅkāḷik kōyilaikkaṇ ṭañcimaṉam taḻutaḻuttut taḷarntēṉ intap payaṅkāḷip payalpōlap payantavarkaḷ eṅkuḷarkāṇ patiyē eṉṉai vayaṅkāḷil oruvaṉeṉa niṉaiyēlkaip piḷḷaieṉa matitti ṭāyē.
translation: I used to tremble in my heart just hearing the names of tigers and bears. Seeing the temple of victorious Kali in the town, I became afraid, my mind faltered, and I grew weak. O Master, where can you find anyone who gets as scared as this cowardly boy? Do not think of me as a strong man; regard me as a child in your hands.
commentary: Spiritual strength is found in admitting total helplessness before God. Vallalar presents himself as a "cowardly boy," afraid of everything, to make a powerful point: he is a child who needs to be held and protected. This vulnerability is the very thing that invites God's grace.

tamil: சிறுசெயலைச் செயும்உலகச் சிறுநடையோர் பலபுகலத் தினந்தோ றுந்தான்
உறுசெயலை அறியாஇச் சிறுபயலைப் பிடித்தலைத்தல் உவப்போ கண்டாய்
தெறுசெயலைத் தவிர்த்தெல்லாச் சித்தியும்பெற் றிடஅழியாத் தேகன் ஆகப்
பெறுசெயலை எனக்களித்தே மறுசெயலைப் புரிகஎனைப் பெற்ற தேவே.
translit: ciṟuceyalaic ceyumulakac ciṟunaṭaiyōr palapukalat tiṉantō ṟuntāṉ uṟuceyalai aṟiyāic ciṟupayalaip piṭittalaittal uvappō kaṇṭāy teṟuceyalait tavirttellāc cittiyumpeṟ ṟiṭaaḻiyāt tēkaṉ ākap peṟuceyalai eṉakkaḷittē maṟuceyalaip purikaeṉaip peṟṟa tēvē.
translation: As worldly people of petty ways who perform trivial deeds say many things, is it a pleasure, tell me, to seize and torment this little boy who does not know the proper action to take each day? Grant me the attainment of an imperishable body with all siddhis, averting destructive deeds. O God who gave birth to me, then perform the next action.
commentary: The ultimate goal is a complete transformation of life in this world, more than a reward in the next. Vallalar asks God to stop the petty harassments of worldly life by granting him the final attainment: an imperishable, deathless body equipped with all siddhis (supernatural powers). This state of being, he argues, will resolve his struggles and allow God to proceed with the divine plan.

translit: aṅkē uṉṟaṉ aṉparkaḷ ellām amarkiṉṟār iṅkē nītāṉ eṉṉaḷa viṉṉum iraṅkāyēl eṅkē pōkēṉ yāroṭu nōkēṉ etuceykēṉ ceṅkēḻ vēṇit tiṅkaḷ aṇintaruḷ civaṉēyō.
translation: Over there, all your devotees are seated. If, over here, you still show me no compassion, where can I go? To whom can I lament my sorrow? What can I do? O Siva, who graciously wears the crescent moon in your red-hued matted locks!
commentary: The sight of other devotees enjoying God’s presence makes the feeling of separation even more painful. In a cry of pure desperation, Vallalar expresses a sense of absolute spiritual homelessness: if God will not have him, there is nowhere else in the universe to turn. This is the ultimate lament of a soul that has staked its entire existence on divine love.

translit: īyō ṭuṟaḻum ciṟiyēṉ aḷavil entāyniṉ cēyō ṭuṟaḻum pēraruḷ vaṇṇat tiruvuḷḷam kāyō paḻamō yātō aṟiyēṉ kavalkiṉṟēṉ tīyō ṭuṟaḻum tiruvaruḷ vaṭivac civaṉēyō.
translation: Toward me, who am as insignificant as a fly, I do not know if your sacred will, O my Father, with its nature of great grace like that shown to your own son, is an unripe fruit or a ripe one, and I am distressed. O Siva, whose form of sacred grace is like a fire!
commentary: Using the metaphor of a fruit, Vallalar expresses his anxiety while waiting for divine grace. He asks God if grace is ready for him, like a ripe fruit, or if the time is not yet right. This uncertainty, coming from one who feels as small as a fly, is a moving expression of a devotee's painful suspense.

tamil: உடைய நாயகன் பிள்ளைநான் ஆகில்எவ் வுலகமும் ஒருங்கின்பம்
அடைய நான்அருட் சோதிபெற் றழிவிலா யாக்கைகொண் டுலகெல்லாம்
மிடைய அற்புதப் பெருஞ்செயல் நாடொறும் விளைத்தெங்கும் விளையாடத்
தடைய தற்றநல் தருணம்இத் தருணமாத் தழைக்கஇத் தனியேற்கே.
translit: uṭaiya nāyakaṉ piḷḷaināṉ ākilev vulakamum oruṅkiṉpam aṭaiya nāṉaruṭ cōtipeṟ ṟaḻivilā yākkaikoṇ ṭulakellām miṭaiya aṟputap peruñceyal nāṭoṟum viḷaitteṅkum viḷaiyāṭat taṭaiya taṟṟanal taruṇamit taruṇamāt taḻaikka:it taṉiyēṟkē.
translation: If I am the child of the Master who possesses all, then for every world to attain bliss as one, I must receive the Grace-Light and an indestructible body. I must perform great and wondrous deeds daily, playing everywhere and filling the world. For this to happen without hindrance, this very moment is the perfect, flourishing time for me, this solitary one.
commentary: Here, personal salvation becomes a universal mission. Vallalar states that if he is truly God’s child, he must be given an immortal body and divine light so he can bring bliss to all worlds. His transformation is the necessary first step for a cosmic work of compassion.

tamil: கோது கொடுத்த மனச்சிறியேன் குற்றம் குணமாக் கொண்டேஇப்
போது கொடுத்த நின்அருளாம் பொருளை நினைக்கும் போதெல்லாம்
தாது கொடுத்த பெருங்களிப்பும் சாலா தென்றால் சாமிநினக்
கேது கொடுப்பேன் கேட்பதன்முன் எல்லாம் கொடுக்க வல்லாயே.
translit: kōtu koṭutta maṉacciṟiyēṉ kuṟṟam kuṇamāk koṇṭēip pōtu koṭutta niṉaruḷām poruḷai niṉaikkum pōtellām tātu koṭutta peruṅkaḷippum cālā teṉṟāl cāminiṉak kētu koṭuppēṉ kēṭpataṉmuṉ ellām koṭukka vallāyē.
translation: I am a small person with a mind that produces faults, but you have taken my faults as virtues. Whenever I think of the treasure of Your grace that You just gave me, even the great ecstasy given by flower pollen is not enough. My Lord, what can I give You? You are able to give everything even before one asks.
commentary: In a moment of deep gratitude, Vallalar marvels at how God’s grace is so vast it sees his flaws as virtues. This gift of grace is so overwhelming that he is left wondering what he could possibly give in return to a God who gives everything without even being asked.

tamil: கன்றுடைய பசுப்போலே கசிந்துருகும் அன்பரெலாம் காணக் காட்டும்
என்றுடைய நாயகனே எல்லாஞ்செய் வல்லவனே இலங்குஞ் சோதி
மன்றுடைய மணவாளா மன்னவனே என்னிருகண் மணியே நின்னை
அன்றுடையேன் இன்றுவிடேன் ஆணைஉன்மேல் ஆணைஉன்மேல் ஆணை ஐயா.
translit: kaṉṟuṭaiya pacuppōlē kacinturukum aṉparelām kāṇak kāṭṭum eṉṟuṭaiya nāyakaṉē ellāñcey vallavaṉē ilaṅkuñ cōti maṉṟuṭaiya maṇavāḷā maṉṉavaṉē eṉṉirukaṇ maṇiyē niṉṉai aṉṟuṭaiyēṉ iṉṟuviṭēṉ āṇaiuṉmēl āṇaiuṉmēl āṇai aiyā.
translation: You show yourself to all the devotees who melt and dissolve in love like a cow with its calf. O Master who has always been mine! O omnipotent one! O Bridegroom of the radiant Hall! My King! The apple of my two eyes! I possessed you in the past, and I will not let you go today. I swear on you, I swear on you, I swear on you, my Lord!
commentary: Shifting from longing to certainty, Vallalar declares an unbreakable bond with God. He sees how God melts the hearts of devotees, and he stakes his own claim with fierce, possessive love. The triple oath is a powerful assertion that his connection to God is eternal, something he has always had and will never relinquish.

tamil: திருநி லைத்துநல் அருளொடும் அன்பொடும் சிறப்பொடும் செழித்தோங்க
உருநி லைத்திவண் மகிழ்வொடு வாழ்வுற உவந்துநின் அருள்செய்வாய்
இருநி லத்தவர் இன்புறத் திருவருள் இயல்வடி வொடுமன்றில்
குருநி லைத்தசற் குருஎனும் இறைவநின் குரைகழற் பதம்போற்றி.
translit: tiruni laittunal aruḷoṭum aṉpoṭum ciṟappoṭum ceḻittōṅka uruni laittivaṇ makiḻvoṭu vāḻvuṟa uvantuniṉ aruḷceyvāy iruni lattavar iṉpuṟat tiruvaruḷ iyalvaṭi voṭumaṉṟil kuruni laittacaṟ kurueṉum iṟaivaniṉ kuraikaḻaṟ patampōṟṟi.
translation: So that sacredness may be established and flourish with good grace, love, and excellence, please be pleased to grant your grace, that I may be established in form here and live with joy. Praise to your resounding, ankleted feet, O Lord! You are the true Guru established as the Guru in the Hall, appearing with a form of sacred grace so that the people of this great world may rejoice.
commentary: The request for a stable physical life is made for a spiritual purpose. Vallalar asks to be a joyful, embodied presence on earth so he can serve as a conduit for grace, allowing others to experience divine happiness. He wishes to live for the world's benefit, reflecting the role of a Guru (spiritual teacher).

tamil: குற்றம் புரிதல் எனக்கியல்பே குணமாக் கொள்ளல் உனக்கியல்பே
சிற்றம் பலவா இனிச்சிறியேன் செப்பும் முகமன் யாதுளது
தெற்றென் றடியேன் சிந்தைதனைத் தெளிவித் தச்சந் துயர்தீர்த்தே
இற்றைப் பொழுதே அருட்சோதி ஈக தருணம் இதுவாமே.
translit: kuṟṟam purital eṉakkiyalpē kuṇamāk koḷḷal uṉakkiyalpē ciṟṟam palavā iṉicciṟiyēṉ ceppum mukamaṉ yātuḷatu teṟṟeṉ ṟaṭiyēṉ cintaitaṉait teḷivit taccan tuyartīrttē iṟṟaip poḻutē aruṭcōti īka taruṇam ituvāmē.
translation: To commit faults is my nature; to accept them as virtues is your nature. O Lord of the small sacred hall! What more flattering words can this small person say? Make this devotee's mind clear and certain, dispel my fear and sorrow, and grant the Grace-Light. This very day is the opportune moment.
commentary: The most honest prayer is simply admitting our flawed nature and God's compassionate one. Vallalar suggests this simple truth is more meaningful than any elaborate praise. This radical honesty clears the way for a direct and urgent request: for the Grace-Light to bring clarity and end all fear today.

tamil: அருளா ரமுதே என்னுடைய அன்பே என்றன் அறிவேஎன்
பொருளாய் அகத்தும் புறத்தும்என்னைப் புணர்ந்த கருணைப் பொருப்பேமெய்த்
தெருளாம் ஒளியே வெளியாகச் சிற்றம் பலத்தே நடிக்கின்றோய்
இருளா யினஎல் லாம்தவிர்த்தென் எண்ணம் முடிப்பாய் இப்போதே.
translit: aruḷā ramutē eṉṉuṭaiya aṉpē eṉṟaṉ aṟivēeṉ poruḷāy akattum puṟattumeṉṉaip puṇarnta karuṇaip poruppēmeyt teruḷām oḷiyē veḷiyākac ciṟṟam palattē naṭikkiṉṟōy iruḷā yiṉael lāmtavirtteṉ eṇṇam muṭippāy ippōtē.
translation: Oh nectar full of grace! My love! My knowing! Oh mountain of compassion who, as my very substance, has united with me inside and out! Oh light of true clarity! You who dance openly in the Chitrambalam, dispel everything that is darkness and fulfill my intention right now.
commentary: God is experienced as the very substance of life, present both within and without. The dance in the Chitrambalam (the small hall, a symbol for the inner space of consciousness) is a vision of the Divine active within the self. The prayer asks this inner light to fulfill its purpose by dispelling all remaining darkness.

tamil: மந்திரம் அறியேன் மற்றை மணிமருந் தறியேன் வேறு
தந்திரம் அறியேன் எந்தத் தகவுகொண் டடைவேன் எந்தாய்
இந்திரன் முதலாம் தேவர் இறைஞ்சப்பொன் மன்றில் வேணிச்
சந்திரன் ஆட இன்பத் தனிநடம் புரியும் தேவே.
translit: mantiram aṟiyēṉ maṟṟai maṇimarun taṟiyēṉ vēṟu tantiram aṟiyēṉ entat takavukoṇ ṭaṭaivēṉ entāy intiraṉ mutalām tēvar iṟaiñcappoṉ maṉṟil vēṇic cantiraṉ āṭa iṉpat taṉinaṭam puriyum tēvē.
translation: I do not know mantras, I do not know gems or medicines, I do not know other methods. By what merit will I reach you, my father? Oh God who performs the unique dance of bliss in the golden hall, as the moon in your braided locks dances, while Indra and the other gods worship you!
commentary: The true path to God requires no complex rituals, secret mantras, or accumulated merit. By confessing ignorance of all conventional religious methods, the speaker stands in total humility. This state of sincere helplessness, without any claim to worthiness, becomes the most powerful way to open oneself to grace.

tamil: கருணைக் கடலே அதில்எழுந்த கருணை அமுதே கனியமுதில்
தருணச் சுவையே சுவைஅனைத்தும் சார்ந்த பதமே தற்பதமே
பொருண்மெய்ப் பரமே சிதம்பரமாம் பொதுவில் நடிக்கும் பரம்பரமே
தெருண்மெய்க் கருத்தில் கலந்தெனையும் சித்தி நிலைகள் தெரித்தருளே.
