translit: karuṇaik kaṭalē atileḻunta karuṇai amutē kaṉiyamutil taruṇac cuvaiyē cuvaiaṉaittum cārnta patamē taṟpatamē poruṇmeyp paramē citamparamām potuvil naṭikkum paramparamē teruṇmeyk karuttil kalanteṉaiyum citti nilaikaḷ terittaruḷē.
translation: Oh ocean of compassion! Oh nectar of compassion that arose from it! Oh fresh sweetness in the ripened nectar! Oh state that contains all sweetness! Oh state of That-ness! Oh supreme reality of true substance! Oh supreme Being who dances in the common space of Chidambaram! Mingle with my truly clarified thought and graciously reveal to me the states of siddhi.
commentary: This verse builds an image of God as the ultimate source of all sweetness, starting from a vast ocean of compassion and refining it to the most potent essence. The speaker asks for union with this divine nature, called Tatpadam (the state of "That-ness" or ultimate reality), believing this union will naturally grant him siddhi (higher spiritual capacities and powers).

tamil: கலக்கம் அற்றுநான் நின்றனைப் பாடியே களிக்கின்ற நாள்எந்நாள்
இலக்கம் உற்றறிந் திடஅருள் புரிகுவாய் எந்தைஇவ் விரவின்கண்
துலக்க முற்றசிற் றம்பலத் தாடுமெய்ச் சோதியே சுகவாழ்வே
அலக்கண் அற்றிடத் திருவருள் புரியும்என் அப்பனே அடியேற்கே.
translit: kalakkam aṟṟunāṉ niṉṟaṉaip pāṭiyē kaḷikkiṉṟa nāḷennāḷ ilakkam uṟṟaṟin tiṭaaruḷ purikuvāy entaiiv viraviṉkaṇ tulakka muṟṟaciṟ ṟampalat tāṭumeyc cōtiyē cukavāḻvē alakkaṇ aṟṟiṭat tiruvaruḷ puriyumeṉ appaṉē aṭiyēṟkē.
translation: When is the day I will rejoice, singing of you without agitation? Grant your grace so I can know you as the goal, my father, on this very night. Oh true Jothi that dances in the radiant Chitrambalam! Oh blissful life! My father, grant your sacred grace to me, your servitor, so that my suffering may cease.
commentary: The speaker longs for a state of constant, peaceful joy in God, free from mental turmoil. This is not a vague future hope; he begs for this transformation to happen "on this very night." The appeal is to God as Jothi, a divine light dancing in the inner space of consciousness, to end his suffering now.

translit: paṇṭu niṉtirup pātama laraiyē pāṭi yāṭiya pattimai yōraippōl toṇṭu koṇṭeṉai āṇṭaṉai iṉṟutāṉ tuṭṭaṉ eṉṟutu rattiṭal naṉṟukol kuṇṭu nīrkkaṭal cūḻula kattuḷōr kuṟṟam āyiraṅ kōṭicey tālummuṉ koṇṭu piṉkulam pēcuva rōeṉaik kuṟikkoḷ vāyeṇ kuṇantikaḻ vaḷḷalē.
translation: Like the devotees of the past who sang and danced to your sacred lotus feet, you accepted my service and ruled me. Is it right to cast me away today, calling me a wicked one? People of this world, surrounded by the deep sea, might commit a billion faults, but do others later bring up those faults and speak ill of their background? Take me into your consideration, oh benefactor who shines with eight qualities.
commentary: The speaker takes an intimate, almost argumentative tone with God, reminding God of their past relationship. He questions if it is fair to be rejected now for his flaws, using a human analogy: good people do not hold past mistakes against others. It is a bold appeal to God's own nature as a benefactor, asking for the same level of forgiveness and consideration.

translit: kaṇṇelām nirampap pēroḷi kāṭṭik karuṇaimā maḻaipoḻi mukilē viṇṇelām niṟainta viḷakkamē eṉṉuḷ mēviya meymmaiyē maṉṟuḷ eṇṇelām kaṭantē ilaṅkiya patiyē iṉṟunī ēḻaiyēṉ maṉattup puṇṇelām tavirttup poruḷelām koṭuttup pukunteṉa tuḷaṅkalan taruḷē.
translation: O Cloud pouring a great rain of compassion, showing a vast light that fills the eyes! O Lamp filling all of heaven! O Truth dwelling within me! O Lord shining in the sacred hall, transcending all thought! Today, heal all the wounds in this poor one's mind, give all substance, and enter to merge with my soul in grace.
commentary: God is addressed in many ways: as an overwhelming light, a rain of compassion, and the truth dwelling inside. The speaker asks this many-sided reality to perform a complete inner healing, mending the "wounds in the mind" and fully merging with his soul. This is a prayer for total psychological and spiritual integration.

translit: aṉpilēṉ eṉiṉum aṟivilēṉ eṉiṉum aṉṟuvan tāṇṭaṉai ataṉāl tuṉpilēṉ eṉa:iv vulakelām aṟiyac colliṉēṉ colliya nāṉē iṉpilēṉ eṉa:iṉ ṟuraittiṭal aḻakō eṉaiula kavamatit tiṭileṉ eṉpilē kalantāy niṉakkumvan tiṭumē eytuka virainteṉa tiṭattē.
translation: Even though I am without love, even though I am without knowledge, you came that day and made me yours. Because of that, I declared for all the world to know, "I have no suffering." Is it fitting, then, for me who said that to now say, "I have no bliss"? If the world holds me in contempt, what does it matter? You have merged into my very bones; the shame will come upon you too. Come to me, quickly.
commentary: In a tone of startling intimacy, the speaker holds God accountable for his spiritual state. He argues that since he has already publicly declared his freedom from suffering because of God, his current lack of bliss brings shame upon God himself. It expresses a deep bond where the devotee's well-being is inseparable from the divine's reputation.

translit: vāṉvēṇṭu ciṟṟam palattē vayaṅki vaḷaramutat tēṉvēṇṭi ṉēṉit taruṇat taruḷceyka ceytilaiyēl ūṉvēṇṭum eṉṉuyir nīttuniṉ mēṟpaḻi yōviḷaippēṉ nāṉvēṇṭu mōpaḻi tāṉvēṇṭu mōcolka nāyakaṉē.
translation: In the Little Hall that heaven itself desires, I asked for the ambrosial honey that shines and ever grows. Grant your grace right now. If you do not, I will abandon this life that clings to flesh and make you bear the blame. Do you want me, or do you want the blame? Tell me, O Master!
commentary: This verse expresses an extreme state of spiritual longing, framed as an ultimatum. Life without the "ambrosial honey" of grace is so meaningless that the speaker would rather die and let the blame fall on God for failing him. This intense language reveals a love so absolute that it cannot bear separation, asking for grace from the "Little Hall" (ciṟṟampalam), the sacred center of consciousness.

translit: cevvaṇat tavarum maṟaiyumā kamamum tēvarum muṉivarum piṟarum ivvaṇat tatueṉ ṟaṟintiṭaṟ karitām entainiṉ tiruvaruḷ tiṟattai evvaṇat taṟivēṉ eṅṅaṉam pukalvēṉ eṉtarat tiyaluva tēyō ovvaṇat taracē eṉakkeṉa iṅkōr uṇarcciyum uṇṭukol uṇarttē.
translation: O my Father, the power of your sacred grace is such that the righteous, the Vedas, the Agamas, the celestials, the sages, and all others find it impossible to know its nature. How, then, can I know it? How can I speak of it? Is it possible for one of my stature? O peerless King! Is there even a single perception here that I can call my own? Please, make me realize it.
commentary: The tone shifts from demanding intimacy to deep awe. The speaker acknowledges that the nature of divine grace is a mystery that even the highest scriptures (Vedas and Agamas) and wisest sages cannot fathom. Faced with this immensity, he feels his own powerlessness, realizing that every flicker of his own awareness is a gift from God.

translit: uṇarntuṇarn tāṅkē uṇarntuṇarn tuṇarā uṇarntavar uṇarcciyāṉ nuḻaintē tiṇarntaṉar āki viyantiṭa viḷaṅkum civapatat talaivaniṉ iyalaip puṇarntaniṉ aruḷē aṟiyumnāṉ aṟintu pukaṉṟiṭum tarañciṟi tuḷaṉō koṇarntoru poruḷeṉ karaṅkoḷak koṭutta kurueṉak kūṟaleṉ kuṟippē.
translation: O Chief of the state of Siva! Though they seek to realize it again and again, they do not realize it. Yet those who have truly realized it enter through that very realization, become dense with it, and stand in wonder as you shine. Only your grace, united with you, knows your nature. Do I have even a slight capacity to know and declare it? My sole intention is to call you the Guru who brought a substance and placed it in my hands to hold.
commentary: Divine reality, the ultimate state of Siva (Civapatam), cannot be captured by the striving mind. It can only be entered into through a direct, intuitive realization that leaves one in a state of wonder. The speaker confesses that he has no power to describe this state; only grace itself can know it. His only purpose, he says, is to praise God as the Guru who made this sublime reality a tangible experience for him.

translit: ayalaṟiyēṉ niṉatumalar aṭiaṉṟic ciṟitum ampalattē nitampuriyum āṉanta naṭaṅkaṇ ṭuyalaṟiyēṉ eṉiṉumatu kaṇṭukoḷum ācai orukaṭalō eḻukaṭalō uraikkavoṇā tuṭaiyēṉ mayalaṟiyā maṉattamarnta māmaṇiyē maruntē matimuṭiem perumāṉniṉ vāḻttaṉṟi maṟṟōr ceyalaṟiyēṉ eṉakkaruḷat tiruvuḷañcey tiṭuvāy tirueḻuttain tāṇaioru tuṇaiciṟitiṅ kilaṉē.
translation: I know nothing else besides your flower-like feet. Having seen the dance of bliss you perform daily in the Ampalam, I know no sleep. Yet, the desire I have to witness it is not one ocean or seven oceans; it is an immensity I cannot express. O great gem who has settled in a mind that knows no delusion! O medicine! My great Lord with the moon on your crown, I know no action other than praising you. Please resolve in your sacred will to show me grace. I swear on the sacred five letters, I have not even a little support here.
commentary: This verse expresses a consuming, single-minded devotion, where the speaker's entire world shrinks to the worship of God's feet. His longing to see God’s dance in the Ampalam (the sacred expanse of consciousness) is an infinite ocean of desire. Feeling utterly alone and without support, he swears on the sacred five-letter mantra of Siva that he is completely dependent on God's grace.

translit: koḻuntēṉum ceḻumpākum kulavupacum pālum kūṭṭiuṇṭāṟ pōliṉikkuṅ kuṇaṅkoḷcaṭaik kaṉiyē toḻuntēva maṭantaiyarkku maṅkalanāṇ kaḻuttil tōṉṟaviṭam kaḻuttiṉuḷē tōṉṟaniṉṟa cuṭarē eḻuntēṟum aṉparuḷat tēṟṟutiru viḷakkē eṉuyirkkut tuṇaiyēeṉ irukaṇṇuḷ maṇiyē aḻuntēṟa aṟiyāteṉ avalaneñcam antō apayamuṉak kapayameṉai āṇṭaruḷka viraintē.
translation: O ripe fruit on the matted locks, as sweet as eating fresh honey, rich syrup, and fine fresh milk all mixed together! O radiance, who contained the poison within your own throat, ensuring the sacred marriage necklaces remained on the necks of the worshipping celestial women! O sacred lamp lit in the hearts of devotees who rise up to you! O companion to my very life! O pupil of my two eyes! Alas, my wretched heart does not know how to lift itself from despair. Refuge! I seek refuge in you! Swiftly take me as your own and grant me grace.
commentary: Vallalar calls to God using a series of deeply intimate and loving names, from a sweet fruit to the pupil of his own eye. These tender images contrast God’s cosmic power, like saving the world from poison, with His personal closeness as a companion to one's own soul. The verse ends with a desperate cry for refuge, asking this intimate God to swiftly rescue him from his heart's despair.

translit: eṉṉālōr turumpumacait teṭukkamuṭi yātē ellāñcey vallavaṉeṉ ṟellārum pukalum niṉṉāliv vulakiṭaināṉ vāḻkiṉṟēṉ aracē niṉaruḷpeṟ ṟaḻiyāta nilaiyaiaṭain tiṭaeṉ taṉṉālōr cutantaramum illaikaṇṭāy niṉatu cakalacutan tarattaieṉpāl tayavuceyal vēṇṭum piṉnāḷeṉ ṟiṭilciṟitum tarittirukka māṭṭēṉ pērāṇai uraittēṉeṉ pērācai ituvē.
translation: I cannot move even a single blade of grass by my own power. O King, I live in this world only by you, whom everyone praises as the All-Powerful One who does everything. Know this: to attain the imperishable state by receiving your grace, I have no independence whatsoever of my own. You must kindly grant your total independence to me. If you say, 'another day,' I cannot bear it for even a moment. I have stated this with a great oath; this is my immense desire.
commentary: Acknowledging his own complete powerlessness, Vallalar states that he lives only through God, the one who does everything. He then makes a bold and urgent demand: since he has no independence (sutāntaram) to attain the final state, God must grant His own total independence to him. It is an immense, non-negotiable desire that cannot wait another day.

translit: iccaielām pukaṉṟēṉeṉ ilaccaielām viṭuttēṉ iṉicciṟitum tariyēṉiṅ kitutaruṇat taṭaintē accaielām veḷippaṭutti accamelām akaṟṟi aruṭcōtit taṉiaracē āṅkāṅkum ōṅka viccaielām eṉakkaḷittē aviccaielām tavirttu meyyuṟaeṉ ṉoṭukalantu viḷaṅkiṭutal vēṇṭum paccaielām cemmaielām poṉmaielām paṭarnta paṭikamaṇi viḷakkēam palamviḷaṅkum patiyē.
translation: I have declared all my desires; I have cast off all my shame. I can wait here no longer. This is the opportune moment. Arriving now, you must reveal all core truths, remove all fear, grant me all true knowledgeand eliminate all ignorance. O supreme King of the Grace-Light, for you to flourish everywhere, you must truly merge with me and shine forth. O crystal-gem lamp radiating all shades of green, red, and gold! O Master who illumines the Ampalam!
commentary: Having cast off all shame, Vallalar makes a series of powerful, direct demands. He insists that this is the perfect moment for God to act, removing his fear and replacing his ignorance (aviccai) with true knowledge (viccai). The ultimate goal is for God to merge with him completely so that the Grace-Light, ArutJothi, can shine through him, illuminating the inner space of consciousness (Ampalam). This is the voice of a devotee who has reached such an intimate relationship with God that they can ask for everything.

translit: taruvakaiit taruṇamnalla taruṇamitil eṉakkē taṉittaaruṭ peruñcōti tantaruḷka itutāṉ oruvakaiī tilaieṉilvē ṟoruvakaieṉ ṉuṭaiya uṭaluyirai oḻittiṭuka uvappiṉoṭē inta iruvakaiyum cammatamē tiruvaṭicāṭ ciyatāy iyampiṉaṉeṉ itayamuṉṟaṉ itayamaṟin tatuvē aruvakaiyō uruvakaiyum ākieṉṉuḷ amarntāy ammēeṉ appāeṉ ayyāeṉ aracē.
translation: This is the time to give; it is a good and opportune time. At this moment, please grant me the unique Great Grace-Light. This is one option. If this is not to be, then the other option is this: joyfully put an end to my body and life. I consent to both these options. I declare this with your sacred feet as my witness. Your heart already knows my heart. You who are both form and formless have settled within me. O my Mother, my Father, my Master, my King!
commentary: Here, Vallalar presents God with a stark choice. The time for waiting is over: either grant him the ultimate realization of the Great Grace-Light, ArutPerunJothi, or grant him death. He declares that he joyfully accepts either outcome, as living an ordinary life is no longer an option. This is the ultimate expression of spiritual yearning, where life has no meaning apart from union with the divine.

translit: varumuṉ vantatāk koḷḷutal eṉakku vaḻakkam vaḷḷalnī makiḻntaruṭ cōti tarumuṉ tantaṉai eṉṟiruk kiṉṟēṉ tantai nītaral cattiyam eṉṟē kurumuṉ poyyurai kūṟalēṉ iṉiik kuvalai yattiṭaik kavalaiyait tariyēṉ tirumuṉ viṇṇappam ceytaṉaṉ karuṇai ceyka vāḻkaniṉ tiruvaruṭ pukaḻē.
translation: It is my custom to consider things received even before they arrive. Generous one, even before you joyfully bestow your grace-Jothi, I am certain you have already given it, for I know it is true that you, the father, will grant it. I do not speak falsehoods before the Guru. Hereafter, I will not bear any anxiety in this world. I have submitted this petition before your sacred presence. Show your compassion. Long live the fame of your sacred grace.
commentary: This verse is a powerful declaration of faith. Having made his plea, Vallalar now decides to live in the absolute certainty that his request is already granted. It is his "custom," he says, to consider a thing received even before it arrives. By resting in the trust that God, the Father, will surely give the Grace-Jothi, he frees himself from all worldly anxiety. His petition has been made, and now he lives in the peaceful assurance of its fulfillment.

translit: viṉaittaṭaitīrt teṉaiāṇṭa meyyaṉmaṇip potuvil meyññāṉa naṭampurintu viḷaṅkukiṉṟa vimalaṉ eṉaittaṉivait taruḷoḷiīn teṉṉuḷiruk kiṉṟāṉ ellāñcey vallacittaṉ iccaiyaruṭ cōti tiṉaittaṉaipeṟ ṟavarēṉum cālumuṉṉē ulakil cettavarkaḷ ellārum tirumpavaru keṉṟu niṉaittavuṭaṉ etirvantu niṟparkaṇṭāy eṉatu neñcēnī añcēluḷ añcēlañ cēlē.
translation: The true one who cleared the hindrances of my karma and made me his own, the immaculate one who shines, performing the dance of true wisdom in the bejeweled common space, has set me apart, given me the light of grace, and dwells within me. He is the all-powerful Siddhan, the Grace-Jothi of my desire. Even those who have received but a millet seed's measure of that Grace-Jothi are enough: the moment they think, 'Let all who died in the world before now return', the dead will come and stand before them, you will see. O my heart, do not fear; deep inside, do not fear; do not fear at all.
commentary: The God who cleared Vallalar's karma (vinai) and performs the dance of true wisdom (mey-jnana) now dwells within him as the all-powerful Siddhan, the Grace-Jothi. So great is this grace that even one who has received only a millet seed's measure of it can raise the dead by a single thought. With such power dwelling within, Vallalar tells his heart that there is nothing left to fear.

tamil: அணியே எனதுமெய் யறிவே பொதுவளர் அரசே திருவளர் அமுதே
இனிதருள் வாய்இது தருணம் அமுதரு ளாய்இது தருணம்
மணியே எனதுகண் மணியே பொதுவளர் மதியே திருவருண் மதியே
அருள்புரி வாய்இது தருணம் அருள்புரி வாய்இது தருணம்.
translit: aṇiyē eṉatumey yaṟivē potuvaḷar aracē tiruvaḷar amutē iṉitaruḷ vāyitu taruṇam amutaru ḷāyitu taruṇam maṇiyē eṉatukaṇ maṇiyē potuvaḷar matiyē tiruvaruṇ matiyē aruḷpuri vāyitu taruṇam aruḷpuri vāyitu taruṇam.
translation: My jewel! My true awareness! O King who flourishes in the common space! O sacred, growing nectar! Sweetly grant your grace, this is the moment; grant your nectar, this is the moment. My gem! The very gem of my eye! O moon who grows in the common space! O moon of sacred grace! Bestow your grace, this is the moment.
commentary: This is a song of intense and urgent longing for union with God. Using intimate names like "my jewel" and "gem of my eye," Vallalar pleads for grace, feeling that the perfect moment has finally arrived. The repetition of "this is the moment" conveys a powerful sense that the final merging with the divine is imminent.

translit: ituvē taruṇam eṉaiaṇaitaṟ kiṅkē potuvē naṭikkum puṉitā - vituvēynta ceṉṉiyaṉē cutta civaṉē uṉakkaṭiyēṉ aṉṉiyaṉē allēṉ aṟintu.
translation: This is the very moment to embrace me here, O pure one who dances in the common space! O one whose head is adorned with the moon! O pure Sivan! Know that I, your slave, am not a stranger to you.
commentary: To be ready for God, one must realize they are not a stranger to the divine. Vallalar insists that this is the moment for God to embrace him because he is already family, an inseparable part of the divine being. He is a child returning home.

translit: āti yētiru ampalat tāṭalcey aracē nīti yēelām vallavā nallavā niṉaintē ōti yēuṇar taṟkari tākiya oruvāṉ cōti yēeṉaic cōtiyēl cōtiyēl iṉiyē.
translation: O Primal one! O King who dances in the sacred hall! O Justice! All-powerful one! Good one! O singular celestial Jothi, so difficult to realize even through meditation and recitation! From now on, do not test me, do not test me.
commentary: After long spiritual effort, the soul can ask for the trials to end. Vallalar praises God as the primal dancer in the sacred hall (ampalam) and the supreme celestial Jothi-light, but then pleads with him to stop the tests. It is a deeply human and relatable appeal from one who feels he has endured enough and is now ready for final, unconditional grace.

translit: pōtō viṭinta taruḷaracēeṉ poruṭṭuvanteṉ tātōr eḻumaiyum naṉmaiyuṟ ṟōṅkat taruvatutāṉ mātōṭa nīkkum kaṉiraca mōvanta vāṉkaṉiyiṉ kōtō aṟintilaṉ yātō tiruvuḷam kūṟukavē.
translation: O King of Grace! Has the morning dawned? You have come for my sake. What you give so that my seven generations of forebears may flourish in goodness: is it the juice of the fruit that removes great flaws, or only the rind of that heavenly fruit? I do not know. What is your divine will? Please tell me.
commentary: At the threshold of grace, Vallalar asks in humility what exactly he is being given: the full sweetness of the fruit, which removes every flaw, or only its outer rind. He knows God has come for his sake and that the gift will bless his whole line, but he waits to be told the measure of grace.

translit: appaṉai ippaṉai ākkic civikai amarntavaṉcol appaṉai eṉṉuyirk kāṉacen tēṉai amutaiannāḷ appaṉai āḻi kaṭattik karaiviṭ ṭaḷittacaṭai appaṉaic ciṟṟam palavaṉai nāṉtutit tāṭuvaṉē.
translation: I will praise and dance for the Father with matted locks, the One of Chitrambalam. He is the Father sung by the one who rode the palanquin, who turned the barren palmyra into a fruitful one. He is the pure honey for my soul, the nectar. He is the Father who, on that day, carried Appar across the sea and brought him to shore.
commentary: Vallalar connects his own devotion to the Tamil Saivite saints: Sambandar, who rode the pearl palanquin and by his song made the barren palmyras bear fruit, and Appar, whom God brought safely across the sea. That same Father is the pure honey of his soul, and by worshipping the One in Chitrambalam he places his own experience within this line of grace.

tamil: மாதோர் புடைவைத்த மாமருந் தேமணி யேஎன் மட்டில்
translit: mātōr puṭaivaitta māmarun tēmaṇi yēeṉ maṭṭil yātō tiruvuḷam yāṉaṟi yēṉitaṟ keṉṉaceyvēṉ pōtō kaḻikiṉṟa tantōniṉ taṉṉaip poruntukiṉṟa cūtōr aṇuvum teriyēṉniṉ pātat tuṇaituṇaiyē.
translation: O great medicine who keeps a woman at your side! O Gem! What is your divine will regarding me? I do not know. What can I do about this? Alas, time is passing. I do not know even an atom of the stratagem for attaining you. Your feet are my refuge, my only refuge.
commentary: The feeling of urgency returns, with Vallalar confessing his complete helplessness as time slips away. He admits he knows no "stratagem" or clever technique to win God’s favor. The path is not about human strategy. It is about total surrender, recognizing that one's only true refuge is at God's feet.

translit: ārntaaruṭ peruñcōti appānāṉ aṭuttavartam cōrntamukam pārkka:iṉit tuṇiyēṉ niṉaruḷāṇai nērntavarkaḷ nērntapaṭi nekiḻnturaikkum vārttaikaḷum ōrntucevi pukattuṇiyēṉ uṉāṇai uṉāṇai.
translation: O Father, ArutPerunJothi! From now on I cannot bear to look upon the drooping faces of those who come to me; this I swear by your grace. Nor can I bear to let into my ears the words that the afflicted speak, breaking down, about what has befallen them. I swear on you, I swear on you.
commentary: Here Jeevakarunyam speaks in its rawest form. Vallalar swears before ArutPerunJothi that he can no longer bear to see the drooping faces of those who come to him in need, nor to hear them tell, with breaking voices, what has befallen them. The suffering of others has become unbearable to him. His oath is a plea that God remove their suffering at its root.

translit: aḻiyā nilaiyātatu mēviniṉ aṉpiṉōṭum oḻiyā tuṉaippāṭi niṉṟāṭi ulakiṉūṭē vaḻiyām uyirkkiṉpam purintu vayaṅkalvēṇṭum iḻiyā taruḷvāy potumēviya entainīyē.
translation: Attaining the imperishable state, I must, with your love, unceasingly sing of you, stand and dance in the midst of the world, giving joy to souls on the path, and so flourish. O my Father who resides in the Potu, grant this without fail.
commentary: Here, Vallalar defines the ultimate purpose of his spiritual quest. Attaining the "imperishable state" is not for personal escape or private salvation. The goal is to be able to stand in the world and actively bring joy to other souls. He asks this of the God who resides in the Potu, a term for the universal, common space, emphasizing that his mission is for the benefit of all.

translit: karumpacaikkum moḻicciṟiyār kalmaṉattil payiṉṟupayiṉ ṟirumpacaikkum maṉampeṟṟēṉ yāṉōiv vēḻaikaḷtam arumpacikku maruntaḷippēṉ antōiṅ keṉṉālē turumpacaikka muṭiyātē cōtinaṭap perumāṉē.
translation: By associating again and again with the stone hearts of petty people whose speech outdoes sugarcane in sweetness, I have acquired a heart harder than iron. Am I the one who can provide the medicine for the severe hunger of these poor people? Alas, I am unable to move even a blade of grass. O Great Lord of the Jothi dance!
commentary: In a moment of deep self-reproach, Vallalar feels his heart has become hard as iron through worldly attachments. He laments his spiritual weakness, feeling completely powerless to help the poor and hungry people around him. Addressing the Lord of the divine Jothi (light), he declares himself utterly useless, unable to perform even the smallest act of service.

tamil: மதிக்களவா மணிமன்றில் திருநடஞ்செய் திருத்தாளை வழுத்தல் இன்று
பதிக்களவா நலந்தருவல் என்றுநினை ஏத்துதற்குப் பணிக்கின் றேன்நீ
விதிக்களவாச் சித்திகள்முன் காட்டுகஇங் கென்கின்றாய் விரைந்த நெஞ்சே
பொதிக்களவா முன்னர்இங்கே சத்தத்துக் களவென்பார் போன்றாய் அன்றே.
translit: matikkaḷavā maṇimaṉṟil tirunaṭañcey tiruttāḷai vaḻuttal iṉṟu patikkaḷavā nalantaruval eṉṟuniṉai ēttutaṟkup paṇikkiṉ ṟēṉnī vitikkaḷavāc cittikaḷmuṉ kāṭṭuka:iṅ keṉkiṉṟāy virainta neñcē potikkaḷavā muṉṉariṅkē cattattuk kaḷaveṉpār pōṉṟāy aṉṟē.
translation: O restless heart! I command you to praise the sacred feet that perform the divine dance in the immeasurable, bejeweled hall. But you say, “First show me here the siddhis that defy fate!” In this, you are just like those who are called ‘thieves of sound’ before the ‘theft of the bundle’, are you not?
commentary: Vallalar depicts an inner struggle, scolding his own mind for its transactional approach to faith. He tells his heart to simply worship God, but his mind bargains back, demanding siddhis (supernatural powers) as a sign before it will commit. He dismisses this as a foolish and premature demand, arguing that true devotion must come first, without conditions.

tamil: ஆடியகால் மலர்களுக்கே அன்புடையார் யாவரிங்கே அவர்க்கே இன்பம்
ஓடியதோ நெஞ்சேநீ உன்னுவதென் பற்பலவாய் உன்னேல் இன்னே
பாடிஅவன் திருப்பாட்டைப் படிகண்டாய் இன்புகலப் படிகண் டாயே.
translit: āṭiyakāl malarkaḷukkē aṉpuṭaiyār yāvariṅkē avarkkē iṉpam kūṭiyateṉ ṟāraṇamum ākamamum āṇaiyiṭṭuk kūṟumvārttai ōṭiyatō neñcēnī uṉṉuvateṉ paṟpalavāy uṉṉēl iṉṉē pāṭiavaṉ tiruppāṭṭaip paṭikaṇṭāy iṉpukalap paṭikaṇ ṭāyē.
translation: O heart, has the word sworn by both the Vedas and the Agamas, that bliss comes only to those who possess love for His dancing, flower-like feet, fled your memory? Why do you think in so many different ways? Do not think! This very moment, sing His sacred song. See, you have found the way! You have found the way for bliss to merge with you.
commentary: He reminds his restless heart that even the most ancient scriptures, the Vedas and Agamas, agree on one thing: true joy belongs only to those who simply love God. He urges his mind to stop its endless, complex thinking and instead take the direct path. The solution is to begin singing God's praise this very instant, for that is the simple, immediate way to experience bliss.

translit: oṉṟumuṉ eṇpāl eṇṇiṭak kiṭaitta vuvaikkumēṟ ṟaṉaiaruḷ oḷiyāl naṉṟukaṇ ṭāṅkē aruṭperuñ cōti nātaṉaik kaṇṭavaṉ naṭikkum maṉṟukaṇ ṭataṉil cittelām valla maruntukaṇ ṭuṟṟatu vaṭivāy niṉṟukoṇ ṭāṭun taruṇamiṅ kituvē neñcamē añcalai nīyē.
translation: This, right here, is the moment to celebrate: having seen yourself clearly by the light of grace, beyond the One that can be grasped by the mind's calculations; having seen the Lord, ArutPerunJothi, right there; having seen the hall where He dances, and the medicine within it that is capable of all powers; and now standing, having become That which you have attained as your very form. O heart, do not be afraid!
commentary: This verse is a powerful declaration of spiritual arrival. After the struggle and self-doubt, he experiences a clear realization: he has seen himself, seen God as the Vast Grace-Light (ArutPerunJothi), and understood that all power resides within the divine dance. The final step is becoming one with this divine reality. Having attained this state, he assures his own heart that there is nothing left to fear.

translit: kalaivaḷar muṭiya teṉṉaiāṭ koṇṭa karuṇaiyaṅ kaṇṇatu ñāṉa nilaivaḷar poruḷa tulakelām pōṟṟa niṉṟatu niṟaiperuñ cōti malaivaḷar kiṉṟatu aruḷveḷi naṭuvē vayaṅkuva tiṉpamē mayamāyt talaivaḷar tirucciṟ ṟampalan taṉilē taṉitteṉak kiṉittatōr kaṉiyē.
translation: It has a crown where the arts flourish. It has eyes of mercy that enslaved me. It is the substance where the state of gnosis grows. It stands, praised by all the worlds. It is a mountain of full, great Jothi that grows in the midst of the space of grace. It flourishes in the sacred Thiru Chitrambalam, being made entirely of bliss. It is a fruit that is uniquely sweet, just for me.
commentary: God is described through a series of beautiful and intimate images that blend the cosmic with the personal. God is a vast mountain of Jothi (light) filling the space of grace, the source of gnosis (divine wisdom), and a king adorned with all arts. Yet this immense being is also experienced as something deeply personal: a fruit of unique sweetness, found in the sacred inner space of Thiru Chitrambalam, meant for the devotee alone.

translit: maṉṟuḷniṉ ṟāṭum vaḷḷalē eṉatu vaḷḷaleṉ ṟeṉakkuḷē terinta aṉṟutāṉ toṭaṅki ammaiyē appā aiyaṉē aṉpaṉē aracē eṉṟuniṉ taṉaiyē niṉaittiruk kiṉṟēṉ eṭṭuṇai eṉiṉumvē ṟiṭattil ceṉṟuniṉ ṟaṟiyēṉ teyvamē ituniṉ tiruvuḷam terintatu tāṉē.
translation: O magnanimous one dancing in the hall! Beginning on the very day I knew within myself that you are my Benefactor, I have been thinking only of you, calling you Mother, Father, Master, Beloved One, King. I have not gone and stood elsewhere, not even for an instant. O God, this is surely known to your sacred will.
commentary: This is a heartfelt declaration of total, steady devotion. From the moment he truly knew God as his own benefactor, his mind has been fixed on God alone, addressing the divine with every name of love: Mother, Father, Master. It shows a spiritual life centered on a constant, loving remembrance that never turns to any other source for support.

translit: uḷḷalēṉ uṭaiyār uṇṇavum vaṟiyār uṟupaci uḻantuven tuyarāl vaḷḷalē neñcam varuntavum paṭumō maṟṟitai niṉaittiṭun tōṟum eḷḷalēṉ uḷḷam erikiṉṟa tuṭampum erikiṉṟa teṉceyvēṉ antō koḷḷalēṉ uṇavum tarikkilēṉ intak kuṟaiyelām tavirttaruḷ entāy.
translation: I cannot bear it. While the wealthy eat, the poor suffer from gnawing hunger and are tormented by intense sorrow. O Benefactor, how can my heart endure such grief? Whenever I think of this, my stainless heart burns, my body also burns. What can I do? Alas! I cannot take food, I cannot sustain myself. My Father, please grant your grace and remove all this want.
commentary: The sight of others suffering from hunger is a source of intense, physical pain. This verse reveals a core part of Vallalar's path: empathy so deep that the hunger of the poor becomes a fire in his own body, making it impossible for him to eat or find peace. It is a shared suffering that he begs God to resolve.

tamil: ஐவகைத் தொழிலும் என்பால் அளித்தனை அதுகொண் டிந்நாள்
செய்வகை தெரிவித் தென்னைச் சேர்ந்தொன்றாய் இருத்தல் வேண்டும்
பொய்வகை அறியேன் வேறு புகலிலேன் பொதுவே நின்று
மெய்வகை உரைத்தேன் இந்த விண்ணப்பம் காண்க நீயே.
translit: aivakait toḻilum eṉpāl aḷittaṉai atukoṇ ṭinnāḷ ceyvakai terivit teṉṉaic cērntoṉṟāy iruttal vēṇṭum poyvakai aṟiyēṉ vēṟu pukalilēṉ potuvē niṉṟu meyvakai uraittēṉ inta viṇṇappam kāṇka nīyē.
translation: You bestowed the five cosmic functions upon me. With that power, you must now reveal the way to act, and you must join with me and be as one. I do not know any kind of falsehood; I have no other refuge. Standing in the common expanse, I have spoken the truth. You yourself must see this appeal.
commentary: Vallalar makes the astonishing claim that God has granted him the five cosmic functions: the powers of creation, preservation, destruction, illusion, and grace. Having received this supreme power, his prayer is for the wisdom to use it correctly and for the final goal of complete union with God. He makes this appeal with absolute sincerity, standing in the open expanse of truth with nothing to hide.

tamil: உருவ ராகியும் அருவின ராகியும் உருஅரு வினராயும்
ஒருவ ரேஉளார் கடவுள்கண் டறிமினோ உலகுளீர் உணர்வின்றி
இருவ ராம்என்றும் மூவரே யாம்என்றும் இயலும்ஐ வர்கள்என்றும்
எருவ ராய்உரைத் துழல்வதென் உடற்குயிர் இரண்டுமூன் றெனலாமே.
translit: uruva rākiyum aruviṉa rākiyum uruaru viṉarāyum oruva rēuḷār kaṭavuḷkaṇ ṭaṟimiṉō ulakuḷīr uṇarviṉṟi iruva rāmeṉṟum mūvarē yāmeṉṟum iyalumai varkaḷeṉṟum eruva rāyurait tuḻalvateṉ uṭaṟkuyir iraṇṭumūṉ ṟeṉalāmē.
translation: There is only one God, who exists with form, without form, and with-and-without form. See and know this! O people of the world, why do you wander about without understanding, senselessly declaring that there are two gods, or three, or even five? Can one say a body has two or three souls?
commentary: God is one. All arguments about whether the divine has a physical form, is formless, or is a combination of both are beside the point because all these aspects belong to that single reality. Vallalar dismisses debates over whether there are two, three, or five gods as senseless. To make his point clear, he asks a simple question: would anyone claim that a single human body has two or three souls?

translit: cēypōl ulakat tuyiraiel lāmeṇṇic cērntupeṟṟa tāypōl uraipparcaṉ mārkkacaṅ kattavar cāṟṟumeṭṭik kāypōl piṟartamaik kaṇṭāl kacantu kaṭukaṭuttē nāypōl kuraippartuṉ mārkkacaṅ kattavar nāṉilattē.
translation: The members of the Sanmarkka Sangam consider all the lives of the world as their own children and speak like a nurturing mother. In contrast, the members of the Tunmarkka Sangam on this earth, upon seeing others, are bitter like the proverbial strychnine fruit, grow harsh, and bark like dogs.
commentary: The true spiritual path is defined by one's attitude toward others. Followers of Sanmarkkam (the true path), see all living beings as their own children and speak with the gentleness of a mother. In contrast, those on the evil path are filled with bitterness, reacting to others with the harshness of a snarling dog. Your capacity for universal kindness is the true measure of your spiritual life.

translit: vaṇṭaṇipūṅ kuḻalammai eṅkaḷciva kāma valliyoṭu maṇimaṉṟil vayaṅkiyaniṉ vaṭivam kaṇṭavaraik kaṇṭavartam kālmalarmut tēvar kaṉamuṭikkē muṭikkiṉṟa kaṭimalarām eṉṟāl paṇṭakuniṉ tiruttoṇṭar aṭipperumai evarē pakarntiṭuvar maṟaikaḷelām pakarntiṭuvāṉ pukuntē viṇṭularntu veḷuttaavai veḷuttamaṭṭō avaṟṟai viyantōtum vētiyarum veḷuttaṉaruḷ uṭampē.
translation: With our Mother Sivakama Valli, whose flower-adorned hair is circled by bees, Your form shines in the jeweled hall. If the feet of those who have merely seen those who saw You are fragrant flowers placed upon the heavy crowns of the three great gods, then who could ever describe the greatness of the feet of Your ancient devotees? All the Vedas tried to describe it, but they split, withered, and grew pale. Not only they; the Vedic scholars who extol those scriptures also grew pale in their innermost being.
commentary: The spiritual greatness of God's true devotees is beyond all description. Vallalar creates a powerful chain of reverence: if the feet of people who have merely seen someone who saw a devotee are worshipped by the highest gods, then how can one even begin to measure the glory of the original devotees themselves? He says that even the sacred Vedas tried and failed to capture this greatness, and the scholars who study them were left pale and humbled by the task. The direct experience of devotion is a reality that surpasses any scripture.

translit: kiḻakkuveḷut tatukaruṇai aruṭcōti utayam kiṭaittateṉa tuḷakkamalam kiḷarntateṉa takattē caḻakkuveḷut tatucāti ācciramā cāram camayamatā cārameṉac caṇṭaiyiṭṭa kalaka vaḻakkuveḷut tatupalavām poynnūlkaṟ ṟavartam maṉamveḷuttu vāyveḷuttu vāyuṟavā titta muḻukkuveḷut tatucivamē poruḷeṉumcaṉ mārkka muḻuneṟiyil paranāta muracumuḻaṅ kiyatē.
translation: The east grew white. My heart-lotus blossomed, knowing the compassionate Grace-Light had dawned. In my heart, deceit grew pale. The riotous conflict of fighting over caste, life-stage, conduct, religion, and creed faded away. The whole contention grew pale. The minds and mouths of those who studied the many false scriptures grew pale; the very foundation of their vehement arguments was exposed as empty. The drum of the supreme sound resounded, announcing the complete path of Sanmarkkam, which proclaims that Sivam alone is the true substance.
commentary: The dawning of divine grace within the soul makes all worldly conflicts and false knowledge fade into irrelevance. Vallalar uses the image of a sunrise to describe this inner awakening to the Grace-Light, Aruṭcōti. In this new light, all the divisions that cause human conflict, such as caste, religion, and social status, are seen as meaningless. The true path, Sanmarkkam, reveals that the ultimate reality, Sivam, transcends all these arguments.

translit: ciṟcapaik kaṇṇum poṟcapaik kaṇṇum tirunaṭam puriyum tirunaṭa rāja eṉakkaruḷ purinta niṉakkaṭi yēṉkaim māṟṟai aṟintilaṉ pōṟṟiniṉ aruḷē.
translation: O King of the Sacred Dance, you who perform your holy dance in both the Hall of Consciousness and the Golden Hall! You have bestowed grace upon me. I, your slave, do not know how to repay you. All praise to your grace.
commentary: In the face of boundless divine grace, the only fitting human response is gratitude. Vallalar addresses God as the cosmic dancer in both the Hall of Consciousness (Ciṟsapai) and the Golden Hall of the elements (Poṟsapai). He feels he can offer nothing in return for the grace he has received except pure praise.

translit: nāyiṉum ciṟiyēṉ āyiṉum periyēṉ yātiṟ periyēṉ tītiṟ periyēṉ eṉṉaiāṇ ṭaruḷiṉai eṉṉaiāṇ ṭavaṉē ampalat tāṭalcey emperum poruḷē.
translation: I am more lowly than a dog, yet I am also great. In what way am I great? I am great in wrongdoing. Even so, you took me as your own and ruled me with grace, O my Master! O my great Substance who dances in the sacred Hall!
commentary: Grace is given freely. Vallalar expresses a paradox: he is lower than a dog, and his only "greatness" is in his capacity for wrongdoing. Yet, despite his unworthiness, God chose to claim him and bestow grace, demonstrating that divine compassion is unconditional.

translit: uṇmaiurait taruḷeṉ ṟōtiṉēṉ entaipirāṉ vaṇmaiyuṭaṉ eṉaṟivil vāynturaittāṉ - tiṇmaiyuṟu cittinilai ellām terivit taruḷkiṉṟēm ittaruṇam cattiyamē eṉṟu.
translation: “Graciously speak the truth,” I implored my Father, the Lord. With great generosity, he entered my intelligence and declared: “We are now, at this very moment, graciously revealing all the states of firm Siddhi. This is the absolute truth.”
commentary: The highest spiritual truth can be revealed directly, here and now. When Vallalar asked for the truth, God responded by promising to reveal all the states of Siddhi, or spiritual perfection, at that very moment. This is a firm declaration that complete realization is possible now, in this life.

translit: ulakamelām pōṟṟa oḷivaṭiva ṉāki ilakaaruḷ ceytāṉ icaintē - tilakaṉeṉa nāṉēcaṉ mārkkam naṭattukiṉṟēṉ namperumāṉ tāṉē eṉakkut taṉittu.
translation: He became a form of light praised by the entire world and willingly bestowed grace for it to shine. I, as the foremost leader, conduct the Sanmarkkam. Our great Lord Himself is with me, alone.
commentary: Vallalar now understands his life's mission as divinely ordained. God, experienced as a form of light, has empowered him to establish the Sanmarkkam (the True Path of universal love and harmony). He is not acting alone or out of his own authority; God Himself is his sole and constant companion in this work for the world.

translit: taṉittuṇaiyāy eṉṟaṉṉait tāṅkikkoṇ ṭeṉṟaṉ maṉitta uṭampaḻiyā vāṟē - kaṉittuṇaiyām iṉṉamutam tanteṉakkē ellāmum vallacitti taṉṉaiyuntan tuṭkalantāṉ ṟāṉ.
translation: Becoming my sole support, He sustained me. He gave me sweet, ripened ambrosia so my human body would not perish. He also gave me the siddhi that can do everything, and then He Himself mingled within me.
commentary: God's grace is described as having tangible, life-altering effects. It sustains the soul and makes the physical body immortal through a divine "ambrosia." Beyond this, God grants siddhi (the power to accomplish anything) and, in the final act of intimacy, merges completely with the devotee's own being.

translit: carkkaraiot tāṉeṉakkē tantāṉ aruḷeṉmaṉak kaṟkaraiyac ceytē kaḷippittāṉ - kaṟka iṉiyāṉ aruṭcōti entaieṉṉuḷ uṟṟāṉ iṉiyāṉ mayaṅkēṉ iruntu.
translation: He is like sugar. He gave me grace, made the stone of my mind melt, and made me rejoice. The Grace-Light, my Father, who is sweet to learn of, has entered within me. From now on, I will not be deluded.
commentary: The experience of God's presence is deeply felt, as sweet as sugar. This divine sweetness melts the "stone of the mind," dissolving stubbornness, ignorance, and sorrow into pure joy. With the Grace-Light now dwelling inside him, the speaker feels a newfound certainty, free from the delusions that once clouded his mind.

translit: uṉṉaiviṭa māṭṭēṉnāṉ uṉāṇai emperumāṉ eṉṉaiviṭa māṭṭāy iruvarumāy - maṉṉieṉṟum vaṇmai elāmvalla vāymaiaru ḷālulakuk kuṇmaiiṉpam ceytum uvantu.
translation: I will not leave you, I swear on you, my great Lord! You will not leave me. The two of us, united forever, will joyfully bring true bliss to the world, through the grace of truth that is capable of all generosity.
commentary: This is a declaration of an unbreakable, mutual bond between the soul and God. The relationship is no longer one of supplicant and deity, but of inseparable partners. Having achieved this union, their shared purpose becomes clear: to work together joyfully to bring true bliss to all humanity, empowered by a grace that is both truthful and infinitely generous.

translit: nañcuṇ ṭuyirkaḷaik kāttava ṉēnaṭa nāyakaṉē pañcuṇṭa ciṟṟaṭip pāvaipaṅ kānam parāparaṉē mañcuṇṭa ceñcaṭai maṉṉāpoṉ ampala vāvalavā piñcuṇṭa vāykkup paḻamaḷit tāṇṭa periyavaṉē.
translation: O One who drank poison to save all lives! O Lord of the Dance! O One who shares Your half with the Goddess whose small feet are softer than cotton! O our Supreme One! O King with red matted locks holding the clouds! O Lord of the Golden Hall, O Masterful One! O Great One who fed a ripe fruit to an immature mouth and took me as Your own!
commentary: The great God of cosmic myths, who dances creation and saves the world, is also the one who personally cares for the individual soul. Vallalar connects these grand, impersonal images of Siva with the tender, intimate act of being fed like a child, showing that the ultimate power is also the ultimate parent.

translit: appūṟu ceñcaṭai appāciṟ ṟampalat tāṭukiṉṟōy tuppūṟu vaṇṇac ceḻuñcuṭa rētaṉic cōtiyaṉē veppūṟu nīkkiya veṇṟu pūttapoṉ mēṉiyaṉē uppūṟu vāykkuttit tippūṟu kāṭṭiya uttamaṉē.
translation: O Father with red matted hair holding water, you who dance in the Sitrambalam! O rich flame the color of coral, O singular Jothi! O golden-bodied one, adorned with white ash that removes the heat of affliction! O supreme one, who poked my salt-sore mouth and revealed an outpouring of sweetness.
commentary: God is the singular flame, or Jothi, whose dance happens within our own consciousness, the Sitrambalam (hall of consciousness). Vallalar uses the striking image of a mouth sore from salt to describe the pain of worldly life. Grace is the experience of that very pain being transformed into an outpouring of sweetness.

translit: nāṉceyta puṇṇiyam eṉṉuraik kēṉpotu naṇṇiyatōr vāṉceyta māmaṇi eṉkaiyil peṟṟunal vāḻvaṭaintēṉ ūṉceyta tēkam oḷivaṭi vākaniṉ ṟōṅkukiṉṟēṉ kōṉceyta viccai kuṇikkaval lārevar kūṟumiṉē.
translation: What can I say of the merit I have earned? I received in my hand the great sky-gem that reached the Common Space and have attained the good life. My fleshly body now stands exalted, having become a form of light. Tell me, who can ever measure the miraculous art performed by the King?
commentary: The culmination of spiritual life is the transformation of the physical body into an immortal body of light. Vallalar declares that this has happened to him as a miraculous act of God, beyond any merit of his own. This physical transmutation is a divine art beyond human understanding.

translit: paṇṇiya pūcai niṟaintatu ciṟṟam palanaṭaṅkaṇ ṭeṇṇiya eṇṇam palittaṉa meyiṉpam eytiyatōr taṇṇiyal āramu tuṇṭaṉaṉ kaṇṭaṉaṉ cāmiyaināṉ naṇṇiya puṇṇiyam eṉṉuraik kēṉinta nāṉilattē.
translation: The worship I performed is now fulfilled. Having seen the dance in the Sitrambalam, my every thought has borne fruit. I have partaken of the cool, rare nectar of true bliss; I have seen the Master. In all this world, what can I say of the merit that I have attained?
commentary: All spiritual effort and worship find their completion in the direct vision of God's dance in the Sitrambalam. With this experience, every longing is fulfilled, and the seeker tastes the nectar of true bliss. The path of seeking is over; the life of realized union has begun.

translit: aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ ammaiyi ṉōṭaṟi vāṉantamām aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ appaṉeṉ uḷḷat tamarntaṉpiṉāl aruṭperuñ cōtitteḷ ḷāramu tamtan taḻivaṟṟatōr aruṭperuñ cōticceṅ kōlum koṭuttaṉaṉ aṟputamē.
translation: My Father, ArutPerunJothi, who is the bliss of consciousness, along with my Mother, ArutPerunJothi, settled lovingly in my heart. He gave me the clear, rare nectar of ArutPerunJothi and the deathless scepter of ArutPerunJothi. A miracle!
commentary: God, as ArutPerunJothi (the Vast Grace-Light), is experienced as both Father and Mother dwelling within the heart. This union brings tangible gifts: the nectar of immortality and a "scepter," which symbolizes spiritual authority and a divinely governed life. God is close, living within.

translit: aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ akattil ōṅkiṉa maruṭperum tiraielām maṭintu nīṅkiṉa iruṭperu malamutal yāvum tīrntaṉa teruṭperum cittikaḷ cērnta eṉṉaiyē.
translation: ArutPerunJothi surged within my being. All the great veils of delusion folded up and disappeared. The great darkness of the primal malams and all such things are resolved. The great siddhis of clarity have joined with me.
commentary: The rising of ArutPerunJothi (the Vast Grace-Light) within is a purifying force that dissolves all internal obstacles. Vallalar describes this as removing the veils of delusion and the darkness of malam (the soul's inherent impurities). Once these are gone, clarity prevails, and siddhis (perfected spiritual abilities) naturally arise.

translit: ōvuṟāt tuyarceyum uṭamputāṉ eṉṟum cāvuṟā tiṉpamē cārntu vāḻalām māvuṟāc cuttacaṉ mārkka naṉṉeṟi mēvuṟār taṅkaḷai viṭuka neñcamē.
translation: This body, which causes ceaseless suffering, can live forever, abiding only in bliss. O my heart, abandon those who do not embrace the good path of the Pure Sanmarkkam, which is free of all delusion.
commentary: The body is usually seen as a temporary vessel doomed to suffering and decay. Vallalar presents a different possibility: through the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure Path), this same body can become immortal and a source of unending bliss. He therefore urges his own heart to turn away from anyone who rejects this path to physical and spiritual perfection.

translit: pottiya malappiṇip puḻukku rampaitāṉ cittiyal cuttacaṉ mārkkac cērppiṉāl nittiya mākiyē nikaḻum eṉpatu cattiyam cattiyam cakattu ḷīrkaḷē.
translation: This hovel of worms, shrouded in the disease of malam, will become eternal by joining the Pure Sanmarkkam, which embodies siddhi. This is the truth, the truth, O people of the world!
commentary: Vallalar uses stark language, calling the body a "hovel of worms," to contrast its ordinary state with its ultimate potential. He insists with great certainty that this very body, burdened by its inherent impurity (malam), can be made eternal. The key is the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure Path), which leads to siddhi (spiritual perfection) for the body itself, more than for the soul.

translit: vāṉāki vāṉaṭuvē maṉṉumoḷi yākiatil tāṉāṭu vāṉākic caṉmārkkar uḷḷiṉikkum tēṉākit teḷḷamutāyt tittikkum tēvēnī yāṉāki eṉṉuḷ irukkiṉṟāy eṉṉēyō.
translation: Becoming the sky, becoming the light abiding in the midst of the sky, becoming the one who dances within it, you are the Divine One who is sweet as honey in the hearts of Sanmarkkam followers and as clear nectar. You have become me and exist within me. What a wonder this is!
commentary: The divine is experienced as both the vast cosmos and an intimate presence within one's own heart. For followers of the Sanmarkkam, this immense power is sweet and personal, a reality that eventually dissolves the separation between God and self.

translit: ñāṉā karaccuṭarē ñāṉa maṇiviḷakkē āṉā aruṭperuñciṟ ṟampalattē āṉantat tēṉār amutām civamē civamēnī nāṉāki eṉṉuḷ naṭikkiṉṟāy eṉṉēyō.
translation: O brilliant flame from the source of wisdom! O jeweled lamp of wisdom! O Sivam, O Sivam, you who are the nectar of blissful honey in the unending, great, vast hall of grace! You have become me and are dancing within me. What a wonder this is!
commentary: This verse deepens the theme of divine intimacy. God, addressed here as Sivam (the Auspicious One), is the source of all wisdom and bliss. Yet this ultimate reality is not distant; it becomes the devotee's own self, dancing within them in a union of overwhelming sweetness.

translit: eṉtarattuk kēlāta eṇṇaṅkaḷ eṇṇukiṉṟēṉ muṉtarattiṉ ellām muṭittuk koṭukkiṉṟāy niṉtarattai eṉpukalvēṉ niṉiṭappālmēvupacum poṉtarattai eṉuraikkēṉ poṟpotuvil naṭikkiṉṟōy.
translation: I think thoughts unsuited to my station, yet you step forward and accomplish them all for me. What can I say of your stature? What can I say of the stature of the one of fresh gold who graces your left side, O you who dance in the golden hall.
commentary: The speaker is overcome with awe at God's unconditional generosity. He feels his own aspirations are unworthy, yet God steps in to make them a reality without being asked. This boundless grace, which includes the presence of the Goddess (the golden one at God's left), leaves the devotee speechless.

translit: eṉṉuṭaiya viṇṇappam itukēṭka emperumāṉ niṉṉuṭaiya peruṅkaruṇai nitiuṭaiyēṉ ātaliṉāl poṉṉuṭaiyāṉ ayaṉmutalām puṅkavarai viyavēṉeṉ taṉṉuṭaiya ceyalellām tampirāṉ ceyalaṉṟē.
translation: My Lord, hear this, my plea. Since I possess the treasure of Your great compassion, I am not impressed by Brahma and the other eminent gods. Are not all of my own actions the Master's actions?
commentary: Having the treasure of God's grace makes all other forms of power and status seem meaningless. In this state of surrender, one realizes that personal actions are no longer driven by individual will but are simply the expression of the divine working through them.

translit: ōṅkumaṉpar ellārum uḷḷē viḻittuniṟkat tūṅkiya eṉtaṉṉai eḻuppiaruḷ tūyaporuḷ vāṅkukaeṉ ṟeṉpāl valiyak koṭuttamutum pāṅkuṟaniṉ ṟūṭṭiṉaiyē entāyniṉ paṇpituvē.
translation: While all the exalted devotees stood awake within, You, the pure Being of Grace, awakened me who was sleeping. You forcefully gave me ambrosia, saying "Take it," and You stood and fed me perfectly. O my Mother, such is Your nature.
commentary: Grace can arrive in a moment of unexpected awakening. While other devotees are progressing on their path, God personally rouses Vallalar from a state of spiritual slumber, feeding him the ambrosia of grace directly, like a mother tending to her child.

translit: nāṭpāril aṉparelām nalkukaeṉ ṟēttiniṟpa āṭpāril aṉpōr aṇuttuṇaiyum illēṟkē nīṭpāy aruḷamutam nīkoṭuttāy niṉṉai iṅkē kēṭpār ilaieṉṟu kīḻmēla tākkiṉaiyē.
translation: While devotees all over the world stand praising You, begging, "Grant us grace," You gave the ambrosia of grace abundantly to me, who lacks even an atom of devotion among Your servants. You have turned everything upside down, as if there is no one here to question You.
commentary: The logic of divine grace is often paradoxical. God seems to bypass the obviously devout to shower grace upon the one who feels least deserving. Vallalar expresses his astonishment at this divine act which turns human expectations of merit and reward completely upside down.

translit: ellārkkum kaṭaiyāki iruntēṉuk karuḷpurintē ellārkkum tuṇaiyāki irukkavaittāy emperumāṉ ellārkkum potuvilnaṭam iṭukiṉṟāy ivvaṇṇam ellārkkum ceyyāmai yātukuṟit ticaieṉakkē.
translation: You showed grace to me, who was the very last of all, and made me a support for everyone, my Lord. You dance in the common space for all. Why, then, have You not done this for everyone? Tell me the reason.
commentary: The experience of personal grace leads to a deep yearning for the well being of all. Having been lifted up by God, Vallalar now turns and asks the most important question: Why has this transformative experience not been given to everyone? This plea reveals that his own salvation is incomplete without the salvation of all other souls.

translit: nāṉāṉāṉ tāṉāṉāṉ nāṉumtā ṉumāṉāṉ tēṉāṉāṉ teḷḷamutāyt tittittu niṟkiṉṟāṉ vāṉāṉāṉ ñāṉa maṇimaṉṟil āṭukiṉṟāṉ kōṉāṉāṉ eṉṉuṭ kulāvukiṉṟa kōmāṉē.
translation: He became me. He became Himself. He became both me and Him. He became honey; He stands as clear ambrosia, making everything sweet. He became the sky; He dances in the jeweled hall of wisdom. He is the King, the great Lord who moves about within me.
commentary: The highest state of spiritual union dissolves the boundaries between the self and God. Here, God becomes the individual soul, God remains God, and God also becomes the very relationship between the two. This presence is felt, as the sweetness of life, the vastness of the sky, and the king who dances within one's own heart.

translit: ellāk kuṟaiyum tavirntēṉuṉ iṉṉaruḷ eytiṉaṉnāṉ vallāriṉ vallavaṉ āṉēṉ karuṇai maruntarunti nallār evarkkum upakarip pāṉiṅku naṇṇukiṉṟēṉ kollā viratattil eṉṉaik kuṟikkoṇṭa kōlattaṉē.
translation: O you of beautiful form, who marked me for the vow of not-killing! I have overcome all deficiencies; I have attained your sweet grace. Having consumed the medicine of compassion, I have become mightier than the mighty. I am now here to serve all good people.
commentary: Spiritual attainment finds its true purpose in service fueled by compassion. The strength gained from divine grace is for helping others. This power comes from a specific inner change, described here as taking the "medicine of compassion," and is guided by a core ethical principle: the vow of not-killing, which is the foundation of a life dedicated to universal kindness.

translit: muṉṉāḷcey puṇṇiyam yātō ulakam muḻutumeṉpāl innāḷ aṭaintiṉpam eytiṭa ōṅkiṉaṉ eṇṇiyavā ṟennāḷum ivvuṭam pēiṟa vāta iyaṟkaipeṟṟēṉ eṉṉācai appaṉaik kaṇṭukoṇ ṭēṉeṉ itayattilē.
translation: What merit did I perform in a former life? Today I have been elevated so that the entire world may come to me and attain bliss. As I wished, I have received the nature of this very body being deathless forever. I have seen my beloved Father in my heart.
commentary: The experience of grace is so great it feels entirely unearned. Vallalar has been elevated for the benefit of the whole world and has also attained a deathless physical body, a central goal of his path. The source of this extraordinary state is simple: he found God within his own heart.

translit: kaṇṭēṉ ciṟṟampalat tāṉanta nāṭakam kaṇṭukaḷi koṇṭēṉ ellāmvalla cittaṉaik kūṭik kulaviamu tuṇṭēṉ meyññāṉa uruaṭain tēṉpoy ulakoḻukkam viṇṭēṉ camaraca caṉmārkkam peṟṟa viyappituvē.
translation: I have seen the blissful dance in the Chitrambalam and rejoiced. I have joined with the all-powerful Siddhar, mingled with him, and consumed the ambrosia. I have attained a form of true wisdom. I have renounced the ways of the false world. Such is the wonder of having received the Samarasa Sanmarkkam.
commentary: This verse is a joyful summary of the path fulfilled. Seeing the divine dance in the Chitrambalam (the inner hall of consciousness) leads to ecstatic union with the all-powerful Divine, called a Siddhar or perfected being. This union transforms the person, granting a body of true wisdom and leading to the renunciation of worldly falsehoods in favor of the Samarasa Sanmarkkam, the universal path of truth and harmony.

translit: kaṇkoṇṭa pūtalam ellāmcaṉ mārkkam kalantukoṇṭē paṇkoṇṭa pāṭalil pāṭip paṭittup paravukiṉṟār viṇkoṇṭa ciṟcapai oṉṟē niṟaintu viḷaṅkukiṉṟa teṇkoṇṭa maṟṟai matamārkkam yāvum iṟantaṉavē.
translation: All across the visible earth, people have embraced the Sanmarkkam; they sing, recite, and praise it in melodious songs. The celestial Hall of Consciousness alone fills everything and shines forth. All the other innumerable religious paths are dead.
commentary: Vallalar sees the whole visible earth taking up the Sanmarkkam, singing and reciting it in song. The Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness) alone fills everything and shines. Of all the other religious paths have fallen. When the one Light fills all, the many paths that stood apart from it have nothing left to stand on.

translit: tāḻaip paḻampiḻi pāloṭu carkkaraic cāṟaḷinta vāḻaip paḻampacu neynaṟun tēṉum maruvacceytu māḻaip palāccuḷai māmpaḻam āti vaṭittaḷavi ēḻaik kaḷittaṉai yēaru ḷāramu teṉṟoṉṟaiyē.
translation: You have blended milk from squeezed pandanus fruit with sugar syrup, ripened bananas, pure cow's ghee, and fragrant honey; you have strained and mixed in golden jackfruit segments, mangoes, and more, and have given this to me, this poor one, as that single thing called the ambrosia of grace.
commentary: Divine grace is described here as an intensely real and delicious experience. Vallalar lists the most exquisite and sweet ingredients to convey the flavor of this "ambrosia of grace," a divine nectar personally prepared and given to him by God. The detailed recipe emphasizes how personal, loving, and overwhelmingly blissful the experience of grace is.

translit: teṉpāl mukaṅkoṇṭa tēvēcen tēṉil ciṟantapacu viṉpāl kalantaḷi mukkaṉic cāṟum eṭuttaḷavi aṉpāl makiḻntu makaṉē varukeṉ ṟaḻaittaruḷi eṉpāl aḷittaṉai yēaru ḷāramu teṉṟoṉṟaiyē.
translation: O God who faces the south! You mixed the finest cow's milk in pure honey, measured out the juice of the three fruits, and then, joyfully and with love, you called, "Come, my son," and graciously gave to me the one thing called the rare nectar of grace.
commentary: Building on the previous verse, this one emphasizes the parental love with which grace is given. The "God who faces the south" probably alludes to Dakshinamurthy or Shiva as the ultimate teacher, but here he acts as a loving father. He prepares a divine drink with the "three fruits" (mango, jackfruit, and banana, a classic Tamil offering of sweetness) and personally invites Vallalar, "Come, my son." This transforms the moment from a divine bestowal into an act of intimate, familial love.

translit: cettār eḻuntaṉar cuttacaṉ mārkkam ciṟantatunāṉ ottār uyarntavar illā oruvaṉai uṟṟaṭaintē cittāṭu kiṉṟaṉaṉ cākā varamum ciṟakkappeṟṟēṉ ittā raṇiyil eṉakkiṇai yāreṉ ṟiyampuvaṉē.
translation: The dead have risen. The Suddha Sanmarkkam has flourished. Having reached the One who has no equal or superior, I perform siddhis. I have also received the great boon of immortality. I will declare: who on this earth is my equal?
commentary: This is a triumphant announcement of a new era. The flourishing of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the True Path of Purity) has brought about a reality where even death is overcome. The statement "The dead have risen" heralds the highest achievement of this path. Now united with the Supreme One, Vallalar can perform siddhis (supernatural powers) and has the boon of immortality. His bold claim to have no equal declares that he is the first to realize this state, serving as the pioneer for a new kind of human existence.

translit: karuṇai yāmperuṅ kaṭalamu taḷittaṉai eṉakkē taruṇa vārica malarppatam tantaṉai niṉṉai aruṇa vaṇṇaoṇ cuṭarmaṇi maṇṭapat taṭiyēṉ poruḷna yappuṟak kaṇṭukaṇ ṭuḷamakiḻ pōtē.
translation: You gave me the nectar from the great ocean of compassion. You gave me your tender, lotus-flower feet. This happened at the very moment I, your slave, rejoiced in my heart, beholding You again and again as my treasured substance with great longing, in the Hall of Gems radiant with sun-colored light.
commentary: The act of seeing God with loving devotion is itself the moment grace is received. Vallalar describes a state where the joy of beholding the divine in the radiant "Hall of Gems" is the very experience of being given the nectar of compassion. The gift lies in the loving look itself.

translit: muntaināḷ ayarntēṉ ayarntiṭēl eṉaeṉ muṉṉarnī tōṉṟiṉai antō antanāḷ toṭaṅki makiḻntiruk kiṉṟēṉ appaṉē ayyaṉē aracē intanāḷ kavalai iṭarpayam ellām eṉṉaiviṭ ṭoḻintiṭap purintāy entanāḷ purintēṉ ipperum pēṟiṅ keytutaṟ kuriyameyt tavamē.
translation: In former days, I grew weary. You appeared before me saying, "Do not grow weary." Oh! From that day on, I have been joyful, O Father, O Master, O King! Today, you have made all worry, trouble, and fear leave me and vanish. On what day did I ever perform the true penance required to attain this great fortune here?
commentary: Grace can arrive suddenly and completely, transforming weariness into unshakable joy. Vallalar recounts how a single divine intervention banished all his past despair and present fears. He is left in a state of humble wonder, feeling he has done nothing to deserve such a life-altering gift.

translit: vāykkuṟum puraittut tirintuvīṇ kaḻittu malattilē kiṭantuḻait tiṭṭa nāykkuyar taviciṭ ṭorumaṇi muṭiyum naṉṟuṟac cūṭṭiṉai antō tūykkuṇat tavarkaḷ pukaḻmaṇi maṉṟil cōtiyē niṉperun tayavait tāykkuṟu tayaveṉ ṟeṇṇukō tāyiṉ tayavumuṉ taṉipperun tayavē.
translation: For this dog that wandered about speaking mischief, wasting its time, lying and struggling in mala, you placed a high throne and fittingly crowned it with a jeweled crown. Oh! O Jothi in the Hall of Gems, praised by those of pure character! Should I think of your great compassion as that of a mother? Even a mother's compassion is your own unique, great compassion.
commentary: Divine grace is so vast that it can lift even the most unworthy soul from the depths of mala (spiritual impurity) and grant it the highest honor. Vallalar uses the striking image of a stray dog being crowned like a king to show the radical transformation grace makes possible. He concludes that God's compassion is the ultimate source of all love, so complete that even a mother's love is just a small reflection of it.

translit: pēriṭar tavirttup pēraruḷ purinta perumaniṉ taṉṉaieṉ ṟaṉakkē cāruṟu tāyē eṉṟuraip pēṉō tantaiyē eṉṟuraip pēṉō cīruṟu kuruvē eṉṟuraip pēṉō teyvamē eṉṟuraip pēṉō yāreṉa uraippēṉ eṉṉeṉap pukaḻvēṉ yātumoṉ ṟaṟintilēṉ antō.
translation: O Great One who averted my great calamity and bestowed vast grace! Shall I say you are the mother who is my support? Shall I say you are the father? Shall I say you are the glorious guru? Shall I say you are God? Who shall I say you are? How shall I praise you? Alas, I know nothing at all.
commentary: The divine cannot be confined to any single role or relationship we understand. After trying to name God as a mother, father, or guru, Vallalar finds all labels fall short. The experience of grace leaves him in awe, realizing that the divine encompasses all these roles and yet transcends them completely.

translit: ciṟuneṟik keṉaittāṉ iḻuttatōr koṭiya tīmaṉa māyaiyaik kaṇattē veṟuviya tākkit taṭutteṉai āṇṭa meyyaniṉ karuṇaieṉ pukalvēṉ uṟunaṟun tēṉum amutummeṉ karumpil uṟṟacā ṟaṭṭacark karaiyum naṟuneyuṅ kalanta cuvaipperum paḻamē ñāṉamaṉ ṟōṅkumeṉ naṭpē.
translation: The cruel, evil-minded māyā pulled me toward the petty path; in an instant, you made it powerless, stopped it, and ruled me. O Truth, what can I say of your compassion? You are the great, flavorful fruit mixed with fragrant, choice honey, nectar, juice from soft sugarcane, crystallized sugar, and fragrant ghee! You are my friend, flourishing in the Hall of Wisdom!
commentary: Divine grace can instantly liberate a person from māyā, the illusion that pulls one toward a petty and meaningless life. To describe the feeling of this liberation, Vallalar uses the metaphor of a perfect fruit made of every conceivable sweetness: honey, nectar, and sugarcane juice. This overwhelming bliss comes from an intimate friend who dwells within the Hall of Wisdom.

translit: pulliya neṟikkē iḻutteṉai alaitta poymmaṉa māyaiyaik kaṇattē melliya tākkit taṭutteṉai āṇṭa meyyaniṉ karuṇaieṉ pukalvēṉ valliniṉ ammai makiḻamaṉ ṟōṅkum vaḷḷalē maṟaikaḷā kamaṅkaḷ colliya patiyē mikutayā nitiyē toṇṭaṉēṉ uyirkkumeyt tuṇaiyē.
translation: The illusion of the false mind pulled me to the lowly path and tormented me; in an instant, you weakened it, stopped it, and ruled me. O Truth, what can I say of your compassion? O benefactor flourishing in the hall so that your mother, the Valli, rejoices! O Lord spoken of by the Vedas and Agamas! O treasure of abundant mercy! O true companion to the soul of this devotee!
commentary: Like the previous verse, this one celebrates the power of grace to instantly subdue the "false mind" of illusion. Here, Vallalar connects his personal experience to the great traditions, addressing God as the Lord praised in the Vedas and Agamas (ancient Hindu scriptures). By mentioning Valli, the divine consort, he hints that his union with God brings joy to the entire cosmic reality, and he affirms that this God is the only true companion for the soul.

translit: aruntavar kāṇṭaṟ karumperuṅkaruṇai aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ uḷattē iruntaṉaṉ ammā nāṉceyta tavantāṉ eṉṉaiyō eṉṉaiyō eṉṟāḷ tiruntuteḷ ḷamutuṇ ṭaḻivelān tavirtta tiruvuru aṭaintaṉaṉ ñāṉa maruntumā maṇiyum mantira niṟaivum vāyttaṉa vāyppiṉeṉ ṟāḷē.
translation: "The Vast Grace-Light, the great compassion that is difficult even for great ascetics to see, is present within my heart. Oh! What penance could I have performed, what penance!" she exclaimed. "I have drunk the pure, clear nectar and attained the sacred form that averts all destruction. The medicine of wisdom, the great gem, and the fullness of mantra have all come to me through this good fortune," she added.
commentary: Using the voice of a female devotee, a common practice in Tamil poetry to express intimacy, Vallalar highlights the astonishing nature of grace. The speaker is in awe that she has received the "Vast Grace-Light" within her heart, a gift that even great ascetics struggle to attain through years of penance. This grace has given her everything: an immortal form, the medicine of wisdom, and the power of sacred utterance (mantra), all as a matter of sheer good fortune, not personal achievement.

translit: iṉpilē vayaṅkum civaparam poruḷē eṉuyirk kamutamē eṉtaṉ aṉpilē paḻutta taṉipperum paḻamē aruḷnaṭam puriyumeṉ aracē vaṉpilē viḷainta māyaiyum viṉaiyum maṭintaṉa viṭintatāl iravum tuṉpilēṉ iṉināṉ aruṭperuñ cōtic cūḻalil tulaṅkukiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: O Sivam, the supreme substance shining in bliss! O nectar of my soul! O unique, great fruit ripened in my love! O my king who performs the dance of grace! The illusion and vinai that grew from hardness have perished. The night has dawned. I am without sorrow now; I shine in the environs of the Vast Grace-Light.
commentary: This verse declares the ultimate spiritual victory. By cultivating a deep, loving relationship with the divine, called Sivam (the supreme reality), all bondage has been destroyed. The illusion and vinai (the karmic residue of past actions) that arise from a hardened ego have vanished. The long night of spiritual ignorance is over, and a new life begins, shining perpetually and without sorrow in the presence of the Vast Grace-Light.

translit: uyirelām orunī tirunaṭam puriyum orutirup potueṉa aṟintēṉ ceyirelām tavirntēṉ tiruvelām aṭaintēṉ cittelām vallatoṉ ṟaṟintēṉ mayirelām puḷakit tuḷamelām kaṉintu malarntaṉaṉ cuttacaṉ mārkkap payirelām taḻaikkap patiyelām kaḷikkap pāṭukiṉ ṟēṉpotup pāṭṭē.
translation: I have realized that all lives are the one sacred common space where You, the One, perform the sacred dance. I have shed all flaws; I have attained all grace. I have known the One that is all-powerful consciousness. Every hair on my body stands on end, my whole being melts, and I have blossomed. I sing the song of the common space so the crops of the Pure True Path may flourish and all realms may rejoice.
commentary: This verse expresses a core realization: every living being is a sacred space where God's cosmic dance unfolds. Recognizing this truth frees the soul from all its flaws and inspires it to sing for the benefit of all. The goal is to help the "Pure True Path" (Suddha Sanmarkkam), a life of universal unity, flourish everywhere.

translit: paṭittaeṉ paṭippum kēḷviyum ivaṟṟiṉ payaṉatām uṇarcciyum aṭiyēṉ piṭittanal nilaiyum uyirummey iṉpum perumaiyum ciṟappumnāṉ uṇṇum vaṭittateḷ ḷamutum vayaṅkumey vāḻvum vāḻkkainaṉ mutalummaṉ ṟakattē naṭittapoṉ ṉaṭiyum tirucciṟṟam palattē naṇṇiya poruḷumeṉ ṟaṟintēṉ.
translation: I have realized that my learning and listening, the realization that is their fruit, the good state your servant has grasped, my life, true bliss, greatness, excellence, the distilled clear ambrosia I drink, a radiant true life, and the fine foundation of life are all Your golden feet that danced within the hall and the Reality abiding in the sacred subtle space.
commentary: The soul now understands that everything of value in its life comes from a single divine source. All learning, happiness, and even life itself are seen as expressions of God's grace, symbolized by the "golden feet" of the dancing Lord. This divine reality is experienced directly within the Thiru Chitrambalam, the sacred, subtle space of one's own consciousness.

translit: kalaiyaṉē ellām vallaōr talaimaik kaṭavuḷē eṉiru kaṇṇē nilaiyaṉē ñāṉa nītimaṉ ṟiṭattē niruttañcey karuṇaimā nitiyē pulaiyaṉēṉ poruṭṭuṉ tiruvaṭi avaṉi poruntiya putumaieṉ pukalvēṉ cilaiyainēr maṉattēṉ ceytavam peritō tiruvaruṭ peruntiṟal peritē.
translation: O Master of all arts, O singular, all-powerful, supreme God, O my two eyes! O steadfast One, O great treasury of compassion who performs the dance in the hall of wisdom and justice! What can I say of the wonder of Your sacred feet coming to earth for the sake of me, a base, lowly one? Is the penance performed by me, with my stone-like mind, so great, or is the immense power of Your sacred grace greater?
commentary: Humbled and astonished, the soul contemplates the magnitude of grace. It views itself as a lowly one with a hard, resistant mind, making the divine visitation an unimaginable wonder. The closing question is a statement of faith: this transformation comes from the infinite and unconditional power of God's compassion.

translit: tarampiṟar aṟiyāt talaivaōr mukkaṇ taṉimutal pēraruṭ cōtip parampara ñāṉa citampara naṭañcey parāpara nirāmaya nimala urampeṟum ayaṉmāl mutaṟperun tēvar uḷattati cayittiṭa eṉakkē varantaru kiṉṟāy vaḷḷalniṉ karuṇai mākaṭaṟ kellaikaṇ ṭilaṉē.
translation: O Lord whose nature others cannot know! O singular, three-eyed Primal One, O vast grace-light, O Supreme Being! O Supreme-beyond-supreme who dances in the Chidambaram of wisdom, O flawless One, O stainless One! To the astonishment of the hearts of the great gods, beginning with the mighty Brahma and Vishnu, you grant boons to me. O generous Giver, I have seen no limit to the great ocean of Your compassion.
commentary: The personal nature of grace is a source of constant wonder. God, whose true nature is incomprehensible even to the highest celestial beings, chooses to give blessings directly to an ordinary person, revealing a compassion so vast it has no limits.

translit: yāṉmuṉam purinta peruntavam yātō eṉcolvēṉ eṉcolvēṉ antō ūṉmaṉam uruka eṉtaṉait tēṟṟi oḷiuruk kāṭṭiya talaivā ēṉmaṉam iraṅkāy iṉṟunī eṉṟēṉ eṉṟacol oliaṭaṅ kutaṉmuṉ āṉmakiḻ kaṉṟiṉ aṇaitteṉai eṭuttāy aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ aracē.
translation: What great penance did I perform in the past? What can I say, what can I say? Alas! O Master, you who consoled me and showed me your form of light, making my flesh and mind melt! “Why does your heart not show compassion today?” I asked. Before the sound of those words faded, you embraced and lifted me up like a mother cow delighting in its calf, O my King, O Vast Grace-Light!
commentary: A sincere, desperate cry to God receives an immediate and tender response. Vallalar recounts asking God for compassion and being instantly embraced, like a calf by its mother, by the ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light.

translit: paṉippaṟut tellām vallacit tākkip paramparam tarukiṉṟa teṉṟōr taṉippaḻam eṉakkē tantaitāṉ tantāṉ tamiyaṉēṉ uṇṭaṉaṉ ataṉtaṉ iṉippaināṉ eṉeṉ ṟiyampuvēṉ antō eṉṉuyir iṉittateṉ karaṇam caṉippaṟa iṉitta tattuvam ellām taṉittaṉi iṉittaṉa taḻaittē.
translation: The Father gave me a unique fruit that removes all fear, makes one an all-powerful Siddhar, and grants the supreme state. I, a solitary one, ate it. Oh, how can I describe its sweetness? My very life became sweet. My inner faculties became sweet, destroying the cause of birth. All the tattvas flourished and became sweet, each one individually.
commentary: The experience of divine grace is like eating a fruit of indescribable sweetness that transforms one's entire being. This transformation makes one a Siddhar (a perfected one), removing the cycle of birth and death and suffusing every part of existence, down to the fundamental elements (tattvas), with bliss.

translit: viṇṇelām kalanta veḷiyilā ṉantam viḷaintatu viḷaintatu maṉaṉē kaṇṇelām kaḷikkak kāṇalām potuvil kaṭavuḷē eṉṟunam karuttil eṇṇalām eṇṇi eḻutalām eḻuti ēttalām eṭutteṭut tuvantē uṇṇalām viḻaintārk kutavalām ulakil ōṅkalām ōṅkalām iṉiyē.
translation: O mind, bliss has blossomed, it has blossomed in the space that pervades the entire sky! To the delight of our eyes, we can see God himself in the common expanse. In our minds, we can contemplate this, we can write it down, and having written, we can praise it. We can joyfully take it up again and again and consume it. We can help those who desire it. In the world, we can now rise high, we can rise high.
commentary: This sublime experience of God is open to all. God can be seen in the Podu (the common expanse), a space open to everyone. This realization is a joy that can be contemplated, shared, and used to elevate all of humanity.

translit: vaḷḷalām karuṇai maṉṟilē amuta vāriyaik kaṇṭaṉam maṉamē aḷḷalām eṭuttuk koḷḷalām pāṭi āṭalām aṭikkaṭi viyantē uḷelām nirampa uṇṇalām ulakil ōṅkalām utavalām uṟalām kaḷelām uṇṭavaṇṭeṉa iṉpam kāṇalām kaḷikkalām iṉiyē.
translation: O mind, we have seen the ocean of amrita in the Hall of Grace of the generous Lord! We can scoop it, take it, sing, and dance, marveling again and again. We can consume it until our inner being is completely full. We can rise high in the world, help others, and attain union. Like a bee that has drunk all the nectar, we can now experience bliss and rejoice.
commentary: Grace is an infinite ocean of amrita (divine ambrosia), an abundant sea to be scooped up and celebrated with joyful abandon. The goal of this spiritual feasting is to become so full of bliss that it naturally overflows into helping others, leading to union with the divine source.

tamil: சனிதொ லைந்தது தடைத விர்ந்தது தயைமி குந்தது சலமொடே
துனிதொ லைந்தது சுமைத விர்ந்தது சுபமி குந்தது சுகமொடே
கனிஎ திர்ந்தது களைத விர்ந்தது களிமி குந்தது கனிவொடே
புனித மன்றிறை நடம லிந்தது புகழ்உ யர்ந்தது புவியிலே.
translit: caṉito laintatu taṭaita virntatu tayaimi kuntatu calamoṭē tuṉito laintatu cumaita virntatu cupami kuntatu cukamoṭē kaṉie tirntatu kaḷaita virntatu kaḷimi kuntatu kaṉivoṭē puṉita maṉṟiṟai naṭama lintatu pukaḻu yarntatu puviyilē.
translation: Misfortune is gone, obstacles are removed, and grace has increased with serenity. Sorrow is gone, burdens are removed, and auspiciousness has increased with happiness. The fruit has appeared, weariness is removed, and joy has increased with compassion. The dance of the Lord of the sacred hall abounds; His praise has risen high in the world.
commentary: This verse is a triumphant declaration of all that vanishes when grace arrives. Every form of suffering, from external misfortune to internal sorrow and weariness, is simply gone. In its place, positive qualities like grace, happiness, and compassion flourish. The "dance of the Lord" signifies that the divine presence is now vibrantly active and visible in the world.

tamil: உரையும் உற்றது ஒளியும் உற்றது உணர்வும் உற்றது உண்மையே
பரையும் உற்றது பதியும் உற்றது பதமும் உற்றது பற்றியே
புரையும் அற்றது குறையும் அற்றது புலையும் அற்றது புன்மைசேர்
திரையும் அற்றது நரையும் அற்றது திரையும் அற்றவி ழுந்ததே.
translit: uraiyum uṟṟatu oḷiyum uṟṟatu uṇarvum uṟṟatu uṇmaiyē paraiyum uṟṟatu patiyum uṟṟatu patamum uṟṟatu paṟṟiyē puraiyum aṟṟatu kuṟaiyum aṟṟatu pulaiyum aṟṟatu puṉmaicēr tiraiyum aṟṟatu naraiyum aṟṟatu tiraiyum aṟṟavi ḻuntatē.
translation: Truly, speech has been attained, light has been attained, and consciousness has been attained. By holding fast, Parai has been attained, the Lord has been attained, and the divine state has been attained. Fault is gone, deficiency is gone, and impurity is gone. The wrinkle of decay is gone, grey hair is gone, and the concealing veil has fallen away.
commentary: Attaining the divine state is a complete victory over limitation, affecting both the inner and outer self. "Holding fast" to the goal brings union with both the masculine aspect of God (the Lord) and the feminine creative power, Parai. This union removes all inner faults and, remarkably, all outer signs of decay, including wrinkles and grey hair, as the veil of ignorance that separates the soul from God finally lifts.

translit: ampalattē āṭukiṉṟa āramutē aracē āṉanta mākaṭalē aṟivēeṉ aṉpē umparkaṭkē aṉṟiinta ulakarkaṭkum aruḷvāṉ oḷirkiṉṟa oḷiyēmey uṇarntōrtam uṟavē empalattē vākieṉak keḻumaiyumnaṟ ṟuṇaiyāy eṉuḷattē viḷaṅkukiṉṟa eṉiṟaiyē niṉatu cempatattē malarviḷaṅkak kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ eṉatu ciṟumaielām tīrntēmeyc celvamaṭain tēṉē.
translation: O rare nectar dancing in the sacred space, O King! O great ocean of bliss, O Wisdom, my Love! O Light that shines to bestow grace on the celestials and on the people of this world! O Kin of those who have realized the truth! Becoming my strength and my good companion through all seven births, you shine within my heart, my Lord. I have seen the flower shining at your sacred feet. All my littleness has vanished; I have attained the true wealth.
commentary: In this personal address, God is an intimate companion, love, and wisdom shining within one's own heart. A key point is that this grace is meant for ordinary people on Earth. Seeing the "flower at his feet" is a devotional image for realizing this closeness to God, an awareness that dissolves all inadequacy and constitutes the only true wealth.

translit: aṭiviḷaṅkak kaṉakacapait taṉinaṭaṉam puriyum aruṭcuṭarē eṉuyiruk kāṉaperun tuṇaiyē tuṭiviḷaṅkak karattēntum cōtimalai maruntē coṟpatamel lāmkaṭanta ciṟcorupap poruḷē poṭiviḷaṅkat tirumēṉip puṇṇiyaṉē ñāṉap pōṉakaraic civikaiyiṉmēl poruntavaitta puṉitā paṭiviḷaṅkac ciṟiyēṉniṉ patamalarkaṇ ṭuvantēṉ parivoḻintēṉ aruṭcelvam pariceṉappeṟ ṟēṉē.
translation: O flame of grace performing the unique dance in the golden hall, your feet radiant! O great companion to my soul! O medicine from the mountain of Jothi, holding the shining drum in your hand! O reality of pure consciousness that transcends all words and states! O holy one whose sacred body gleams with ash! O pure one who placed the man of great wisdom upon a palanquin! For all the world to see, I, the lowly one, have beheld your lotus feet and rejoiced. My anxieties have vanished; I have received the wealth of grace as a gift.
commentary: Here, Vallalar praises God using classic imagery associated with Lord Siva: the cosmic dancer, the one holding a drum, the ascetic covered in sacred ash.
