He also gives a specific example of God's grace: honoring the child-saint Thirujnanasambandar, the one fed with the milk of wisdom, by seating him in a palanquin. Beholding God's sacred feet brings personal liberation, a gift that ends all anxiety and fills him with the "wealth of grace."

translit: aṉpuṭai yavarēel lāmuṭai yavarē aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ āṇṭava rēeṉ vaṉpuṭai maṉattainaṉ maṉamākki eṉatu vacañceyvit taruḷiya maṇimaṉṟat tavarē iṉpuṭai yavarēeṉ iṟaiyava rēeṉ irukaṇuḷ maṇikaḷuḷ icaintirun tavarē eṉpuṭai eṉaittūkki eṭuttīriṅ kitaṉai eṇṇukiṉ ṟēṉamu tuṇṇukiṉ ṟēṉē.
translation: O You who are full of love! O You who possess all things! O ArutPerunJothi, my Master! O one from the jeweled hall who transformed my hard heart into a good heart and graciously brought it under my control! O you who are full of bliss, my Lord! O you who reside harmoniously within the pupils of my two eyes! You lifted me up, this frame of bones. As I contemplate this, I am consuming nectar.
commentary: Vallalar addresses God as the One who is full of love and who possesses all things. Vallalar sees God's greatest act of grace in the inner change of his own stubborn mind into a heart filled with goodness. He experiences the divine, ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light), as an intimate presence within his very eyes. Contemplating this transformation from a mere "frame of bones" to a vessel of grace is a state of pure bliss.

translit: kalakkam nīṅkiṉēṉ kaḷippuṟu kiṉṟēṉ kaṉaka ampalam kaṉintaceṅ kaṉiyē tulakkam uṟṟaciṟ ṟampalat tamutē tūya cōtiyē cukapperu vāḻvē vilakkal illatōr taṉimutal aracē vēta ākamam viḷampumeyp poruḷē alakkaṇ aṟṟamey aṉpartam uḷattē amarnta tōrcacci tāṉanta civamē.
translation: My turmoil is gone; I am becoming joyful. O ripe, red fruit from the golden hall! O nectar from the radiant small hall! O pure Jothi! O great life of bliss! O unique, primal King who cannot be prevented! O true reality proclaimed by the Vedas and Agamas! O Satchidananda-Sivamthat resides in the hearts of true devotees who are free from suffering!
commentary: Inner turmoil has vanished, replaced by pure joy. Vallalar addresses God with rich metaphors: a ripe fruit, pure nectar, and a radiant light (Jothi). This divine reality, he says, is the ultimate truth pointed to by all sacred scriptures, the Vedas and Agamas. It is directly experienced as Satchidananda-Sivam (Being-Consciousness-Bliss-Sivam), the very nature of God which dwells in the hearts of devotees free from suffering.

translit: ōṅkāra aṇaimītu nāṉirunta taruṇam uvanteṉatu maṇavāḷar civantavaṭi vakaṉṟē īṅkārap paḷikkuvaṭi veṭuttetirē niṉṟār iruntaruḷka eṉaeḻuntēṉ eḻuntiruppa teṉnī āṅkāram oḻieṉṟār oḻintiruntēṉ appō tavarnāṉō nāṉavarō aṟintilaṉmuṉ kuṟippai ūṅkāra iraṇṭuruvum oṉṟāṉōm aṅkē uṟaintaaṉu pavamtōḻi niṟaintaperu veḷiyē.
translation: The moment I was on the couch of Omkara, my Bridegroom gladly set aside his red form, took on the crystal form of Īṅkāram, and stood before me. I rose, saying, 'Please, be seated.' He said, 'Why do you rise? Discard your ego.' I remained, having discarded it. At that moment I lost the former sense of difference: was he I, or was I he? I could not tell. Our two forms of Ūṅkāram became one. The experience that settled there, my friend, was the vast, full expanse.
commentary: This verse is a vivid, personal account of the final stage of mystical union. While meditating on Omkara (the primordial sound 'Om'), Vallalar encounters God, who gives him a single command: "Discard your ego." The moment he lets go of his separate self, the distinction between devotee and deity vanishes. He cannot tell if he is God or God is him. The two merge into one, and the resulting state is the direct experience of becoming the vast, boundless expanse of being.

translit: collukiṉṟēṉ paṟpalanāṉ collukiṉṟa vellām turicalavē cūtalavē tūymaiyuṭai yaṉavē vellukiṉṟa vārttaiaṉṟi veṟumvārttai eṉvāy viḷampāteṉ aiyarniṉṟu viḷampukiṉṟa paṭiyāl cellukiṉṟa paṭiyēnī kāṇpāyit tiṉattē tēmoḻiap pōteṉainī teḷintukoḷvāy kaṇṭāy ollukiṉṟa vakaiellām collukiṉṟē ṉaṭināṉ uṇmaiitu uṇmaiitu uṇmaiitu tāṉē.
translation: I say many things, and everything I say is without fault, without deceit, and pure. My mouth speaks no empty words, only victorious ones, for my Father stands within and speaks through me. You will see it happen just as I say, this very day. O sweet-tongued one, then you will understand me clearly. I am telling you everything I can, my friend. This is the truth, this is the truth, this is the truth.
commentary: The speaker makes a bold claim: his words are perfectly true because they are not his own. He states with absolute confidence that God, his Father, is speaking directly through him. Because of this, his words are "victorious" and will be proven true this very day. The triple repetition, "This is the truth," emphasizes his firm certainty in his role as a divine messenger.

translit: tantai taṉmaiyē taṉaiyaṉtaṉ taṉmai eṉṟu cāṟṟutal cattiyam kaṇṭīr entai empirāṉ aintoḻil puriyum iṟaivaṉ maṉṟuḷē iyalnaṭam purivāṉ maintaṉ eṉṟeṉai āṇṭavaṉ ellām valla nāyakaṉ nallacīr uṭaiyāṉ anta ṇāḷaṉmey aṟivuṭai yavaṉeṉ appaṉ taṉmaieṉ taṉmaieṉ ṟaṟimiṉ.
translation: The saying, "The nature of the son is the nature of the father," is the truth, you see. My Father, my Lord, is the God who performs the five functions and who dances the natural dance in the Hall. He who accepted me as his son is the all-powerful Master, the one of glorious attributes, the Gracious One, the one who possesses true wisdom. Know that the nature of my Father is my nature.
commentary: Using the simple truth that a son shares his father's nature, the speaker declares that his own nature has become identical to God's. He identifies his Father as the supreme Lord who performs the five cosmic functions (creation, preservation, destruction, concealment, and grace). Since this all-powerful, wise, and gracious God has accepted him as a son, he now shares that same divine nature.

translit: eṉuṭalum eṉuyirum eṉporuḷum niṉṉaeṉa icaintañ ñāṉṟē uṉṉiṭaināṉ koṭuttaṉaṉmaṟ ṟeṉṉiṭaivē ṟoṉṟumilai uṭaiyāy iṅkē puṉṉikarēṉ kuṟṟamelām poṟuttatuvum pōtāmal puṇarntu koṇṭē taṉṉikareṉ ṟeṉavaittāy iññāṉṟeṉ koṭuppēṉniṉ taṉmaik kantō.
translation: On the very day I agreed that my body, my life, and my possessions were yours, I gave them to you, O Master. Now, nothing else is left with me. As if it were not enough to forgive all the faults of this lowly one, you united with me and made me your equal. Today, what can I give in return for this nature of yours? Oh!
commentary: Overwhelmed by divine generosity, the speaker reflects on the nature of grace. He had already surrendered everything, his body, life, and possessions, to God. Yet God forgave his flaws and elevated him to a state of equality. This act of grace is so immense that the speaker is left speechless, feeling there is nothing he could possibly give in return for such a gift.

translit: eṉṉuraikkēṉ eṉṉuraikkēṉ intaati cayantaṉṉai emma ṉōrkāḷ poṉṉuraikkum maṇimaṉṟil tirunaṭaṉam purikiṉṟa puṉitaṉ eṉṉuḷ miṉuraikkum paṭikalantāṉ piriyāmal viḷaṅkukiṉṟāṉ meymmai yāṉa taṉṉuraikkum eṉṉuraikkum camaracamcey taruḷkiṉṟāṉ cakattiṉ mītē.
translation: What can I say? What can I say about this wonder, O my people? The Holy One, who performs the sacred dance in the jeweled hall that outshines gold, has mingled within me like a flash of lightning. He shines there without separation. Here in this world, he graciously makes his true word and my word one and the same.
commentary: The speaker struggles to express the wonder of his inner state. God, the dancer in the golden hall of consciousness, has mingled with his being "like a flash of lightning" and now shines there constantly. Because of this inseparable union, God has created a perfect harmony (samarasam) between the divine word and his own word, making them one and the same for all the world to witness.

translit: āṭukiṉṟa cēvaṭikkē āḷāṉēṉ māḷāta ākkai peṟṟēṉ kūṭukiṉṟa caṉmārkka caṅkattē naṭuviruntu kulāvu kiṉṟēṉ pāṭukiṉṟēṉ entaipirāṉ patappukaḻai aṉpiṉoṭum pāṭip pāṭi nīṭukiṉṟēṉ iṉpakkūt tāṭukiṉṟēṉ eṇṇamelām nirampi ṉēṉē.
translation: I have become a servant to his dancing, sacred feet. I have received a body that does not perish. I sit in the midst of the gathered assembly of the Sanmarkkam and rejoice. I sing the praise of my Father and Lord's feet. Singing again and again with love, I thrive. I dance the dance of bliss. All my aspirations have been fulfilled.
commentary: Devotion has brought about a complete and joyful transformation. Vallalar describes receiving a deathless body, finding fellowship in the community of the Sanmarkkam (path of true goodness), and living a life filled with ecstatic singing and dancing. All his deepest desires are fulfilled here and now, as a continuous celebration of grace.

translit: āṇai āṇainī añcalai añcalai aruḷoḷi tarukiṉṟām kōṇai mānilat tavarelām niṉṉaiyē kuṟikkoḷvar niṉakkēem āṇai ampalat taracaiyum aḷittaṉam vāḻkanī makaṉēeṉ ṟēṇai peṟṟiṭa eṉakkaruḷ purintaniṉ iṇaimalarp patampōṟṟi.
translation: "I swear, I swear, do not fear, do not fear. We are giving you the light of grace. All the people of this vast, flawed world will look to you. By Our authority, We have granted you sovereignty over the sacred space. Live long, my son!", thus you bestowed grace upon me that I might receive this assurance. Praise to your paired, flower-like feet.
commentary: God speaks directly, offering the deepest reassurance: "Do not fear." This divine promise is also a commission, granting the speaker the light of grace and appointing him as a guide for the world. It marks the transition from a personal spiritual quest to a universal mission, founded on God's own authority. The devotee praises the feet of the Lord who gave this assurance.

translit: nāykkum ōrtavi ciṭṭuppoṉ māmuṭi naṉṟu cūṭṭiṉai eṉṟuniṉ aṉparkaḷ vāykku vanta paṭipala pēcavē matiyi lēṉaiyum maṉṉaruṭ cattiyām tāykkuk kāṭṭinal taṇṇamu tūṭṭiōr tavaḷa māṭappoṉ maṇṭapat tēṟṟiyē cēykku nēraeṉ kaiyilpoṟ kaṅkaṇam tikaḻak kaṭṭiṉai eṉṉainiṉ ceykaiyē.
translation: While your devotees freely say many things, such as, "You provide a throne even for a dog and fittingly crown it with gold," you showed even me, a witless one, to the Mother who is the sovereign power of grace. You fed me good, cool ambrosia, raised me to a golden pavilion in a white mansion, and tied a gleaming golden bracelet on my hand as if for a son. What a deed of yours this is to me!
commentary: Vallalar expresses his astonishment at God's grace using the humble image of a dog being crowned king. While others might observe this as a general principle of God's generosity, he feels it as a deeply personal reality. He, feeling witless and unworthy, has been nourished by the divine, raised to a place of honor, and treated like a beloved son. The verse conveys a sense of wonder at a grace that completely disregards human hierarchies of worth.

translit: taṉṉaiviṭat talaimaioru takaviṉumiṅ kiyalāt taṉittalaimaip perumpatiyē taruṇatayā nitiyē poṉṉaṭieṉ cirattirukkap purintaparam poruḷē puttamutam eṉakkaḷitta puṇṇiyaṉē nītāṉ eṉṉaiviṭa māṭṭāynāṉ uṉṉaiviṭa māṭṭēṉ iruvarumoṉ ṟākiiṅkē irukkiṉṟōm itutāṉ niṉṉaruḷē aṟintateṉil ceyuñceykai aṉaittum niṉceyalō eṉceyalō nikaḻttiṭuka nīyē.
translation: O great Master of singular sovereignty, a supremacy beyond which no higher authority can possibly exist! O treasure of timely compassion! O supreme reality who made your golden feet rest on my head! O virtuous one who gave me fresh ambrosia! You will not let me go; I will not let you go. We have become one and are here together. Since this is known by your grace, then as for all the deeds being done: are they your deeds or my deeds? You yourself must declare it.
commentary: Having achieved an inseparable union with God, the distinction between the self and the divine disappears. In this state of oneness, Vallalar poses a searching question: are the actions flowing through him his own, or are they God's? By asking God to be the one to answer, he expresses the complete dissolution of his own agency. It is the final step of surrender, where the very sense of being a separate actor is given over to the divine.

translit: kaṭalkaṭantēṉ karaiyaṭaintēṉ kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ kōyil katavutiṟan tiṭappeṟṟēṉ kāṭciyelām kaṇṭēṉ aṭarkaṭanta tiruamutuṇ ṭaruḷoḷiyāl aṉaittum aṟintuteḷin taṟivuruvāy aḻiyāmai aṭaintēṉ uṭalkuḷirntēṉ uyirkiḷarntēṉ uḷḷamelām taḻaittēṉ uḷḷapaṭi uḷḷaporuḷ uḷḷaṉavāy niṟaintēṉ iṭartavirkkum cittielām eṉvacamōṅ kiṉavē ittaṉaiyum potunaṭañcey iṟaivaṉaruṭ ceyalē.
translation: I have crossed the ocean and reached the shore. I have found the temple. I received the blessing of the doors being opened. I have seen all the visions. I have consumed the sacred ambrosia that transcends all density. By the light of grace, I came to know and understand all things, became the very form of consciousness, and attained immortality. My body has cooled, my life-force has surged, my whole inner self has flourished. I am filled with all that exists, embodying Reality as it truly is. All the siddhis that remove affliction have thrived in my possession. All of this is the graceful act of the Lord who performs the universal dance.
commentary: This is a declaration of final victory in the spiritual quest, using the metaphor of a long sea voyage ending on a welcome shore. Crossing the ocean is overcoming life's struggles, and finding the temple is discovering the divine within. Gaining entry, seeing the visions, and eating the divine food represent the stages of enlightenment, culminating in an immortal body made of pure consciousness. Vallalar makes it clear that this ultimate attainment, including the siddhis (supernatural powers), is a gift of God's grace, not his own doing.

translit: kāṟṟālē puviyālē kakaṉamata ṉālē kaṉalālē puṉalālē katirāti yālē kūṟṟālē piṇiyālē kolaikkaruvi yālē kōḷālē piṟa:iyaṟṟum koṭuñceyalka ḷālē vēṟṟālē eññāṉṟum aḻiyātē viḷaṅkum meyaḷikka vēṇṭumeṉṟēṉ viraintaḷittāṉ eṉakkē ēṟṟālē iḻiveṉanīr niṉaiyātīr ulakīr entaiaruṭ peruñjōti iṟaivaṉaiccār vīrē.
translation: I asked for a body that would shine forever, indestructible at any time by wind, by earth, by the vast sky, by fire, by water, or by the sun and other celestial lights; indestructible by the god of death, by disease, by weapons of murder, by planetary forces, by cruel deeds done by others, or by anything else. He swiftly granted it to me. O people of the world, do not think this demeaning because it was received as a gift. Come and take refuge in my Father, the Lord of the Vast Grace-Light.
commentary: A central part of Vallalar's teaching is the possibility of transforming the physical body into an immortal, indestructible form. He states plainly that he asked God for a body that could not be harmed by any force, natural or man-made, and that his prayer was granted. He tells the people of the world not to think it lowly to ask God and receive in this way, and invites all humanity to take refuge in ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light), who grants this deathless body.

translit: ellā ulakamum eṉvacam āyiṉa ellā uyirkaḷum eṉuyir āyiṉa ellā ñāṉamum eṉñāṉam āyiṉa ellā vittaiyum eṉvittai āyiṉa ellā pōkamum eṉpōkam āyiṉa ellāiṉpamum eṉiṉpam āyiṉa ellām vallaciṟ ṟampalat teṉṉappar ellām nalkieṉ uḷḷattuḷ ḷārē.
translation: All worlds have come under my control. All living beings have become my own life. All wisdom has become my wisdom. All arts have become my arts. All enjoyments have become my enjoyment. All joys have become my joy. My Father of Chitrambalam, the all-powerful, granted all this and resides within my heart.
commentary: The ultimate result of divine union is an expansion of consciousness to encompass all of reality. The sense of a small, separate self dissolves, and one's own being merges with the entire cosmos. To feel all life as one's own life, and all worlds as one's own domain, is the final state of this realization. Vallalar attributes this state to the grace of the Lord of Chitrambalam (the inner space of consciousness), who by taking up residence within the heart, gives the soul everything.

translit: caṉmārkka caṅkattīr ciṟṟaṭiyēṉ umatu tāḷvaṇaṅkic cāṟṟukiṉṟēṉ tayaviṉoṭum kēṭpīr eṉmārkkat teṉainumakkuḷ oruvaṉeṉak koḷvīr ellāmcey vallanama tiṟaivaṉaiyē toḻuvīr puṉmārkkat tavarpōlē vēṟucila pukaṉṟē puntimayak kaṭaiyātīr pūraṇameyc cukamāyt taṉmārkka māyviḷaṅkum cuttacivam oṉṟē taṉāṇai eṉāṇai cārntaṟimiṉ īṇṭē.
translation: O members of the Sanmarkka Sangam! This humble servant bows to your feet and declares this; please listen with kindness. Accept me as one among you on my path. Worship only our Lord, who is all-powerful. Do not become confused in mind by speaking of various other things like those on lowly paths. Only the one Suddha Sivam shines as its own path, as perfect, true bliss. By Its oath and by my oath, know this to be true right here and now.
commentary: Vallalar directly instructs his community, the Sanmarkka Sangam (the association for the true path), on the essentials of his teaching. First, he asks them to see him as an equal among them. Second, he urges them to avoid the confusion of worshipping many different powers and instead focus solely on the one all-powerful God. This God, called Suddha Sivam (pure Sivam), is itself the path and the destination: a state of perfect, blissful truth.

translit: ātiyum naṭuvum antamum illā aruṭperuñ cōtieṉ uḷattē nītiyil kalantu niṟaintatu nāṉum nittiyaṉ āyiṉēṉ ulakīr cātiyum matamum camayamum tavirttē cattiyac cuttacaṉ mārkka vītiyil umaittāṉ niṟuvuval uṇmai viḷampiṉēṉ vammiṉō viraintē.
translation: ArutPerunJothi, which has no beginning, middle, or end, has justly mingled with my heart and filled it completely. And I too have become eternal, O people of the world! Casting aside caste, creed, and religion, I will establish you on the path of the true, pure Sanmarkkam. I have declared the truth; come quickly!
commentary: Through union with ArutPerunJothi (the vast grace-light), which he experiences as a timeless reality filling his heart, Vallalar himself has become eternal. His personal liberation now turns into a universal mission: he will guide all people onto the path of the true Sanmarkkam. This path requires leaving behind all worldly divisions of caste, creed, and organized religion, and he urgently invites everyone to join him.

translit: vātu pēciya maṉitar kāḷoru vārttai kēṇmīṉkaḷ vantunum pōtu pōvataṉ muṉṉa rēaruṭ potuvi lēnaṭam pōṟṟuvīr tītu pēciṉīr eṉṟi ṭātumait tiruvu ḷaṅkoḷum kāṇmiṉō cūtu pēcilaṉ naṉmai colkiṉṟēṉ cuṟṟam eṉpatu paṟṟiyē.
translation: O you people who engage in debates, come and listen to this one word. Before your time passes, praise the dance in the common expanse of grace. See for yourselves: it will accept you in its sacred heart without saying, "You spoke ill." I do not speak deceitfully; I am telling you what is good for you, out of a sense of kinship.
commentary: This is a plea to those lost in intellectual or religious debates to stop arguing and simply turn toward God. Vallalar warns that life is short and should be spent experiencing the divine dance of grace, which takes place in a "common expanse" available to all. He offers a beautiful assurance: God's heart is so vast that it welcomes everyone without judgment, even those who once spoke against it. He speaks this truth out of a deep sense of kinship with all people.

translit: tūkkamum tuyarum accamum iṭarum tolaintaṉa tolaintaṉa eṉaiviṭ ṭēkkamum viṉaiyum māyaiyum iruḷum irintaṉa oḻintaṉa muḻutum ākkamum aruḷum aṟivummey aṉpum aḻivuṟā uṭampummey iṉpa ūkkamum eṉaiyē uṟṟaṉa ulakīr uṇmaiiv vācakam uṇarmiṉ.
translation: Sleep, sorrow, fear, and trouble have vanished, vanished from me. Longing, karma, illusion, and darkness have fled, completely eliminated. Prosperity, grace, knowledge, true love, an imperishable body, and the vitality of true bliss have all come to me. O people of the world, realize that these words are the truth.
commentary: This verse is a personal testimony of total transformation. Vallalar catalogs all the aspects of ordinary, suffering human life that have been completely removed from him: sleep, fear, sorrow, and even karma (the binding effects of past actions). In their place, he has been filled with everything eternal: grace, true knowledge, unbreakable love, and an imperishable body overflowing with blissful energy. He offers his own life as proof that such a perfected state is real.

translit: picculakar meccap pitaṟṟiniṉṟa pētaiyaṉēṉ iccaielām eyta icaintaruḷic ceytaṉaiyē accamelām tīrntēṉ aruḷamutam uṇkiṉṟēṉ niccalumpē rāṉanta nittiraicey kiṉṟēṉē.
translation: I, the fool who stood raving in a way that even the world's madmen would praise, you have graciously consented and fulfilled all my desires. I am free of all fear; I consume the nectar of grace. Daily, I sleep the sleep of supreme bliss.
commentary: The speaker humbly remembers how he once babbled foolishly to win the praise of a deluded world. Yet God, in boundless compassion, fulfilled all his deepest desires. Now, all fear is gone, replaced by a constant state of blissful peace, which he calls the 'sleep of supreme bliss.'

Note 346

tamil: இத்தலைப்பின் கீழ்த் தொகுக்கப்பெற்றுள்ள 161 பாக்களும் தனிப்பாடல்கள்.ஆறாந் திருமுறைக் காலத்தில் பல சமயங்களிற் பாடப் பெற்றவை. முன் பதிப்புகளில்இவை தனிப்பாடல்கள் என்ற தலைப்பில் ஆறாந் திருமுறையின் பிற்பகுதியில்உள்ளன. ஆ. பா. இவற்றைத் தனித்திருஅலங்கல், தனித்திருத் தொடை,தனித்திரு மாலை என மூன்று கூறாக்கி முறையே ஆறாந்திருமுறை முன், இடை,முடிந்த பகுதிகளின் ஈற்றில் வைத்துள்ளனர். இப்பதிப்பில் இவை ஒருவாறு பொருள்வரிசையில் முன் பின்னாக அமைக்கப்பெற்று இவண் வைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன.
translit: ittalaippiṉ kīḻt tokukkappeṟṟuḷḷa 161 pākkaḷum taṉippāṭalkaḷ. āṟān tirumuṟaik kālattil pala camayaṅkaḷiṟ pāṭap peṟṟavai. muṉ patippukaḷil ivai taṉippāṭalkaḷ eṉṟa talaippil āṟān tirumuṟaiyiṉ piṟpakutiyil uḷḷaṉa. ā. pā. ivaṟṟait taṉittiru-alaṅkal, taṉittirut toṭai, taṉittiru mālai eṉa mūṉṟu kūṟākki muṟaiyē āṟāntirumuṟai muṉ, iṭai, muṭinta pakutikaḷiṉ īṟṟil vaittuḷḷaṉar. ippatippil ivai oruvāṟu poruḷ varicaiyil muṉ piṉṉāka amaikkappeṟṟu ivaṇ vaikkappaṭṭuḷḷaṉa.
translation: The 161 poems gathered under this heading are all taṉippāṭalkaḷ, separate verses sung on various occasions during the period of the Sixth Thirumurai. In earlier editions they stand under the heading Taṉippāṭalkaḷ in the latter part of the Sixth Thirumurai. Ā. Pā. divided them into three parts — Taṉittiru-alaṅkal, Taṉittiru-toṭai and Taṉittiru-mālai — placing them respectively at the end of the opening, middle and closing portions of the Sixth Thirumurai. In this edition they have been arranged broadly in order of subject matter and placed here.

translit: tāḻaippaḻam - tēṅkāy.
translation: tāḻaippaḻam — i.e. coconut.

translit: aṭaṅkunāḷ illā tamarntāṉaik kāṇaṟkē toṭaṅkunāḷ nallataṉ ṟō - neñcē toṭaṅkunāḷ nallataṉ ṟō.
translation: To see the One who abides without ever ending, is not the day we begin a good day? O heart, is not the day we begin a good day?
commentary: The spiritual path can begin at any moment. The poet asks his own heart a simple question meant to cut through all procrastination: to seek the One who is timeless, isn't today the perfect day to start?

translit: vallavā ṟellāmum vallāṉaik kāṇaṟkē nallanāḷ eṇṇiya nāḷ - neñcē nallanāḷ eṇṇiya nāḷ.
translation: To see the One who is capable of everything, the day you decide upon is the good day. O heart, the day you decide upon is the good day.
commentary: No calendar governs the meeting with God. To see the One who can do all things, the good day is simply the day the heart decides. Vallalar speaks to his own heart, and repeats it so that it will not be forgotten.

translit: kālaṅ kaṭanta kaṭavuḷaik kāṇaṟkuk kālaṅ karutuva tēṉ - neñcē kālaṅ karutuva tēṉ.
translation: To see the God who transcends time, why look for an auspicious time? O heart, why look for an auspicious time?
commentary: God is beyond time, so there is no sense in waiting for an auspicious hour to seek God. Vallalar sets aside the habit of watching for lucky times and turns his heart toward the timeless One now. The refrain asks it twice: why look for an auspicious time?

translit: ālam amutākkum aṇṇalaik kāṇaṟkuk kālaṅ karutuva tēṉ - neñcē kālaṅ karutuva tēṉ.
translation: To see the great Lord who turns poison into nectar, why look for an auspicious time? O heart, why look for an auspicious time?
commentary: God is a power that transforms poison into nectar, so you do not need to wait for a special or 'auspicious' time to seek him. Every moment is the right moment to turn towards the divine.

translit: taṭaiyātum illāt talaivaṉaik kāṇaṟkē taṭaiyātum illaikaṇ ṭāy - neñcē taṭaiyātum illaikaṇ ṭāy.
translation: To see the Master who is without any obstacle, know that there is no obstacle for you. O heart, know that there is no obstacle for you.
commentary: The path to God is as open and unobstructed as God himself. Any barriers you perceive between yourself and the divine are an illusion; in reality, nothing stands in your way.

translit: kaiyuḷ amutattai vāyuḷ amutākkap paiyuḷuṉakkeṉṉai yō - neñcē paiyuḷ uṉakkeṉṉai yō.
translation: To bring the ambrosia in my hand to my mouth, what is this sorrow for you, O mind? What is this sorrow for you?
commentary: Experiencing God's grace is as simple as bringing the food in your hand to your mouth. The mind creates needless sorrow and complication around a process that is direct, immediate, and already within your grasp.

translit: eṉṉuyir nātaṉai yāṉkaṇ ṭaṇaitaṟkē uṉṉuva teṉṉaikaṇ ṭāy - neñcē uṉṉuva teṉṉaikaṇ ṭāy.
translation: To see and unite with the Lord of my very soul, what is there to think about, O mind? See, what is there to think about?
commentary: Union with the divine is not something to be achieved through thinking or planning. It is an immediate, intuitive experience, and the mind's endless analysis only gets in the way.

translit: nāṉpeṟṟa celvattai nāṉpaṟṟik koḷḷaṟkē ēṉpaṟṟu vāyeṉpa tār - neñcē ēṉpaṟṟu vāyeṉpa tār.
translation: To take hold of the treasure I have received, who is there to say, 'Why do you grasp it?' O heart, who is there to say, 'Why do you grasp it?'
commentary: The treasure of grace is already his, received as a gift. Vallalar tells his heart that no one can forbid him from taking hold of what has been given; there is nothing to hesitate over.

translit: tattuvā tītat talaivaṉaik kāṇaṟkut tattuva muṉṉuva tēṉ - neñcē tattuva muṉṉuva tēṉ.
translation: To see the Lord who transcends all tattvas, why do you ponder the tattvas, O mind? Why do you ponder the tattvas?
commentary: The tattvas are the fundamental building blocks of reality in Indian philosophy, such as earth, water, mind, and intellect. To see the Lord, who exists beyond all these categories, you must stop analyzing them. You cannot use the mind's conceptual maps to reach a destination that is beyond all maps.

translit: okka amutattai uṇṭōm iṉiccaṟṟum vikkal varātukaṇ ṭāy - neñcē vikkal varātukaṇ ṭāy.
translation: We have drunk the ambrosia together. From now on, there will not be the slightest hiccup, O mind. See, there will not be the slightest hiccup.
commentary: After tasting the ambrosia of divine grace, the spiritual path becomes smooth and effortless. Vallalar reassures his mind that their shared experience of God has ended the old struggles and interruptions, symbolized as "hiccups." This marks a transition from a state of striving to one of settled, confident peace.
NOTES
Note 291

translit: kāṇavē - pi. irā., patippu.
translation: kāṇavē — reading of the P. Irā. edition.

tamil: எனக்கும் உனக்கும் இசைந்த பொருத்தம் என்ன பொருத்த மோ
இந்தப் பொருத்தம் உலகில் பிறருக் கெய்தும் பொருத்த மோ.
translit: eṉakkum uṉakkum icainta poruttam eṉṉa porutta mō intap poruttam ulakil piṟaruk keytum porutta mō.
translation: What kind of connection is this that fits so well between you and me? Is this a connection that others in the world can attain?
commentary: The connection with God feels so uniquely perfect and personal that it seems almost unbelievable. The question comes from pure wonder: the poet is so overwhelmed by the intimacy of grace that he marvels that such a special bond could even exist, for himself or for anyone.

tamil: தனக்கு நிகரிங் கில்லா துயர்ந்த தம்பம் ஒன்ற தே
தாவிப் போகப் போக நூலின் தரத்தில் நின்ற தே
கனக்கத் திகைப்புற் றங்கே நானும் கலங்கி வருந்த வே
கலக்கம் நீக்கித் தூக்கி வைத்தாய் நிலைபொ ருந்த வே.
translit: taṉakku nikariṅ killā tuyarnta tampam oṉṟa tē tāvip pōkap pōka nūliṉ tarattil niṉṟa tē kaṉakkat tikaippuṟ ṟaṅkē nāṉum kalaṅki varunta vē kalakkam nīkkit tūkki vaittāy nilaipo runta vē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: There was a pillar, towering without equal here. As I tried to climb higher and higher, it tapered to the thinness of a thread. When I stood there, greatly bewildered, distressed, and suffering, you removed my distress and lifted me up, placing me securely in that state. What kind of connection is this that fits so well between you and me? Is this a connection that others in the world can attain?
commentary: The spiritual path is like climbing a great pillar that becomes impossibly thin, symbolizing a point where human effort is no longer enough. Just as the devotee faces failure and despair, God intervenes directly, lifting him to the goal. The path requires our effort, but its successful completion is purely an act of grace.

tamil: இங்கோர் மலையின் நடுவில் உயர்ந்த தம்பம் நணுக வே
ஏறிப் போகப் போக நூலின் இழைபோல் நுணுக வே
அங்கே திகைத்து நடுங்கும் போதென் நடுக்கம் நீக்கி யே
அதன்மேல் உயர்ந்த நிலையில் வைத்தாய் அடிமை ஆக்கி யே.
translit: iṅkōr malaiyiṉ naṭuvil uyarnta tampam naṇuka vē ēṟip pōkap pōka nūliṉ iḻaipōl nuṇuka vē aṅkē tikaittu naṭuṅkum pōteṉ naṭukkam nīkki yē ataṉmēl uyarnta nilaiyil vaittāy aṭimai ākki yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: As I approached a tall pillar in the middle of a mountain here, and as I climbed higher and higher, it grew as fine as a thread's filament. When I stood there bewildered and trembling, you removed my trembling, made me your devotee, and placed me in a high state upon it. What kind of connection is this that fits so well between you and me? Is this a connection that others in the world can attain?
commentary: This verse reinforces the idea that the spiritual path reaches a point of crisis where only God's help can save you. The climb leads to a state of helpless trembling, where the devotee's own power has run out. By accepting his status as God's devotee (aṭimai, servant), he opens himself to the grace that lifts him beyond his limits to the final state.

tamil: இரவில் பெரிய வெள்ளம் பரவி எங்கும் தயங்க வே
யானும் சிலரும் படகில் ஏறி யேம யங்க வே
விரவில் தனித்தங் கென்னை ஒருகல் மேட்டில் ஏற்றி யே
விண்ணில் உயர்ந்த மாடத் திருக்க விதித்தாய் போற்றி யே.
translit: iravil periya veḷḷam paravi eṅkum tayaṅka vē yāṉum cilarum paṭakil ēṟi yēma yaṅka vē viravil taṉittaṅ keṉṉai orukal mēṭṭil ēṟṟi yē viṇṇil uyarnta māṭat tirukka vitittāy pōṟṟi yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: At night, a great flood spread, causing confusion everywhere. As I and a few others boarded a boat and became distressed, you quickly singled me out, lifted me onto a rocky mound, and destined me to live in a mansion that towers to the sky. Praise be to you! What kind of connection is this that fits so well between you and me? Is this a connection that others in the world can attain?
commentary: The world is often a place of chaos and confusion, like a great flood at night where everyone is lost. In this powerful image, many people are adrift together in a boat, but divine grace intervenes to single out and save the devotee. This rescue is a personal and specific act of being lifted out of shared turmoil and placed in a state of supreme safety and peace.

tamil: மேலைப் பாற்சிவ கங்கை என்னுமோர் தீர்த்தம் தன்னை யே
மேவிப் படியில் தவறி நீரில் விழுந்த என்னை யே
ஏலத் துகிலும் உடம்பும் நனையா தெடுத்த தேஒன் றோ
எடுத்தென் கரத்தில் பொற்பூண் அணிந்த இறைவன் நீயன் றோ.
translit: mēlaip pāṟciva kaṅkai eṉṉumōr tīrttam taṉṉai yē mēvip paṭiyil tavaṟi nīril viḻunta eṉṉai yē ēlat tukilum uṭampum naṉaiyā teṭutta tēoṉ ṟō eṭutteṉ karattil poṟpūṇ aṇinta iṟaivaṉ nīyaṉ ṟō. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: When I went to the sacred water body called Sivaganga in the western part, slipped on the steps, and fell into the water, was it just that you lifted me out without my fine clothes or body getting wet? Are you not the Lord who then adorned my hand with a golden bracelet? What kind of connection is this that fits so well between you and me? Is this a connection that others in the world can attain?
commentary: Vallalar recounts an actual event: at the sacred tank called Sivaganga he slipped on the steps and fell into the water, and God lifted him out with neither his clothes nor his body wet. More than that, God then placed a golden bracelet on his hand. Grace does not only rescue; it honours and blesses.

tamil: என்ன துடலும் உயிரும்பொருளும் நின்ன தல்ல வோ
எந்தாய் இதனைப் பெறுக எனநான் இன்று சொல்ல வோ
சின்ன வயதில் என்னை ஆண்ட திறத்தை நினைக்கு தே
சிந்தை நினைக்கக் கண்ர் பெருக்கிஉடம்பை நனைக்கு தே.
translit: eṉṉa tuṭalum uyirumporuḷum niṉṉa talla vō entāy itaṉaip peṟuka eṉanāṉ iṉṟu colla vō ciṉṉa vayatil eṉṉai āṇṭa tiṟattai niṉaikku tē cintai niṉaikkak kaṇr perukkiuṭampai naṉaikku tē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: My father, are not my body, life, and wealth yours? Must I even say today, "Please accept them"? My mind recalls the way you took charge of me when I was young. As it remembers, tears stream down and drench my body.
commentary: Surrendering to God is the simple, heartfelt recognition that your body, life, and all you have already belong to him. Recalling God's protective grace from his youth, Vallalar is overwhelmed by the realization of a love that has always been in charge. The tears are a physical expression of this gratitude.

tamil: அப்பா நின்னை அன்றி எங்கும் அணைப்பார் இல்லை யே
அந்தோ நின்னை அன்றி எங்கும் அருள்வார் இல்லை யே
எப்பா லவர்க்கும் நின்னை அன்றி இறைமை இல்லை யே
எனக்கும் நின்மே லன்றி உலகில் இச்சை இல்லை யே.
translit: appā niṉṉai aṉṟi eṅkum aṇaippār illai yē antō niṉṉai aṉṟi eṅkum aruḷvār illai yē eppā lavarkkum niṉṉai aṉṟi iṟaimai illai yē eṉakkum niṉmē laṉṟi ulakil iccai illai yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Father, there is no one anywhere to embrace me but you. Alas, there is no one anywhere to bestow grace but you. For anyone, anywhere, there is no divinity other than you. And as for me, I have no desire in the world apart from you.
commentary: This is a statement of absolute and singular devotion. God is the highest being and the only source of comfort, grace, and divinity itself. Having realized this, Vallalar finds that all his worldly desires have dissolved, replaced by a single, all-consuming longing for God alone.

tamil: அரசே உன்னை அணைக்க எனக்குள் ஆசை பொங்கு தே
அணைப்போம் என்னும் உண்மை யால்என் ஆவி தங்கு தே
விரைசேர் பாதம் பிடிக்க என்கை விரைந்து நீளு தே
மேவிப் பிடித்துக் கொள்ளுந் தோறும் உவகை ஆளு தே.
translit: aracē uṉṉai aṇaikka eṉakkuḷ ācai poṅku tē aṇaippōm eṉṉum uṇmai yāleṉ āvi taṅku tē viraicēr pātam piṭikka eṉkai viraintu nīḷu tē mēvip piṭittuk koḷḷun tōṟum uvakai āḷu tē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O King, a desire to embrace you surges within me. My life endures because of the truth that we will embrace. My hands rush out to grasp your fragrant feet. Each time I approach and hold them, joy rules me.
commentary: Devotion here is expressed as a powerful, almost physical yearning for union with God. The promise of this future union is so real to Vallalar that it becomes the very reason he continues to live. He describes worship as an immediate, joyful act of reaching out and touching the divine.

tamil: தனிஎன்மேல்நீ வைத்த தயவு தாய்க்கும் இல்லை யே
தகும்ஐந் தொழிலும் வேண்டுந் தோறும் தருதல் வல்லை யே
வினவும் எனக்கென் உயிரைப் பார்க்க மிகவும் நல்லை யே
மிகவும் நான்செய் குற்றம் குறித்து விடுவாய் அல்லை யே.
translit: taṉieṉmēlnī vaitta tayavu tāykkum illai yē takumain toḻilum vēṇṭun tōṟum tarutal vallai yē viṉavum eṉakkeṉ uyiraip pārkka mikavum nallai yē mikavum nāṉcey kuṟṟam kuṟittu viṭuvāy allai yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: The singular kindness you have shown me, not even a mother possesses. You are skilled at bestowing the five proper cosmic functions (creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, and grace) whenever they are needed. To me who inquires, you are far dearer than my own life. You will not abandon me over the many wrongs I have committed.
commentary: Vallalar describes two aspects of God at once: the intimately personal and the supremely cosmic. The same God whose love is more tender and forgiving than a mother's is also the master of the five great cosmic powers that run the universe. This unique combination of ultimate power and unconditional personal mercy assures him that he is safe and will never be abandoned for his mistakes.

tamil: என்னை ஆண்ட வண்ணம் எண்ணில் உள்ளம் உருகு தே
என்னை விழுங்கி எங்கும் இன்ப வெள்ளம் பெருகு தே
உன்ன உன்ன மனமும் உயிரும் உடம்பும் இனிக்கு தே
உன்னோ டென்னை வேறென் றெண்ணில் மிகவும் பனிக்கு தே.
translit: eṉṉai āṇṭa vaṇṇam eṇṇil uḷḷam uruku tē eṉṉai viḻuṅki eṅkum iṉpa veḷḷam peruku tē uṉṉa uṉṉa maṉamum uyirum uṭampum iṉikku tē uṉṉō ṭeṉṉai vēṟeṉ ṟeṇṇil mikavum paṉikku tē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: When I reflect on the way you took charge of me, my heart melts. A flood of bliss swallows me and overflows everywhere. The more I think of you, the sweeter my mind, life, and body become. If I think of myself as separate from you, I tremble violently.
commentary: The practice of remembering God's presence in one's life has a powerful effect. It literally melts the heart, dissolving the sense of a hard, separate self, and floods the being with bliss. For Vallalar, union with God is a state of sweetness and joy, while the mere thought of being separate is a source of terror.

tamil: உன்பே ரருளை நினைக்குந் தோறும் உடம்பு பொடிக்கு தே
உண்டு பசிதீர்ந் தாற்போல் காதல் மிகவும் தடிக்கு தே
அன்பே அமையும் என்ற பெரியர் வார்த்தை போயிற் றே
அன்போர் அணுவும் இல்லா எனக்கிங் கருளல் ஆயிற் றே.
translit: uṉpē raruḷai niṉaikkun tōṟum uṭampu poṭikku tē uṇṭu pacitīrn tāṟpōl kātal mikavum taṭikku tē aṉpē amaiyum eṉṟa periyar vārttai pōyiṟ ṟē aṉpōr aṇuvum illā eṉakkiṅ karuḷal āyiṟ ṟē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Whenever I think of your great grace, my body tingles. Like satisfying hunger by eating, my love for you grows immense. The saying of the great ones, "Love alone is enough," has been disproven, for you have bestowed your grace here on me, who lacks even an atom of love.
commentary: This is a classic expression of devotional humility. He feels he has received God's grace without earning it, contrasting his own perceived lack of love with the immense gift he's been given. The old teaching says "love is the only requirement," but he feels he did not have even that, making the grace an act of pure, unearned compassion.

tamil: நினைக்க நினைக்கத் தித்திப் பெனது நினைவில் கொடுக்கு தே
நின்பால் அன்றிப் பிறர்பால் செல்ல நெஞ்சம் நடுக்கு தே
எனைத்துன் பொழித்தாட் கொண்ட நின்னை அன்னை என்ப னோ
எந்தாய் அன்பி லேன்நின் னடிக்கு முன்னை அன்ப னோ.
translit: niṉaikka niṉaikkat tittip peṉatu niṉaivil koṭukku tē niṉpāl aṉṟip piṟarpāl cella neñcam naṭukku tē eṉaittuṉ poḻittāṭ koṇṭa niṉṉai aṉṉai eṉpa ṉō entāy aṉpi lēṉniṉ ṉaṭikku muṉṉai aṉpa ṉō. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: The more I think of you, the more sweetness it brings to my mind. My heart trembles at the thought of going to anyone but you. You who dispelled my suffering and made me yours, shall I call you Mother? My Father, I am without love; am I some ancient devotee of your feet?
commentary: The sweetness of divine thought makes any other focus impossible. In his overwhelming gratitude, he struggles to find the right name for God, calling him both Mother and Father. He wonders aloud if his deep connection is a reward for some ancient devotion, since he feels so undeserving of it in this life.

tamil: உன்னை மறக்கில் எந்தாய் உயிர்என் உடம்பில் வாழு மோ
உன்பால் அன்றிப் பிறர்பால் என்றன் உள்ளம் சூழு மோ
என்னைக் கொடுக்க வாங்கிக் கொண்ட தென்ன கருதி யோ
எந்தாய் நின்னைக் கொடுக்க என்பால் இன்று வருதி யோ.
translit: uṉṉai maṟakkil entāy uyireṉ uṭampil vāḻu mō uṉpāl aṉṟip piṟarpāl eṉṟaṉ uḷḷam cūḻu mō eṉṉaik koṭukka vāṅkik koṇṭa teṉṉa karuti yō entāy niṉṉaik koṭukka eṉpāl iṉṟu varuti yō. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: My Father, if I were to forget you, would this life remain in my body? Would my heart ever turn its thoughts to anyone but you? When you accepted me as I gave myself, what did you have in mind? My Father, will you come to me today to give yourself?
commentary: Forgetting God would be like death itself; his entire being is oriented toward this one relationship. He poses a poignant question about the nature of surrender: he has given himself completely to God, but he asks when God will fully give Himself in return, completing the union.

tamil: நெடுநாள் முயன்றும் காண்டற் கரிய நிலையைக் காட்டி யே
நிறைந்தென் அகத்தும் புறத்தும் சூழ்ந்தாய் ஒளியை நாட்டி யே
நடுநா டியநின் அருளுக் கென்மேல் என்ன நாட்ட மோ
நாய்க்குத் தவிசிட் டனைநின் தனக்கிங் கிதுவோர் ஆட்ட மோ.
translit: neṭunāḷ muyaṉṟum kāṇṭaṟ kariya nilaiyaik kāṭṭi yē niṟainteṉ akattum puṟattum cūḻntāy oḷiyai nāṭṭi yē naṭunā ṭiyaniṉ aruḷuk keṉmēl eṉṉa nāṭṭa mō nāykkut taviciṭ ṭaṉainiṉ taṉakkiṅ kituvōr āṭṭa mō. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: You showed me the state that is so hard to attain even after long striving. Establishing your light, you filled and surrounded me, within and without. Your grace seeks impartiality, so what special interest does it have in me? You have given a throne to a dog; is this just a game to you?
commentary: He marvels at receiving a spiritual state that is normally unattainable, feeling it as a light that fills him completely. Using the powerful image of giving a throne to a dog, he expresses his sense of unworthiness. He asks God if this immense, unearned favor is some kind of divine play, unable to otherwise comprehend why he was chosen.

tamil: நாகா திபனும் அயனும் மாலும் நறுமு றென்ன வே
ஞான அமுதம் அளித்தாய் நானும் உண்டு துன்ன வே
சாகாக்கலையை எனக்குப் பயிற்றித் தந்த தயவை யே
சாற்றற் கரிது நினக்கென் கொடுப்ப தேதும் வியவை யே.
translit: nākā tipaṉum ayaṉum mālum naṟumu ṟeṉṉa vē ñāṉa amutam aḷittāy nāṉum uṇṭu tuṉṉa vē cākākkalaiyai eṉakkup payiṟṟit tanta tayavai yē cāṟṟaṟ karitu niṉakkeṉ koṭuppa tētum viyavai yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: While Indra, lord of the heavens, Ayan, and Māl grumbled in envy, you gave me the nectar of wisdom to consume, that I might draw near to you. The compassion you showed in teaching and giving me the art of immortality is impossible to describe. What could I give to you? That is a great wonder in itself.
commentary: The gift of grace he received is so extraordinary that even the great gods of the cosmos, Brahma and Vishnu, are portrayed as envious. Vallalar is saying that the state of immortal wisdom granted by God's direct compassion is higher than any status in the celestial hierarchy. This gift is so immense that the idea of giving anything in return seems impossible.

tamil: யாது கருதி என்னை ஆண்ட தைய ஐய வோ
யானுன் அடிப்பொற் றுணைகட் குவந்து தொழும்பு செய்ய வோ
ஓது கடவுட் கூட்டம் அனைத்தும் அடிமை அல்ல வோ
உடையாய் அவர்க்குள் எனையும் ஒருவன் என்று சொல்ல வோ.
translit: yātu karuti eṉṉai āṇṭa taiya aiya vō yāṉuṉ aṭippoṟ ṟuṇaikaṭ kuvantu toḻumpu ceyya vō ōtu kaṭavuṭ kūṭṭam aṉaittum aṭimai alla vō uṭaiyāy avarkkuḷ eṉaiyum oruvaṉ eṉṟu colla vō. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: With what purpose did you make me yours, O Father, O Lord? Was it so I would joyfully serve your pair of golden feet? Is not the entire assembly of celebrated gods your slave? O Master, was it to announce me as one among them? Between me and you.
commentary: Vallalar probes the mystery of why he was chosen by God. He wonders if it was just to add another servant to God's retinue, but he dismisses this, since even the gods themselves are God's servants. The verse is a heartfelt question about his own destiny, asking if God's plan is to elevate him, a humble soul, to the status of the divine beings.

tamil: தலையும் காலும் திரித்து நோக்கித் தருக்கி னேனை யே
தாங்கித் தெரித்த தயவை நினைக்கில் உருக்கு தூனை யே
புலையும் கொலையும் தவிர்ந்த நெறியில் புனிதர் மதிக்க வே
புகுவித் தாயை என்வாய் துடிப்ப தேத்தித் துதிக்க வே.
translit: talaiyum kālum tirittu nōkkit tarukki ṉēṉai yē tāṅkit teritta tayavai niṉaikkil urukku tūṉai yē pulaiyum kolaiyum tavirnta neṟiyil puṉitar matikka vē pukuvit tāyai eṉvāy tuṭippa tēttit tutikka vē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: I, who swaggered in pride, mistaking head for foot: when I think of the compassion that held me up and showed me the way, it melts my very flesh. You placed me on the path that shuns flesh-eating and murder, so that the holy esteem me. My mouth trembles as I praise and extol you for leading me in. Between me and you.
commentary: He remembers his past self, filled with pride, and is overcome with emotion at the thought of God's grace choosing him anyway. The path God placed him on is defined by the core ethical principle of shunning meat-eating and violence. This transformation from a flawed man to one respected by the pure is so great it leaves him trembling with gratitude.

tamil: தாயே எனக்குத் தயவு புரிந்த தருணத் தந்தை யே
தனியே நின்னை நினைக்கக் கிளர்வ தெனது சிந்தை யே
நாயேன் எண்ணம் அனைத்தும் முடித்துக் கொடுத்த பண்ப னே
நான்செய் தவத்தால் எனக்குக் கிடைத்த நல்ல நண்ப னே.
translit: tāyē eṉakkut tayavu purinta taruṇat tantai yē taṉiyē niṉṉai niṉaikkak kiḷarva teṉatu cintai yē nāyēṉ eṇṇam aṉaittum muṭittuk koṭutta paṇpa ṉē nāṉcey tavattāl eṉakkuk kiṭaitta nalla naṇpa ṉē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O Mother! O Father who graciously showed me compassion! When I think of you in solitude, my mind is stirred. O virtuous one who fulfilled every wish of this dog! O good friend, obtained by the penance I performed! Between me and you.
commentary: God is the most intimate of relations: a mother, a father, and a dear friend. This divine friend has fulfilled every desire of a man who sees himself as a "dog," showing the depth of God's personal compassion. Vallalar sees this friendship as the direct result of his spiritual efforts (tavam, or penance), a reward for his seeking.

tamil: ஏறா நிலையில் விரைந்து விரைந்திங் கென்னை ஏற்றி யே
இறங்கா திறங்கும் படிகள் முழுதும் எடுத்தாய் போற்றி யே
மாறாக் கருணை என்மேல் வைக்க வந்த தென்னை யோ
மதியி லேன்நின் அருட்குச் செய்த தவந்தான் முன்னை யோ.
translit: ēṟā nilaiyil viraintu viraintiṅ keṉṉai ēṟṟi yē iṟaṅkā tiṟaṅkum paṭikaḷ muḻutum eṭuttāy pōṟṟi yē māṟāk karuṇai eṉmēl vaikka vanta teṉṉai yō matiyi lēṉniṉ aruṭkuc ceyta tavantāṉ muṉṉai yō. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: You rushed to raise me to a state that cannot be climbed. Praise to you, for you removed all the steps of descent so I cannot come down! Why did you place your unfailing compassion on me? What previous penance did I, a witless one, perform to deserve your grace? Between me and you.
commentary: God has lifted him to a spiritual state so high it is normally impossible to reach, and has even removed the ladder so he cannot fall back down. This is the experience of irreversible grace. He is left wondering what he could have possibly done to merit such unceasing compassion, especially since he sees himself as witless.

tamil: இடமும் வலமும் இதுவென் றறியா திருந்த என்னை யே
எல்லாம் அறிவித் தருள்செய் கருணை என்னை என்னை யே
நடமும் நடஞ்செய் இடமும் எனக்கு நன்று காட்டி யே
நாயி னேனை வளர்க்கின் றாய்நல் லமுதம் ஊட்டி யே.
translit: iṭamum valamum ituveṉ ṟaṟiyā tirunta eṉṉai yē ellām aṟivit taruḷcey karuṇai eṉṉai eṉṉai yē naṭamum naṭañcey iṭamum eṉakku naṉṟu kāṭṭi yē nāyi ṉēṉai vaḷarkkiṉ ṟāynal lamutam ūṭṭi yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: I, who did not even know left from right, what is this grace, oh, what is this grace that has graciously taught me everything! You have clearly shown me the Dance and the place of the Dance, and you are nurturing this dog, feeding me good nectar. Between me and you.
commentary: From a state of complete ignorance, not even knowing left from right, he has been given total understanding through grace. This new awareness includes a direct vision of the cosmic Dance of God and the sacred space where it happens. He is now being nurtured with the sweet nectar of this divine wisdom.

tamil: விதுவும் கதிரும் இதுவென் றறியும் விளக்கம் இன்றி யே
விழித்து மயங்கி னேன்பால் பெரிய கருணை ஒன்றி யே
அதுவும் அதுவும் இதுவென் றெனக்குள் அறியக் காட்டி யே
அடிய னேனை வளர்க்கின் றாய்நல் லமுதம் ஊட்டி யே.
translit: vituvum katirum ituveṉ ṟaṟiyum viḷakkam iṉṟi yē viḻittu mayaṅki ṉēṉpāl periya karuṇai oṉṟi yē atuvum atuvum ituveṉ ṟeṉakkuḷ aṟiyak kāṭṭi yē aṭiya ṉēṉai vaḷarkkiṉ ṟāynal lamutam ūṭṭi yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Without the clarity to tell the moon from the sun, I stared in confusion. You united with great compassion for me, showed me within myself how “That and that are this,” and now you raise this slave, feeding me good ambrosia.
commentary: In his previous state of confusion, he could not even distinguish the sun from the moon, a metaphor for his inability to grasp fundamental spiritual realities. Grace intervened, showing him from within how the ultimate "That" and the immediate "this" are related. This unifying insight is the ambrosia that now sustains him.

tamil: இருளும் ஒளியும் வந்த வகையை எண்ணி எண்ணி யே
இரவும் பகலும் மயங்கி னேனை இனிது நண்ணி யே
அருளும் பொருளும் கொடுத்து மயக்கம் நீக்கிக் காட்டி யே
அன்பால் என்னை வளர்க்கின் றாய்நல் லமுதம் ஊட்டி யே.
translit: iruḷum oḷiyum vanta vakaiyai eṇṇi eṇṇi yē iravum pakalum mayaṅki ṉēṉai iṉitu naṇṇi yē aruḷum poruḷum koṭuttu mayakkam nīkkik kāṭṭi yē aṉpāl eṉṉai vaḷarkkiṉ ṟāynal lamutam ūṭṭi yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Pondering and pondering how darkness and light came to be, I was bewildered night and day. You approached me graciously, gave me grace and substance, dispelled my delusion, and showed me clearly. With love, you raise me, feeding me good ambrosia.
commentary: He was once trapped in intellectual confusion, endlessly trying to figure out the origins of darkness and light. Instead of a philosophical answer, God gave him a direct experience of grace (aruḷ) and substance (poruḷ). This loving gift ended his bewilderment, and it is this love that now nourishes him like sweet ambrosia.

tamil: அண்டத் தகத்தும் புறத்தும் உன்றன் ஆணை செல்லு தே
அவனே எல்லாம் வல்லான் என்று மறைகள் சொல்லு தே
பிண்டத் தகத்தும் புறத்தும் நிறைந்த பெரிய சோதி யே
பேயேன் அளவில் விளங்கு கின்ற தென்ன நீதி யே.
translit: aṇṭat takattum puṟattum uṉṟaṉ āṇai cellu tē avaṉē ellām vallāṉ eṉṟu maṟaikaḷ collu tē piṇṭat takattum puṟattum niṟainta periya cōti yē pēyēṉ aḷavil viḷaṅku kiṉṟa teṉṉa nīti yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Your command prevails inside and outside the cosmos. The Vedas declare, “He alone is all-powerful.” O great Jothi that fills the inside and outside of the physical body, by what justice do you shine in one as lowly as this ghoul?
commentary: The same infinite divine power that governs the entire cosmos (aṇṭam) also fills the individual human body (piṇṭam). Vallalar expresses his astonishment at this truth, which is affirmed by the ancient scriptures (maṟaikaḷ or Vedas). He refers to God as the great Jothi, or divine light, and is humbled that such an immense presence would choose to shine within someone who feels so lowly.

tamil: கருணா நிதிநின் தன்னைக் காணக் கண்கள் துடிக்கு தே
காண்போம் என்று நினைக்குந் தோறும் உடம்பு பொடிக்கு தே
அருள்நா டகஞ்செய் பதங்கள் பாடி ஆட விரைவ தே
ஆடும் பொதுவை நினைக்க நினைக்க நெஞ்சம் கரைவ தே.
translit: karuṇā nitiniṉ taṉṉaik kāṇak kaṇkaḷ tuṭikku tē kāṇpōm eṉṟu niṉaikkun tōṟum uṭampu poṭikku tē aruḷnā ṭakañcey pataṅkaḷ pāṭi āṭa viraiva tē āṭum potuvai niṉaikka niṉaikka neñcam karaiva tē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O treasury of compassion, my eyes tremble with longing to see you. Each time I think, “I will see you,” my body tingles all over. I rush to sing of and dance to the feet that perform the drama of grace. As I think and think of the common space where you dance, my heart melts.
commentary: The longing for God is described as an overwhelming, physical experience that causes the body to tremble and tingle. This yearning inspires joyful worship through song and dance. The focus of this devotion is the potu, the sacred "common space" where God performs the eternal dance of grace. Simply thinking of this divine space causes the devotee's heart to melt in love.

tamil: அருளார் சோதி என்னுள் விளங்க அளித்த காலத் தே
அடியேன் குறைகள் யாவும் தவிர்ந்த திந்த ஞாலத் தே
பொருளாய் எனையும் நினைக்க வந்த புதுமை என்னை யோ
பொன்னென் றைய மதிப்ப துதவாத் துரும்பு தன்னை யோ.
translit: aruḷār cōti eṉṉuḷ viḷaṅka aḷitta kālat tē aṭiyēṉ kuṟaikaḷ yāvum tavirnta tinta ñālat tē poruḷāy eṉaiyum niṉaikka vanta putumai eṉṉai yō poṉṉeṉ ṟaiya matippa tutavāt turumpu taṉṉai yō. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: The moment you granted that the grace-filled Jothi shine within me, all this slave's faults vanished in this world. What is this marvel, that you came to regard even me as a being of substance? It is as if you, my Lord, valued a useless piece of straw as gold.
commentary: The instant the divine grace-light, the Jothi, shines within, all of one's faults are erased. Vallalar marvels at this miracle, feeling that his Lord (aiya) has taken something he considered worthless, like a piece of straw, and treated it as precious gold. Grace freely gives the soul its worth.

tamil: எனக்குள் நீயும் உனக்குள் நானும்இருக்கும் தன்மை யே
இன்று காட்டிக் கலக்கம் தவிர்த்துக் கொடுத்தாய் நன்மை யே
தனக்குள் ளதுதன் தலைவர்க் குளதென் றறிஞர் சொல்வ தே
சரியென் றெண்ணி எனது மனது களித்து வெல்வ தே.
translit: eṉakkuḷ nīyum uṉakkuḷ nāṉumirukkum taṉmai yē iṉṟu kāṭṭik kalakkam tavirttuk koṭuttāy naṉmai yē taṉakkuḷ ḷatutaṉ talaivark kuḷateṉ ṟaṟiñar colva tē cariyeṉ ṟeṇṇi eṉatu maṉatu kaḷittu velva tē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: You revealed today the state of you being within me and I within you, dispelling my confusion and granting me goodness. My mind considers it true what the wise say: "What is mine is my Lord's." It rejoices and triumphs. Between you and me.
commentary: The ultimate spiritual realization is the dissolving of separation, the direct experience that you are inside God and God is inside you. This is a lived reality that ends all mental confusion and brings a deep sense of peace. The traditional wisdom of "what is mine is my Lord's" becomes a joyful truth, since the boundary between "mine" and "the Lord's" has disappeared.

tamil: கருணைப் பொதுவில் பெரிய சோதித் தருவில் கனித்த தே
கனித்த பெரிய தனித்த கனிஎன் கருத்துள் இனித்த தே
தருணத் துண்டு மகிழ்வுற் றேன்அம் மகிழ்ச்சி சொல்ல வே
தனித்துக் கரைந்த எனது கருத்தின் தரத்த தல்ல வே.
translit: karuṇaip potuvil periya cōtit taruvil kaṉitta tē kaṉitta periya taṉitta kaṉieṉ karuttuḷ iṉitta tē taruṇat tuṇṭu makiḻvuṟ ṟēṉam makiḻcci colla vē taṉittuk karainta eṉatu karuttiṉ taratta talla vē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: A fruit ripened on the great Jothi tree in the common expanse of Grace. That great, unique, ripened fruit sweetened my consciousness. I ate it at the opportune moment and rejoiced. To describe that joy is beyond the capacity of my mind, which has dissolved in solitude. Between you and me.
commentary: The experience of grace is like tasting a unique, sweet fruit that grows on the tree of divine light, or Jothi. This "fruit" is the direct taste of God's presence, a moment of perfect communion that floods the consciousness with sweetness. The resulting joy is so immense that it overwhelms the mind, which can only dissolve in the experience, leaving no capacity to describe it in words.

tamil: என்னா ருயிர்க்குத் துணைவ நின்னை நான்து திக்க வே
என்ன தவஞ்செய் தேன்முன் உலகு ளோர்ம திக்க வே
பொன்னார் புயனும் அயனும் பிறரும் பொருந்தல் அரிய தே
புலைய னேனுக் களித்த கருணை மிகவும் பெரிய தே.
translit: eṉṉā ruyirkkut tuṇaiva niṉṉai nāṉtu tikka vē eṉṉa tavañcey tēṉmuṉ ulaku ḷōrma tikka vē poṉṉār puyaṉum ayaṉum piṟarum poruntal ariya tē pulaiya ṉēṉuk kaḷitta karuṇai mikavum periya tē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O companion to my precious soul, what penance did I perform in the past that I now praise you, earning the world's esteem? It is a state difficult to attain for him of the golden shoulders, for Brahma, and for others. The grace you bestowed on me, a lowly one, is exceedingly great. Between you and me.
commentary: Vallalar expresses astonishment at the immensity of the grace he has received, feeling it is a gift far beyond what he, a self-described "lowly one," could ever deserve. He emphasizes how extraordinary this is by saying that even the great gods Vishnu and Brahma strive for this state and find it difficult to attain. His experience leads to a deeper humility and a sense of wonder at the boundless, unconditional nature of God's compassion.

tamil: என்கண் மணியுள் இருக்கும் தலைவ நின்னைக் காண வே
என்ன தவஞ்செய் தேன்முன் அயனும் அரியும் நாண வே
புன்கண் ஒழித்துத் தெள்ளா ரமுதம் புகட்டி என்னை யே
பொருளாய் எண்ணி வளர்க்கின் றாய்நீ எனக்கோர் அன்னை யே.
translit: eṉkaṇ maṇiyuḷ irukkum talaiva niṉṉaik kāṇa vē eṉṉa tavañcey tēṉmuṉ ayaṉum ariyum nāṇa vē puṉkaṇ oḻittut teḷḷā ramutam pukaṭṭi eṉṉai yē poruḷāy eṇṇi vaḷarkkiṉ ṟāynī eṉakkōr aṉṉai yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O Lord who dwells within the pupil of my eye, what penance did I perform before that I may now see you, putting Brahma and Vishnu to shame? You have eliminated my suffering, fed me clear and precious ambrosia, and, considering me a being of value, you nurture me like a mother. Between you and me.
commentary: God's presence is described as something incredibly intimate, as close as the light within one's own eye. This closeness is more than a feeling; it actively removes suffering and nourishes the soul with divine ambrosia, like a mother tenderly caring for her child. The grace received is so great that it seems to surpass the spiritual goals of even the highest gods, reinforcing the idea that this gift is given out of love.

tamil: அறிவி லேன்செய் குற்றம் அனைத்தும் பொறுத்த தன்றி யே
அமுதும் அளித்தாய் யார்செய் வார்கள் இந்த நன்றி யே
செறிவி லாத பொறியும் மனமும் செறிந்து நிற்க வே
செய்தாய் மேலும் தெரித்தாய் சாகாக் கல்வி கற்க வே.
translit: aṟivi lēṉcey kuṟṟam aṉaittum poṟutta taṉṟi yē amutum aḷittāy yārcey vārkaḷ inta naṉṟi yē ceṟivi lāta poṟiyum maṉamum ceṟintu niṟka vē ceytāy mēlum terittāy cākāk kalvi kaṟka vē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: You forgave all the faults I committed in my ignorance. You also gave me ambrosia. Who else performs such a benevolent act? You made my scattered senses and mind become focused and still. And beyond this, you revealed that I must learn the deathless art. Between you and me.
commentary: Divine grace is more than forgiveness; it is an active transformation. God pardons all past faults committed in ignorance and calms the restless mind, bringing the scattered senses into sharp focus. This inner stillness becomes the foundation for learning the ultimate secret: the "deathless science" of realizing an immortal state of being.

tamil: ஒருநா ழிகையில் யோக நிலையை உணர்த்தி மாலை யே
யோகப் பயனை முழுதும் அளித்தாய் மறுநாள் காலை யே
திருநாள் நிலையும் தீர்த்த நிலையும் தெய்வ நிலையு மே
சிறியேன் அறியக் காட்டித் தெரித்தாய் வேதக் கலையு மே.
translit: orunā ḻikaiyil yōka nilaiyai uṇartti mālai yē yōkap payaṉai muḻutum aḷittāy maṟunāḷ kālai yē tirunāḷ nilaiyum tīrtta nilaiyum teyva nilaiyu mē ciṟiyēṉ aṟiyak kāṭṭit terittāy vētak kalaiyu mē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: In a single nāḻikai one evening, you made me realize the state of yoga; by the next morning, you had granted its full benefit. For this lowly one to know, you showed and explained the nature of sacred festivals, holy waters, the divine state, and even the Vedic arts. This is between me and you.
commentary: Spiritual progress, which can take lifetimes of effort, is here shown as a gift bestowed with astonishing speed. The state of yoga (union with the divine) is realized in a single evening, with its full benefits granted by morning. A nāḻikai is a traditional unit of time, about 24 minutes. This shows that the inner meaning of all religious traditions was revealed to him directly, making external seeking unnecessary.

tamil: அண்டப் பரப்பின் திறங்கள் அனைத்தும்அறிய வேண்டி யே
ஆசைப் பட்ட தறிந்து தெரித்தாய் அறிவைத் தூண்டி யே
பிண்டத் துயிர்கள் பொருத்தும் வகையும்பிண்டம் தன்னை யே
பிரியும் வகையும் பிரியா வகையும்தெரித்தாய் பின்னை யே.
translit: aṇṭap parappiṉ tiṟaṅkaḷ aṉaittumaṟiya vēṇṭi yē ācaip paṭṭa taṟintu terittāy aṟivait tūṇṭi yē piṇṭat tuyirkaḷ poruttum vakaiyumpiṇṭam taṉṉai yē piriyum vakaiyum piriyā vakaiyumterittāy piṉṉai yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Knowing I longed to understand all the secrets of the cosmic expanse, you stimulated my intellect and explained them. You later explained the way souls are joined to bodies, the way they separate, and the way they remain inseparable. This is between me and you.
commentary: The deepest secrets of the universe are given directly by God. Sensing the soul's deep yearning for knowledge, the divine itself awakens the intellect and reveals everything. This includes the mysteries of how souls are joined to physical bodies (piṇṭam), how they leave the body at death, and how they need never leave it at all: the way of the deathless body.

tamil: வேதா கமங்கள் புகன்ற விரிவை ஒன்றொன் றாக வே
விளங்க விரைந்து தெரித்தாய் பயிலும் ஆசை போக வே
பூதா திகளைப் பொருத்தும் பகுதிப் பொருத்தம் முற்று மே
பொய்மை நீக்கிக் காணக் காட்டித் தெரித்தாய் மற்று மே.
translit: vētā kamaṅkaḷ pukaṉṟa virivai oṉṟoṉ ṟāka vē viḷaṅka viraintu terittāy payilum ācai pōka vē pūtā tikaḷaip poruttum pakutip poruttam muṟṟu mē poymai nīkkik kāṇak kāṭṭit terittāy maṟṟu mē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: One by one, you swiftly and clearly explained the vast teachings of the Vedas and Agamas until my desire to study them was satisfied. You also showed and explained the entire method of how the elements and their parts are joined together, so I could see it with all falsehood removed. This is between me and you.
commentary: True spiritual knowledge makes book-learning obsolete. Here, God reveals the entire meaning of the Vedas and Agamas (foundational scriptures) so perfectly that the need to study them simply dissolves. This direct perception extends to the very building blocks of reality, showing how the elements combine to form the world, free from any distortion or falsehood.

tamil: வள்ளால் உன்னைப் பாடப் பாட வாய்ம ணக்கு தே
வஞ்ச வினைகள் எனைவிட் டோடித் தலைவ ணக்கு தே
எள்ளா துனது புகழைக் கேட்கச் செவிந யக்கு தே
எந்தாய் தயவை எண்ணுந் தோறும் உளம்வி யக்கு தே.
translit: vaḷḷāl uṉṉaip pāṭap pāṭa vāyma ṇakku tē vañca viṉaikaḷ eṉaiviṭ ṭōṭit talaiva ṇakku tē eḷḷā tuṉatu pukaḻaik kēṭkac cevina yakku tē entāy tayavai eṇṇun tōṟum uḷamvi yakku tē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O generous one, as I sing of you again and again, my mouth becomes fragrant. Deceitful karmas flee from me, bowing their heads. My ears delight in hearing your glory without scorn. My father, every time I think of your grace, my heart marvels. This is between me and you.
commentary: The practice of devotion brings about real, tangible changes. Singing God's praises literally makes the mouth fragrant, while the negative effects of past actions (karmas) are driven away. This verse portrays worship as a force that actively purifies and transforms the devotee's entire being.

tamil: இறைவா நின்னைக் கனவி லேனும் யான்ம றப்ப னோ
எந்தாய் உலகத் தவர்கள் போல்நான் இனி இறப்ப னோ
மறைவா சகமும் பொருளும் பயனும் மதிக்கும் மதியி லே
வாய்க்கக் கருணை புரிந்து வைத்தாய் உயர்ந்த பதியி லே.
translit: iṟaivā niṉṉaik kaṉavi lēṉum yāṉma ṟappa ṉō entāy ulakat tavarkaḷ pōlnāṉ iṉi iṟappa ṉō maṟaivā cakamum poruḷum payaṉum matikkum matiyi lē vāykkak karuṇai purintu vaittāy uyarnta patiyi lē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O Lord, will I ever forget you, even in a dream? My father, will I now die like the people of this world? In the supreme state, you graciously established within my discerning intellect the sacred word, its meaning, and its fruit. This is between me and you.
commentary: Through grace, Vallalar has reached a state of constant remembrance of God. He asks rhetorically if he will now die an ordinary death, implying that the divine connection has granted him a state beyond mortality. God has placed the ultimate truth directly into his mind, transforming his very existence.

tamil: தலைவா எனக்குக் கருணை அமுதம் தரஇத் தலத்தி லே
தவம்செய் தேன்அத் தவமும் உன்றன் அருள்வ லத்தி லே
அலைவா ரிதியில் துரும்பு போல அயனும் மாலு மே
அலைய எனக்கே அளிக்கின் றாய்நீ மேலும் மேலு மே.
translit: talaivā eṉakkuk karuṇai amutam tara:it talatti lē tavamcey tēṉat tavamum uṉṟaṉ aruḷva latti lē alaivā ritiyil turumpu pōla ayaṉum mālu mē alaiya eṉakkē aḷikkiṉ ṟāynī mēlum mēlu mē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O Leader, I performed austerities in this place for you to give me the ambrosia of compassion, and that austerity itself was accomplished by the power of your Grace. While Brahma and Vishnu wander like specks of dust in the tossing ocean, you grant it to me alone, again and again.
commentary: Vallalar makes a powerful point about spiritual effort: any austerities he performed were accomplished only through the power of God's grace. He sees this grace as a rare gift, one that even the great gods Brahma and Vishnu are still striving for, highlighting its supreme value and his unique connection to the divine.

tamil: உடையாய் எனக்குப் புரிந்த தயவை உன்ன உன்ன வே
உடம்பு பூரிக் கின்ற தொளிர்பொன் மலைய தென்ன வே
தடையா தினிஉள் மூல மலத்தின் தடையும் போயிற் றே
சமய விகற்பம் எல்லாம் நீங்கிச் சமம தாயிற் றே.
translit: uṭaiyāy eṉakkup purinta tayavai uṉṉa uṉṉa vē uṭampu pūrik kiṉṟa toḷirpoṉ malaiya teṉṉa vē taṭaiyā tiṉiuḷ mūla malattiṉ taṭaiyum pōyiṟ ṟē camaya vikaṟpam ellām nīṅkic camama tāyiṟ ṟē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O my Lord, as I contemplate the kindness you have shown me, my body thrills like a shining golden mountain. The obstacle of the root impurity within is gone. All religious distinctions have ceased, and everything has become equal.
commentary: Contemplating divine grace has a tangible effect, making the body thrill with bliss. This contemplation removes the very root of spiritual ignorance, the ego-impurity known as mūla malam that keeps the soul feeling separate from God. Once this is gone, all religious divisions and arguments disappear, and a vision of pure equality emerges.

tamil: மயங்குந் தோறும் உள்ளும் புறத்தும் மயக்கம் நீக்கி யே
மகிழ்விக் கின்றாய் ஒருகால் ஊன்றி ஒருகால் தூக்கி யே
உயங்கு மலங்கள் ஐந்தும் பசையற் றொழிந்து வெந்த தே
உன்பே ரருட்பொற் சோதி வாய்க்குந் தருணம் வந்த தே.
translit: mayaṅkun tōṟum uḷḷum puṟattum mayakkam nīkki yē makiḻvik kiṉṟāy orukāl ūṉṟi orukāl tūkki yē uyaṅku malaṅkaḷ aintum pacaiyaṟ ṟoḻintu venta tē uṉpē raruṭpoṟ cōti vāykkun taruṇam vanta tē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Whenever I am confused, you remove the confusion within and without and make me joyful, planting one foot and lifting the other. The five vexing impurities have lost their substance and burned away. The moment to receive your great, gracious, golden light has arrived.
commentary: God's grace is a continuous process of removing confusion and bringing joy. The image of God "planting one foot and lifting the other" evokes the cosmic dance of Siva, a symbol of the dynamic power that both creates and dissolves, conceals and reveals. This divine action purifies the soul of its five core impurities, including ego, karma, and illusion. With this purification, the soul becomes ready for the ultimate experience of God as light.

tamil: எனக்கும் நின்னைப் போல நுதற்கண் ஈந்துமதனை யே
எரிப்பித் தாய்பின் எழுப்பிக் கொடுத்தாய் அருவ மதனை யே
சினக்குங் கூற்றை உதைப்பித் தொழித்துச் சிதைவு மாற்றி யே
தேவர் கற்பம் பலவும் காணச் செய்தாய் போற்றி யே.
translit: eṉakkum niṉṉaip pōla nutaṟkaṇ īntumataṉai yē erippit tāypiṉ eḻuppik koṭuttāy aruva mataṉai yē ciṉakkuṅ kūṟṟai utaippit toḻittuc citaivu māṟṟi yē tēvar kaṟpam palavum kāṇac ceytāy pōṟṟi yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Like yourself, you gave me a forehead eye and had me burn the god of desire. Then you had me resurrect him in a formless state. You made me kick away the angry god of death, ending decay, and made me witness many eons of the gods. Praise to you!
commentary: Vallalar claims an extraordinary union with God, in which he is given the very powers of Lord Siva. He reenacts mythical events in his own spiritual body: using a third eye of wisdom to burn away personal desire, then reviving it in a purified, formless state. He overcomes death itself, an echo of Siva's famous feat of kicking Yama, the god of death. This is seeing God and becoming a participant in God's divine play, transcending desire, death, and even time.

tamil: கள்ளம் அறியேன் நின்னால் கண்ட காட்சி ஒன்று மே
கருத்தில் உளது வேறோர் விடயம் காணேன் என்று மே
உள்ள துரைக்கின் றேன்நின் அடிமேல் ஆணை முன்னை யே
உள்ளே விளங்கிக் காண்கின் றாய்க்கிங் கொளிப்ப தென்னை யே.
translit: kaḷḷam aṟiyēṉ niṉṉāl kaṇṭa kāṭci oṉṟu mē karuttil uḷatu vēṟōr viṭayam kāṇēṉ eṉṟu mē uḷḷa turaikkiṉ ṟēṉniṉ aṭimēl āṇai muṉṉai yē uḷḷē viḷaṅkik kāṇkiṉ ṟāykkiṅ koḷippa teṉṉai yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: I know no deceit. The one vision I had from you is all that is in my thoughts; I never see any other thing. I am telling you what is in my heart, and I swear on your feet. You who perceive and understand what is within me, what is there to hide?
commentary: Speaking directly to God, Vallalar expresses a state of absolute sincerity. His mind is so filled with the divine vision he has received that nothing else can enter it. There is no need for complex prayers or hidden motives because God already knows his heart completely. It is a moment of pure, open-hearted devotion, where the soul stands naked and honest before its creator.

tamil: என்னை அடிமை கொண்டாய் நானும் நினக்கு நல்ல னோ
எல்லாம் வல்ல தலைவ நினக்கு நல்லன் அல்ல னோ
முன்னை வினைகள் அனைத்தும் நீக்கி அமுதம் ஊட்டி யே
மூவர்க் கரிய நிலையில் வைத்தாய் என்னை நாட்டி யே.
translit: eṉṉai aṭimai koṇṭāy nāṉum niṉakku nalla ṉō ellām valla talaiva niṉakku nallaṉ alla ṉō muṉṉai viṉaikaḷ aṉaittum nīkki amutam ūṭṭi yē mūvark kariya nilaiyil vaittāy eṉṉai nāṭṭi yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: You took me as your servant; am I worthy of you? O all-powerful Lord, am I not worthy of you? You removed all my past karmas, fed me ambrosia, and established me in a state rare even for the Three Gods.
commentary: This verse captures the overwhelming feeling of receiving grace. Vallalar oscillates between humility ("Am I worthy?") and confident joy ("Am I not worthy?"). The answer is that God himself has made him worthy by wiping away all karmas (the residue of past actions) and elevating him to a state of consciousness so high that it is rare even for the primary gods of the Hindu tradition. The worthiness comes from God's power.

tamil: சோதி மலையில் கண்டேன் நின்னைக் கண்க ளிக்க வே
துய்த்தேன் அமுதம் அகத்தும் புறத்தும் பரிம ளிக்க வே
ஓதி உணர்தற் கரிய பெரிய உணர்வை நண்ணி யே
translit: cōti malaiyil kaṇṭēṉ niṉṉaik kaṇka ḷikka vē tuyttēṉ amutam akattum puṟattum parima ḷikka vē ōti uṇartaṟ kariya periya uṇarvai naṇṇi yē ōtā taṉaittumuṇarkiṉṟēṉniṉ aruḷai eṇṇi yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: I saw you on the mountain of light, a joy for my eyes. I consumed the ambrosia as it filled me inside and out. Attaining the great consciousness that is difficult to grasp even through study, I now understand all things without being taught, just by contemplating Your grace.
commentary: The highest spiritual truth is found in direct experience. Vallalar describes a vision of God as Jothi, or pure Light, and an inner state of bliss that filled him completely. This encounter gave him an understanding beyond scholarly learning. Grace itself has become his teacher.

tamil: ஏழு நிலைகள் ஓங்கும் தெய்வ மாடம் ஒன்றி லே
ஏற்றிக் களிக்க வைத்தாய் அதன்மேல் இலங்கு குன்றி லே
வாழும் பரிசு கவிக்கும் குடையும் மதிக்கும் தூசு மே
மகிழ்ந்து கொடுத்துப் பின்னும் கொடுத்தாய் மணிப்பொற் காசு மே.
translit: ēḻu nilaikaḷ ōṅkum teyva māṭam oṉṟi lē ēṟṟik kaḷikka vaittāy ataṉmēl ilaṅku kuṉṟi lē vāḻum paricu kavikkum kuṭaiyum matikkum tūcu mē makiḻntu koṭuttup piṉṉum koṭuttāy maṇippoṟ kācu mē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: You raised me into a towering, seven-storied divine mansion and made me rejoice. On the shining peak above it, you gave me the gift of dwelling there, a royal canopy, and esteemed garments; rejoicing, you gave me even more: gems and gold coins.
commentary: This verse uses rich imagery to describe spiritual attainment. The "seven-storied divine mansion" represents ascending planes of consciousness, a climb into divine awareness. The gifts of a canopy, fine clothes, and treasures are metaphors for the honor, dignity, and spiritual wealth that God bestows upon the soul that reaches this peak.

tamil: இந்த உலகில் உள்ளார் பலரும் மிகவும் நன்மை யே
என்பால் செய்ய வைத்தாய் இதுநின் அருளின் தன்மை யே
அந்த உலகில் உள்ளார் பலரும் என்னை நோக்கி யே
அப்பா வாழி எனவும் புரிந்தாய் அடிமை யாக்கி யே.
translit: inta ulakil uḷḷār palarum mikavum naṉmai yē eṉpāl ceyya vaittāy ituniṉ aruḷiṉ taṉmai yē anta ulakil uḷḷār palarum eṉṉai nōkki yē appā vāḻi eṉavum purintāy aṭimai yākki yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: You made many people in this world do great good for me; this is the nature of Your grace. And having made me your servant, you also caused many in the other world to look at me and exclaim, “Father, may you live long!”
commentary: Grace is more than an internal feeling; it reshapes one's entire reality. Vallalar notes that God's grace has made people on Earth treat him with kindness and has earned him the reverence of beings in heavenly realms. His spiritual status is recognized by both humans and divine beings.

tamil: அழியாக் கருணை அமுத வடிவின் ஓங்கும் சோதி யே
அரசே எனக்குள் விளங்கும் ஆதி யாம்அ னாதி யே
ஒழியாத் துயரை ஒழித்த பெரிய கருணை யாள னே
ஒன்றாய் ஒன்றில் உபய மாகி ஒளிரும் தாள னே.
translit: aḻiyāk karuṇai amuta vaṭiviṉ ōṅkum cōti yē aracē eṉakkuḷ viḷaṅkum āti yāma ṉāti yē oḻiyāt tuyarai oḻitta periya karuṇai yāḷa ṉē oṉṟāy oṉṟil upaya māki oḷirum tāḷa ṉē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O soaring Light in the form of immortal, compassionate ambrosia! O King! O Beginningless Primal One who shines within me! O great, compassionate One who ended my ceaseless sorrow! O One with shining feet, who, as the One, becomes two within the One!
commentary: This verse is a hymn of praise, listing the essential qualities of God. God is the immortal Light (Jothi), the compassionate king, the timeless presence within, and the one who ends all suffering. The final line points to the mystery of how the single, absolute Divine manifests as both active power and silent consciousness while remaining unified.

tamil: பாலும் தேனும் கலந்த தென்ன என்னுள் இனிக்க வே
பரம ஞான அமுதம் அளிக்கின் றாய்த னிக்க வே
ஏலும் உயிர்கள் எல்லாம் நினக்குப் பொதுவ தென்ப ரே
இன்று நோக்கி ஓர வாரன் என்பர் அன்ப ரே.
translit: pālum tēṉum kalanta teṉṉa eṉṉuḷ iṉikka vē parama ñāṉa amutam aḷikkiṉ ṟāyta ṉikka vē ēlum uyirkaḷ ellām niṉakkup potuva teṉpa rē iṉṟu nōkki ōra vāraṉ eṉpar aṉpa rē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: You sweeten my inner being like a blend of milk and honey; you alone give me the nectar of supreme wisdom. They say all souls are equal to you, yet your devotees will say that today you look upon me with partiality.
commentary: The gift of divine wisdom feels intensely personal and sweet, like a blend of milk and honey. While it is understood that God's grace is available to all beings equally, Vallalar's experience is so rich that he feels uniquely singled out. He imagines his devotees remarking that God, who is meant to be impartial, seems to be showing him special favor today.

tamil: ஐயா நான்செய் பிழைகள் ஏழு கடலில் பெரிய தே
அனைத்தும் பொறுத்த தயவு பிறருக் கரிய தரிய தே
மெய்யா நீசெய் உதவி ஒருகைம் மாறு வேண்டு மே
வேண்டா தென்ன அறிந்தும் எனக்குள் ஆசை தூண்டு மே.
translit: aiyā nāṉcey piḻaikaḷ ēḻu kaṭalil periya tē aṉaittum poṟutta tayavu piṟaruk kariya tariya tē meyyā nīcey utavi orukaim māṟu vēṇṭu mē vēṇṭā teṉṉa aṟintum eṉakkuḷ ācai tūṇṭu mē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Oh master, the mistakes I have made are larger than the seven seas; the grace you showed in forgiving them all is rare, truly rare, for others to receive. Truly, the help you have given requires something in return, and though I know you want nothing, the desire to give it stirs within me.
commentary: Acknowledging his past failings as being vaster than the oceans, Vallalar is stunned by the depth of God's forgiveness, a grace he feels is rarely given to others. This overwhelming love awakens a powerful, heartfelt desire to give something in return. He knows that the Divine needs nothing, yet his heart insists on finding a way to express its gratitude for a gift so immense.

tamil: பூத வெளியின் நடமும் பகுதி வெளியின் ஆட்ட மும்
போக வெளியில் கூத்தும் யோக வெளியுள் ஆட்ட மும்
நாத வெளியில் குனிப்பும் பரம நாத நடமு மே
நன்று காட்டிக் கொடுத்தாய் என்றும் நலியாத் திடமு மே.
translit: pūta veḷiyiṉ naṭamum pakuti veḷiyiṉ āṭṭa mum pōka veḷiyil kūttum yōka veḷiyuḷ āṭṭa mum nāta veḷiyil kuṉippum parama nāta naṭamu mē naṉṟu kāṭṭik koṭuttāy eṉṟum naliyāt tiṭamu mē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: The dance in the elemental expanse, the performance in the expanse of primordial matter, the revelry in the expanse of experience, the performance in the expanse of yoga, the bending dance in the expanse of sound, and the dance of the supreme sound, you revealed them all to me so well, and gave me strength that never falters.
commentary: God has shown Vallalar the dance at every level of existence: in the expanse of the elements, of primordial matter, of experience, of yoga, of sound, and of the supreme sound beyond it. He speaks of them as dances he was shown. Having seen them, he received a strength that never fails.

tamil: எட்டும் இரண்டும்இதுஎன் றெனக்குச் சுட்டிக் காட்டி யே
எட்டா நிலையில் இருக்கப் புரிந்தாய் இட்டுக் கூட்டி யே
துட்ட வினையைத் தீர்த்து ஞானச் சுடருள் ளேற்றி யே
தூண்டா தென்றும் விளங்க வைத்தாய் உண்மை சாற்றி யே.
translit: eṭṭum iraṇṭumitueṉ ṟeṉakkuc cuṭṭik kāṭṭi yē eṭṭā nilaiyil irukkap purintāy iṭṭuk kūṭṭi yē tuṭṭa viṉaiyait tīrttu ñāṉac cuṭaruḷ ḷēṟṟi yē tūṇṭā teṉṟum viḷaṅka vaittāy uṇmai cāṟṟi yē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: Pointing out to me, "This is the eight and the two," you brought me together and made me exist in a state beyond reach. You resolved my wicked karma, placed me within the flame of wisdom, and by speaking the truth, you made me shine forever without needing to be trimmed.
commentary: God has revealed a core mystical secret, symbolized here by the code "the eight and the two," which often alludes to the sacred sounds that form the mantra Om. This revelation has purified his past karma and ignited an inner flame of wisdom that now burns steadily on its own, a constant and self-sustaining light.

tamil: அருளாம் பெரிய வெளிக்குள் சோதி வடிவ னாகி யே
அரசு செலுத்தும் தனித்த தலைமைப் பரம யோகி யே
பொருளாய் எனையும் உளங்கொண் டளித்த புனித நாத னே
போற்று நாத முடிவில் நடஞ்செய் கமல பாத னே.
translit: aruḷām periya veḷikkuḷ cōti vaṭiva ṉāki yē aracu celuttum taṉitta talaimaip parama yōki yē poruḷāy eṉaiyum uḷaṅkoṇ ṭaḷitta puṉita nāta ṉē pōṟṟu nāta muṭivil naṭañcey kamala pāta ṉē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
translation: O supreme Yogi, the solitary head who, having taken the form of light, rules within the great expanse of grace! O holy Lord, who considered me a worthy object and graciously accepted me! O you with lotus feet that dance at the praised culmination of sound!
commentary: God is addressed here as the ultimate spiritual master (parama yōki), a being of pure light who presides over the universe from a vast world of grace. Vallalar marvels that this supreme being would consider him worthy of attention. The divine is also pictured as a dancer whose performance takes place at the very source of all cosmic sound (nāta).

tamil: உருவும் அருவும் உபய நிலையும் உடைய நித்த னே
உயிருள் நிறைந்த தலைவ எல்லாம் வல்ல சித்த னே
மருவும் துரிய வரையுள் நிறைந்து வயங்கும் பரம மே
மன்றில் பரமா னந்த நடஞ்செய் கின்ற பிரம மே.
translit: uruvum aruvum upaya nilaiyum uṭaiya nitta ṉē uyiruḷ niṟainta talaiva ellām valla citta ṉē maruvum turiya varaiyuḷ niṟaintu vayaṅkum parama mē maṉṟil paramā ṉanta naṭañcey kiṉṟa pirama mē. eṉakkum uṉakkum
