translation: I know nothing of deceit; come dance, come dance. You have taken me by the hand and joined with me; come dance with me, come dance. I am speaking what is truly in my heart; come dance, come dance. My desire for you is surging; come dance, come dance. I am not one to be cast away; come dance with me here, come dance. If you delay even a moment, I cannot bear it; come dance, come dance. You ended all scorn and took me to rule me; come dance, come dance. My Lord, come dance, come dance. Come dance, come dance.
commentary: Here the soul emphasizes its own sincerity and transparency. There is no deceit, only the raw truth of a heart overflowing with desire for God. The plea becomes even more intense, with the speaker confessing that even a moment's delay in this union is unbearable. This verse captures the vulnerability and impatience of a love that has reached its boiling point.

tamil: என்னுடைய நாயகரே ஆடவா ரீர். ஆடவா ரீர்
translit: naccukiṉṟēṉ niccaliṅkē āṭavā rīr nāṇamaccam viṭṭēṉeṉṉō ṭāṭavā rīr viccaiyelām tantukaḷit tāṭavā rīr viyanturaitta taruṇamitē āṭavā rīr eccukamum ākiniṉṟīr āṭavā rīr ellāmcey vallavarē āṭavā rīr. iccaimaya māyiruntēṉ āṭavā rīr eṉṉuṭaiya nāyakarē āṭavā rīr. āṭavā rīr
translation: I desire you constantly, come dance. I have abandoned shame and fear, come dance with me. Granting all mystic arts, come dance joyfully. This is the wondrous moment I spoke of, come dance. You who have become every pleasure, come dance. O all-powerful one who does everything, come dance. I am consumed by desire, come dance. My Lord, come dance. Come, dance.
commentary: This verse marks a peak of devotional abandon. The soul has cast off all social restraints like shame and fear, existing in a state of pure, constant desire for God. Union with God brings spiritual release and mystic powers (viccai) and access to every form of pleasure, because God is their ultimate source. The speaker is completely "consumed by desire," ready for the final, joyful dance of merging.

translit: eṉuyiruk kuyirāṉīr āṭavā rīr eṉaṟivuk kaṟivāṉīr āṭavā rīr eṉṉuṭaieṉ piṟkalantīr āṭavā rīr eṉṉuṭaiya:uḷ ḷattiruntīr āṭavā rīr eṉurimait tāyaṉaiyīr āṭavā rīr eṉatutaṉit tantaiyarē āṭavā rīr eṉorumaic caṟkuruvē āṭavā rīr eṉṉuṭaiya nāyakarē āṭavā rīr.
translation: You are the life of my life, come dance. You are the consciousness of my consciousness, come dance. You have mingled with my very bones, come dance. You dwell within my heart, come dance. You who are like my very own mother, come dance. My one and only father, come dance. My one true guru, come dance. My Lord, come dance.
commentary: God is the very essence of one's own existence: the life within our life, the consciousness behind our consciousness. Vallalar experiences this divine presence at every level, from the physical body ("mingled with my very bones") to the most essential human relationships of mother, father, and true spiritual guide (satguru). All love and all reality are found in the one Lord.

translit: āṭavā rīr eṉṉō ṭāṭavā rīr ampalattil āṭukiṉṟīr āṭavā rīr.
translation: Come, dance, with me come dance. You who dance in the Ambalam, come dance.
commentary: The Ambalam is the sacred space of consciousness where God performs the cosmic dance that animates the universe. By inviting the God who dances there to dance with him personally, Vallalar asks for that universal, divine energy to merge with his own individual being, transforming worship from observation into participation.

sections.title: Play the Ball Game, My Friend

translit: āṭēṭi pantu āṭēṭi pantu āṭēṭi pantu āṭēṭi pantu.
translation: Play the ball game, my friend, play the ball game! Play the ball game, my friend, play the ball game!
commentary: This simple refrain establishes the poem's central theme of playfulness and joy. The repeated invitation to play the ball game sets a tone of exuberant celebration, framing the spiritual life as a delightful interaction with the Divine. The word Kaṇṇikaḷ notes the poetic form, which is a series of couplets.

translit: vāḻieṉ tōḻieṉ vārttaikēḷ eṉṟum maraṇamil lāvaram nāṉpeṟṟuk koṇṭēṉ cūḻiyaṟ ceñcuṭar tōṟṟuṟu kīḻpāl tūytticai nōkkiṉēṉ cīrttikaḻ citti ūḻitō ṟūḻiniṉ ṟāṭuvaṉ nīyum uṉṉuti yēliṅkē maṉṉaru ḷāṇai āḻi karattaṇin tāṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi
translation: Blessings to you, my friend, listen to my words. I have received the boon of never dying. I looked toward the pure eastern direction, where the magnificent red flame appears, and achieved glorious siddhi. I will stand and dance for eon after eon. If you also wish for this, by the King's command of grace, wear the ring on your hand and play the ball game. Seeing the ArutPerunJothi, play the ball game, my friend.
commentary: The speaker announces a staggering achievement: she has received the boon of immortality. She attained this by turning to the east, the direction of new beginnings, and receiving a spiritual attainment, or siddhi. The invitation to her friend is to join in this immortal life, which is described as a dance of joy in the presence of the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light).

translit: icaiyāmal pōṉavar ellārum nāṇa iṟavāp peruvaram yāṉpeṟṟuk koṇṭēṉ vacaiyātum illāta mēṟṟicai nōkki vantēṉeṉ tōḻinī vāḻikāṇ vēṟu nacaiyātē eṉṉuṭai naṇpatu vēṇṭil naṉmārkka māmcutta caṉmārkkam taṉṉil acaiyāmal niṉṟaṅkē āṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi
translation: To the shame of all who disagreed and departed, I have received the great boon of immortality. I came facing the flawless western direction, my friend, may you flourish! Desire nothing else. If you want my friendship, stand unswervingly in the good path, the Suddha Sanmarkkam, and there, play the ball game. Seeing the ArutPerunJothi, play the ball game, my friend.
commentary: Having achieved immortality, the speaker now addresses those who disbelieved her. Her attainment is a vindication of her path, the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure True Path). She offers her friendship, but with a condition: her friend must abandon all other desires and commit completely to this one path.

translit: iṉpālē ulakattār ellārum kāṇa iṟavāp peruvaram yāṉpeṟṟuk koṇṭēṉ teṉpālē nōkkiṉēṉ cittāṭu kiṉṟa tirunāḷ itutoṭṭuc cērntatu tōḻi tuṉpālē acaintatu nīkkieṉ ṉōṭē cuttacaṉ mārkkattil ottava ḷāki aṉpālē aṟivālē āṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi
translation: So that all the people of the world can joyfully see, I have received the great boon of immortality. I looked to the south, my friend. From this day forward, the holy day of performing siddhis has come. Cast aside the unsteadiness caused by suffering, become one with me in the Suddha Sanmarkkam, and with love and wisdom, play the ball game. Seeing the ArutPerunJothi, play the ball game, my friend.
commentary: Immortality is a truth to be joyfully shown to the whole world. Facing south, the speaker declares that from this day the holy time of performing siddhis has arrived. The path requires leaving suffering behind and joining her as an equal in the Suddha Sanmarkkam, guided by love and wisdom.

translit: catumaṟaiākama cāttiram ellām cantaip paṭippunam contap paṭippō vituneṟi cuttacaṉ mārkkattil cākā vittaiyaik kaṟṟaṉaṉ uttaram eṉumōr potuvaḷar ticainōkki vantaṉaṉ eṉṟum poṉṟāmai vēṇṭiṭil eṉtōḻi nītāṉ atuitu eṉṉāmal āṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi
translation: Are the four Vedas, the Agamas, and all the Shastras anything but marketplace learning? Is that our own true learning? In the clear path of the Suddha Sanmarkkam, I have mastered the science of not dying. I came facing the direction of the north, a space of universal growth. My friend, if you truly desire never to perish, then without wavering over 'this' or 'that', play the ball game. Seeing the ArutPerunJothi, play the ball game, my friend.
commentary: This verse makes a radical claim, setting aside the most revered scriptures of Hinduism: the Vedas, Agamas, and Shastras. Vallalar calls them "marketplace learning," secondhand knowledge that is not one's own. True, personal learning is the "science of not dying," which is taught only in the Suddha Sanmarkkam. The final plea is for the friend to stop hesitating between different paths and commit to this one way to achieve eternal life.

translit: tappālē cakattavar cāvē tuṇintār tāmuḷam nāṇanāṉ cātalait tavirttē eppālum ekkālum iruttalē peṟṟēṉ eṉtōḻi vāḻinī eṉṉoṭu kūṭi tuppālē viḷaṅkiya cuttacaṉ mārkkac cōtieṉ ṟōtiya vītiyai viṭṭē appālē pōkāmal āṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi
translation: Through error, the people of the world have chosen death. To make them feel ashamed in their hearts, I have avoided dying and have received the state of existing everywhere, for all time. My friend, may you live long! Join with me and, without straying from the path proclaimed as the Jothi of the powerfully radiant Suddha Sanmarkkam, do not go beyond it. Play ball, O friend; having seen the Vast Grace-Light, play ball.
commentary: Vallalar’s immortality is a deliberate lesson for a world that has mistakenly accepted death as inevitable. His achievement is meant to make people feel ashamed for giving up, proving that a deathless life is possible. This is the goal of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (Pure True Path), which is the way of the divine Jothi (Light). He urges his companion to stay firmly on this path without deviation.

translit: veṅkēta maraṇattai viṭuvittu viṭṭēṉ viccaie lāmkaṟṟeṉ iccaiyiṉ vaṇṇam eṅkēyum āṭutaṟ keytiṉēṉ tōḻi eṉmoḻi cattiyam eṉṉōṭum kūṭi iṅkē kaḷippatu naṉṟinta ulakō ētak kuḻiyil iḻukkum ataṉāl aṅkēpā rātēnī āṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi
translation: I have freed myself from cruel, grievous death. I have learned all the supernatural arts and have attained the ability to perform anywhere according to my will, O friend. My words are truth. It is good to rejoice with me here. This world, however, will pull you into a pit of ruin. Therefore, do not look there. Play ball, O friend; having seen the Vast Grace-Light, play ball.
commentary: Conquering death has also granted him supernatural abilities, allowing him to act freely anywhere in creation. He invites his friend to share in this joyous state, but with a strong warning: the ordinary world is a trap that will pull a person down into ruin. The true celebration is spiritual, and requires turning one's gaze away from the world's empty promises.

translit: civamē poruḷeṉ ṟaṟivāl aṟintēṉ cettārai mīṭkiṉṟa tiṇmaiyaip peṟṟēṉ uvamēyam illāta orunilai taṉṉil oṉṟiraṇ ṭeṉṉāta uṇmaiyil niṉṟēṉ tavamē purikiṉṟār ellārum kāṇat tayavāl aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ kayavātē tōḻi avamēpō kāteṉṉō ṭāṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi
translation: Through Gnosis, I have known that Sivam is the ultimate substance. I have received the firm power to resurrect the dead. I stand in the truth that cannot be called one or two, a state without comparison. So that all who perform austerities may see, I call you out of compassion. Do not falter, O friend. Do not let this go to waste; play ball with me. Having seen the Vast Grace-Light, play ball.
commentary: Direct spiritual knowledge, or Gnosis, has revealed that Sivam (the ultimate Divine Principle) is the sole reality. This supreme understanding has conferred astonishing powers, including the ability to resurrect the dead, and has established him in a state beyond all comparison or duality. His invitation to others is an act of pure compassion, an urgent call to all spiritual seekers not to let this chance for transformation pass by.

translit: tuñcāta nilaioṉṟu cuttacaṉ mārkkac cūḻalil uṇṭatu collaḷa vaṉṟē eñcāta aruḷālē yāṉpeṟṟuk koṇṭēṉ iṟantārai ellām eḻupputal vallēṉ viñcāta aṟivālē tōḻinī iṅkē vētucey maraṇattuk ketuceyvō meṉṟē añcāmal eṉṉōṭē āṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi
translation: There is a deathless state within the sphere of the Suddha Sanmarkkam; it is beyond words. Through unfailing grace, I have received it. I am able to raise all who have died. O friend, instead of being afraid with your limited knowledge, wondering, "What can we do about this vexing death?", play ball with me. Having seen the Vast Grace-Light, play ball.
commentary: A deathless state, which is beyond the reach of words, exists within the Suddha Sanmarkkam. Attained through pure grace, it grants the power to overcome death entirely, even to the point of raising the dead. This reality stands in stark contrast to the fear and powerlessness most people feel, which comes from limited, worldly knowledge. The invitation is to stop worrying about death and step into this new, fearless existence.

translit: īramum aṉpumkoṇ ṭiṉṉaruḷ peṟṟēṉ eṉmārkkam iṟavāta caṉmārkkam tōḻi kāramum mikupuḷic cāramum tuvarppum kaippōṭē uppōṭē kacappōṭē kūṭṭi ūramu tuṇṭunī oḻiyātē antō ūḻitō ṟūḻiyum ulavāmai nalkum āramu tuṇṭeṉṉō ṭāṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi
translation: With compassion and love, I have received sweet grace. My path is the deathless Sanmarkkam, O friend. Alas, do not perish by eating the world's food, a combination of pungent, excessively sour, astringent, bitter, salty, and acrid tastes. There is a rare ambrosia that grants imperishability through eon after eon. Partake of it and play ball with me. Having seen the Vast Grace-Light, play ball.
commentary: This verse contrasts two kinds of nourishment: the food of the world and the "ambrosia" of divine grace. The six tastes of ordinary food represent all worldly experiences and emotional states, which bind us to a body that perishes. He urges us to turn instead to a spiritual nectar, received through compassion and love, that grants an imperishable life. The invitation to "play ball" is a call to feast on this eternal sustenance.

translit: tuticeyum muttarum cittarum kāṇac cuttacaṉ mārkkattil uttama ñāṉap paticeyum cittikaḷ paṟpala vākap pāriṭai vāṉiṭaip paṟpala kālam viticeyap peṟṟaṉaṉ iṉṟutoṭ ṭeṉṟum meyyaruṭ cōtiyāl viḷaivippaṉ nīav aticayam pārkkalām āṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu. āṭēṭi āṭēṭi pantu āṭēṭi pantu aruṭperuñ cōtikaṇ ṭāṭēṭi pantu.
translation: Witnessed by praising muttars and siddhars, I have received the power to enact, for many ages on earth and in the sky, the numerous siddhis that establish the supreme seat of wisdom in the Suddha Sanmarkkam. From this day forward, forever, I will bring them about through the True Grace-Light. You can watch that wonder. Play ball, O girl, play ball! Having seen the Vast Grace-Light, play ball! Play ball, play ball, O girl, play ball! Having seen the Vast Grace-Light, play ball!
commentary: The speaker makes a public declaration that he has been granted immense powers, known as siddhis (supernatural accomplishments). This is not a secret; he states it is witnessed by siddhars (perfected masters) and muttars (liberated souls). The purpose of these powers is to demonstrate and establish the wisdom of the Suddha Sanmarkkam (Pure Path) for all to see. The invitation to "watch that wonder" turns this cosmic claim into a personal call to witness a new, miraculous reality.

translit: pūvāma lēnitam kāytta iṭattum pūvār malarkoṇṭu pantāṭā niṉṟēṉ cāvā varamtantu vāḻvāyō pantē cāvāmal eṉṉoṭu vīḻvāyō pantē.
translation: At the place that fruits daily without ever flowering, I am playing ball with a flower that does not fade. O ball, will you live, granting the boon of deathlessness? O ball, will you fall with me, without dying?
commentary: This verse uses beautiful paradoxes to describe the spiritual life. The "place that fruits daily without ever flowering" is a state of grace where divine results manifest instantly, without the usual stages of effort. The "flower that does not fade" is the immortal soul itself. The final questions to the ball, a symbol for the soul, are a meditation on a life where even "falling" is part of a joyful, deathless game.
NOTES
Note 335

tamil: சதுர்மறை - பொ. சு., ச. மு. க.
translit: caturmaṟai - po. cu., ca. mu. ka.
translation: caturmaṟai — reading of the Po. Su. and S. Mu. Ka. Editions.

translit: ñāṉa maruntim maruntu - cukam nalkiya ciṟcapā nāta maruntu.
translation: This medicine is the medicine of gnosis, the medicine of the Lord of the Chit Sabhai who granted bliss.
commentary: The cure for all suffering is ñāṉam, or direct spiritual knowledge. This divine medicine is an experience of God, who is the Lord of the Chit Sabhai, the universal Hall of Consciousness.

translit: aruṭperuñ cōti maruntu - eṉṉai aintoḻil ceytaṟ kaḷitta maruntu poruṭperum pōka maruntu - eṉṉaip puṟattum akattum puṇarnta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: It is the medicine of the Vast Grace-Light, the medicine bestowed on me to perform the five cosmic functions. It is the medicine of great, substantive bliss, the medicine that united with me both outwardly and inwardly.
commentary: This divine medicine is the Vast Grace-Light itself, granting the devotee powers normally reserved for God, such as performing the five cosmic functions of creation and dissolution. It brings a real and tangible bliss, unifying the devotee with God in every aspect of life, both internally and externally.

translit: ellāmcey valla maruntu - eṉṉuḷ eṉṟum viṭāmal iṉikku maruntu collāl aḷavā maruntu - cuyañ jōti aruṭperuñ jōti maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: It is the medicine with the power to do all things, the medicine that is eternally sweet within me without fail. It is the medicine that cannot be measured by words, the medicine that is the self-effulgent Jothi, the Vast Grace-Light.
commentary: The divine medicine grants limitless power and a constant, sweet presence within. It is an experience so deep it cannot be described with words, because it is the self-luminous reality of the Vast Grace-Light itself.

translit: kāṇātu kāṭṭu maruntu - eṉṟaṉ kaiyiṟpoṟ kaṅkaṇam kaṭṭu maruntu āṇākip peṇṇām maruntu - atu vāki maṇimaṉṟil āṭu maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: It is the medicine that reveals the unseen, the medicine that tied the golden bracelet of authority on my hand. It is the medicine that becomes both male and female, the medicine that becomes "That" and dances in the Maṇimaṉṟam (Hall of Gems).
commentary: This medicine provides spiritual vision, revealing what is normally hidden. It grants divine authority, symbolized by the golden bracelet of honor placed on his hand by God. The divine reality is beyond all dualities, becoming both male and female, and is the ultimate principle that dances as the cosmos.

translit: cuttacaṉ mārkka maruntu - aruṭ cōti malaiyil tulaṅku maruntu citturu vāṉa maruntu - eṉṉaic cittelām ceyyaccey vitta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: It is the medicine of the Pure Sanmarkkam, the medicine that shines on the mountain of Grace-Light. It is the medicine that is the form of consciousness-power, the medicine that enabled me to perform all siddhis.
commentary: This divine medicine is the very essence of Vallalar's path, the Suddha Sanmarkkam (the Pure Path). It is pure consciousness itself, and by partaking of it, one can attain siddhis, or extraordinary spiritual powers.

translit: aṉpark keḷiya maruntu - maṟṟai aivarkkum kāṇṭaṟ kariya maruntu eṉpaṟṟil ōṅku maruntu - eṉṉai iṉpa nilaiyil iruttu maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: A medicine easily accessible to devotees, a medicine difficult for the other five to perceive, a medicine that flourishes in my devotion, the medicine that establishes me in a state of bliss. This is the medicine of wisdom.
commentary: The divine medicine is available only through love and devotion. Vallalar makes a startling claim: even the five great gods of traditional religion cannot perceive it, yet it is easily found by a simple devotee. It grows in response to one's own devotion, establishing the soul in a state of bliss.

translit: nātānta nāṭṭu maruntu - para ñāṉa veḷiyil naṭikku maruntu pōtāntark keytu maruntu - eṉṉuḷ poṉṉaṭi kāṭṭip puṇarnta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine from the realm of Nadanta, the medicine that dances in the space of supreme wisdom, the medicine attained by those at the summit of consciousness, the medicine that revealed its golden feet within me and united with me. This is the medicine of wisdom.
commentary: God is a medicine from the highest spiritual realms, beyond the primal sound of creation (Nadanta), a reality that dances in the space of pure wisdom. It is attained only by those who reach the very peak of consciousness (Bodhanta), and for Vallalar, it was a personal reality that revealed its "golden feet" and merged with him from within.

translit: āti aṉāti maruntu - tiru ampalat tēnaṭa māṭu maruntu jōti mayamā maruntu - eṉṉaic cōtiyā tāṇṭa turiya maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is the beginning and without beginning, the medicine that dances in the sacred hall, the medicine that is formed of Jothi, the Turiya medicine that took me as its own without testing me.
commentary: God is the eternal medicine, both the beginning and what is beyond any beginning, the light-filled presence dancing in the sacred hall. It is the reality of Turiya, and it took Vallalar as its own without first putting him to the test: grace given freely.

translit: āṟantat tōṅku maruntu - ataṟ kappāluk kappālum āṉa maruntu ūṟanta millā maruntu - eṉak kuḷḷē kalanta uṟavā maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that rises above the six antas, the medicine that is beyond the beyond, the medicine whose wellspring is endless, the medicine that has mingled within me and become my very own kin.
commentary: The medicine of wisdom (ñāṉa maruntu) is beyond the six systems of thought and beyond whatever lies beyond them. Its source never runs dry. Yet this transcendent medicine is not far away: it has mingled within Vallalar and become his own kin. The highest is also the closest.

translit: eṉṉuyirk kaṉpā maruntu - kalan teṉṉuyirk kuḷḷē irunta maruntu eṉṉuyir kākku maruntu - eṉṟum eṉṉuyi rākiya iṉpa maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is love for my soul, the medicine that mingled and abided within my soul, the medicine that protects my soul, the medicine of bliss that is forever my very own soul. This is the medicine of wisdom.
commentary: The divine grace that heals and completes us, which Vallalar calls a "medicine," is not something external. It is the love for our own soul, a presence that lives inside us, protecting and becoming the very bliss of our existence.

translit: eṉṉaṟi vuṭkoḷ maruntu - eṉṟum eṉṉaṟi vāki ilaṅku maruntu eṉṉaṟi viṉpa maruntu - eṉṉuḷ eṉṉaṟi vukkaṟi veṉṉu maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine my knowledge comprehends, the medicine that forever becomes my knowledge and shines, the medicine that is the bliss of my knowledge, the medicine within me that is the knowledge for my knowledge. Gnosis.
commentary: The divine medicine is not simply an object of knowledge, something the mind learns about from the outside. It merges with awareness itself, becoming the very act of knowing and the source of intelligence, the "knowledge for my knowledge." This is more than knowing God; it is knowing as God.

translit: eṉkuru vāṉa maruntu - eṉṟum eṉteyva māki irukku maruntu eṉaṉṉai yeṉṉu maruntu - eṉṟum eṉtantai yākiya iṉpa maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that became my guru, the medicine that is forever my God, the medicine that is my mother, the medicine of bliss that is forever my father. Gnosis.
commentary: The one divine principle is experienced in every essential relationship. It is the ultimate teacher (guru), the supreme being (God), and the source of unconditional love, like a mother and father. All that a person seeks from others is found within this single inner reality.

translit: eṉperu vāḻvā maruntu - eṉṟum eṉcelva māki irukku maruntu eṉṉuyir naṭpā maruntu - eṉak keṭṭeṭṭuc cittiyum īnta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is my great life, the medicine that is forever my wealth, the medicine that is the friend to my soul, the medicine that granted me the sixty-four siddhis. Gnosis.
commentary: The grace of God is the true source of all value. It is the substance of a good life, the only real wealth, and the most loyal friend to the soul. It can also unlock higher capacities, called siddhis, which are byproducts of this inner connection.

translit: eṉṉiṟai yāṉa maruntu - makiḻn teṉakkuttaṉ poṉmēṉi īnta maruntu taṉṉaṟi vāku maruntu - eṉṉait tanta marunteṉṟaṉ conta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is my Lord, the medicine that joyfully bestowed its golden form upon me, the medicine that is self-knowledge, the medicine that gave me to myself, my very own medicine. Gnosis.
commentary: While this divine "medicine" is the Lord who reveals His own glorious nature, its greatest gift is the return of your own true self. It is the experience of becoming fully and authentically yourself, a state of pure self-knowledge.

translit: uḷḷatti ṉuḷḷā maruntu - eṉṟaṉ uyiruk kaṉāti uṟavā maruntu teḷḷat teḷikku maruntu - eṉṉaic civamākkik koṇṭa civāya maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine within the heart, the medicine that is the beginningless relation to my soul, the medicine that brings perfect clarity, the Sivam-medicine that made me Sivam and accepted me. Gnosis.
commentary: The divine is a presence found within your own heart, an ancient, unbreakable bond with your soul. Experiencing it brings ultimate clarity and, above all, transforms you into the very nature of the divine, which he calls Sivam (the ultimate, benevolent reality).

translit: meypporu ḷeṉṉu maruntu - ellā vētā kamattum viḷaṅku maruntu kaipporu ḷāṉa maruntu - mūṉṟu kaṇkoṇṭa eṉṉiru kaṇṇuḷ maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is the True Substance, the medicine that shines in all Vedas and Agamas, the medicine that is a treasure in my hand, the three-eyed medicine that dwells within my two eyes.
commentary: This medicine is the "True Substance," the ultimate reality that underpins all sacred texts like the Vedas and Agamas. It is a "treasure in my hand," something tangible and directly possessed. The mention of a third eye signifies the opening of divine perception, allowing one to see the world with three eyes, which is the vision of God.

translit: matiyil viḷainta maruntu - yārkkum matikkappa ṭātapoṉ vaṇṇa maruntu katitarum iṉpa maruntu - aruṭ kaṇṇāleṉ ṟaṉṉaik kalanta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that grew from the intellect, the priceless, golden-hued medicine, the medicine of bliss that grants final release, the medicine that merged with me through its eye of grace.
commentary: Most spiritual paths consider the intellect a barrier, but Vallalar says this medicine "grew from the intellect," suggesting that reason, when rightly used, can lead to the divine. This medicine is priceless and grants the ultimate goal of spiritual life, liberation from suffering. It is given through a look from God’s "eye of grace," a moment of pure, uncaused compassion.

translit: kaṟpūra jōti maruntu - pacuṅ kaṟpūra naṉmaṇaṅ kāṭṭu maruntu poṟpūviṉ ōṅku maruntu - eṉtaṟ pōtam tavirttaciṟ pōta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is a camphor Jothi, the medicine that emanates the fine fragrance of raw camphor, the medicine that towers in the golden flower, the medicine of pure consciousness that ended my self-awareness.
commentary: The divine is experienced here as a pure, smokeless flame of camphor, a Jothi or divine light that is both seen and smelled. This experience of light and fragrance has a powerful effect: it dissolves the ego. The medicine of "pure consciousness" (ciṟ pōtam) replaces the ordinary awareness of being a separate self (taṟ pōtam), leading to a state of egoless clarity.

translit: mēlai veḷiyā maruntu - nāṉ vēṇṭuntō ṟellām viḷaiyu maruntu cālai viḷakku maruntu - cutta camaraca caṉmārkka caṅka maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is the space beyond, the medicine that manifests whenever I need it, the medicine that is the lamp of the Sālai, the medicine of the assembly of the Suddha Samarasa Sanmarkkam.
commentary: This medicine is the vast "space beyond," the ultimate reality, yet it is also immediately available whenever needed. Vallalar connects this sublime concept to his practical mission on earth. The medicine is the "lamp of the Sālai," the charitable hall where he fed the poor, and the very essence of his community, the Suddha Samarasa Sanmarkkam (the Pure Universal True Path). For him, the highest spiritual truth must manifest as compassionate action in the world.

translit: eṉṉaittā ṉākku maruntu - iṅkē iṟantārai ellām eḻuppu maruntu tuṉṉumeyc cōti maruntu - aruṭ cōtiyāl eṉṉait tulakku maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that makes me Itself, the medicine that here raises all who have died, the medicine that is the dense, true Jothi, the medicine that makes me shine with the Jothi of grace.
commentary: This divine medicine has the power to overcome all limitations, including death itself. By making the devotee one with God, the true Jothi (divine light), it grants a deathless life. The claim that it can raise all who have died shows the absolute power Vallalar ascribes to grace.

translit: poyyark karitā maruntu - eṉṉaip puṟattum akattum puṇarnta maruntu kaiyiṟ kiṭaitta maruntu - civa kāmak koṭiyaik kalanta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine inaccessible to the false, the medicine that joined with me outside and inside, the medicine that came into my hand, the medicine united with Sivakāmak Koṭi, the divine Consort.
commentary: Grace is a tangible reality for the sincere devotee. While inaccessible to the false, it is as real as an object held "in my hand" for the true seeker. This medicine satisfies the soul's deepest longing for God, here called the "vine of desire for Sivam" (the supreme divine being).

translit: āṇavam tīrkku maruntu - para māṉantat tāṇṭava māṭum maruntu māṇava vaṇṇa maruntu - eṉṉai valiya aḻaittu vaḷarkku maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that cures ego-conceit, the medicine that performs the cosmic dance of supreme bliss, the medicine that has the nature of the great one, the medicine that forcefully called and now nurtures me.
commentary: The fundamental sickness of the soul is āṇavam, the ego-conceit of being a separate self, and this medicine is its cure. Grace is the active, blissful energy of God, which forcefully seeks out the soul, calls to it, and lovingly helps it grow.

translit: vāṉaṭu vāṉa maruntu - eṉṉai māmaṇi mēṭaimēl vaitta maruntu ūṉam tavirtta maruntu - kalan tuḷḷē iṉikkiṉṟa uṇmai maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is sky within sky, the medicine that placed me upon the great jeweled dais, the medicine that removed my defects, the true medicine that mingles within and tastes sweet.
commentary: The experience of this divine medicine has infinite depth, like a "sky within sky." It elevates the soul, removes all its flaws, and places it in a state of honor. This grace is an idea and a felt reality, an unmistakable sweetness tasted directly within one's own being.

translit: malaiyilak kāṉa maruntu - eṉṟaṉ maṟaippait tavirttamey vāḻkkai maruntu kalainalam kāṭṭu maruntu - eṅkum kaṇṇākik kāṇum kaṉatta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is a mountain-like goal, the medicine of true life that removed my veil of concealment, the medicine that reveals the excellence of all knowledge, the profound medicine that becomes the eye everywhere and sees.
commentary: This medicine is the ultimate spiritual goal, as solid and unmoving as a mountain. It grants true life by removing the inner veil that hides reality from us. It is also the source of all real knowledge, a universal consciousness that becomes the eye in all beings and sees through them.

translit: aṟputa jōti maruntu - ellām ākiyaṉ ṟāki amarnta maruntu taṟpatam tanta maruntu - eṅkum tāṉētā ṉākit taṉitta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine of wondrous light, the medicine that, having become all things and yet being other than them, remains settled, the medicine that granted the supreme state of Self, the medicine that, becoming Itself everywhere, remains unique.
commentary: The divine is a medicine of wondrous light, or Jothi. It exists as all things in the universe, yet it is also separate from and beyond them. This medicine grants the supreme state of Self (tatpadam), a realization of one's true nature. While it becomes everything, everywhere, it never loses its own unique identity.

translit: taṉṉai aḷitta maruntu - eṉṟum cākāta nalvaram tanta maruntu poṉṉaṭi īnta maruntu - aruṭ pōṉakam tanta puṉita maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that gave itself, the medicine that granted the great boon of never dying, the medicine that bestowed its golden feet, the holy medicine that gave the food of grace.
commentary: The greatest gift of this medicine is itself; God gives God's own being to the soul. This act of grace leads to the ultimate boon of a deathless life. The 'golden feet' are a classic symbol for divine refuge, while the 'food of grace' is the spiritual nourishment that sustains the soul.

translit: kaṇṇuk kiṉiya maruntu - eṉṟaṉ kaipporu ḷāntaṅkak kaṭṭi maruntu eṇṇuk kaṭaṅkā maruntu - eṉṉai ētakkuḻiviṭ ṭeṭutta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine pleasing to the eyes, the medicine that is a block of gold, my very own possession, the medicine beyond all count, the medicine that lifted me from the pit of misery.
commentary: The divine medicine is described as something beautiful to behold and as precious as a block of pure gold. It is an intimate, personal possession. Though its qualities are beyond all counting, it is also the direct power that rescues a person from the depths of misery.

translit: cuṭṭap paṭāta maruntu - eṉṟaṉ tūkkamum cōrvum tolaitta maruntu eṭṭutaṟ koṇṇā maruntu - nāṉ eṭṭip piṭikka icainta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that cannot be defined, the medicine that dispelled my drowsiness and fatigue, the medicine that is impossible to reach, the medicine that consented for me to reach out and grasp it.
commentary: Here, Vallalar captures a key spiritual paradox. The divine is beyond all human definition and seems impossible to reach, yet it makes itself available to be experienced. It is a presence that awakens the soul, removing spiritual tiredness and confusion.

translit: uṉṉaṟ karitā maruntu - eṉak kuḷḷum puṟattum ulāvu maruntu taṉṉan taṉitta maruntu - cuttac cākkirā tītac capēca maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is impossible to conceive, the medicine that roams within and without me, the medicine that stands utterly alone, the medicine of Sabesan from the state beyond pure waking consciousness.
commentary: The divine is unthinkable, yet it is intimately present everywhere, both inside us and in the world around us. Vallalar identifies this ultimate reality with Sabesan (Lord of the cosmic assembly, Siva) and links it to a state of awareness beyond ordinary consciousness, a pure, transcendent wakefulness.

translit: oṉṟiloṉ ṟāṉa maruntu - anta oṉṟil iraṇṭāki ōṅku maruntu aṉṟimūṉ ṟāṉa maruntu - nāṉ kākiain tāki amarnta maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that is one within the one, the medicine that, from that one, becomes two and rises up, the medicine that then becomes three, the medicine that becomes four, then five, and so abides.
commentary: The one divine reality manifests as the diverse world we experience. This verse describes the unfolding of creation: from the absolute One, to the dualities of existence (two), then to primary forces (three), aspects of mind (four), and the physical elements (five). All of this multiplicity, Vallalar says, is still the one original 'medicine'.

translit: veḷikkuḷ veḷiyā maruntu - ellā veḷiyum kaṭantu viḷaṅku maruntu oḷikkuḷ oḷiyā maruntu - ellā oḷiyumtā ṉākiya uṇmai maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: A medicine that is space within space, a medicine that shines transcending all spaces. A medicine that is light within light, the true medicine that has itself become all light. Gnosis.
commentary: The divine medicine is the very essence of reality, the space within all space and the light within all light. It is the light within every light and has itself become all light, the fundamental, true substance of all that is luminous and conscious.

translit: āṟāṟuk kappāl maruntu - ataṟ kappuṟat tīrāṟuk kappāl maruntu īṟāti illā maruntu - eṉṉai ellām ceyacceyta iṉpa maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: A medicine beyond the thirty-six principles, a medicine beyond the twelve that are further beyond that. A medicine with no end or beginning, the blissful medicine that made me do everything. Gnosis.
commentary: This healing power exists beyond all the categories of creation, which are sometimes numbered as thirty-six principles (tattvas). It is the eternal, uncaused source of everything, and yet it is also the intimate, blissful power that inspires and moves one's own life and actions.

translit: āraṇat tōṅku maruntu - aruḷ ākama mākiaṇ ṇikku maruntu kāraṇam kāṭṭu maruntu - ellām kaṇṭa marunteṉṉuḷ koṇṭa maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine exalted in the Vedas, the medicine that becomes the gracious Agamas and draws near. The medicine that reveals the ultimate cause, the all-seeing medicine that I have taken into myself. Gnosis.
commentary: This divine medicine is the inner truth praised in the holy scriptures, the Vedas and Agamas. It is the power that reveals the ultimate cause of existence, and it is a truth that can be directly experienced, taken into oneself to see and understand everything.

translit: malamaintu nīkku maruntu - puvi vāṉaṇṭa mellām vaḷarkku maruntu nalamik karuḷu maruntu - tāṉē nāṉākit tāṉāḷu nāṭṭu maruntu. ñāṉa
translation: The medicine that removes the five impurities, the medicine that nurtures the earth, sky, and all worlds. The medicine that graciously bestows great good, the native medicine that rules as itself, having become me. Gnosis.
commentary: Taking this medicine purifies the soul by removing the five spiritual impurities (malam) that cause bondage and suffering. This divine power sustains all worlds and, in its final work, merges with the self so completely that one realizes the divine itself is ruling through a life that has become its own.

translit: ñāṉa maruntim maruntu - cukam nalkiya ciṟcapā nāta maruntu.
translation: This medicine is the medicine of Gnosis, the medicine of the Lord of the Chit Sabhai who grants bliss.
commentary: The medicine is finally identified as Gnosis, which is direct, divine knowledge. This supreme knowledge is a gift from the Lord who presides over the Chit Sabhai, the inner 'Hall of Consciousness' that is the sacred space of awareness within each person.

translit: civaciva civaciva jōti - civa civaciva civaciva civaciva jōti civaciva civaciva jōti.
translation: Siva-Siva, Siva-Siva, Light! Siva, Siva-Siva, Siva-Siva, Siva-Siva, Light! Siva-Siva, Siva-Siva, Light!
commentary: This opening is a pure chant, not a philosophical statement. The intense repetition of "Siva-Siva" and "Jothi" (Light) is a meditative practice designed to focus the mind and evoke a direct feeling of the divine presence.

translit: ciṟpara māmparañ jōti - aruṭ cittellām valla citampara jōti taṟpara tattuva jōti - eṉṉait tāṉākkik koṇṭa tayāniti jōti. civaciva
translation: The Light of the supreme, transcendent consciousness; the Light of Chidambaram, all-powerful through grace; the Light that is the principle of the Supreme Being; the Light, a treasure of compassion, that has made me Itself.
commentary: The divine Light is defined here as consciousness itself, the fundamental principle (tattuvam) of reality. Vallalar connects this Light to Chidambaram, the inner space of pure awareness. The final line reveals the ultimate spiritual goal: this compassionate Light absorbs the devotee into its own nature, dissolving the separation between the soul and God.

translit: citturu vāmcuyañ jōti - ellām ceytiṭa valla citampara jōti attuvi tāṉanta jōti - eṉṉai āṭkoṇ ṭaruḷumciṟ ṟampala jōti. civaciva
translation: The self-luminous Light that is the form of consciousness; the Chidambaram Light with the power to do all things; the Light of non-dual bliss; the Light of Sitrambalam that graciously took me as its own.
commentary: This Light is self-luminous, needing no external source to shine because it is the very form of consciousness. Vallalar makes a distinction between Chidambaram, the vast, infinite space of consciousness, and Sitrambalam, the 'small hall', suggesting the divine is experienced both as the cosmos and as an intimate presence in the heart. It is this personal, indwelling presence that has claimed him.

translit: ciṉmaya māmperuñ jōti - aruṭ celva maḷikkum citampara jōti taṉmaya māyniṟai jōti - eṉṉait tantamey jōti catāṉanta jōti. civaciva
translation: The great Light that is pure consciousness; the Chidambaram Light that bestows the wealth of grace; the Light that pervades all things as Itself; the true Light that gave Itself to me, the Light of eternal bliss.
commentary: The Light is described as both transcendent and immanent; it is pure consciousness, and it also fills everything that exists. The most personal point for Vallalar is that this cosmic reality is a gift freely given to him, bringing eternal bliss.

translit: ātiī ṟillāmuṟ jōti - araṉ ātiyar tammai aḷittapiṟ jōti ōti uṇarvarum jōti - ellā uyirkaḷiṉ uḷḷum oḷirkiṉṟa jōti. civaciva
translation: The primordial Light with no beginning or end; the subsequent Light that brought forth Aran and the other gods; the Light incomprehensible through recitation or learning; the Light that shines within all living beings.
commentary: This divine Light is the absolute origin, existing before even the gods like Aran (a name for Siva). Vallalar makes a key distinction: you cannot understand this Light by studying scriptures or performing rituals. It is beyond the mind, yet it is accessible because it shines as the inner life-force within every living being.

translit: maṉṉiya poṉvaṇṇa jōti - cuka vaṇṇatta tāmperu māṇikka jōti tuṉṉiya vaccira jōti - muttu jōti marakata jōtiyuḷ jōti. civaciva
translation: The eternal, golden-colored Jothi, the great ruby Jothi of blissful color, the dense diamond Jothi, the pearl Jothi, the emerald Jothi, the Jothi within the Jothi.
commentary: Vallalar uses the metaphor of precious gems to describe the indescribable qualities of the divine Light, or Jothi. Each gem, from gold and ruby to diamond and emerald, represents a different facet of its beauty, value, and permanence. The final phrase, "the Jothi within the Jothi," suggests an infinite depth, a light that contains its own source.

translit: pārmutal aintumām jōti - aintil pakkamēl kīḻnaṭup paṟṟiya jōti ōraim poṟiyuru jōti - poṟik kuḷḷum puṟattum oḷirkiṉṟa jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that is the five elements beginning with earth, the Jothi that pervades the sides, top, bottom, and center of those five, the Jothi that is the form of the five sense organs, the Jothi that shines inside and outside the sense organs.
commentary: The divine Light is not a remote, spiritual reality separate from the physical world. Vallalar states that the Jothi is the very substance of the five elements (earth, water, fire, air, space) and the perceiving power of the five senses. It is both the world we experience and the means by which we experience it, present inside and outside of our own bodies.

translit: aimpula mumtāṉām jōti - pulat takattum puṟattu malarntoḷir jōti poymmayal pōkkumuḷ jōti - maṟṟaip poṟipulaṉ uḷḷum puṟattumām jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that is itself the five sense perceptions, the Jothi that blossoms and shines inside and outside the senses, the inner Jothi that removes false delusion, the Jothi that is inside and outside the sense organs and sense perceptions.
commentary: The Jothi is our physical sense organs and the very experience of perception itself: the act of seeing, hearing, and feeling. This light shines both within our consciousness and through the world we perceive. By recognizing this inner light, we can see through illusion and understand reality as it truly is.

translit: maṉamāti ellāmām jōti - avai vāḻa akampuṟam vāḻkiṉṟa jōti iṉamāṉa uḷḷaka jōti - caṟṟum ēṟā tiṟaṅkā tiyakkumōr jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that is everything, beginning with the mind, the Jothi that lives inside and outside, allowing them to live, the kindred inner Jothi, a Jothi that operates without any increase or decrease.
commentary: The divine Jothi is also the source of our inner world, beginning with the mind. As the life-force animating our mental faculties, it is constant and unchanging, a steady flame that neither grows nor diminishes. This provides a stable foundation for our ever-changing thoughts and feelings.

translit: mukkuṇamu mūṉṟām jōti - avai muṉpiṉ iyaṅka muṭukkiya jōti ekkuṇat tuḷḷumām jōti - kuṇam ellām kaṭantē ilaṅkiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that is the three gunas, the Jothi that impelled them to operate back and forth, the Jothi that is within every quality, the Jothi that shines, having transcended all qualities.
commentary: The divine Jothi is the source of the three gunas (the fundamental qualities of inertia, activity, and balance) that govern all of nature and our minds. It is the power that sets these qualities in motion and exists within them, yet it also transcends them completely. The Jothi is both the dynamic play of the universe and the serene stillness that lies beyond all activity.

translit: pakutimūṉ ṟākiya jōti - mūlap pakutikaḷ mūṉṟum paṭaittaruḷ jōti vikuti palavākkum jōti - caṟṟum vikutioṉ ṟiṉṟi viḷakkiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that became the three divisions, The Jothi that graciously created the three root divisions, The Jothi that makes many derived forms, The Jothi that shines without a single derived form.
commentary: A central paradox of the divine is expressed here: the One becomes the many. The Jothi is the origin of all of creation's divisions and the countless forms that arise from them. Yet, while being the source of this infinite diversity, the Jothi itself remains perfectly simple, formless, and undivided.

translit: kāla mutaṟkāṭṭum jōti - kāla kāraṇat tappāl kaṭantoḷir jōti kōlam palavākum jōti - oṉṟum kuṟikkap paṭācciṟ kuṇapperuñ cōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that reveals the origin of time, The Jothi that transcends and shines beyond the cause of time, The Jothi that becomes many forms, The great Jothi of conscious nature, which cannot be defined as any one thing.
commentary: The divine Light is the very origin of time, but it also exists outside of time's flow. While it manifests as all the different forms in the world, its own nature is pure consciousness, so vast and absolute that it cannot be pinned down or defined by any single characteristic.

translit: tattuvam ellāmām jōti - antat tattuvam ellām taruvikkum jōti attuvi tapperuñ jōti - ellām aruḷil viḷaṅka amarttiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that is all the tattvas, The Jothi that brings forth all those tattvas, The great Jothi of non-duality, The Jothi that established all things to shine within Grace.
commentary: The Jothi is both the creator of and the reality within the tattvas (the fundamental principles or building blocks of existence, from the most subtle to the most gross). As the single source of everything, it is the great Jothi of non-duality: there is nothing but It. Everything that exists is held within its all-pervading Grace.

translit: cattarkaḷ ellāmām jōti - avar cattikaḷ ellām taḻaippikkum jōti muttar aṉupava jōti - para muttiyām jōtimeyc cittiyām jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that is all the powerful beings, The Jothi that makes all their powers flourish, The Jothi that is the experience of the liberated ones, The Jothi that is supreme liberation, the Jothi that is true siddhi.
commentary: The divine Light is the source of power for all beings, from gods to saints. For those who have achieved spiritual liberation, the Jothi is their direct experience. It is more than the path to the goal, it is the goal itself: supreme liberation and siddhi (the state of perfected spiritual attainment).

translit: āṟantat tēniṟai jōti - avaik kappuṟat tappālum ākiya jōti vīṟum peruveḷi jōti - mēlum veṭṭa veḷiyil viḷaṅkiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that fills the six antas, The Jothi that is beyond and even further beyond them, The Jothi of the glorious great expanse, The Jothi that shines higher still in the utterly open space.
commentary: The divine Light fills the six antas, the six culminations named Vedanta, Siddhanta, Bodhanta, Nadanta, Yoganta and Kalanta. Yet it is also beyond them and beyond even that, shining in the vast, open expanse.

translit: pēraruṭ jōtiyuḷ jōti - aṇṭa piṇṭaṅkaḷ ellām piṟaṅkiya jōti vāramuṟ ṟōṅkiya jōti - maṉa vākkuk keṭṭātatōr māmaṇijōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi within the Vast Grace-Light, the Jothi that shines brightly in all universes and bodies, the Jothi that rose full of love, a great gem-like Jothi unattainable by mind and speech.
commentary: Here, the Jothi is the light within the "Vast Grace-Light," a core concept for Vallalar. This divine light fills all bodies and universes with love, yet remains a mystery that the mind and words can never fully grasp.

translit: oṉṟāṉa pūraṇa jōti - aṉpil oṉṟāta uḷḷattil oṉṟāta jōti eṉṟā oḷirkiṉṟa jōti - eṉṉuḷ eṉṟum viḷaṅkiya eṉṉuyir jōti. civaciva
translation: The one, perfect Jothi, the Jothi that does not unite with hearts that fail to unite in love, the Jothi that shines eternally, the Jothi of my very life, ever-luminous within me.
commentary: This verse states a core principle: the perfect, unified Jothi is available only to those whose hearts are filled with love. For those who lack this unifying love, the divine light remains inaccessible, even though it shines eternally as the very essence of our own life.

translit: meyyēmey yākiya jōti - cutta vētānta vīṭṭil viḷaṅkiya jōti tuyya civāṉanta jōti - kuru turiyat talattē tulaṅkiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that is Truth itself, the Jothi shining in the house of pure Vedanta, the pure Jothi of Siva's bliss, the Jothi gleaming on the Guru's plane of Turiya.
commentary: The Jothi is identified with ultimate reality itself. It is the light found in the "house of pure Vedanta" (the culmination of spiritual knowledge), the blissful consciousness of the divine (Siva), and the direct experience seen in Turiya, the silent, wakeful consciousness beyond dreaming and deep sleep.

translit: civamaya māmcutta jōti - cutta cittānta vīṭṭil ciṟantoḷir jōti uvamaiyil lāpperuñ cōti - eṉa tuḷḷē nirampi oḷirkiṉṟa jōti. civaciva
translation: The pure Jothi that is pervaded by Siva, the Jothi that shines excellently in the house of pure Siddhanta, the great Light beyond compare, the Jothi that fills and shines within me.
commentary: While the previous verse mentioned Vedanta, here the divine light is associated with Saiva Siddhanta, another major school of philosophy focused on Siva. Yet the point is direct experience: this supreme, incomparable light completely fills and illuminates him from within.

translit: eṉṉaittā ṉākkiya jōti - iṅkē iṟantārai ellām eḻuppumōr jōti aṉṉaikku mikkaruṭ jōti - eṉṉai āṇṭamu tamtanta āṉanta jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that made me Itself, a Jothi that raises all who have died here, the Jothi of grace far exceeding a mother's, the Jothi of bliss that gave the ambrosia that saved me.
commentary: The divine light, Jothi, has the power to transform a person completely, making them one with itself. Vallalar describes its effects as miraculous: it can even raise the dead and provides a grace deeper than a mother's love. This experience grants amutam, the nectar of deathless life.

translit: cittam civamākkum jōti - nāṉ ceyta tavattāl terinta:uṭ jōti puttamu tākiya jōti - cuka pūraṇa māyoḷir kāraṇa jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that makes the mind one with Sivam; the inner Jothi revealed by the austerities I performed; the Jothi that is fresh nectar; the Causal Jothi that shines as perfect bliss.
commentary: Spiritual discipline (tavam, or austerities) can quiet the mind, revealing an inner light that makes the mind one with God (Sivam). This Jothi is the first cause of all things, the very source of existence, which is experienced directly as pure bliss.

translit: tampattil ēṟṟiya jōti - appāl cārmaṇi mēṭaimēl tāṉvaitta jōti vimpap peruveḷi jōti - aṅkē vītiyum vīṭum viḷakkiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi raised upon the pillar; the Jothi placed upon the beautiful, jeweled dais beyond; the Jothi of the great space of forms; the Jothi that illuminated the path and the dwelling there.
commentary: This verse uses architectural images to place the Jothi at the very center of existence. Like a lamp raised on a pillar or placed on a throne, it is the supreme, illuminating principle. It is both the light of the cosmos, filling the "great space of forms," and the light for the individual soul, showing the spiritual path and its ultimate destination.

translit: cukamaya mākiya jōti - ellā jōtiyu māṉa corūpa:uṭ jōti akamitan tīrttaruḷ jōti - cacci tāṉanta jōti catāṉanta jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that is the embodiment of bliss; the inner Jothi of true form, which has become all other Jothis; the Jothi that graciously dissolves the sense of 'I' and 'this'; the Jothi of Being-Consciousness-Bliss, the Jothi of eternal bliss.
commentary: Here, the Jothi is identified as the source of all bliss and the single, true reality from which all other forms of light or consciousness appear. Most importantly, experiencing this inner Jothi dissolves the ego, the feeling of being a separate 'I' distinct from the world ('this'). Vallalar equates it with Sacchidananda (Being-Consciousness-Bliss), a classic name for the nature of God, showing this light is God's very substance.

translit: nitta parāṉanta jōti - cutta niratica yāṉanta nittiya jōti attuvi tāṉanta jōti - ellā āṉanta vaṇṇamum ākiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi of eternal, supreme bliss; the Jothi of pure, unsurpassed, eternal bliss; the Jothi of non-dual bliss; the Jothi that has become every shade and form of bliss.
commentary: The Jothi is bliss itself, in its highest, purest, and most complete form. Vallalar calls it 'non-dual bliss', a happiness where there is no separation between the one experiencing it and the bliss being experienced. This light is more than a source of joy; it is the reality that has become every possible kind and expression of happiness that exists.

translit: poyyāta puṇṇiya jōti - ellāp poruḷum viḷaṅkap puṇarttiya jōti naiyā taruḷceyta jōti - oru nāṉumtā ṉumoṉṟāy naṇṇiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The unfailing Jothi of merit; the Jothi that conjoined all things, making them luminous; the Jothi that bestowed grace without causing me to suffer; the Jothi where the singular 'I' and 'He' united as one.
commentary: This divine light is the unfailing reward for a life of goodness (puṇṇiyam, merit). It is the unifying force that connects all things and makes them shine with meaning. In a personal testimony, Vallalar notes that this grace was given to him gently, without painful struggle. The ultimate experience of this Jothi is the merging of the individual self ('I') with God ('He') until they are one.

translit: kaṇṇiṟ kalantaruḷ jōti - uḷak kaṇṇuyirk kaṇṇaruṭ kaṇṇumām jōti eṇṇiṟpa ṭāpperuñ cōti - nāṉ eṇṇiya vaṇṇam iyaṟṟiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The gracious Jothi that has mingled in my eye, the Jothi that is the eye of the inner eye, the eye of the soul, and the eye of grace. The great Jothi that is beyond measure, the Jothi that has created all that I have conceived.
commentary: The Jothi is the very power of sight, from the physical to the spiritual. It is in the physical eye, but it is also the 'inner eye' of self-awareness and the 'eye of the soul' that perceives divine truth. This immeasurable light is also a creative force, bringing into existence whatever the illuminated mind conceives.

translit: vintu oḷinaṭu jōti - para vintu oḷikkuḷ viḷaṅkiya jōti namtuyar tīrttaruḷ jōti - para nātānta nāṭṭukku nāyaka jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi at the center of the light of vindhu, the Jothi that shines from within the light of the supreme vindhu. The gracious Jothi that has ended our suffering, the Jothi that is the Lord of the supreme land of Nāthāntam.
commentary: This verse describes the divine light in deeply mystical terms. It is the light within the vindhu, the primordial seed-point from which the universe is said to emerge. The Jothi is also the lord of Nāthāntam, a state of consciousness that transcends even the subtlest cosmic sound, a place beyond all creation where suffering ends.

translit: tāṉaṉṟi oṉṟilā jōti - eṉṉait taṉmayam ākkiya cattiya jōti nāṉiṉṟu kaṇṭatōr jōti - tāṉē nāṉāki vāḻntiṭa nalkiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi besides which nothing else exists, the Jothi of Truth that made me one with itself. The Jothi that I have seen today, the Jothi that granted that I might live as Itself.
commentary: The experience of this light reveals that nothing else truly exists besides it. This is more than a philosophical idea; it is a lived reality where the individual self is absorbed into the divine, becoming one with it and living as an expression of that truth.

translit: taṉṉikar illatōr jōti - cutta caṉmārkka caṅkam taḻuviya jōti eṉṉuḷ niṟaintamey jōti - eṉṉai īṉṟain toḻilceyeṉ ṟēviya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that has no equal, the Jothi embraced by the Suddha Sanmarkka Sangam. The true Jothi that has filled me within, the Jothi that brought me forth and commanded, "Perform the five divine functions."
commentary: The divine light is the central reality of the Suddha Sanmarkkam, the path Vallalar established. He then makes a bold statement about his own state: this light has filled him and empowered him to perform the five great cosmic acts of God. This indicates a complete identification with the divine, where the enlightened soul participates in the very functioning of the cosmos.

translit: accam tavirttamey jōti - eṉṉai āṭkoṇ ṭaruḷiya ampala jōti iccai elāmtanta jōti - uyirk kiṅkumaṅ keṉṉāmal eṅkumām jōti. civaciva
translation: The true Jothi that has banished fear, the Jothi of the sacred space that graciously accepted me as its own. The Jothi that has granted all my desires, the Jothi that is everywhere for the soul, without distinction of here or there.
commentary: The presence of the Jothi within oneself removes all fear. This divine light, which animates the sacred space of consciousness (Ambalam), is equally present everywhere, accessible to the soul at all times.

translit: kālaiyil nāṉkaṇṭa jōti - ellāk kāṭciyum nāṉkāṇak kāṭṭiya jōti ñālamum vāṉumām jōti - eṉṉuḷ nāṉākit tāṉāki naṇṇiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi I saw in the morning; the Jothi that revealed all visions for me to see. The Jothi that is the world and the heavens; the Jothi that drew near, becoming me within me while also being itself. Siva Siva.
commentary: The divine light (Jothi) is the source of all sight, both physical and visionary. It is the very fabric of the universe, and yet it is also deeply personal. The verse culminates in the core mystical experience: the light draws so near that it becomes one with the devotee's own self, without losing its own distinct, absolute nature.

translit: ēkānta mākiya jōti - eṉṉuḷ eṉṟum piriyā tirukkiṉṟa jōti cākāta varantanta jōti - eṉṉait tāṉākkik koṇṭatōr cattiya jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi that is sublime solitude; the Jothi that resides within me, never to be separated. The Jothi that granted the boon of deathlessness; the one true Jothi that has made me itself. Siva Siva.
commentary: This verse describes the ultimate fruits of realizing the divine light. It brings an inner solitude of perfect completeness. This union is permanent and confers the gift of deathlessness, culminating in the final transformation where the devotee's identity is completely merged with the divine light.

translit: cutta civamaya jōti - eṉṉai jōti maṇimuṭi cūṭṭiya jōti cattiya māmperuñ jōti - nāṉē tāṉāki āḷat tayavucey jōti. civaciva
translation: The Jothi of pure Siva-consciousness; the Jothi that crowned me with a jeweled crown of light. The great Jothi that is truth; the Jothi that graciously empowers me to rule, I myself having become It. Siva Siva.
commentary: The union with the divine light is described as a coronation. It is an experience of pure Siva-consciousness that bestows a crown of light, symbolizing spiritual authority. Having become one with the light of truth, Vallalar is now empowered to "rule" from this transformed state of being.

translit: civaciva civaciva jōti - civa civaciva civaciva civaciva jōti civaciva civaciva jōti.
translation: Siva Siva, Siva Siva, Jothi. Siva, Siva Siva, Siva Siva, Siva Siva, Jothi.
commentary: This final verse is an ecstatic chant. The repetition of "Siva" (the name for the supreme reality) and "Jothi" (light) serves as a powerful mantra, dissolving analysis into pure, devotional experience. It captures the overflowing joy of the state described in the previous verses.
NOTES
Note 316

translit: māṇikka - ca. mu. ka. patippu.
translation: māṇikka — reading of the S. Mu. Ka. Edition.

translit: jōtiyuḷ jōtiyuḷ jōti - cutta jōti civajōti jōtiyuḷ jōti jōtiyuḷ jōtiyuḷ jōti.
translation: Light within Light within Light. Pure Light, Siva-Jothi, Light within Light. Light within Light within Light.
commentary: This opening verse uses repetition to convey a sense of infinite depth. The divine is light and light within light, endlessly. This is a direct, mystical perception of reality as pure Jothi (light), the essence of Siva (ultimate consciousness).

translit: civamē poruḷeṉṟu tēṟṟi - eṉṉaic civaveḷik kēṟum cikarattil ēṟṟic civamākkik koṇṭatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Making it clear that Siva is the one substance, it lifted me to the peak that ascends into the space of Siva. See how it has made me into Siva itself: the Sacred Dancing Light in the Sacred Hall of Consciousness. Light.
commentary: The first step is the clear understanding that Siva (the divine consciousness) is the only true substance. This realization itself becomes the path, lifting the soul into the "space of Siva." The ultimate goal, already achieved by the speaker, is to merge completely and become that divine reality: the Sacred Dancing Light that shines in the inner space of consciousness.

translit: vittellām oṉṟeṉṟu nāṭṭi - atil viḷaivu palapala vēṟeṉṟu kāṭṭic cittellām tantatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Establishing that all seeds are one, and showing that the yields from them are many and varied, see how it has bestowed all Siddhis: the Sacred Dancing Light in the Sacred Hall of Consciousness. Light.
commentary: All of creation springs from a single source, like countless different plants growing from one fundamental type of seed. Recognizing this unity behind all diversity is the key that unlocks all Siddhis, the spiritual powers and attainments that come from aligning with the creative principle of the universe.

translit: colvanta antaṅkaḷ āṟum - oru collālē āmeṉṟac collālē vīṟum celvam koṭuttatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: The six antas spoken of in words: with the one word that says 'It is,' with that very word, see how it granted glorious wealth: the Sacred Dancing Light in the Sacred Hall of Consciousness. Light.
commentary: The 'six antas' are the six culminations of spiritual knowledge: Vedanta, Siddhanta, Bodhanta, Nadanta, Yoganta and Kalanta. Vallalar says the divine light holds them all in a single word, 'It is,' and through that word bestows a wealth far greater than any intellectual understanding.

translit: taṅkōl aḷaveṉak kōtic - cutta camaraca cattiya caṉmārkka nītic ceṅkōl aḷittatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Stating that its own standard is the measure, see how it has granted the scepter of justice of the Path of Pure, Universal, True Harmony: the Sacred Dancing Light in the Sacred Hall of Consciousness. Light.
commentary: The true path is not based on old rules or human authority; it sets its own divine standard. The Light (Jothi) itself provides the ultimate measure of right and wrong, giving Vallalar the "scepter of justice" for his path of pure universal harmony (Suddha Samarasa Sathya Sanmarkkam). This means the path's authority comes directly from God, not from any book or institution.

translit: āpattai nīkki vaḷarttē - caṟṟum acaiyāmal aviyāmal aṭiyēṉ uḷattē tīpattai vaittatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Look, it removed all danger, nurtured me, and placed a lamp in my heart that never flickers or goes out: the Jothi of the sacred dance in the sacred Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: The divine Light (Jothi) offers a deep sense of inner security. Vallalar describes it as a personal gift: the Light cleared away his troubles and lit a lamp inside his own heart, a flame of awareness that can never be extinguished. This guidance and peace are found within.

translit: meyyoṉṟu caṉmārkka mētāṉ - eṉṟum viḷaṅkap paṭaippāti meyttoḻil nītāṉ ceyyeṉṟu tantatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Look, declaring that the one truth is indeed the Sanmarkkam, it gave me the command, "You must perform the true functions starting with creation to make it ever manifest": the Jothi of the sacred dance in the sacred Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: Here, Vallalar receives a divine mission directly from the Light (Jothi). The one truth is his path, the Sanmarkkam, and his job is to teach it and to help make it real in the world. He is empowered to participate in the divine acts of creation, a task that goes far beyond the role of a typical spiritual teacher.

translit: eṉpāl varupavark kiṉṟē - aruḷ īkiṉṟēṉ īkiṉṟēṉ īkiṉṟēṉ eṉṟē teṉpāl iruntatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Look, saying, "To those who come to me, I bestow grace this very day, I bestow grace, I bestow grace," it was present in the south: the Jothi of the sacred dance in the sacred Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: Divine grace is an immediate, eager reality. The repetition of "I bestow grace" emphasizes the certainty and generosity of the divine. The mention of the "south" grounds this promise in a specific place, Vadalur, where Vallalar established his community, making it a center from which grace radiates.

translit: turiyat talamūṉṟiṉ mēlē - cutta turiyap patiyil atuata ṉālē teriyat terivatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Look, above the three planes of Turiyam, in the realm of pure Turiyam, it reveals itself clearly through its own very nature: the Jothi of the sacred dance in the sacred Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: The divine light is perceived in the highest states of awareness. Beyond the three familiar states of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep lies Turiyam, a fourth state of pure consciousness. Vallalar says the Jothi is found even beyond this, in a state of pure Turiyam, where it reveals itself on its own terms.

translit: paraitūkkik kāṭṭiya kālē - āti paraiivark kappālap pāleṉṟu mēlē tiraitūkkik kāṭṭutal pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Regarding the foot that Parai lifted and showed, look, primordial Parai lifts the veil higher, saying "Beyond this one, and beyond that," and reveals it: the Jothi of the sacred dance in the sacred Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: Spiritual progress happens through a series of ever-deepening revelations. Parai, the supreme divine power, first shows a glimpse of grace, symbolized by the "lifted foot." But this is just the beginning. The divine then reveals that there are further realities, lifting one veil after another to lead the soul toward the ultimate Jothi.

translit: taṟpara mēvaṭi vāki - atu taṉṉaik kaṭantu taṉiuru vākic ciṟparat tuḷḷatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: It becomes the very form of the Supreme Beyond, transcends even that to become a unique form, and exists in the Supreme Consciousness. See it! It is the Jothi of the sacred dance in the Thiru Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: The divine light is both the ultimate reality and something beyond it. It can embody the highest concept of God, the Supreme Beyond, yet it also transcends that concept to exist as a unique, singular form within pure consciousness. This light is a perceivable presence in the highest spiritual state.

translit: navaveḷi nālvakai yāti - oru naṭuveḷik kuḷḷē naṭattiya nītic civaveḷi yāmitu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: It is the source of the nine spaces and the four kinds of being; it is the principle of order enacted within a central space. See it! This is the very Space of Siva. It is the Jothi of the sacred dance in the Thiru Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: The Light in the Thiru Chitrambalam is the source of the nine spaces and the four kinds of beings. Its justice is enacted within a central space, and that space is the Space of Siva (Siva veḷi). Vallalar asks us to see it. Each verse of the song ends in the same word, Jothi, the Light itself.

translit: mēruveṟ pucciyiṉ pālē - niṉṟu viḷaṅkumōr tampattiṉ mēlukku mēlē cērumōr mēṭaimēl pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: On the peak of Mount Meru, standing high above a shining pillar, see it upon a platform. It is the Jothi of the sacred dance in the Thiru Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: Vallalar places the vision at the summit: on the peak of Mount Meru, above a shining pillar, upon a platform. It is the highest point that can be named, and there, above everything, stands the same Light: the Jothi of the sacred dance in the Thiru Chitrambalam.

translit: āraṇa vītik kaṭaiyum - cutta ākama vītikaḷ antak kaṭaiyum cēra naṭukkaṭai pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: At the end of the street of the Vedas and at the end of the streets of the pure Agamas, see it in the central shop where they join. It is the Jothi of the sacred dance in the Thiru Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: The ultimate truth is not found by choosing one scripture over another, but at the point where all spiritual paths converge. Vallalar pictures the Vedas (ancient sacred hymns) and the Agamas (texts on ritual and philosophy) as streets leading to a central place. The divine light, the Jothi, is found in this inner space he calls Thiru Chitrambalam (the holy hall of consciousness), where all true teachings meet.

translit: pāṭal maṟaikaḷōr kōṭi - aruṭ pāta uruva corūpaṅkaḷ pāṭi tēṭa iruntatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: See that it was there, sought by ten million sung scriptures that sang of the forms and true natures of the feet of grace. It is the Jothi of the sacred dance in the Thiru Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: Innumerable scriptures have tried to capture the nature of God, describing divine forms and the experience of grace. Vallalar says that the very thing all these texts were searching for has always been this same reality: the divine light dancing within the space of consciousness.

translit: nīṭu civākamaṅ kōṭi - aruḷ nēruṟap pāṭiyum āṭiyum ōṭit tēṭa iruntatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: See, the very thing sought through singing, dancing, and running to directly attain grace, following millions of enduring Sivagamas (Saivite scriptures), is the Jothi of the sacred dance in the holy Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: The devotional path involves intense practices like singing hymns, ecstatic dancing, and going on pilgrimages, all in pursuit of divine grace. Vallalar reminds us that the goal of all this fervent activity is to arrive at the direct experience of the divine Jothi within the Chitrambalam, the inner hall of consciousness.

translit: patti neṟiyil ceḻittē - aṉpil pāṭumey yaṉpar patiyil paḻuttē tittit tiruppatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: See, flourishing in the path of devotion, ripening in the state of true devotees who sing with love, what is utterly sweet is the Jothi of the sacred dance in the holy Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: For those who live a life of sincere devotion (patti neṟi), their spiritual practice ripens into a state of pure love. The ultimate fruit of this love, he says, is the deeply sweet experience of the divine light.

translit: pittāṭu māyaikku mēlē - cuttap pirama veḷiyiṉil pēraru ḷālē cittāṭu kiṉṟatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: See, above the maddening dance of maya, in the pure space of Brahman, it performs its play of consciousness through great grace: the Jothi of the sacred dance in the holy Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: The ordinary world is governed by maya, the cosmic illusion that creates confusion and attachment. Vallalar points to a higher reality: a pure, open space of awareness he calls Brahman. It is in this clear space, far above worldly delusion, that the divine Jothi performs its dance of pure consciousness.

translit: taruneṟi ellāmuḷ vāṅkum - cutta caṉmārkkam eṉṟōr taṉippērkoṇ ṭōṅkum tiruneṟik kēceṉṟu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Go to that sacred path which absorbs all established ways and flourishes with the unique name Suddha Sanmarkkam, and see the Jothi of the sacred dance in the holy Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: The Suddha Sanmarkkam takes into itself all the paths that have been given, and rises with its own unique name. Vallalar says: go to this sacred path, and there see the divine light dancing in the hall of consciousness.

translit: emporuḷ emporuḷ eṉṟē - collum ellāc camayattuḷ ellārkkum oṉṟē cemporuḷ eṉpatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: See, for everyone in all the religions that proclaim, 'It is our Reality! Our Reality!', the one and only true Reality is the Jothi of the sacred dance in the holy Chitrambalam. Jothi.
commentary: While different religions may claim exclusive ownership of the ultimate truth, Vallalar says there is only one true Reality for all people. This single, universal truth is the divine light, the Jothi, accessible to everyone in the inner space of consciousness.

translit: caiva mutalāka nāṭṭum - pala camayaṅkaḷ ellām taṉittaṉik kāṭṭum teyvam ituvantu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Come and see this Deity, the one pointed to individually by all the established religions, beginning with Saivism. It is the Divine Dancing Light in Thiru Chitrambalam. Light. Light!
commentary: Every religion, beginning with Saivism (the worship of Siva), points toward the same ultimate divinity. Vallalar invites everyone to see that this single, universal God is the Divine Dancing Light in Thiru Chitrambalam, the sacred space of consciousness.

translit: eḷḷalil vāṉmutal maṇṇum - amu tellām itilōr iṟaiyaḷa veṉṉum teḷḷamu tāmitu pārīr -tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Come see this clear nectar, compared to which all the flawless nectars from heaven to earth are said to be just a tiny fraction. It is the Divine Dancing Light in Thiru Chitrambalam. Light. Light!
commentary: The experience of this divine light is a "clear nectar" of such supreme quality that even the most celebrated ambrosias of heaven and earth seem like a mere drop in comparison. It is the ultimate source of spiritual nourishment.

translit: ettālum ākātē ammā - eṉṟē ellā ulakum iyamputal cummā cettārai mīṭpatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: When all the worlds proclaim, "Oh, it is impossible by any means!", that is just empty talk. See it resurrect the dead! It is the Divine Dancing Light in Thiru Chitrambalam. Light. Light!
commentary: People often declare that some things, like overcoming death, are impossible. Vallalar dismisses this as empty talk. He states that the power of the divine light is so great it can even bring the dead back to life, demonstrating that nothing is impossible for divine grace.

translit: piṟantu piṟantuḻaṉ ṟēṉai - eṉṟum piṟavā tiṟavāp perumaitan tūṉaic ciṟantoḷir vittatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: See how it granted me, who wandered through birth after birth, the great glory of being without birth or death, and made my physical body shine with excellence. It is the Divine Dancing Light in Thiru Chitrambalam. Light. Light!
commentary: Divine grace accomplishes two things: it liberates the soul from the endless cycle of birth and death, and it transforms the physical body into a perfected, radiant vessel. Most spiritual paths aim to escape the body, but for Vallalar, true attainment involves the body itself becoming luminous with divine light.

translit: varuvitta vaṇṇamum nāṉē - inta mānilat tēceyum vaṇṇamum tāṉē terivit taruḷiṟṟup pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: See how it graciously revealed the purpose for which I was made to come, and the way it itself acts on this great earth. It is the Divine Dancing Light in Thiru Chitrambalam. Light. Light!
commentary: The encounter with the Divine Light reveals a person's unique purpose in life. It is an experience that brings absolute clarity, showing why one was born and how God is actively working in the world through them. The spiritual path becomes a guided mission.

translit: pāriṭam vāṉiṭa maṟṟum - iṭam paṟṟiya muttarkaḷ cittarkaḷ muṟṟum cēriṭa māmitu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Look! This is the gathering place for all the muttarkal and cittarkal who occupy the earthly realm, the celestial realm, and every other space. The sacred Dancing Jothi in the holy Chit Sabhai. Jothi.
commentary: The Divine Light is the universal destination for all perfected beings. The muttarkal (liberated ones) and the cittarkal (siddhas, masters with supernatural abilities) from every world all find their ultimate home in this singular, unifying Light. It is the common ground of all enlightened souls.

translit: uypiḷḷai paṟpalar āval - koṇṭē ulakat tiruppa:iṅ keṉṉaittaṉ ēval ceypiḷḷai ākkiṟṟup pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: While countless children desiring salvation wait in the world, look! It has made me its child who carries out its commands. The sacred Dancing Jothi in the holy Chit Sabhai. Jothi.
commentary: The speaker has been chosen to actively serve the divine will. While many people seek liberation for their own sake, grace has transformed him into an instrument for God's work on earth. This defines the highest spiritual state as one of active, loving service.

translit: uruvum uṇarvumcey naṉṟi - aṟi uḷamum eṉakkē utaviya taṉṟit tiruvum koṭuttatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Look! Besides granting me form, feeling, and a mind that knows gratitude, it also gave me divine wealth. The sacred Dancing Jothi in the holy Chit Sabhai. Jothi.
commentary: The divine gifts are the essentials for life, like a body and mind and the highest spiritual treasure. This "divine wealth" (tiru) refers to the priceless inner state of grace, bliss, and union with God.

translit: eṇṇiya eṇṇaṅkaḷ ellām - nāṉ eṇṇiya vāṟē iṉitutan teṉṉait tiṇṇiyaṉ ākkiṟṟup pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Look! It sweetly granted everything I envisioned, just as I envisioned it, and made me resolute. The sacred Dancing Jothi in the holy Chit Sabhai. Jothi.
commentary: When a person's intentions are fully aligned with the divine, their spiritual aspirations are fulfilled perfectly. This experience removes all doubt, creating a state of unshakeable inner resolve and certainty on the path.
