translit: pērula kellām matikkat - taṉ piḷḷaieṉ ṟeṉṉaip peyariṭ ṭaḻaittē cīruṟac ceytatu pārīr - tiruc ciṟṟam palattē tirunaṭa jōti. jōti
translation: Look! So that the great world would respect me, it named me "its child," called me so, and made me glorious. The sacred Dancing Jothi in the holy Chit Sabhai. Jothi.
commentary: God recognizes Vallalar as "its child" to make him a public witness to grace. The glory he receives is meant to inspire others, showing the world what is possible through divine connection.

translit: jōtiyuḷ jōtiyuḷ jōti - cutta jōti civajōti jōtiyuḷ jōti jōtiyuḷ jōtiyuḷ jōti.
translation: Light within Light within Light: the Pure Light, the Siva-Light, Light within Light, Light within Light within Light.
commentary: This verse is a cascade of pure adoration, trying to capture the infinite nature of God as Light (Jothi). By repeating "Light within Light," Vallalar describes a reality that is layered, boundless, and all-pervasive. This is the "Pure Light" (suddha jothi), the ultimate source, identified as "Siva-Light," the light of absolute grace and being.
NOTES
Note 317

tamil: ஈகின்றோம் ஈகின்றோம் ஈகின்றோம் என்றே - ச. மு. க.
translit: īkiṉṟōm īkiṉṟōm īkiṉṟōm eṉṟē - ca. mu. ka.
translation: īkiṉṟōm īkiṉṟōm īkiṉṟōm eṉṟē — reading of the S. Mu. Ka. Edition.

translit: añcā tē neñcē añcā tē añcā tē neñcē añcā tē.
translation: Do not fear, O heart, do not fear.
commentary: The poem opens with a simple, powerful command to the self. By repeating "Do not fear," Vallalar turns the phrase into a mantra, an active tool for calming the mind and training it to trust in a higher power rather than succumbing to anxiety.

tamil: அஞ்சலென் பார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: vañcami lārnāmvaruntiṭil appōtē añcaleṉ pāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: We are without guile. If we suffer, He who says, "Do not fear," is right here in the Ambalam at that very moment. Do not fear.
commentary: Divine protection is not something to be earned through complex rituals, but is instantly available to those with a sincere heart. For those who are "without guile," God's comforting presence is immediate, arriving the very moment suffering begins. The Ambalam (sacred hall) is this ever-present inner space where God resides, always ready to say, "Do not fear."

tamil: அய்யர் இதோதிரு வம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: tuyyar aruṭperuñ jōtiyār nammuṭai ayyar itōtiru vampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: The pure one, ArutPerunJothi, our Lord, is right here in the sacred Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The divine presence is the ultimate reality itself, which Vallalar calls ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light). The source of all grace and illumination is right here, within.

tamil: அண்ணல் இதோதிரு வம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: maṇṇil namaiyāṇṭa vaḷḷalār nammuṭai aṇṇal itōtiru vampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: The great benefactor who ruled us on this earth, our Lord, is right here in the sacred Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The God who is present is not a stranger. This verse describes an existing, personal relationship with a loving benefactor who has already taken charge of the devotee's life on earth, making His protection a lived reality.

tamil: அப்பர் இதோதிரு வம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: ippuvi yilnammai ēṉṟukoṇ ṭāṇṭanam appar itōtiru vampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: Our Father, who accepted and ruled us in this world, is right here in the sacred Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: Moving from benefactor to an even more intimate term, this verse calls the divine 'Father' (Appar). It deepens the sense of a personal, familial bond, assuring the heart that it has been lovingly accepted and cared for.

tamil: அத்தர் இதோதிரு வம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: cittar elāmvalla tēvar namaiyāṇṭa attar itōtiru vampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: The God who is the Siddhar capable of all things, the Father who has made us His own, is right here in the sacred Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: God is the Siddhar who can do all things, the Father who has already made us His own. This all-powerful One is present in the Ambalam, so the heart has nothing to fear.

tamil: ஆதி இதோதிரு வம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: cōti aruṭperuñ cōtiyār nammuṭai āti itōtiru vampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: The Jothi, the Vast Grace-Light, our Primal Source, is right here in the sacred Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: God's nature is Jothi, a divine light. This light is the primal source of all existence, and it is found within the inner hall of consciousness.

tamil: ஆண்டவ னார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: tāṇṭava ṉāreṉṉait tāṉtaṭut tāṭkoṇṭa āṇṭava ṉāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: The great Dancer, the Lord who intervened and made me His own, is right here in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The 'great Dancer' is a traditional name for God as the cosmic power that animates the entire universe. Vallalar says this same immense power is also the intimate, personal Lord who intervened in his life to grant grace, and this God is present within.

tamil: தன்பர் இதோதிரு வம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: vaṉpar maṉattai matiyā tavarnama taṉpar itōtiru vampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He who pays no heed to the minds of the hard-hearted, our Beloved, is right here in the sacred Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: God's presence is not found through a rigid intellect or a cold heart. To the 'hard-hearted', God is inaccessible. To the devoted, however, God is a tender 'Beloved' who is immediately present in the inner Ambalam.

tamil: அருளுடை யார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: teruḷuṭai yārelāñ ceyyaval lārtiru aruḷuṭai yāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: The one of perfect clarity, who is able to do all things, the possessor of sacred Grace, is right here in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The qualities we strive for, like perfect clarity and the power to accomplish all things, belong to God. This all-powerful being, the very source of Grace, resides within the inner space of the Ambalam.

tamil: தம்மை யினோடிதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: nammai āṭkoḷḷa naṭampuri vārnama tammai yiṉōṭitō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He who dances to make us His own is here in the Ambalam with our Mother. Do not fear.
commentary: The cosmic dance of God is a deeply personal act: He dances in order to claim each soul as His own. He is here in the Ambalam together with our divine Mother, so the heart need not fear.

tamil: அன்னைஒப் பார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: taṉṉaiop pārciṟ capainaṭañ ceykiṉṟār aṉṉaiop pāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He who has no equal performs the dance in the Chit Sabhai. He is like a mother. Look, He is in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The dance of the supreme, incomparable God happens within the Chit Sabhai, the sacred space of your own consciousness. Though peerless, His nature is as tender as a mother's, and His presence within you removes all cause for fear.

tamil: தாடுகின் றார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: pāṭukiṉ ṟārkkaruṭ paṇpiṉar ñāṉakkūt tāṭukiṉ ṟāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He is gracious to those who sing His praise. He performs the dance of wisdom. Look, He is in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The divine dance is revealed as the "dance of wisdom," an expression of ultimate truth. God bestows grace upon those who approach Him with simple, heartfelt praise, making this wisdom accessible to them.

tamil: ஆதரிப் பார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: kātarip pārkaṭkuk kāṭṭik koṭārnammai ātarip pāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He will not betray us to those who would harm us; He Himself will support us. Look, He is in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: This verse makes a powerful statement about divine protection. God will never hand us over to those who would harm us; He Himself is our direct support. Knowing this, the heart has no reason to fear.

tamil: ஆளவல் லார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: nīḷaval lārkkumēl nīḷavallār nammai āḷaval lāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He is great beyond the greatest; He is the one with the power to rule us. Look, He is in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The one who possesses supreme power is also the one who has the right to rule our lives. This is a comforting thought, not a frightening one, because His rule is an expression of benevolent guidance. Knowing this supreme, loving power is always present allows us to live without fear.

tamil: ரன்புடை யார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: iṉpuṭai yārnam itayat tamarntapē raṉpuṭai yāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He who is joy, He of great love who settled in our heart: here He is, in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The divine is an external reality in a temple and is the very joy and love residing within our own hearts. This verse unifies the inner and outer experience of God: the presence in the heart is the same presence in the sacred hall (Ambalam). Realizing this identity is the key to overcoming fear.

tamil: அபயர் இதோதிரு வம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: upaya patattainam uccimēṟ cūṭṭiya apayar itōtiru vampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: The one who grants fearlessness, who placed His two feet upon our head: here He is, in the sacred Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: True fearlessness is a gift of grace, not an act of human will. The image of the divine placing His feet on one's head is a traditional sign of the highest possible blessing and initiation. This intimate, personal act of grace comes from the same being who fills the universe, and its acceptance removes all fear.

tamil: ஆண்டுகொண் டார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: vēṇṭukoṇ ṭāreṉṉai mēlnilaik kēṟṟiyē āṇṭukoṇ ṭāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He who claimed me, raised me to a higher state, and made me His own: here He is, in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The relationship with the divine is deeply personal, and it changes the soul. God actively seeks out the soul, lifts it to a higher level of consciousness, and claims it as His own, an intimate act of grace that happens here and now in the Ambalam.

tamil: அச்சம் தவிர்த்தவர் அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: eccampe ṟēlmaka ṉēeṉṟeṉ ṉuḷuṟṟa accam tavirttavar ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He who dispelled the fear within me by saying, "Let nothing remain, my son": here He is, in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The command "Let nothing remain" is a call to empty the self of everything that is not pure consciousness: ego, past actions, and attachments. By heeding this inner voice, fear dissolves, and one finds the source of that voice present in the Ambalam.

tamil: அமுதர் இதோதிரு வம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: namutaṉ mutaṟpala naṉmaiyu māmñāṉa amutar itōtiru vampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: He who is the nectar of wisdom, our Origin and many other virtues: here He is, in the sacred Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The divine is the very essence of the "nectar of wisdom," a truth experienced as blissful and life-sustaining. This source of all existence and goodness is immediately present in the sacred Ambalam.

tamil: அடிகள் இதோதிரு வம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: ceṭikaḷ tavirttaruṭ celva maḷikkiṉṟa aṭikaḷ itōtiru vampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: The Master who removes impurities and grants the wealth of grace is right here in the sacred Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The spiritual path involves two actions: clearing away the inner obstacles or "impurities" that block our vision, and receiving the "wealth of grace" that is our true inheritance. The Master who guides this entire process is accessible right here in the sacred hall (Ambalam).

tamil: அரசுடை யார்இதோ அம்பலத் திருக்கின்றார் அஞ்சா தே
translit: viracula kellām virittain toḻiltarum aracuṭai yāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār añcā tē
translation: The Sovereign who unfurled all the bustling worlds and performs the five cosmic functions is right here in the Ambalam. Do not fear.
commentary: The supreme power that creates, sustains, and transforms all of existence is not a remote ruler. This cosmic sovereign, who performs the five great cosmic acts, is also present right here. The scale of God's power is vast, yet God's presence is intimate.

translit: ceṟivuṭai yāruḷat tēnaṭañ ceykiṉṟa aṟivuru vāritō ampalat tirukkiṉṟār
translation: The one whose form is Intelligence, who dances in the hearts of the deeply concentrated, is right here in the Ambalam.
commentary: God's true form is pure Intelligence. This divine intelligence is felt as a living, rhythmic movement, a "dance," within the consciousness of those who quiet their minds and focus deeply. This inner experience confirms the divine presence in the Ambalam.

translit: añcā tē neñcē añcā tē añcā tē neñcē añcā tē
translation: Do not fear, O heart, do not fear.
commentary: After reassuring the seeker that God is present as the source of good, the purifier, and the intelligence within, Vallalar addresses the heart directly. This repetition is like a mantra, a powerful and loving instruction to absorb the truth of divine nearness and release all anxiety.
NOTES
Note 293

tamil: வஞ்சமிலா நாம் - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு. பி. இரா. பதிப்பு.
translit: vañcamilā nām - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu. pi. irā. patippu.
translation: vañcamilā nām — reading of the first edition, Po. Su., P. Irā. Editions.

translit: itunalla taruṇam - aruḷceyya itunalla taruṇam.
translation: This is the right moment; this is the right moment to bestow grace.
commentary: This simple, powerful refrain declares that the opportunity for divine grace is immediate. It is not something to be earned over lifetimes or postponed to a future date. The poem begins by announcing that the perfect time for God to act, and for the soul to receive, is this very moment.

translit: potunalla naṭamvalla puṇṇiya rēkēḷum poyyētum colkilēṉ meyyē pukalkiṉṟēṉ. itunalla
translation: Oh, virtuous one, master of the good dance in the universal space, please listen! I am not telling any lies; I am speaking only the truth. This is the right moment.
commentary: Addressing God as the universal cosmic dancer, the speaker insists this is a statement of fact. This claim to truthfulness sets the stage for the dramatic changes described in the following verses.

translit: matitta camayamata vaḻakkellā māyntatu varuṇāc ciramameṉu mayakkamum cāyntatu kotitta lōkācārak kotippellām oḻintatu kolaiyum kaḷavumaṟṟaip pulaiyum aḻintatu. itunalla
translation: All the esteemed practices of religions and doctrines have vanished. The delusion called Varnashrama has collapsed. All the seething fury of worldly customs is gone. Killing, theft, and other base acts have been destroyed. This is the right moment.
commentary: A spiritual revolution has swept away the old world order. All divisions of religion and social caste (Varnashrama, the traditional social hierarchy) have been dismantled. With them, the violence and base behaviors they fostered have also disappeared, clearing the way for a new, unified existence.

translit: kuṟitta vētākamak kūccalum aṭaṅkiṟṟu kutittamaṉamuruṭṭuk kuraṅku muṭaṅkiṟṟu veṟittavev viṉaikaḷum ventu kulaintatu vintaicey koṭumāyaic cantaiyum kalaintatu. itunalla
translation: The clamor of the prescribed Vedas and Agamas has been silenced. The leaping, mischievous monkey of the mind has been crippled. Raging, fierce karmas are burned and ruined. The marketplace of cruel Maya that performs wonders has been dispersed. This is the right moment.
commentary: The internal world has been transformed as completely as the external one. The clamor of scripture (Vedas and Agamas), the restless monkey-mind, the weight of past actions (karmas), and the world of illusion (Maya) have all been silenced. This describes a state of absolute inner stillness and freedom, where the soul is no longer a victim of its own conditioning.

translit: kōpamum kāmamum kuṭikeṭṭup pōyiṟṟu koṭiyaōr āṅkāram poṭippoṭi āyiṟṟu tāpamum cōpamum tāṉtāṉē ceṉṟatu tattuvam ellāmeṉ ṟaṉvacam niṉṟatu. itunalla
translation: Anger and lust have been utterly ruined and have left. The cruel ego is ground to dust. Affliction and sorrow have departed on their own. All the tattvas have come under my control. This is the right moment.
commentary: The transformation is now complete, reaching the core of the self. Negative emotions like anger and lust are gone, the ego is annihilated, and all sorrow has ceased. The speaker has achieved total self-mastery, even gaining control over the tattvas, the fundamental principles that constitute one's own body and mind.

translit: karaiyā eṉatumaṉak kallum karaintatu kalantu koḷaṟkeṉ karuttum viraintatu puraiyā nilaiyileṉ puntiyum taṅkiṟṟu poypaṭāk kātal tatumpimēl poṅkiṟṟu.
translation: My unmelting, stone-like mind has melted. My mind has hastened to merge. My intellect has settled in a flawless state. Unfailing love has brimmed and surged.
commentary: After all the spiritual obstacles are cleared, the heart finally opens. The hard, resistant mind melts with a surge of pure, unfailing love for God. This emotional opening is the final and most needed step, making the soul ready to unite with the divine.

translit: itunalla taruṇam - aruḷceyya itunalla taruṇam.
translation: This is the right moment to bestow grace. This is the right moment.
commentary: This is a direct plea to God, stating that the soul is now perfectly prepared. Having achieved inner silence, self-mastery, and a heart full of love, the speaker declares that there could be no better moment for God to grant the ultimate gift of grace.
NOTES
Note 314

tamil: கொதித்த - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ சு, பி. இரா., ச. மு. க.
translit: kotitta - mutaṟpatippu., po cu, pi. irā., ca. mu. ka.
translation: kotitta — reading of the first edition, of Po. Su., of P. Irā., and of S. Mu. Ka.

tamil: என்ன புண்ணியம் செய்தே னோ - அம் மாநான்
translit: eṉṉa puṇṇiyam ceytē ṉō - am mānāṉ eṉṉa puṇṇiyam ceytē ṉō.
translation: What merit have I earned, O mother? What merit have I earned?
commentary: The experience of grace is so great that the first response is humility. The speaker questions what good deeds, or puṇṇiyam, they could have possibly performed to deserve such a blessing, feeling that their own merit is nothing compared to the gift received.

translit: maṉṉarnātar ampalavar vantārvantār eṉṟutiruc ciṉṉanātam eṉṉiraṇṭu cevikaḷiṉuḷ colkiṉṟatē. eṉṉa
translation: The sacred sound of the chinnam tells my two ears, "The Lord of kings, the Lord of the Stage, has come, he has come!"
commentary: The divine arrival is announced within the speaker's own consciousness. The sound of the chinnam, a sacred trumpet heralding a deity's presence, is heard internally. This reveals that God's coming is an intimate, personal experience, a direct communion with the "Lord of the Stage" within one's own being.

translit: poruḷnāṉ mukaṉumālum teruḷnāṉma ṟaiyunāḷum pōṟṟumciṟ ṟampalattē ēṟṟuma ṇiviḷakkāy aruḷnāṭa kampuriyum karuṇāni tiyaruṉṉai āḷavantār vantāreṉṟek kāḷanātam colkiṉṟatē. eṉṉa
translation: The sound of the ekkāḷam says, "The Treasury of Compassion, who performs the drama of grace as the lit gem-lamp in the sacred hall that Brahma, Vishnu, and the wise four Vedas praise daily, has come, he has come to rule you!"
commentary: Another trumpet blast reinforces the message, describing God as a "Treasury of Compassion" who stages a "drama of grace." This beautiful phrase suggests that God's actions in the world are a loving play, performed specifically for the soul's benefit. Even the highest gods like Brahma and Vishnu are just spectators to this personal event.

translit: pāṭiyanal lōrtamakkē nāṭiyatel lāmaḷippār pattivalai yuṭpaṭuvār cattiyarnit tiyarmaṉṟil āṭiyapoṟ pātarvētam tēṭiyaciṟ pōtaruṉṉai aṇaiyavantār vantāreṉṟē iṇaiyilnātam colkiṉṟatē. eṉṉa
translation: An incomparable music says, "He who gives the good people who sing to him all they desire, who is caught in the net of devotion, who is Truth, who is Eternal, the one with golden feet who danced in the hall, the teacher of pure consciousness whom the Vedas seek, has come, he has come to embrace you!"
commentary: God allows himself to be "caught in the net of devotion." Sincere love and singing are the way to reach him. The promise of his arrival grows more intimate, moving from a royal procession to a personal embrace.

translit: entaramuṭ koṇṭañāṉa cuntarareṉ maṇavāḷar ellāmcey vallacittar nallōr uḷattamarntār mantiramā maṉṟiliṉpam tantanaṭa rājaruṉṉai maruvavantār vantāreṉṟu teruvilnātam colkiṉṟatē. eṉṉa
translation: The music in the street says, "The beautiful one of wisdom who took my station into account, my bridegroom, the all-powerful Siddhar who resides in the hearts of the good, Natarajar, who gave bliss in the great hall of mantras, has come, he has come to unite with you!"
commentary: The relationship with God is now described with the most intimate language possible: he is the soul's bridegroom. This mystical tradition uses the metaphor of marriage to describe the complete and loving union of the soul with the divine. God is also called a Siddhar, a perfected master who has the power to do anything and who chooses to reside in the hearts of good people.

translit: ōtienta vitattālum vētiyaṉum tērvariyār ōṅkāra pañcakattē pāṅkāka naṭikkiṉṟār ātiyantam kāṇpariya jōticuyañ jōtiuṉṉō ṭāṭavantār vantāreṉṟē nāṭinātam colkiṉṟatē. eṉṉa
translation: He is unknowable by any means, even to the one who chants the Vedas. He dances gracefully within the five-fold Omkara (the sacred syllable AUM). He is the Jothi, the self-manifesting Jothi, whose beginning and end are impossible to see. The sound from the subtle channels declares that He has come, come to play with you. What is this?
commentary: The experience shifts from the outside world to the devotee's own body. The sound announcing God's arrival now comes from within, from the subtle energy channels known as nāḍi. The verse presents a stunning contrast: this vast, unknowable Jothi, or divine light, a being whose limits cannot be found, is coming for the simple, joyful purpose of playing with the devotee.

translit: aṟputappē raḻakāḷar coṟpatam kaṭantuniṉṟār aṉparelām toḻamaṉṟil iṉpanaṭam purikiṉṟār ciṟpararel lāmumvalla taṟparar viraintiṅkuṉṉaic cēravantār vantāreṉṟōṅ kāranātam colkiṉṟatē. eṉṉa
translation: He possesses miraculous, great beauty and stands beyond words and states. As all devotees worship, He performs the blissful dance in the sacred hall. The supreme consciousness, the self-dependent one who is all-powerful, has hurried here. The sound of Omkara declares that He has come, come to unite with you. What is this?
commentary: God is portrayed as both the absolute reality, beyond all words and concepts, and as an eager lover who "hurries" to unite with the soul. The sound of Omkara, the cosmic vibration of existence, becomes a personal message announcing the arrival of this all-powerful, self-sufficient, and supremely beautiful being for an intimate union.

translit: āraṇarnā raṇarellām pūraṇareṉ ṟēttukiṉṟa aiyartiru vampalavar meyyarellām vallacittar kāraṇamum kāriyamum tāraṇinī yāka:uṉṉaik kāṇavantār vantāreṉṟē vēṇunātam colkiṉṟatē. eṉṉa
translation: The Lord of the sacred hall, whom Brahma and Vishnu praise as the Complete One, is the Real One, the all-powerful Cittar. The flute's music declares that He has come, come to see you, as you yourself are the cause, the effect, and the foundation. What is this?
commentary: The Lord, who is worshipped as the ultimate reality even by great gods like Brahma and Vishnu, comes to the soul. A mystical flute's sound announces his arrival, but with a stunning revelation: he comes because the soul itself is recognized as the cause, the effect, and the very ground of being. The union with God is the discovery of one's own universal nature.

translit: pākārmoḻi yāḷciva mākāma vallināḷum pārttāṭa maṇimaṉṟil kūttāṭu kiṉṟacittar vākāuṉakkē eṉṟum cākā varaṅkoṭukka valiyavantār vantāreṉṟē valiyanātam colkiṉṟatē.
translation: As the honey-voiced Civakāmavalli watches daily, the Cittar dances in the gem-studded hall. The powerful sound declares that He has willingly come, come to fittingly grant you the boon of deathlessness.
commentary: God's arrival is a deliberate act of grace with a specific purpose: to grant the boon of deathlessness. He is the cosmic dancer, a perfected Cittar, and his consort Civakāmavalli (the embodiment of divine grace) is witness to this event. A powerful inner sound confirms that he has come of his own accord, driven by love, to bestow the ultimate gift of an immortal life.

tamil: என்ன புண்ணியம் செய்தே னோ - அம் மாநான்
translit: eṉṉa puṇṇiyam ceytē ṉō - am mānāṉ eṉṉa puṇṇiyam ceytē ṉō.
translation: What meritorious deeds have I done? O Mother, what meritorious deeds have I done?
commentary: In response to such an immense gift, the only possible feeling is overwhelming wonder and humility. The speaker cannot comprehend what merit could have earned this grace, capturing the soul's awe when touched by the Divine.

translit: varuvāra ḻaittuvāṭi vaṭalūr vaṭaticaikkē vantāṟ peṟalāmnalla varamē.
translation: Go bring Him here, to the north side of Vadalur. If He comes, we can receive a fine boon.
commentary: The soul's longing for God is given a specific, earthly location: Vadalur, the town where Vallalar established his spiritual center. The song begins with an urgent plea to bring the Lord to this very spot, confident that His arrival will bestow a great blessing.

translit: tiruvārpoṉ ṉampalattē ceḻikkuṅkuñ citapātar civacitam parapōtar teyvac capānātar varuvār
translation: The Lord with the thriving, lifted foot in the beautiful golden hall, the teacher of Siva-Cidambaram, the divine Master of the Hall, He will come.
commentary: The divine beloved is identified as Lord Siva, the cosmic dancer of Chidambaram. His "lifted foot" is a classic symbol of liberation and grace in Hindu iconography. By invoking this image, the poem connects the universal Lord with the personal, awaited beloved.

translit: cintai kaḷikkakkaṇṭu civāṉanta matuvuṇṭu teḷintōrel lārumtoṇṭu ceyyap pavurikoṇṭu inta veḷiyilnaṭa miṭattuṇin tīrēaṅkē itaiviṭap peruveḷi irukkuteṉ ṟāliṅkē varuvār
translation: The enlightened ones behold you to their mind's delight, drink the honey of Siva's bliss, and all serve you, whirling ecstatically; you have resolved to dance in that space there. If He is told, 'There is a space greater than this one,' He will come here.
commentary: This verse makes a bold and confident claim. It says that while God may dance elsewhere, if a place of even greater consciousness or devotion were to be found, He would immediately come "here." It is a declaration that the devotee's space, filled with blissful service, has become the supreme stage for the divine performance, a center of spiritual gravity God cannot resist.

translit: iṭukki lāmalirukka iṭamuṇṭu naṭañceyya iṅkam palamoṉṟaṅkē eṭṭam palamuṇṭaiya oṭukkil iruppateṉṉa uḷavukaṇṭu koḷvīreṉṉāl uṇmaiitu vañcamalla ummēl āṇaieṉṟucoṉṉāl varuvār
translation: If you say: "There is a place to dance without being cramped. Here there is one hall; there, there are eight halls, my Lord. Why stay in a confined space? Learn the secret from me. This is the truth, not a deception, I swear it on you", He will come.
commentary: The argument to persuade God becomes more direct, contrasting the "one hall" of the ancient temple with "eight halls" in a new, unconfined space. The soul urges God to move beyond old limitations, swearing an oath on God Himself to prove the sincerity of the offer. This reflects Vallalar's teaching that the divine presence can manifest in new centers of worship, like the one he established at Vadalur.

translit: melliyal civakāma valli yuṭaṉkaḷittu viḷaiyā ṭavumeṅkaḷ viṉaiō ṭavumoḷittu ellaiyil iṉpantaravum nallacama yantāṉitu iṅkumaṅkum naṭamāṭi irukkalām eṉṟapōtu varuvāra ḻaittuvāṭi vaṭalūr vaṭaticaikkē vantāṟ peṟalāmnalla varamē.
translation: This is the right time to rejoice and play with the slender Sivakāma Valli, to drive away our karma, and to grant limitless bliss. When you say, "You can dance both here and there," go bring Him here, to the north side of Vadalur. If He comes, we can receive a fine boon.
commentary: The poem's true destination is finally revealed: Vadalur, the community founded by Vallalar. The invitation is for God to dance with his divine consort, Sivakāma Valli (the embodiment of grace), in order to destroy the effects of past actions (karma) and grant limitless bliss to all. The "fine boon" they hope to receive is the ultimate gift of spiritual transformation.
NOTES
Note 313

tamil: உன்மேலாணை - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு., ச. மு. க.
translit: uṉmēlāṇai - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu., ca. mu. ka.
translation: uṉmēlāṇai — reading of the first edition, of Po. Su., and of S. Mu. Ka.

translit: ivarkkum eṉakkumperu vaḻakkiruk kiṉṟatatu eṉṟum tīrā vaḻakkuk kāṇa ṭi.
translation: Between Him and me there is a great dispute; it is a dispute that can never be settled, you see.
commentary: The relationship with God is framed as a "great dispute" that can never be settled. It is the tension of a deeply personal bond, with no anger in it. The soul feels entitled to make demands of God, refusing to settle for anything less than complete union.

translit: evarkkum periyavarpoṉ ṉampalat tēnaṭam iṭṭār eṉakkumālai iṭṭār itōvantār. ivarkkum
translation: The One greater than all, who dances in the Golden Hall, placed a garland on me. Now, here He has come!
commentary: The source of the "dispute" is an act of divine grace. God, the dancer in the Golden Hall (ponnambalam), has already singled out the soul by placing a garland on her, a traditional gesture of choosing or acceptance. Having been claimed by God, the soul now insists that He must fulfill the responsibilities that come with such a commitment.

translit: aṉṟitō varukiṉṟēṉ eṉṟu pōṉavaraṅkē yārceyta taṭaiyālō iruntāreṉ kaiyiṟcaṅkai iṉṟutam kaiyiṟkoṇṭē vantuniṟ kiṉṟāriṅkē intak katavaimūṭu ivarpōva tiṉieṅkē. ivarkkum
translation: He who left that day saying, "I will be right back," stayed away, who knows what detained Him? Today He stands here, holding in His own hand the conch-shell bangle that slipped from my arm. Shut this door! Where can He possibly go now?
commentary: She playfully scolds God for His long absence and is now determined to keep Him from leaving again. In Tamil love poetry the conch-shell bangles slip from the arms of a woman wasting away in separation; now her Beloved stands before her holding the very bangle she lost, the proof of her long longing. The command to "shut this door" is the soul's cry to make the meeting permanent.

translit: avaravar ulakattē aṟintalar tūṟṟappaṭṭēṉ aṉṟupō ṉavariṉṟu vantuniṟ kiṉṟārkeṭṭēṉ ivarcūtai aṟiyātē muṉṉam ēmāntuviṭṭēṉ intak katavaimūṭu iṉieṅkum pōkaoṭṭēṉ. ivarkkum
translation: Everyone in the world found out, and I became the subject of gossip. I am ruined! The one who left that day is standing here today. Not knowing His cunning, I was deceived before. Shut this door! I will not let Him go anywhere now.
commentary: The soul's intense devotion often appears as madness to the outside world, and she has suffered the world's gossip because of her single-minded longing for God. She calls Him cunning, a term of endearment in this context, acknowledging the divine play that caused her pain. Having been hurt by His absence once, she refuses to be vulnerable again.

translit: ciṉṉa vayatileṉṉaic cērntārpuṉ ṉakaiyōṭu ceṉṟār tayavāliṉṟu vantār ivarkkārīṭu eṉṉaiviṭ ṭiṉiivar eppaṭip pōvārōṭu intak katavaimūṭu iraṭṭaittāṭ kōlaippōṭu. ivarkkum
translation: He united with me in my youth and left with a gentle smile. By His grace, He has come today. Who is His equal? How can He possibly leave me now? Run! Shut this door! Slide the double bolt.
commentary: The union in her "youth" refers to the soul's first taste of divine love, a memory she now uses to hold God to His commitment. The command to shut the door and to "slide the double bolt" shows the absolute finality she seeks. Her frantic joy and determination reveal a soul that will do anything to preserve its reunion with God.

translit: ivarkkum eṉakkumperu vaḻakkiruk kiṉṟatatu eṉṟum tīrā vaḻakkuk kāṇa ṭi.
translation: Between him and me, there is a great dispute. It is a case that will never be settled, you see, friend.
commentary: This refrain brings the song back to its central theme: the loving "dispute" with God. It emphasizes that the entire drama of separation and reunion is the very nature of their eternal relationship.

translit: āṭiya pātamaṉ ṟāṭiya pātam āṭiya pātaniṉ ṟāṭiya pātam.
translation: The dancing feet, the feet that danced that day. The dancing feet, the feet that stand and dance.
commentary: This opening verse establishes the timeless nature of God's dance. The feet are both part of a specific, foundational event in the past ("that day") and an eternal, ongoing reality ("the feet that stand and dance"). Divine action is both a historical anchor and a continuous, living presence.

translit: pāṭiya vētaṅkaḷ tēṭiya pātam patticey pattarkkut tittikkum pātam nāṭiya mātavarnēṭiya pātam nātānta nāṭṭukku nāyaka pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet sought by the chanted Vedas, the feet sweet to devotees who practice devotion, the feet sought by great pursuing ascetics, the feet that are the Master of the land of Nādānta.
commentary: God's feet are the ultimate goal for every kind of spiritual seeker. They are sought by scholars chanting the ancient scriptures (Vedas), by simple people filled with love (bhakti), and by advanced yogis pursuing the supreme state of consciousness beyond all sound, known as Nādānta.

translit: tīrāta valviṉai tīrkkiṉṟa pātam teyvaṅkaḷ ellān tericikkum pātam vārā varavāki vantapoṟ pātam vañca maṉattil vaciyāta pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that resolve incurable, powerful karma, the feet that all the gods come to behold, the golden feet that arrived as an unhoped-for blessing, the feet that do not yield to a deceitful mind.
commentary: These divine feet have the power to liberate the soul, dissolving even the most difficult and seemingly incurable effects of past actions (karma). Their arrival in one's life is an unexpected gift of grace, but this gift cannot be forced or claimed by a deceitful mind; it is available only to a sincere heart.

translit: ārā amutāki aṇṇikkum pātam aṉpar uḷattē amarntaruḷ pātam nārā yaṇaṉviḻi naṇṇiya pātam nāṉpuṉai pāṭal nayantapoṟ pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that draw near as an insatiable nectar, the feet that graciously settle in the hearts of devotees, the feet that reached the eye of Narayanan, the golden feet that delighted in the songs I composed.
commentary: The power of the divine feet spans from the cosmic to the intimately personal. They are revered by other great gods, such as Narayanan (Vishnu), yet they also become a sweet, insatiable nectar within the heart of an individual devotee, taking personal delight in the simple songs the poet offers.

translit: nallavar ellām nayakkiṉṟa pātam nāta muṭivil naṭikkiṉṟa pātam vallavar collellām vallapoṟ pātam mantira yantira tantira pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that all good people desire, the feet that dance at the culmination of sound, the golden feet capable of all that the masters proclaim, the feet that are mantra, yantra, and tantra.
commentary: The divine feet represent the ultimate goal sought by all good people and the final reality experienced at the peak of meditation on sacred sound. Vallalar makes a striking statement here: the feet are the object of worship and the very tools of worship themselves. They are the sacred utterance (mantra), the mystical diagram (yantra), and the spiritual technique (tantra), embodying the path and the destination in one.

translit: eccama yattum ilaṅkiya pātam eḷḷukkuḷ eṇṇeypōl eṅkumām pātam accam tavirtteṉṉai āṭkoṇṭa pātam āṉanta nāṭṭuk katipati pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that shine in every religion, the feet that are everywhere like oil in a sesame seed, the feet that removed my fear and took me as their own, the feet of the Sovereign of the land of bliss.
commentary: The divine is universally present, shining within every religion. The image of oil within a sesame seed is a classic way of describing God's nature: present everywhere within creation, yet hidden until you make the effort to find it. For Vallalar, this universal God became intensely personal, a savior who banished his fear and made him feel completely accepted. These feet are the gateway to a state of pure bliss.

translit: tēvarkaḷ ellārum cintikkum pātam teḷḷamu tāyuḷan tittikkum pātam mūvarum kāṇā muḻumutaṟ pātam muppāḻuk kappāl muḷaittapoṟ pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that all the celestial beings contemplate, the feet that sweeten the mind like clear ambrosia, the feet of the absolute source unseen by the Three, the golden feet that sprouted beyond the three voids.
commentary: The divine reality is so deep that even celestial beings are lost in contemplation of it. It is the absolute source, which Vallalar says is beyond the comprehension of "the Three," the gods of creation, preservation, and dissolution (Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra). By placing this source "beyond the three voids," he points to a state that transcends even the highest mystical experiences of emptiness, a reality beyond all concepts.

translit: turiya veḷikkē uriyapoṟ pātam cukamaya mākiya cuntarap pātam periya poruḷeṉṟu pēcumpoṟ pātam pēṟellān tanta perumpukaḻp pātam. āṭiya
translation: The golden feet that belong to the space of Turiya, the beautiful feet that are the embodiment of happiness, the golden feet spoken of as the Great Substance, the feet of great fame that gave all blessings.
commentary: These feet belong to Turiya, a state of pure consciousness beyond waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. They are happiness itself. Vallalar describes them as the "Great Substance," the fundamental reality that underlies everything in existence. All spiritual attainment and every possible blessing flow from this single source.

translit: cākā varantanta tārakap pātam caccitā ṉanta catōtaya pātam tēkāti ellām ciruṭṭikkum pātam titimutal aintoḻil ceykiṉṟa pātam. āṭiya
translation: The guiding feet that granted the boon of immortality, the feet of Satchitananda, eternally arisen, the feet that create the body and all else, the feet that perform the five functions beginning with sustenance.
commentary: The ultimate promise of the divine feet is the boon of immortality (sākā varam), a central goal of Vallalar's path. They are also identified with Satchitananda (being, consciousness, and bliss), a classic description of the Absolute. Furthermore, they are the power that performs the five cosmic functions (creation, sustenance, dissolution, concealment, and grace), showing they represent God's total and active power in the universe.

translit: ōṅkāra pīṭat toḷirkiṉṟa pātam oṉṟāy iraṇṭāki ōṅkiya pātam tūṅkāta tūkkattil tūkkiya pātam turiyattil ūṉṟit tulaṅkiya pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that shine on the pedestal of Omkara, the feet that became one and two and grew exalted, the feet held aloft in the sleepless sleep, the feet firmly planted in Turiya, shining brightly.
commentary: This verse describes the divine presence using metaphors of sound and consciousness. The feet rest upon Omkara, the primordial sound of 'Om' from which the universe unfolds. They also embody the mystery of the absolute One becoming the duality of the manifest world. The "sleepless sleep" is a yogic term for a state of deep meditation, a lucid awareness that remains when the ordinary mind is silent.

translit: aivaṇṇa muṅkoṇṭa aṟputap pātam apayarellārkkum amutāṉa pātam kaivaṇṇa nellik kaṉiyākum pātam kaṇṇum karuttum kalantapoṟ pātam. āṭiya
translation: The wondrous feet possessing five colors, the feet that are nectar to all who seek refuge, the feet that become a truth as plain as a fruit in the hand, the golden feet where eye and mind have mingled. Dancing.
commentary: The experience of God is described as both mystical ("five colors") and completely tangible. The Tamil idiom of a "fruit in the hand" (kaivaṇṇa nellik kani) means a truth that is undeniable and self-evident. In the end, devotion leads to a state where the separation between seeing and knowing dissolves, and the divine is perceived directly, without the filter of the mind.

translit: āruyirk kātāram ākiya pātam aṇṭa piṇṭaṅkaḷ aḷikkiṉṟa pātam cāruyirk kiṉpam tarukiṉṟa pātam cattiya ñāṉa tayāniti pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that are the foundation for precious lives, the feet that give forth the macrocosms and microcosms, the feet that grant bliss to the souls who draw near, the feet that are the compassionate treasure of truth and knowledge. Dancing.
commentary: The divine is the very source of all existence, creating and sustaining everything from individual beings ('microcosms') to entire universes ('macrocosms'). This creative power is not a cold, mechanical force, but a loving presence that bestows bliss on all who approach it. God is the foundation of life and a treasure of compassionate wisdom.

translit: tāṅki eṉaippeṟṟa tāyākum pātam tantaiyu mākit tayavucey pātam ōṅkieṉ ṉuḷḷē uṟaikiṉṟa pātam uṇmai viḷaṅka uraittapoṟ pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that are the mother who bore and sustained me, the feet that also became the father and showed grace, the feet that rise high and dwell within me, the golden feet that spoke to make the truth clear. Dancing.
commentary: The divine presence is described in the most intimate terms: as a nurturing mother, a gracious father, and a teacher who reveals truth. This is not a distant, abstract God, but a loving parent who sustains us and, at the same time, dwells within our own heart.

translit: eṇṇiya vāṟē eṉakkaruḷ pātam iṟavā nilaiyil iruttiya pātam puṇṇiyar kaiyuḷ poruḷākum pātam poyyar uḷattil poruntāta pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that grant me grace just as I wished, the feet that established me in the deathless state, the feet that are the treasure held in the hands of the virtuous, the feet that will not settle in the hearts of the false. Dancing.
commentary: The divine feet have granted Vallalar grace exactly as he longed for it, and he says plainly that they have established him in the deathless state (iṟavā nilai). This is his own attainment, here and now. For the virtuous these feet are a treasure held in the hand; in the hearts of the false they will not settle.

translit: āṟantat tuḷḷum amarntapoṟ pātam āti aṉātiyum ākiya pātam māṟantam illāeṉ vāḻmutaṟ pātam maṇmutal aintāy vaḻaṅkiya pātam. āṭiya
translation: The golden feet seated within all six Antas, the feet that are both the beginning and the beginningless, the feet that are the source of my unchanging and endless life, the feet that manifested as the five elements starting with earth. Dancing.
commentary: The six Antas (āṟantam) are the six culminations of spiritual knowledge: Vedānta, Siddhānta, Bodhānta, Nādānta, Yogānta and Kalānta. The divine feet are seated within all of them. They are the source of everything, yet themselves without a source; they became the five elements, and they are the wellspring of Vallalar's life that knows neither change nor end.

translit: aruṭperuñ jōtiya tākiya pātam ammaiyum appaṉum ākiya pātam poruṭperum pōkam puṇarttiya pātam poṉvaṇṇa mākiya puṇṇiya pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that are the Vast Grace-Light, the feet that are both mother and father, the feet that bestowed the great bliss of Reality, the sacred feet that are the color of gold. Danced.
commentary: Here, the Lord's feet are identified with the ultimate divine reality itself, the ArutPerunJothi (Vast Grace-Light). They are also called both mother and father, expressing the idea that God is the complete and perfect source of all being, containing both masculine and feminine principles.

translit: nāraṇa ṉātiyar nāṭarum pātam nāṉtavat tāṟpeṟṟa naṟṟuṇaip pātam āraṇam ākamam pōṟṟiya pātam ācaiviṭ ṭārkkē aṇimaiyām pātam. āṭiya
translation: The feet that Narayanan and the other gods find hard to reach, the feet of the good companion I gained through my penance, the feet praised by the Āraṇam and the Āgamas, the feet that are near only to those who have renounced desire. Danced.
commentary: Even the highest gods, like Narayanan (Vishnu), seek these feet, yet they are closest to humans who have freed themselves from desire. Praise from the holiest scriptures, the Āraṇam (Vedas) and the Āgamas, is good, but inner renunciation is what truly brings you near to God.

translit: āṭiya pātamaṉ ṟāṭiya pātam āṭiya pātaniṉ ṟāṭiya pātam.
translation: The danced feet, the feet that danced that day. The danced feet, the feet that danced standing still.
commentary: God's dance is both action and stillness. This verse captures a paradox: the Lord's feet are in constant, creative motion, yet the dancer at the center of that motion is eternally still and unchanging.
NOTES
Note 294

translit: mātavaṉ - ā. pā. pātippu.
translation: mātavaṉ — reading of the Ā. Pā. edition. (The Tamil prints pātippu here for patippu, "edition" — evidently a misprint.)
Note 295

translit: aiyar - ca. mu. ka. patippu.
translation: aiyar — reading of the S. Mu. Ka. edition.

translit: apayam apayam apayam.
translation: Refuge, refuge, refuge.
commentary: The poem begins with a pure and simple plea for sanctuary. Repeating apayam (refuge) three times is an act of total surrender, placing all trust and hope in the divine presence before any qualities of that presence are even named.

translit: upayama tāyeṉ uṟavāyc citamparac capaiyil naṭañceyum cāmi patattiṟkēapayam
translation: To the very feet of the Lord who dances in the Hallof Chidambaram, who is both mother and father to me, my kin: refuge.
commentary: God is found in the sacred dance at Chidambaram, and this cosmic Lord is near. Vallalar approaches God as his closest family, his own mother and father. Refuge is sought in the feet of a beloved relative.

translit: empalat tālemmai ēṉṟuko ḷattillai ampalat tāṭumem aiyar patattiṟkē apayam
translation: To the feet of our Master who dances in the Hall of Thillai, who accepts us as our own strength: refuge.
commentary: Thillai is another name for the sacred space of Chidambaram. This verse expresses a beautiful idea about grace: God accepts us on the basis of our own small strength. Our own effort, however limited, is enough for him.

translit: tavacitam paramākit taṉmaya māycceyum civacitam paramakā tēvar patattiṟkē apayam
translation: To the feet of the Great God, Siva of Chidambaram, who makes the consciousness of our spiritual discipline supreme and absorbs us into Himself: refuge.
commentary: Here, refuge is sought in God as the one who brings spiritual practice to its conclusion. The goal is for our own limited consciousness to be raised and finally absorbed into God's own being. This union is the highest fruit of devotion.

translit: oṉṟum patattiṟ kuyarporu ḷākiyē eṉṟumeṉ uḷḷat tiṉikkum patattiṟkē apayam
translation: To the feet of Him who has become the supreme substance of the state of union, feet that are eternally sweet in my heart: refuge.
commentary: The ultimate goal of "union" with God is more than a philosophical idea. Vallalar describes it as a state of constant, felt sweetness within his own heart. The divine feet are both the path to the highest state of consciousness and a source of intimate, personal joy.

translit: vāṉanta māntillai maṉṟiṭai eṉṟuniṉ ṟāṉantat tāṇṭava māṭum patattiṟkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the feet that forever stand in the great hall of Tillai, which is the vast expanse of space, and perform the dance of bliss.
commentary: The sacred space of the Tillai temple is expanded to mean the entire cosmos. God's creative and joyful energy, symbolized by the "dance of bliss," is happening everywhere and always, throughout the vastness of the universe.

translit: nārā yaṇaṉoṭu nāṉmuka ṉātiyar pārā yaṇamceyum patuma patattiṟkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the lotus feet that Narayana, Nanmugan, and others praise.
commentary: By naming Narayana (the preserver god, Vishnu) and Nanmugan (the creator god, Brahma) as fellow worshippers, Vallalar shows that the God he seeks is the supreme source. This Being is the ultimate reality, adored even by the great gods of the Hindu tradition.

translit: aṉpar ceyumpiḻai āyira mumpoṟut tiṉpa maḷikkunam īcar patattiṟkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the feet of our Lord, who forgives the thousands of faults his devotees commit and grants them bliss.
commentary: This verse expresses a deep trust in God's merciful nature. He is not a stern judge waiting for us to make a mistake, but a loving Lord who willingly forgives countless faults and responds to devotion with bliss.

translit: kuṟṟam ceyiṉum kuṇamākak koṇṭunam aṟṟam tavirkkunam appar patattiṟkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the feet of our Father, who, even when we commit wrongs, accepts them as virtues and protects us from ruin.
commentary: Divine forgiveness here is so absolute that it reinterprets our very failings. God, as a loving Father, does overlook our wrongs and has the power to see them as virtues, protecting us from the ruin our own actions might cause.

translit: cemporuḷ ākic citamparat tēeṉṟum namporuḷ āṉa naṭēcar patattiṟkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the feet of Natesar, who is the ultimate reality and, in Chidambaram, has forever become our own true treasure.
commentary: The ultimate reality of the cosmos, Natesar (the dancing form of Siva), is not a distant, abstract principle. In the sacred space of Chidambaram, which represents the heart or consciousness, that ultimate truth becomes a personal, intimate treasure for every soul.

translit: vecceṉṟa māyai viṉaiyāti yālvanta accam tavirkkunam aiyar patattiṟkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the feet of our Master, who averts the fear that comes from scorching māyā, karma, and the rest.
commentary: The fundamental anxieties of life arise from māyā (the illusion of separateness) and karma (the consequences of past actions). Taking refuge in God is the way to be free from the fear these forces generate.

translit: eṇṇiya eṇṇaṅkaḷ ellā muṭikkunam puṇṇiya ṉārteyvap poṉṉaṭip pōtukkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the divine, golden, flower-like feet of our Virtuous One, who brings to completion all the thoughts we think.
commentary: When one's mind is turned toward God, divine power helps bring one's intentions to fruition. Surrender allows a greater force to work through one's own will, ensuring that what is desired in alignment with the divine comes to pass.

translit: maṉṉam parattē vaṭivil vaṭivākip poṉṉam palattāṭum poṉṉaṭip pōtukkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the golden, flower-like feet that dance in the Golden Hall, becoming the form within the form in the eternal expanse.
commentary: God is the subtle essence within all created things, the inner reality that gives shape to every outer form. This divine essence is revealed in the dance at the Golden Hall of Chidambaram, a symbol for the center of consciousness where the eternal presence can be witnessed.

translit: nāta muṭiyilnaṭampurin taṉparkkup pōtam aḷikkiṉṟa poṉṉaṭip pōtukkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the golden, flower-like feet that perform the dance at the pinnacle of Natham, granting wisdom to devotees.
commentary: Natham refers to the primordial sound or vibration, the subtle source from which the universe arises. By dancing at this ultimate level of reality, God is said to generate and transmit true spiritual wisdom (pōtam) to devotees.

translit: ucci tāḻkiṉṟa uṟavōr uṟavāṉa cacci tāṉantat taṉinaṭap pōtukkē apayam
translation: Refuge in the unique, flower-like dancing foot of Satchitānanda, the kin of the kindred, which makes the head bow down.
commentary: Satchitānanda describes God's nature as absolute being (sat), consciousness (chit), and bliss (ānanda). Vallalar calls this reality the "kin of the kindred," our most intimate and true relation, whose presence inspires a natural and spontaneous reverence.

translit: cittamum uḷḷamum tittit tiṉikkiṉṟa puttamu tākiya poṉṉaṭip pōtukkē apayam
translation: Refuge at the golden flower-feet, the fresh ambrosia that sweetens the mind and heart.
commentary: The experience of the divine is described as a fresh ambrosia (puttamutu) that is deeply sweet. This refers to a tangible, joyful transformation of one's inner world, filling the mind and heart with an overwhelming sense of delight.

translit: apayam apayam apayam.
translation: Refuge, refuge, refuge.
commentary: The simple repetition of "refuge" is an act of ultimate surrender. It is a cry from the soul that has abandoned all other supports and places its entire trust and being in the divine alone.
NOTES
Note 296

translit: pātattiṟkē - pi. irā., ā. pā.
translation: pātattiṟkē — reading of the P. Irā. and Ā. Pā. editions.
Note 297

tamil: முடிவில் - முதற்பதிப்பு., பொ. சு., ச. மு. க.
translit: muṭivil - mutaṟpatippu., po. cu., ca. mu. ka.
translation: muṭivil — reading of the first edition, of Po. Su., and of S. Mu. Ka.

translit: aṟputam aṟputa mē - aruḷ aṟputam aṟputa mē.
translation: A miracle, a miracle! A miracle of grace, a miracle!
commentary: The song opens by declaring that what is happening is a miracle brought about by divine grace. This establishes that the changes described are a direct and astonishing gift from God.

translit: ciṟpatam poṟpatañ cīrē ciṟantatu cittāṭu kiṉṟa tirunāḷ piṟantatu kaṟpata neñcak karicu tuṟantatu kaṟṟapoyn nūlkaḷ kaṇattē maṟantatu aṟputam
translation: The state of consciousness, the golden state, has reached its magnificent peak. The sacred day when Siddhas play has dawned. My stony heart has cast off its impurities. The false scriptures I had learned were forgotten in an instant. A miracle!
commentary: A great spiritual age has begun, a time when perfected beings, or Siddhas, can act freely in the world. This new reality brings personal transformation: the hard, resistant heart becomes pure, and knowledge from misleading books is instantly forgotten, replaced by direct, true experience.

translit: cettār eḻukiṉṟa tirunāḷ aṭuttatu civaneṟi oṉṟē eṅkumtalai eṭuttatu ittā raṇimutal vāṉum uṭuttatu iṟavā varantāṉ eṉakkuk koṭuttatu aṟputam
translation: The sacred day for the dead to rise has arrived. The path of Siva alone has prevailed everywhere. This earth and the sky above are newly clothed. I have been granted the boon of never dying. A miracle!
commentary: The miracle extends to the entire world. Vallalar announces that the day has come when the dead will rise; he means it plainly, as he proclaims again in 'Sound the Trumpet': the dead will rise, on this very earth. The path of Siva, the path of truth, now prevails everywhere, and earth and sky are clothed anew. For himself, Vallalar declares the boon he has received: never to die.

translit: āṉanta nāṭakam āṭutal cārntatu aṭutta taruṇam ituvāka nērntatu īṉanta māyai iruḷviṉai cōrntatu eṉṉaruṭ cōtieṉ uḷḷattil ārntatu aṟputam
translation: The blissful drama has begun to unfold. The opportune moment has arrived right now. Vile Māyā and the darkness of karma have weakened. My Jothi of grace has filled my heart. A miracle!
commentary: The spiritual breakthrough is the start of a "blissful drama" orchestrated by God. At this perfect moment, the old forces that cause suffering, like Māyā (cosmic illusion) and the darkness of past karma, simply fade away. They are replaced by the radiant inner presence of Jothi, the divine light of grace.

translit: cattiya ñāṉa capaieṉṉuḷ kaṇṭaṉaṉ caṉmārkka cittiyai nāṉpeṟṟuk koṇṭaṉaṉ nittiya ñāṉa niṟaiyamu tuṇṭaṉaṉ nintai ulakiyaṟ cantaiyai viṇṭaṉaṉ aṟputam
translation: I have perceived the Sattiya Gnana Sabai within me. I have obtained the siddhi of the Sanmarkkam. I have consumed the full nectar of eternal wisdom. I have left behind the contemptible marketplace of worldly life. A miracle!
commentary: Vallalar sees the Sattiya Gnana Sabai (Hall of True Wisdom) within himself; the Hall he raised at Vadalur stands first as this inner reality. Seeing it is the true siddhi of the Sanmarkkam. He has drunk the full nectar of eternal wisdom and has left behind the contemptible marketplace of worldly life.

translit: vañcakar añciṉar vāymūṭic ceṉṟaṉar vantu tirumpavum vāyilil niṉṟaṉar tañcam emakkaruḷ cāminī eṉṟaṉar caṉmārkka caṅkat tavarkaḷē veṉṟaṉar aṟputam
translation: The deceitful grew fearful, shut their mouths, and left. They came back and stood at the gate. They said, "O Lord, you are our refuge, grant us grace." The people of the Sanmarkkam Sangam have triumphed. A miracle!
commentary: The triumph of truth has a deep effect on its opponents. Those who were once deceitful and critical are silenced by its power. Humbled, they return to the very gate they once scorned, now begging for refuge and grace. The victory of the Sanmarkkam Sangam (the fellowship of the true path) is won by truth alone.

translit: puṟaṅkūṟi ṉārellām pulleṉap pōyiṉar poṟpaṭik kīḻppuṟa mīḷavu mēyiṉar maṟaṅkūṟi ṉōmeṉcey vōmeṉṟu kūyiṉar vāḻiya eṉṟucol vāyiṉar āyiṉar aṟputam
translation: All who slandered others have faded into insignificance. They have returned to linger below the golden step. They cried out, "We spoke with cruelty, what can we do?" Their mouths have become ones that say, "May you live long!" A miracle!
commentary: Even those who spoke slander and cruelty are transformed by this spiritual event. Realizing the error of their harsh words, their arrogance vanishes, and they are left crying out in regret. Their transformation is so complete that their mouths, once used for criticism, now offer blessings.

translit: vevviṉaik kāṭelām vēroṭu ventatu veyya māmāyai virivaṟṟu nontatu cevviya ñāṉam ciṟappuṟa vantatu cittikaḷ yāvaiyum ceytiṭat tantatu aṟputam
translation: The entire forest of cruel karma has burned away, roots and all. Fierce, great Maya has lost its reach and withered. Perfect wisdom has arrived in its full splendor. It has granted the power to perform all siddhis. A miracle!
commentary: The arrival of divine grace has a cleansing effect on the soul. It erases the accumulated effects of past negative actions (karma) and dissolves the cosmic illusion (māyā) that obscures reality. This inner purification brings forth perfect wisdom and unlocks siddhis, or spiritual powers.

translit: cāti camayac caḻakkelām aṟṟatu caṉmārkka ñāṉa capainilai peṟṟatu mētiyiṟ cākāta vittaiyaik kaṟṟatu meyyaruṭ cōtieṉ uḷḷattil uṟṟatu aṟputam
translation: All the falsehood of caste and religion is gone. The Sanmarkkam Hall of Wisdom is firmly established. The art of not dying in this world has been learned. The Jothi of true grace has entered my heart. A miracle!
commentary: This verse summarizes what the Sanmarkkam path brings. The whole falsehood (saḻakku) of caste and religion falls away: Vallalar does not say their quarrels end, he says the deceit itself is gone. The art of not dying on this earth is learned, deathlessness of the body itself, and the true Grace-Light, the Jothi, comes to dwell within the heart.

translit: aṟputam aṟputa mē - aruḷ aṟputam aṟputa mē.
translation: A miracle, a miracle indeed! Grace! A miracle, a miracle indeed!
commentary: After describing the transformations brought by grace, the only response left is pure, ecstatic wonder. This is a simple, heartfelt cry of devotion, expressing awe that is beyond words.

sections.title: The Vision of the Hall of Pure Gold

translit: āṇippoṉ ṉampalat tēkaṇṭa kāṭcikaḷ aṟputak kāṭciya ṭi - ammā aṟputak kāṭciya ṭi.
translation: The sights I saw in the Hall of Pure Gold were a wondrous sight, O mother, a wondrous sight.
commentary: The "Hall of Pure Gold" is the Ambalam, the sacred inner space of consciousness where the divine is experienced. Entering this space is an inward pilgrimage. The devotee begins to share this deeply personal and miraculous vision with a confidant, addressed familiarly as "mother."

translit: jōti malaioṉṟu tōṉṟiṟ ṟatiloru vītiuṇ ṭāccuta ṭi - ammā vītiuṇ ṭāccuta ṭi. āṇi
translation: A mountain of Jothi appeared. On it, a path came into being, O mother, a path came into being.
commentary: The spiritual path begins with an encounter with Jothi, or divine light. This isn't just a vague brightness; it's a substantive reality, a "mountain" of light. Out of this overwhelming brilliance, a clear path emerges, suggesting that the divine itself provides the way for the seeker to approach.

translit: vītiyil ceṉṟēṉav vīti naṭuoru mēṭai iruntata ṭi - ammā mēṭai iruntata ṭi. āṇi
translation: I went along the path. In the middle of that path was a platform, O mother, a platform was there.
commentary: Progress on the spiritual path leads to a specific, elevated stage, described here as a platform. This marks a new level of attainment on the way toward the center of the vision.

translit: mēṭaimēl ēṟiṉēṉ mēṭaimēl aṅkoru kūṭam iruntata ṭi - ammā kūṭam iruntata ṭi. āṇi
translation: I climbed onto the platform. Upon the platform was a hall, O mother, a hall was there.
commentary: Having reached the elevated stage, the seeker ascends further to find a hall. The vision is one of nested structures, each ascent revealing a deeper, more interior space, mapping the soul's inward way.

translit: kūṭattai nāṭaak kūṭamēl ēḻnilai māṭam iruntata ṭi - ammā māṭam iruntata ṭi. āṇi
translation: As I approached the hall, above that hall was a seven-storied mansion, O mother, a mansion was there.
commentary: Inside the hall lies a "seven-storied mansion." In yogic and mystical traditions, the number seven often refers to the primary chakras, or centers of energy and consciousness in the body. The vision is now moving from an external approach to the internal structure of spiritual experience itself.

translit: ēḻnilaik kuḷḷum irunta aticayam eṉṉeṉṟu colvaṉa ṭi - ammā eṉṉeṉṟu colvaṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: How can I describe the wonder that existed within the seven levels? Oh my dear friend, how can I describe it?
commentary: The vision now enters the seven levels (ēḻ nilai) of the Golden Hall. Vallalar can hardly speak of what he found within them. He turns to his confidant and says only: how can I describe it? The verses that follow try, one level at a time.

translit: ōrnilai taṉṉil oḷirmuttu veṇmaṇi cīrnīlam āccuta ṭi - ammā cīrnīlam āccuta ṭi. āṇi
translation: In one stage, a lustrous white pearl-gem became a glorious sapphire blue. Oh my dear friend, it became a glorious sapphire blue.
commentary: At the first level the white pearl-gem turns sapphire blue. The vision moves by transformation: each level is marked by a change of color and jewel. Vallalar reports what he saw simply, as one tells a friend, and repeats the line in wonder.

translit: pārōr nilaiyil karunīlam ceyya pavaḷama tāccuta ṭi - ammā pavaḷama tāccuta ṭi. āṇi
translation: In a magnificent stage, the dark blue became a red coral. Oh my dear friend, it became a red coral.
commentary: At the next level the dark blue becomes red coral. The jewels keep changing as the vision climbs, each color giving way to another. Nothing here stands still; the Light reveals itself level by level.

translit: maṟṟōr nilaiyil marakatap paccaicem māṇikkam āccuta ṭi - ammā māṇikkam āccuta ṭi. āṇi
translation: In another stage, the emerald green became a red ruby. Oh my dear friend, it became a red ruby.
commentary: At another level the emerald green turns into red ruby. The list of jewels is a list of stages passed through, each more radiant than the last. Vallalar names them one by one so that the ascent can be followed.

translit: piṉṉōr nilaiyil perumuttu vaccirap pērmaṇi āccuta ṭi - ammā pērmaṇi āccuta ṭi. āṇi
translation: In a later stage, a great pearl became a renowned diamond gem. Oh my dear friend, it became a renowned gem.
commentary: At a later level the great pearl becomes a diamond, the most renowned of gems. What is precious becomes more precious still, harder and more brilliant. The ascent is nearing its height.

translit: vēṟōr nilaiyil mikumpava ḷattiraḷ veṇmaṇi āccuta ṭi - ammā veṇmaṇi āccuta ṭi. āṇi
translation: In another state, the great mass of coral became a white gem. O mother, truly, it became a white gem.
commentary: At another level a great mass of coral becomes a white gem. Red turns to white, and many turn to one. The colors are being gathered and purified as the vision continues upward.

translit: pukalōr nilaiyil poruntiya paṉmaṇi poṉmaṇi āccuta ṭi - ammā poṉmaṇi āccuta ṭi. āṇi
translation: In a glorious state, the many kinds of gems became a golden gem. O mother, truly, it became a golden gem.
commentary: At the next level the many kinds of gems become a single golden gem. Many give way to one substance. Gold is the color of the Golden Hall itself, and the vision is drawing near its center.

translit: patiyōr nilaiyil pakarmaṇi ellām paṭikama tāccuta ṭi - ammā paṭikama tāccuta ṭi. āṇi
translation: In the state of the Lord, all the gems spoken of became crystal. O mother, truly, they became crystal.
commentary: At the level of the Lord (pati), all the gems become crystal. Every color has passed into clear transparency. What was many and colored is now one and pure, letting the Light pass through it without hindrance.

translit: ēḻnilai mēlē iruntatōr tampam icaintapoṟ ṟampama ṭi - ammā icaintapoṟ ṟampama ṭi. āṇi
translation: The pillar that stood above the seven states is a splendid golden pillar. O mother, truly, it is a splendid golden pillar.
commentary: Above all seven levels stands a pillar of gold. The ascent ends in this single golden pillar, no other color, fitting and complete. It is the summit of the vision in the Hall of Pure Gold.

translit: poṟṟampam kaṇṭēṟum pōtunāṉ kaṇṭa putumaieṉ colvaṉa ṭi - ammā putumaieṉ colvaṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: What can I say of the marvel I saw while beholding and ascending the golden pillar? O mother, what can I truly say of that marvel?
commentary: The "golden pillar" is a classic symbol for the central channel of spiritual energy within the body. The speaker is describing an inner, mystical ascent, and the experience is so great it leaves her speechless with wonder.

translit: ēṟumpō taṅkē etirnta vakaicola eṉṉaḷa vallava ṭi - ammā eṉṉaḷa vallava ṭi. āṇi
translation: It is not within my power to describe what I encountered as I ascended, oh friend, it is not within my power. This is the essential point.
commentary: The deepest spiritual experiences cannot be fully captured by language. Here, the ascent through consciousness is described as something so personal and overwhelming that words fail to do it justice.

translit: āṅkāṅkē cattikaḷ āyiram āyiram ākavan tārkaḷa ṭi - ammā ākavan tārkaḷa ṭi. āṇi
translation: Thousands upon thousands of Shaktis came from all around, oh friend, they truly came in their thousands. This is the essential point.
commentary: As the soul rises through higher planes of consciousness, it encounters countless divine energies, called Śaktis (divine feminine powers). These are the forces and intelligences that govern the different levels of creation.

translit: vantu mayakka mayaṅkāmal nāṉaruḷ vallapam peṟṟaṉa ṭi - ammā vallapam peṟṟaṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: They came to delude me, but without being deluded, I obtained the power of grace, oh friend, I obtained that power. This is the essential point.
commentary: These powerful divine energies also serve as a test for the seeker. They can represent spiritual powers or heavenly delights that might tempt one to stop short of the final goal. The speaker overcomes this "delusion" by relying on the power of divine grace.

translit: vallapat tālanta mātampat tēṟi maṇimuṭi kaṇṭēṉa ṭi - ammā maṇimuṭi kaṇṭēṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: By that power, I climbed the great pillar and saw the jeweled crown, oh friend, I saw the jeweled crown. This is the essential point.
commentary: Protected by grace, the speaker ascends the inner pillar to its peak, symbolized by the "jeweled crown." This represents reaching the highest center of consciousness within the human being, often visualized at the crown of the head.

translit: maṇimuṭi mēlōr koṭumuṭi niṉṟatu maṟṟatu kaṇṭēṉa ṭi - ammā maṟṟatu kaṇṭēṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: Above the jeweled crown stood a supreme summit; I saw that as well, oh friend, I saw that as well. This is the essential point.
commentary: The ascent goes on past the peak of individual consciousness. Vallalar points to a "supreme summit" even beyond the crown, signifying a transcendent reality that is the ultimate source of all, existing beyond the limits of the self.

translit: koṭumuṭi mēlāyi ratteṭṭu māṟṟuppoṟ kōyil iruntata ṭi - ammā kōyil iruntata ṭi. āṇi
translation: On the highest peak, there was a temple made of gold of one-thousand-and-eight fineness, mother. Indeed, there was a temple there.
commentary: At the ultimate peak of existence rests an inner temple. Describing its gold as "one-thousand-and-eight fineness" is a poetic way of saying it is of a purity far beyond anything earthly, a substance made of pure spirit.

translit: kōyilaik kaṇṭaṅkē kōpura vāyilil kūcātu ceṉṟaṉa ṭi - ammā kūcātu ceṉṟaṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: Seeing the temple, I went through the tower gateway without any hesitation, mother. I went without hesitation, indeed.
commentary: Having reached this sacred inner space, the seeker feels no fear or doubt. The long climb has prepared them, and they enter the final sanctuary with a sense of homecoming and complete readiness.

translit: kōpura vāyiluḷ cattikaḷ cattarkaḷ kōṭipal kōṭiya ṭi - ammā kōṭipal kōṭiya ṭi. āṇi
translation: Inside the tower gateway were Shaktis and Shaktars, many crores upon crores of them, mother. Many crores upon crores, indeed.
commentary: The inner temple is teeming with divine life. It is populated by innumerable Shaktis (female divine powers) and Shaktars (male divine powers), representing the infinite energies and aspects of God's creative force.

translit: āṅkavar vaṇṇamveḷ vaṇṇamcev vaṇṇamuṉ aivaṇṇam ākuma ṭi - ammā aivaṇṇam ākuma ṭi. āṇi
translation: Their colors there are white and red, and foremost, five colors in all, mother. Five colors in all, indeed.
commentary: These divine powers have distinct qualities, represented here by colors. White and red often symbolize the core principles of consciousness and energy, while the five colors can relate to the five elements or the five principal functions of the divine.

translit: aṅkava rellāmiṅ kārivar eṉṉavum appālē ceṉṟaṉa ṭi - ammā appālē ceṉṟaṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: While all of them there were asking, “Who is this person?”, I went on beyond them, mother. I went on beyond them, indeed.
commentary: This verse shows the single-minded focus of a soul nearing its goal. Even the wonder of countless divine beings cannot distract the seeker, who moves past their questions, drawn only toward the ultimate source.

translit: appālē ceṉṟēṉaṅ kōrtiru vāyilil aivar iruntāra ṭi - ammā aivar iruntāra ṭi. āṇi
translation: I went further beyond, and there, at a sacred gateway, were five people, mother. Truly, five people were there.
commentary: After passing the vast multitudes, the seeker arrives at a more significant threshold guarded by five figures. These five beings often represent the divine powers that control the five core functions of the cosmos: creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment, and grace.

translit: maṟṟavar niṉṟu vaḻikāṭṭa mēlōr maṇivāyil uṟṟēṉa ṭi - ammā maṇivāyil uṟṟēṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: As they stood and showed the way, I reached a higher, jeweled gateway, mother. Truly, I reached the jeweled gateway.
commentary: Unlike the previous beings who were simply observers, these five gatekeepers actively show the way forward. This marks a transition to a higher state where the soul is welcomed and guided toward an even more sacred space, the "jeweled gateway."

translit: eṇṇumav vāyilil peṇṇō ṭāṇāka iruvar iruntāra ṭi - ammā iruvar iruntāra ṭi. āṇi
translation: At that gateway, there were two people, a woman and a man, mother. Truly, two people were there.
commentary: At the final threshold, the seeker encounters the primordial divine pair, a man and a woman. This represents the union of the two fundamental principles of reality, such as Consciousness and Energy (Siva and Shakti), just before they merge into the ultimate, formless One.

translit: aṅkavar kāṭṭa aṇukkat tiruvāyil aṉpoṭu kaṇṭēṉa ṭi - ammā aṉpoṭu kaṇṭēṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: As they showed me, I saw the intimate sacred gateway with love, mother. Truly, I saw it with love.
commentary: Progress on the spiritual path comes through love. The guardians of the gateway reveal the next passage, which the seeker perceives "with love." This emphasizes that devotion and an open heart are the keys that unlock the deeper mysteries of the divine.

translit: attiru vāyilil āṉanta vallieṉ ammai iruntāḷa ṭi - ammā ammai iruntāḷa ṭi. āṇi
translation: At that sacred gateway, Ananda Valli, my Mother, was there, mother. Truly, my Mother was there.
commentary: The seeker has now arrived at the presence of the Divine, experienced here as the Mother. She is called Ananda Valli, "the creeper of bliss," a name that beautifully captures divine grace as an all-encompassing, life-giving joy. This meeting signifies a state of union with the source of all bliss.

translit: ammaiyaik kaṇṭēṉ avaḷaruḷ koṇṭēṉ amutamum uṇṭēṉa ṭi - ammā amutamum uṇṭēṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: I saw the Mother, I received her grace, and I drank the nectar, O friend. Oh my, I also drank the nectar, O friend.
commentary: This verse describes the fruit of the spiritual path: vision, grace, and bliss. To see the Mother is to have a direct experience of the Divine. To receive her grace is to be blessed by that presence. To drink the nectar (amutham) is to taste the immortal joy of spiritual realization, a state that transforms the seeker completely.

translit: tāṅkum avaḷaru ḷālē naṭarājar canniti kaṇṭēṉa ṭi - ammā canniti kaṇṭēṉa ṭi. āṇi
translation: By her supporting grace, I saw the sacred presence of Natarajar, O friend. Oh my, I saw the sacred presence, O friend.
commentary: The Mother's grace is the essential key that unlocks the door to the Lord. Without her support, seeing the sannidhi (sacred presence) of Natarajar, the cosmic dancer, is impossible.

translit: canniti yilceṉṟu nāṉpeṟṟa pēṟatu cāmi aṟivāra ṭi - ammā cāmi aṟivāra ṭi.
translation: The blessing I received upon going to the sacred presence, the Lord knows it, O friend. Oh my, the Lord knows it, O friend.
commentary: The ultimate spiritual attainment is an experience beyond words. It is a secret known only to the soul and God.

translit: āṇippoṉ ṉampalat tēkaṇṭa kāṭcikaḷ aṟputak kāṭciya ṭi - ammā aṟputak kāṭciya ṭi.
translation: The sights I saw in the Hall of Pure Gold are wondrous sights, O friend. Oh my, they are wondrous sights, O friend.
commentary: The "Hall of Pure Gold" is the innermost sanctum of consciousness where the divine is perceived directly. The sights experienced there are revelations of pure wonder, confirming the beauty and truth at the heart of reality.

translit: vāṉattiṉ mītu mayilāṭak kaṇṭēṉ mayilkuyil āccuta ṭi - akkacci mayilkuyil āccuta ṭi.
translation: I saw a peacock dancing in the sky; the peacock became a cuckoo, O sister! The peacock became a cuckoo.
commentary: This verse uses deep yogic symbolism, which Vallalar himself unlocks: the peacock represents vindu, a concentrated point of spiritual energy, and the cuckoo represents nādam, the primordial divine sound. The verse describes an inner transformation where this potential energy (vindu) dissolves and becomes pure vibration (nādam) within the "sky" of consciousness. It is a shift from form to formlessness, from potential to pure sound.

translit: tuḷḷalai viṭṭut toṭaṅkiṉēṉ maṉṟāṭum vaḷḷalaik kaṇṭēṉa ṭi - akkacci vaḷḷalaik kaṇṭēṉa ṭi.
translation: I gave up my restless agitation and began the journey. I have seen the great Benefactor who dances in the Hall, O sister! I have seen the great Benefactor.
commentary: The way to God begins with quieting the restless mind. Only after abandoning the constant mental and emotional agitation of worldly life can one perceive the divine Benefactor who is always present within the sacred "Hall" of consciousness.

translit: cāti camayac caḻakkaiviṭ ṭēṉaruṭ cōtiyaik kaṇṭēṉa ṭi - akkacci cōtiyaik kaṇṭēṉa ṭi.
translation: I have abandoned the falsehood of caste and religion. I have seen the Jothi of Grace, O sister! I have seen the Jothi.
commentary: Vallalar calls caste and religion a saḻakku, a falsehood and a crookedness. He does not soften them into mere quarrels; he leaves them behind, and only then does he see the Arut Jothi, the Light of Grace that knows no caste and no creed.

translit: poyyai oḻittup puṟappaṭṭēṉ maṉṟāṭum aiyaraik kaṇṭēṉa ṭi - akkacci aiyaraik kaṇṭēṉa ṭi.
translation: I eradicated falsehood and set out. I have seen the Master who dances in the Hall, O sister! I have seen the Master.
commentary: Spiritual seeking is inseparable from ethical purity. The vision of the divine Master is granted only after one has consciously and completely eliminated falsehood from their life.
NOTES
Note 334

translit: mayil - vintu. kuyil - nātam.
translation: mayil (peacock) signifies vintu; kuyil (koel) signifies nātam.

translit: kaiviṭa māṭṭāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē kaṉaka capaiyāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē poyviṭac ceytāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē pūcaipa littateṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē.
translation: Blow the conch, for he will not abandon me. Blow the conch, for he is of the Golden Hall. Blow the conch, for he made me relinquish falsehood. Blow the conch, for my worship has borne fruit.
commentary: The conch is blown to announce a series of spiritual triumphs. These are certainties: God's steady support, His real presence in the inner "Golden Hall," the power He gives to overcome untruth, and the final proof that one's devotion (pūjai, worship) has been accepted and borne fruit.

translit: tūkkam tolaittāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē tuṉpam tavirttāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē ēkkam keṭuttāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē ēma capaiyāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē.
translation: Blow the conch, for he has banished my sleep. Blow the conch, for he dispelled my suffering. Blow the conch, for he ended my yearning. Blow the conch, for he is of the Golden Hall.
commentary: The conch (caṅku) is blown to proclaim what God has done: ended the sleep of delusion, removed suffering, put an end to longing. God is the One of the sacred Hall. The conch announces victory and arrival, and Vallalar wants the whole world to hear it.

translit: poṉṉaṭi tantāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē poṉṉam palattāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē iṉṉal aṟuttāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē eṉṉuḷ amarntāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē.
translation: Blow the conch, for he gave me his golden feet. Blow the conch, for he is the one of Ponnambalam (the Golden Hall). Blow the conch, for he severed my distress. Blow the conch, for he is seated within me.
commentary: Blow the conch again: God gave His golden feet, dwells in the Golden Hall, cut away distress, and now sits within Vallalar. The last line carries the greatest news. The Lord of the Golden Hall is not only out there; He is seated within.

translit: accam tavirttāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē ampala vāṇaṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē iccai aḷittāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē iṉpam koṭuttāṉeṉṟu ūtūtu caṅkē.
translation: Blow the conch, for he removed my fear. Blow the conch, for he is Ampalavāṇan. Blow the conch, for he granted my desire. Blow the conch, for he gave me bliss.
commentary: The blowing of the conch announces a great victory: the removal of fear and the fulfillment of the soul's deepest longing for bliss.
