translit: akara:ukara makaravakara amutacikara caraṇamē aparacapara amaṉacamaṉa amalanimala caraṇamē.
translation: O feet, the ambrosial peak of the sounds A, U, M, and V! O pure and stainless feet, beyond the lower and the higher, beyond mind and equanimity!
commentary: God's being is described as the source of primordial sound. The sounds A, U, and M form the sacred syllable 'Om', the vibration of creation, to which Vallalar adds V, representing grace. The verse then states God is beyond all dualities, including our concepts of high and low or even the states of mental activity and mental stillness.

translit: takarakakaṉa naṭaṉakaṭaṉa cakaḷavakaḷa caraṇamē cakuṇanikuṇa cakamanikama cakitavikita caraṇamē.
translation: O feet that perform the duty of dance in the subtle heart-space! O feet of the formful and the formless! O feet that are with and without qualities, described in the Agamas and Vedas, both united and separate!
commentary: The divine dance happens in the cosmos and within the subtle space of the human heart. God is described through paradoxes: having a form (sakaḷa) yet being formless (akaḷa); possessing qualities (saguṇa) yet being beyond all qualities (niguṇa). By mentioning both the Vedas and Agamas, the core scriptures of two major streams of Hindu thought, Vallalar presents a God who encompasses and transcends all religious traditions.

translit: aṉakavaṉaja amitaamirta akalaakila caraṇamē atulavaṉata acutavacala anilavaṉala caraṇamē.
translation: O feet, the faultless lotus, immeasurable ambrosia, boundless and all-encompassing! O feet of incomparable grace, the pure entrance, which are wind and fire!
commentary: This verse uses a series of metaphors to describe the divine. God's presence is a pure, unfolding lotus and a limitless source of spiritual nectar (amrita). By identifying God's feet with the elements of wind and fire, Vallalar points to a divinity that is the purifying, life-sustaining force within the world.

translit: taṉakakaṉaka capaiyaapaya caratavarata caraṇamē caturacatara cakacacarita taruṇacaraṇa caraṇamē.
translation: O feet of the one in the beautiful golden hall, who grants refuge and gives boons with certainty! O feet of the skillful and graceful one, of innate character! O tender feet, our refuge!
commentary: The 'golden hall' (kanaka sabai) refers to the sacred temple at Chidambaram, which is central to the tradition of Siva as the cosmic dancer. This links Vallalar's universal vision to a specific, beloved place of worship. The verse emphasizes that giving refuge (abhayam) and granting boons (varadam) belong to God's unchanging character.

translit: uḷamumuṇarvum uyirumoḷira oḷirumoruva caraṇamē uruviṉuruvum uruvuḷuruvum uṭaiyatalaiva caraṇamē.
translation: Salutations to the One who shines, making the mind, consciousness, and soul radiate light. Salutations to the Master who is the form of form and the form within form.
commentary: The divine is the source of our own inner light. It is the one supreme radiance that illuminates our mind, our awareness, and our very soul. God is both the form of everything that has form, and the formless essence hidden within every form, a reality that is at once visible and invisible.

translit: iḷakumitaya kamalamataṉai iṟaikoḷiṟaiva caraṇamē irumaiorumai nalamumaruḷum iṉiyacamuka caraṇamē.
translation: Salutations to the Lord who takes possession of the tender heart-lotus. Salutations to the sweet Divine Presence that graciously grants the benefits of duality and unity.
commentary: When a person's heart becomes tender and open, symbolized by a lotus, the divine presence enters and takes possession of it. God grants the ability to experience the divine both as a separate being to be loved (duality) and as the very essence of one's own self (unity), with both paths being gifts of grace.

translit: aṭiyumnaṭuvum muṭiyumaṟiya ariyaperiya caraṇamē aṭiyaritaya veḷiyilnaṭaṉam atuceyatipa caraṇamē.
translation: Salutations to the Great One, whose feet, middle, and crown are difficult to comprehend. Salutations to the Sovereign who performs the dance in the space of His devotees' hearts.
commentary: God is so vast that the human mind cannot comprehend God's beginning, middle, or end. Yet this same infinite being performs an intimate dance within the inner space of the devotee's own heart.

translit: oṭivilkaruṇai amutamutavum upalavaṭiva caraṇamē ulakamuḻutum uṟaiyaniṟaiyum upayacaraṇa caraṇamē.
translation: Salutations to the gem-like form that gives the nectar of ceaseless compassion. Salutations to the pair of sacred feet that reside in and fill the entire world.
commentary: Divine compassion is an endless source of life-giving nectar. God's presence is simultaneously everywhere, filling the entire world, and can also be experienced as a specific point of contact, symbolized by the sacred feet that offer a place of refuge.

translit: aṟivuḷaṟiyum aṟivaiaṟiya aruḷumnimala caraṇamē avacamuṟumey yaṭiyaritayam amarumamala caraṇamē.
translation: Salutations to the Pure One, who bestows the knowing of the Awareness known within awareness. Salutations to the Immaculate One, who abides in the hearts of true devotees overcome with ecstasy.
commentary: Beyond ordinary awareness is a deeper knowing: the awareness of awareness itself. This ultimate insight is a gift of grace. God takes root in the hearts of true devotees who are overcome with ecstatic love.

translit: eṟivilulakiluyiraiuṭalil iṇaiceyiṟaiva caraṇamē eṉaiyumoruvaṉ eṉavuḷuṇarum eṉatutalaiva caraṇamē.
translation: Refuge at your feet, O Lord who joins soul to body in this world of strife. Refuge at your feet, my Master who recognizes within that I too am someone of worth.
commentary: This is a deeply personal prayer acknowledging God as both the power that places us in this difficult world and the one who sees our individual worth. Amidst life's struggles, the singer finds deep comfort in the idea that the supreme Master recognizes him as a unique and valuable person.

translit: niṉaiyumniṉaivu kaṉiya:iṉiya niṟaivutaruka caraṇamē niṉaiyumeṉaiyum orumaipuriyum neṟiyilniṟuvu caraṇamē.
translation: Refuge at your feet, grant the sweet fulfillment that ripens the very thought of you. Refuge at your feet, establish me on the path that makes you and me one.
commentary: The goal of devotion is to transform one's own mind, making the mere thought of God a source of sweetness and joy. Vallalar goes further, asking to be placed on the path that dissolves the separation between the worshipper and the worshipped, leading to complete union.

translit: vaṉaiyumatura amuta:uṇavu maliya:utavu caraṇamē maruvucapaiyil naṭaṉavarata varukavaruka caraṇamē.
translation: Refuge at your feet, grant in abundance the crafted, sweet, nectar-like food. Refuge at your feet, O boon-granting Dancer in the sacred hall, come, come!
commentary: The "nectar-like food" is a prayer for both physical sustenance and the spiritual nourishment of grace. Invoking God as the cosmic Dancer in the sacred hall, the urgent plea "come, come!" expresses an intense longing for a direct, personal experience of the divine presence.

translit: niṉaikkilneñcam iṉikkumeṉṟa niruttamaṉṟil oruttaṉē niṉaikkumaṉpar nilaikkaniṉṟu poruttukiṉṟa karuttaṉē.
translation: O singular One in the Hall of Dance, about whom it is said, "thinking of him sweetens the heart." O Lord of purpose who stands to make devotees who think of you steadfast.
commentary: Remembering God is an experience that brings sweetness to the heart and mind. This devotion is more than a pleasant feeling; it has a practical effect. The Lord's purpose is to make his devotees steadfast, giving them a firm inner foundation.

translit: mayaṅkineñcu kalaṅkiniṉṟu malaṅkiṉēṉai āṇṭavā vayaṅkiniṉṟu tulaṅkumaṉṟil ilaṅkuñāṉa tāṇṭavā.
translation: O you who took me as your own when I stood bewildered, with a troubled heart and confused mind. O luminous Dancer of Wisdom, who stands radiantly in the shining Hall!
commentary: Grace is not a reward for being perfect; it often arrives when we are most lost, heartbroken, and confused. God is the Dancer of Wisdom (jñāna tāṇṭavā), whose radiant light appears in our inner darkness to rescue and claim us.

translit: kaḷaṅkavāta kaḷaṅkoḷcūtar uḷaṅkoḷāta pātaṉē kaḷaṅkilāta uḷaṅkoḷvāruḷ viḷaṅkuñāṉa nātaṉē.
translation: O Lord, your feet are incomprehensible to the minds of corrupt debaters with their tainted arguments. O Lord of Wisdom, you shine within the hearts of the stainless.
commentary: God cannot be reached through clever arguments or intellectual debate, which often come from a place of ego. The divine presence is a reality experienced directly, shining brightly within a heart that is "stainless," or pure and free from arrogance.

translit: taṭuttamalattaik keṭuttunalattaik koṭuttakaruṇait tantaiyē taṉittanilattil iṉittakulattil kuṉittaaṭikoḷ entaiyē.
translation: O Father of grace, you destroyed the obstructing impurity and bestowed well-being. O my Father with the dancing foot, you abide in the solitary state and are sweet to the assembly of your devotees.
commentary: The fundamental cause of suffering is a deep-seated inner impurity (malam), which God's grace alone can destroy. This divine "Father" is both the remote, absolute Being in a "solitary state" and a sweet, intimate companion cherished by the community of devotees.

translit: eccanīṭṭi viccaikāṭṭi iccaiūṭṭum iṉpaṉē accamōṭṭi accunāṭṭi vaiccuḷāṭṭum aṉpaṉē.
translation: O Blissful One, you extend a mere trace of yourself, display your marvels, and feed our longing! O Loving One, you drive away fear, plant a firm axis within, and make us dance from the inside.
commentary: Even a small glimpse of the divine is enough to spark an immense spiritual longing within us. God's love is an active force that calms our fears, gives us an unshakeable inner stability, and fills us with a bliss that makes our very soul dance.

translit: capācivā mahācivā cakācivā cikācivā catācivā catācivā catācivā catācivā.
translation: O Siva of the Hall, O Great Siva, O Siva our Companion, O Siva the Crest-Flame! O Eternal Siva, Eternal Siva, Eternal Siva, Eternal Siva!
commentary: This is a litany of praise, repeating sacred names to focus the mind on different aspects of God. It calls on Siva as the Lord of the cosmic hall (Saba Siva), the Great God (Maha Siva), our constant companion (Saga Siva), the highest flame of wisdom (Sikha Siva), and the eternal one (Sada Siva).

translit: vācivā catācivā mahācivā tayācivā vācivā civācivā civācivā civācivā.
translation: Come, Siva! O Eternal Siva, O Great Siva, O Siva of Compassion! Come, Siva! Siva, Siva, Siva, Siva, Siva, Siva!
commentary: The litany of praise turns into an urgent call: "Come, Siva!" (vā Sivā). God is invoked as the Eternal, the Great and the Compassionate (Daya Siva), and the cry is repeated until only the Name remains. Grace, God's compassion, is what the soul is calling for.
NOTES
Note 342

translit: irumaiulakil - mutaṟpatippu. po. cu. patippu.
translation: irumaiulakil — reading of the first edition and the Po. Su. Edition.

translit: tamkuṟuvampu maṅkanirampu caṅkamiyampum namkoḻukompu caṅkaracampu caṅkaracampu caṅkaracampu caṅkaracampu.
translation: The full assembly proclaims our great support, so that petty slander diminishes: Sankara Sambu, Sankara Sambu.
commentary: Chanting God's name is a powerful defense against negativity from others. By repeating the names Sankara (the benevolent) and Sambu (the source of good), one focuses on divine support, causing the power of worldly gossip and ill will to fade away.

translit: cantamiyaṉṟu antaṇarnaṉṟu cantatamniṉṟu vantaṉameṉṟu canticeymaṉṟu mantiramoṉṟu caṅkaracampu caṅkaracampu.
translation: With rhythmic measure, good priests perpetually stand and offer salutations in the hall of worship. The one mantra is: Sankara Sambu, Sankara Sambu.
commentary: This verse elevates the chanting of God's name above all other rituals. Even for learned priests performing worship, the one essential sacred formula (mantra) and the core of their devotion is the simple, powerful repetition of "Sankara Sambu."

translit: naṉantalaivīti naṭantiṭucāti nalamkoḷumāti naṭampurinīti tiṉaṅkalaiōti civamtarumōti citamparajōti citamparajōti.
translation: The Primordial source of well-being for all peoples walking the wide streets, the Justice who performs the dance, the Teacher who daily recites the scriptures, the Master who grants the state of Sivam: Chidambara Jothi, Chidambara Jothi.
commentary: God is portrayed here as a universal and immediate presence. He is the justice that oversees the world and the source of goodness for all people, from every walk of life. He is the great teacher who reveals the ultimate state of Sivam (benevolent reality), and he is embodied as Chidambara Jothi, the light of consciousness itself.

translit: nakapperuñcōti cukapperuñcōti navapperuñcōti civapperuñcōti akapperuñcōti naṭapperuñcōti aruṭperuñ cōti aruṭperuñ cōti.
translation: Vast Jothi of the smile, vast Jothi of bliss. Vast Jothi of newness, vast Jothi of Sivam. Vast Jothi of the inner realm, vast Jothi of the dance. ArutPerunJothi, ArutPerunJothi.
commentary: This verse describes the divine as a vast, radiant light (Jothi) that expresses itself in many forms. It is the light of a smile, the light of inner bliss, the light of perpetual newness, and the light of the ultimate reality, Sivam. It is the light within the soul and the light of the cosmic dance, culminating in the ultimate name, ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light.

translit: umaikkorupāti koṭuttaruḷnīti uvappuṟuvēti navapperuvāti amaittiṭupūti akattiṭumāti aruṭcivajōti aruṭcivajōti.
translation: The Justice who graciously gave one half to Uma, the blissful Vedic scholar, the great new Teacher, the one who creates sacred glory, the Primordial One who dwells within: Arut Siva Jothi, Arut Siva Jothi.
commentary: This verse celebrates God's compassion and immanence. The act of giving half of himself to the goddess Uma represents a perfect, harmonious union of divine energies. This just and blissful being is not distant; he is the primordial source dwelling inside each person, the radiant Grace-Light of God (Arut Siva Jothi).

note: A separate song in the 1932 edition (numbered 141 in the Tamil source edition).
translit: ōtaaṭaṅ kātumaṭaṅ kātutoṭaṅ kātu ōkaioṭuṅ kātutaṭuṅ kātunaṭuṅ kātu cūtamalaṅ kātuvilaṅ kātukalaṅ kātu jōtiparañ jōticuyañ jōtiperuñ jōti.
translation: It is not confined by scripture, it does not bend, it has no beginning. Its joy does not subside, it cannot be obstructed, it does not tremble. It is not swayed by deceit, it does not swerve, it is not agitated. Jothi, Supreme Jothi, Self-existent Jothi, Vast Jothi.
commentary: The divine light, Jothi, is an absolute reality that exists beyond all human categories. It cannot be contained by any scripture, has no beginning or end, and its joy is eternal and unstoppable. This description, using negatives, points to a reality that is completely free, changeless, and self-sufficient, untouched by the limits of the created world.

translit: ētamuyaṅ kātukayaṅ kātumayaṅ kātu ēṟiiṟaṅ kātuuṟaṅ kātukaṟaṅ kātu cūtamiṇaṅ kātupiṇaṅ kātuvaṇaṅ kātu jōtiparañ jōticuyañ jōtiperuñ jōti.
translation: It does not embrace fault, does not become base, is not deluded. It does not wax and wane, does not sleep, does not whirl about. It does not consent to deceit, is not at odds with anything, does not bow to another. Jothi, Supreme Jothi, Self-existent Jothi, Vast Jothi.
commentary: The divine Jothi is defined by its absolute perfection and autonomy. It is inherently free from any fault, delusion, or weakness. Unlike things in the physical world, it does not change, grow, or decay; it does not sleep or become confused. It is independent, subordinate to nothing, and in harmony with everything because it is the source of all.

translit: akaracapāpati cikaracapāpati aṉakacapāpati kaṉakacapāpati makaracapāpati ukaracapāpati varatacapāpati caratacapāpati.
translation: Sabapathi of 'A', Sabapathi of 'Si', the flawless Sabapathi, the golden Sabapathi. Sabapathi of 'Ma', Sabapathi of 'U', the boon-granting Sabapathi, the true Sabapathi.
commentary: God, as Sabapathi (Lord of the Hall of Consciousness, a name for the dancing Siva), is identified with the foundational sounds of creation. The syllables 'A', 'U', and 'Ma' form the universal sound 'AUM', while 'Si' is the core of the great mantra 'Sivaya Namah'. This verse shows that God is the reality vibrating within these sacred sounds that structure the cosmos.

translit: amalacapāpati apayacapāpati amutacapāpati akilacapāpati nimalacapāpati nipuṇacapāpati nilayacapāpati nipiṭacapāpati.
translation: The pure Sabapathi, Sabapathi who grants fearlessness, the nectarous Sabapathi, Sabapathi of the cosmos. The stainless Sabapathi, the skillful Sabapathi, Sabapathi who is the abode, the all-pervading Sabapathi.
commentary: This verse is a litany of praise describing the character of God as Sabapathi, the Lord of the cosmic dance. He is utterly pure, the one who grants refuge from all fear (abhayam), and the source of divine nectar or immortal bliss. He is the master of the entire cosmos, the stable ground of all existence, and the one who pervades everything completely.

translit: paramanaṭamciva citamparanaṭamē patinaṭamciva capāpatinaṭamē tirunaṭaṉampara kurunaṭamē civanaṭamampara navanaṭamē.
translation: The supreme dance is the dance of Siva-Chidambaram; the dance of the Lord is the dance of Siva-Sabapathi. The sacred dance is the dance of the supreme Guru; the dance of Siva is the new dance in the expanse.
commentary: The central theme becomes the cosmic dance of Siva, which represents the dynamic, creative activity of the universe. This dance takes place in Chidambaram, the inner space of consciousness, and is itself a form of teaching from the supreme Guru (spiritual master). The "new dance" suggests a living, direct revelation of truth available now.

translit: ampalattorunaṭam urunaṭamē arunaṭam orunaṭam tirunaṭamē empalattorunaṭam perunaṭamē itaṉparattiṭunaṭam kurunaṭamē.
translation: The one dance in the sacred space is the dance of form; the rare dance, the one dance, is the sacred dance. The one dance in our vision is the great dance; the dance that transcends this is the Guru's dance.
commentary: Vallalar describes different layers of this one divine dance. The "dance of form" is the entire visible, material universe we perceive with our senses. Yet beyond what we can see, there is a deeper, transcendent reality: the "Guru's dance," which is a spiritual experience beyond ordinary perception.

translit: añcōṭañcavai ēlātē aṅkōṭiṅkeṉal ākātē antōventuyar cērātē añcōkañcukam ōvātē tañcōpamkolai cārātē cantōṭamciva māmītē campōcaṅkara mātēvā campōcaṅkara mātēvā.
translation: The ten senses will not take hold; it becomes impossible to say "there" and "here." Alas, searing sorrow will not touch us; sorrowless bliss will never cease. Distress and murder will not come near; this very contentment is Sivam. Sambho! Sankara! Mahadeva! Sambho! Sankara! Mahadeva!
commentary: This verse describes the inner state of liberation that results from realizing God's presence. In this state, the grip of the senses loosens, the feeling of being a separate self in a specific location dissolves, and all sorrow is replaced by an unending bliss. This bliss is Sivam, the ultimate, auspicious reality. The joyful cries of God's names, Sambho, Sankara, and Mahadeva, express the ecstasy of this attainment.

tamil: எந்தாய் என்றிடில் இந்தா நம்பதம் என்றீ யும்பர மன்றா டும்பத
என்றோ டிந்தன நன்றா மங்கண வெங்கோ மங்கள வெஞ்சா நெஞ்சக
சந்தே கங்கெட நந்தா மந்திர சந்தோ டம்பெற வந்தா ளந்தண
சம்போ சங்கர சம்போ சங்கர சம்போ சங்கர சம்போ சங்கர.
translit: entāy eṉṟiṭil intā nampatam eṉṟī yumpara maṉṟā ṭumpata eṉṟō ṭintaṉa naṉṟā maṅkaṇa veṅkō maṅkaḷa veñcā neñcaka cantē kaṅkeṭa nantā mantira cantō ṭampeṟa vantā ḷantaṇa campō caṅkara campō caṅkara campō caṅkara campō caṅkara.
translation: When I cry, "My Father!", you answer, "Here, take our state," O feet dancing in the celestials' beautiful hall! The firewood that is my body is made good, O beautiful-eyed, fierce King, O benevolent one in my undying heart! To destroy my doubts and let me receive the bliss of the eternal mantra, you came and graced me, O pure one. Sambho! Sankara! Sambho! Sankara! Sambho! Sankara! Sambho! Sankara!
commentary: The tone shifts to one of deeply personal intimacy with God. Vallalar describes a direct call and response: his simple cry of "My Father!" is met with the divine promise of total union. This grace transforms his very body from something mortal ("firewood") into a purified vessel. God's intervention removes all spiritual doubt and grants the bliss of eternal truth, prompting an overflow of gratitude expressed in the repeated chanting of his name.

tamil: நஞ்சோ என்றிடு நங்கோ பங்கெட நன்றே தந்தனை நந்தா மந்தண
நம்பா நெஞ்சில் நிரம்பா நம்பர நம்பா நம்பதி யம்பா தம்பதி
தஞ்சோ வென்றவர் தஞ்சோ பந்தெறு தந்தா வந்தன நுந்தாள் தந்திடு
சம்போ சங்கர சம்போ சங்கர சம்போ சங்கர சம்போ சங்கர.
translit: nañcō eṉṟiṭu naṅkō paṅkeṭa naṉṟē tantaṉai nantā mantaṇa nampā neñcil nirampā nampara nampā nampati yampā tampati tañcō veṉṟavar tañcō panteṟu tantā vantaṉa nuntāḷ tantiṭu campō caṅkara campō caṅkara campō caṅkara campō caṅkara.
translation: So that our anger, which is like poison, may perish, you gave only good, O eternal secret! O Lord who fills the believer's heart, O Lord of our supreme space, our Master, Lord of the Ambalam! For those who cry, "Refuge!", you destroy their distress, O Father! Salutations! Grant me your holy feet. Sambho! Sankara! Sambho! Sankara! Sambho! Sankara! Sambho! Sankara!
commentary: God turns what is poison in us into good: the anger that works in us like poison is destroyed, and only good is given in its place. For all who cry "Refuge!", He destroys their distress. The Ambalam (sacred hall) is both the cosmic stage of God's dance and the space of consciousness within the believer's heart.

blocks.html: Potu Nilai Aruḷvatu - பொது நிலை அருள்வது

note: A separate song in the 1932 edition (numbered 139 in the Tamil source edition).
translit: potunilai aruḷvatu potuviṉil niṟaivatu potunalam uṭaiyatu potunaṭam iṭuvatu atuparam atupati atuporuḷ atucivam araara araara araara araara.
translation: It bestows the universal state, fills the universal space, possesses universal goodness, and performs the universal dance. That is the Supreme, that is the Lord, that is the ultimate Reality, that is Sivam. Hara! Hara! Hara! Hara! Hara! Hara! Hara! Hara!
commentary: The divine is defined here by its utterly public and universal nature. It is a reality that fills the "universal space" and works for the "universal good." Its dance, which sustains the cosmos, is a public performance for all to see. This supreme, all-inclusive reality is Sivam, praised with the ecstatic chant "Hara," another name for Siva.

translit: navanilai taruvatu navavaṭi vuṟuvatu navaveḷi naṭuvatu navanava navamatu civameṉum atupatam atukati atuporuḷ civaciva civaciva civaciva civaciva.
translation: It bestows the nine states, assumes the nine forms, centers the nine expanses, and is the ever-new nine. That which is called Sivam is the sacred state, the final refuge, the true substance. Siva Siva, Siva Siva, Siva Siva, Siva Siva.
commentary: The divine is the source and substance of all cosmic frameworks, symbolized here by the number nine, which in tradition can refer to sacred texts, divine energies, or planes of existence. God bestows these states and embodies them, yet is also described as "ever-new," suggesting constant, fresh creation. This ultimate reality, called Sivam, is the final state and the soul's true destination.

translit: cantira taracira cuntara curavara tantira navapata mantira puranaṭa caṅkara civaciva caṅkara civaciva caṅkara civaciva caṅkara civaciva.
translation: O bearer of the moon on your head, O beautiful one, chief of celestials! O you who are the nine states of the Tantras, the one who dances in the city of Mantras! Sankara Siva Siva, Sankara Siva Siva.
commentary: This is a hymn of praise using traditional epithets for Siva. He is the one who wears the crescent moon (a symbol of grace), is worshipped by the gods, and is the inner meaning of the Tantras (esoteric scriptures) and Mantras (sacred sounds). The "city of Mantras" refers to a mystical center, like the temple of Chidambaram, where divine sound-vibrations manifest the cosmos. Sankara is a name for Siva meaning "the one who brings about good."

note: A separate song in the 1932 edition (numbered 140 in the Tamil source edition).
translit: vāṉaciṟkaṉa mantiratantira vātaciṟkuṇa mantaṇavantaṇa vāracaṟcaṉa vantitacintita vāmaaṟputa maṅkalaimaṅkala ñāṉaciṟcuka caṅkarakaṅkara ñāyacaṟkuṇa vaṅkaṇaaṅkaṇa nātaciṟpara vamparanampara nātataṟpara vimpacitampara.
translation: You are the dense consciousness of space, the Mantra and Tantra; the esoteric, worshipped quality of conscious principles. You are contemplated and praised with love by the virtuous; the wondrous and auspicious one with the auspicious Goddess. You are the bliss of wisdom-consciousness, Sankara who bears the Ganga; the just one of noble qualities, the Lord with the eye. Lord of transcendent consciousness, space-clad and supreme! Lord absorbed in the Absolute, image in Chidambaram!
commentary: God is described here as both the vast, formless consciousness filling all of space and as a personal deity with beloved qualities. He is praised as the one who is with the Goddess, who bears the sacred river Ganga, and who is seen in the form of the dancing Lord at Chidambaram, a famous temple representing the space of consciousness. This single verse holds both the absolute and the personal aspects of the divine together.

translit: pāratattuva pañcakarañcaka pātacattuva caṅkajapaṅkaja pālanittiya vampakanampaka pācaputtaka paṇṭitakaṇṭita nāravittaka caṅkitaviṅkita nāṭakattava nampatinaṅkati nātaciṟpara namparaampara nātataṟpara vimpacitampara.
translation: You are the great principle of the five functions, your pure feet are like the lotus. Eternal protector, one with the divine eye, the trustworthy one. Scholar holding the noose and the book, who cuts through all arguments. Virtuoso of music and gesture, performer of the dance of austerity, our Lord and our refuge. Lord of transcendent consciousness, our supreme one, space-clad; Lord absorbed in the Absolute, image of Chidambaram.
commentary: God is praised here as the power behind the "five functions" that run the universe: creation, preservation, destruction, illusion, and grace. He is also portrayed as the ultimate teacher, holding a "noose" to restrain the ego and a "book" of wisdom to liberate the soul. The verse celebrates a divine being who is both the cosmic orchestrator and a personal guide and protector.

note: A separate song in the 1932 edition (numbered 146 in the Tamil source edition).
translit: patanampuṟu pavariṅkuṟu pavacaṅkaṭam aṟaniṉṟiṭu paramampotu naṭameṉtaṉa tuḷamnampuṟa aruḷampara citakuñcita patarañcita civacuntara civamantira civacaṅkara civacaṅkara civacaṅkara civacaṅkara.
translation: O space-clad Lord! So that the miseries of existence may cease for those here who trust in your feet, bestow your grace that my own heart may believe in the supreme dance you perform in the common expanse. O one with the delightful, raised foot of consciousness, O beautiful Siva, O Siva who is the mantra! Siva Sankara, Siva Sankara.
commentary: This verse is a direct and intimate prayer for grace. Vallalar asks for an end to worldly suffering and for the inner gift of unshakeable faith in God's "supreme dance." This dance is said to happen in the "common expanse," a universal space of consciousness open to everyone. The "raised foot" of the dancing Siva is a classic symbol of liberation, and the prayer is for the heart to truly trust in that promise of freedom.

translit: kalakantarum avalampaṉa katinampala nitamum kaṉakantaru maṇimaṉṟuṟu katitantaruḷ uṭalañ calacantiraṉ eṉaniṉṟavar taḻuvumpata caraṇam caraṇampati caraṇamciva caraṇamkuru caraṇam.
translation: Do not daily trust the path of dependency that brings strife. Grant the state of being in the golden, jeweled hall. I take refuge at the embracing feet of the One who stands with a body like the moon reflected on water. Refuge in the Lord, refuge in Siva, refuge in the Guru.
commentary: The true path to peace is to stop relying on worldly things and people, which only lead to conflict. Instead, one should seek refuge directly in God. The "golden, jeweled hall" is Chidambaram, the sacred space where the divine is always present. The final lines express a total surrender to God as the Lord, the ultimate reality (Siva), and the guiding teacher (Guru).

translit: eṉateṉpatum niṉateṉpatum itueṉṟuṇar taruṇam iṉamoṉṟatu piṟitaṉṟeṉa icaikiṉṟatu paramam taṉateṉpatu maṉateṉpatu jakameṉṟaṉai caraṇam caraṇampati caraṇamciva caraṇamkuru caraṇam.
translation: Now is the time to realize the truth about 'mine' and 'yours', for the Supreme affirms that our kind is one, not different. I take refuge in the One who declared, "The mind is Mine; the world is Mine." Refuge in the Lord, refuge in Siva, refuge in the Guru.
commentary: All sense of 'mine' and 'yours' is an illusion that separates us from a deeper truth. The verse states a core principle of Vallalar's vision: humanity is a single family. This unity comes from recognizing that everything, including our own minds, belongs to God.

sections.title: O One with Fragrant Matted Locks

tamil: வெஞ்சேர்பஞ்சார் நஞ்சார் கண்டா விம்பசி தம்பர னே.
translit: viraicēr caṭaiyāy viṭaiyāy uṭaiyāy vikirtā vipavā vimalā amalā veñcērpañcār nañcār kaṇṭā vimpaci tampara ṉē.
translation: O one with fragrant matted locks, one with the bull, O master! O extraordinary one, glorious one, pure one, spotless one! O one wearing the fierce five-headed serpent, one with a poison-filled throat, O manifest form, Lord of Chidambaram!
commentary: The devotee calls on God using a cascade of classic images associated with Lord Siva. Each title, from the matted hair and the bull to the poison-darkened throat, evokes a well-known story and a specific aspect of divine power. This is a form of worship where reciting God's attributes is a way to feel God's presence.

tamil: அந்தோ வந்தாள் எந்தாய் எந்தாய் அம்பல நம்பதி யே.
translit: araicē kuruvē amutē civamē aṇiyē maṇiyē aruḷē poruḷē antō vantāḷ entāy entāy ampala nampati yē.
translation: O King! O Guru! O Nectar! O Sivam! O beauty, O gem, O Grace, O very substance! Alas, come and rule me! O my Father, my Father, our Lord of the sacred hall!
commentary: The tone shifts from awe to deep intimacy, calling God a king, teacher (Guru), and the very substance of grace. Then comes the sudden cry, "Alas, come and rule me!" (vantāḷ, from vantu āḷ: come and take me as Your own). After all the names of praise, the soul's need breaks through, and it asks the Father to come now and make it His.

tamil: ஒன்றே என்றே நன்றே தந்தாய் அம்பரநம்பர னே.
translit: uruvē uyirē uṇarvē uṟavē uraiyē poruḷē oḷiyē veḷiyē oṉṟē eṉṟē naṉṟē tantāy amparanampara ṉē.
translation: O form, life, consciousness, and kin! O word, substance, light, and space! You blessed me greatly by making me realize you as the One, O our Lord of the sacred space!
commentary: God is the very fabric of existence. This verse lists the fundamental elements of life: physical form, life force, consciousness, relationships, language, and even light and space. The greatest blessing, Vallalar says, is the realization that all of these seemingly separate things are expressions of a single, unified reality: the One.

tamil: அந்தோ வந்தாள் எந்தாய் எந்தாய் அம்பல நம்பதி யே.
translit: aruvē tiruvē aṟivē ceṟivē atuvē ituvē aṭiyē muṭiyē antō vantāḷ entāy entāy ampala nampati yē.
translation: O formless one, O sacredness, O wisdom, O fullness! O That and O This, O beginning and O end! Alas, come and rule me! O my Father, my Father, our Lord of the sacred hall!
commentary: The divine is described here through its dual nature. God is "That," the formless, transcendent reality beyond our grasp, and also "This," the immanent, tangible reality right in front of us. He is both the beginning and the end of all things. The verse then returns to the soul's cry, "come and rule me," showing that this understanding culminates in personal, heartfelt surrender.
NOTES
Note 343

translit: veñcō - ā. pā. patippu.
translation: veñcō — reading of the Ā. Pā. edition.
Note 344

translit: umpari ṉamparaṉē - ā. pā. patippu.
translation: umpari ṉamparaṉē — reading of the Ā. Pā. Edition.

translit: paciyāta amutē pakaiyāta patiyē pakarāta nilaiyē paṟaiyāta cukamē naciyāta poruḷē naliyāta uṟavē naṭarāja maṇiyē naṭarāja maṇiyē.
translation: O Nectar that quells hunger! O Lord who is never hostile! O State that cannot be spoken! O Bliss that cannot be proclaimed! O Imperishable Substance! O Kinship that never fails! O Nataraja, the Gem! O Nataraja, the Gem!
commentary: The "hunger" God quells is the soul's deep yearning for truth, peace, and union with the divine. God is described as a reality that is completely reliable, loving, and beyond the limits of human language and comprehension. Addressing the dancing Lord Nataraja as this "Nectar" links the dynamic, creative energy of the universe with this state of ultimate satisfaction.

translit: puraiyāta maṇiyē pukalāta nilaiyē pukaiyāta kaṉalē putaiyāta poruḷē naraiyāta varamē naṭiyāta naṭamē naṭarāja nitiyē naṭarāja nitiyē.
translation: O flawless Gem! O State beyond all praise! O smokeless Fire! O Treasure that cannot be buried! O Boon that prevents aging! O un-enacted Dance! O Nataraja, the Treasure! O Nataraja, the Treasure!
commentary: God is described with a series of compelling images. A "smokeless Fire" is a pure spiritual energy, providing light and heat without the obscuring residue of worldly life. The "un-enacted Dance" is a beautiful paradox: God's cosmic dance creates and sustains the universe, yet God remains perfectly still and uninvolved, a transcendent source of all action. The "Boon that prevents aging" refers to the timeless, immortal state granted by attaining oneness with the divine.

translit: civañāṉa nilaiyē civayōka niṟaivē civapōka uruvē civamāṉa uṇarvē navanīta matiyē navanāta katiyē naṭarāja patiyē naṭarāja patiyē.
translation: O State of Siva-Knowledge! O Fullness of Siva-Yoga! O Embodiment of Siva-Bliss! O Consciousness that is Siva! O Wisdom, soft as fresh butter! O Goal of the nine sacred sounds! O Nataraja, the Lord! O Nataraja, the Lord!
commentary: This verse maps out the inner path. It begins with Siva-Knowledge (the direct knowing of divine reality), moves to Siva-Yoga (the union with that reality), and culminates in Siva-Bliss (the joy of that union). In the end, one's own consciousness becomes identical with Siva. The reference to navanātham (the nine sacred sounds of creation) identifies God as the source and goal of all cosmic vibration.

translit: tavayōka palamē civañāṉa nilamē talaiyēṟum aṇiyē vilaiyēṟu maṇiyē navavāra naṭamē cuvakāra puṭamē naṭarāja paramē naṭarāja paramē.
translation: O Fruit of ascetic yoga! O Ground of Siva-Knowledge! O Crown Jewel! O Gem of immense value! O ever-new Dance! O Crucible of self-manifestation! O Nataraja, the Supreme! O Nataraja, the Supreme!
commentary: Here, God is both the reward for spiritual practice ('Fruit of ascetic yoga') and the very foundation of it ('Ground of Siva-Knowledge'). The image of a 'Crucible of self-manifestation' suggests that the divine is a space where the self is refined to reveal its true nature. The 'ever-new Dance' conveys that God's creative expression is endless and always fresh.

translit: tutivēta uṟavē cukapōta naṟavē tuṉitīrum iṭamē taṉiñāṉa naṭamē natiyāra nitiyē atikāra patiyē naṭarāja kuruvē naṭarāja kuruvē.
translation: O Kinship extolled by the Vedas! O sweet Nectar of blissful awareness! O Place where suffering ends! O Dance of supreme knowledge! O Treasure, abundant as a river! O Lord of all authority! O Nataraja, the Guru! O Nataraja, the Guru!
commentary: Vallalar identifies Nataraja as the ultimate guru or spiritual teacher. This teacher is the divine principle itself, manifesting as a 'Dance of supreme knowledge'. God is an intimate 'kinship', a safe 'Place where suffering ends', and a source of grace as 'abundant as a river'.

translit: vayamāṉa varamē viyamāṉa paramē maṉamōṉa nilaiyē kaṉañāṉa malaiyē nayamāṉa uraiyē naṭuvāṉa varaiyē naṭarāja turaiyē naṭarāja turaiyē.
translation: O boon that has come under my power! O wondrous Supreme Being! O state of mental silence! O mountain of profound wisdom! O gracious utterance! O central mountain! O Lord Nataraja! O Lord Nataraja!
commentary: This verse expresses a high spiritual attainment. The 'boon that has come under my power' is a striking claim: divine grace becomes a lasting state, one's own. This state is maṉamōṉam (mental silence), a quiet mind that becomes a 'mountain of deep wisdom'. The 'central mountain' evokes the image of the world's axis, positioning God as the stable, immovable center of all existence.

translit: patiyuṟu poruḷē poruḷuṟu payaṉē payaṉuṟu niṟaivē niṟaivuṟu veḷiyē matiyuṟum amutē amutuṟu cuvaiyē maṟaimuṭi maṇiyē maṟaimuṭi maṇiyē.
translation: O Reality that is the Lord! O Fruit of that Reality! O Fullness of that Fruit! O Expanse of that Fullness! O Ambrosia grasped by the mind! O Taste of that Ambrosia! O jewel on the crown of the Vedas! O jewel on the crown of the Vedas!
commentary: This verse describes a cascade of divine experience, where each quality flows from the one before it. God is the ultimate reality, the fruit that comes from it, the fullness of that fruit, and the infinite expanse that contains it all, culminating in the highest truth of the Vedas.

translit: aruḷuṟu veḷiyē veḷiyuṟu poruḷē atuvuṟu matuvē matuvuṟu cuvaiyē maruḷaṟu teruḷē teruḷuṟu moḷiyē maṟaimuṭi maṇiyē maṟaimuṭi maṇiyē.
translation: O Expanse of Grace! O Substance of the Expanse! O Honey of 'That'! O Taste of the Honey! O Clarity that ends confusion! O Light of that Clarity! O jewel on the crown of the Vedas! O jewel on the crown of the Vedas!
commentary: Following a similar cascading pattern, God is revealed as the very substance of the expanse of grace. This reality is the sweet essence of "That" (a name for the ultimate, indescribable being) and the pure clarity that dispels all confusion, shining as the ultimate wisdom of the sacred texts.

translit: taruvaḷar niḻalē niḻalvaḷar cukamē taṭamvaḷar puṉalē puṉalvaḷar nalaṉē tiruvaḷar uruvē uruvaḷar uyirē tirunaṭa maṇiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē.
translation: O shade growing from the tree! O bliss growing in the shade! O water filling the pond! O goodness flourishing from the water! O sacred form where divinity thrives! O life thriving in the form! O jewel of the sacred dance! O jewel of the sacred dance!
commentary: Using images from nature, the verse shows how the divine is both the source and the resulting experience. Just as bliss arises from the shade of a tree, or goodness from life-giving water, the divine is the sacred form and also the very life that animates it.

translit: uyiruṟum uṇarvē uṇarvuṟum oḷiyē oḷiyuṟu veḷiyē veḷiyuṟu veḷiyē ceyiraṟu patiyē civaniṟai nitiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē.
translation: O consciousness within life! O light within consciousness! O space within the light! O space within space! O flawless Lord! O treasure filled with Sivam! O jewel of the sacred dance! O jewel of the sacred dance!
commentary: Here, the focus turns inward, showing a progression from the vastness of life to the subtle core of existence. God is the consciousness within life, the light within that consciousness, and the space within that light, revealed at last as the infinite and flawless treasure of Sivam (the auspicious, ultimate reality).

translit: kalainiṟai matiyē matiniṟai amutē katiniṟai katirē katirniṟai cuṭarē cilainiṟai nilaiyē nilainiṟai civamē tirunaṭa maṇiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē.
translation: O moon full of all arts, O ambrosia that fills the moon, O sunbeam full of refuge, O flame that fills the sunbeam, O state that fills the sacred form, O Sivam that fills that state, O Jewel of the Sacred Dance.
commentary: God's nature is here compared to the completeness of the moon and the intensity of the sun. The full moon represents a perfect, cool wisdom filled with divine ambrosia, while the sunbeam is a powerful ray of grace offering total refuge. God, or Sivam, is the fullness that resides within both light and life.

translit: mikavuyar neṟiyē neṟiyuyar viḷaivē viḷaivuyar cukamē cukamuyar patamē tikaḻuyar uyarvē uyaruyar uyarvē tirunaṭa maṇiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē.
translation: O most exalted path, O highest fruit of the path, O supreme bliss from that fruit, O ultimate state from that bliss, O radiant height of all that is high, O height of the highest of heights, O Jewel of the Sacred Dance.
commentary: The spiritual path is a continuous ascent, with each step leading to a higher one. The path yields a fruit, which leads to a state of bliss, which in turn reveals an even higher state of being. The final description of God as the "height of the highest of heights" portrays divinity as the absolute pinnacle of existence, beyond all relative measures.

translit: iyalkiḷar maṟaiyē maṟaikiḷar icaiyē icaikiḷar tutiyē tutikiḷar iṟaiyē ceyalkiḷar aṭiyē aṭikiḷar muṭiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē.
translation: O Veda from which perfect speech arises, O music that arises from the Veda, O praise that arises from the music, O Lord revealed by that praise, O sacred feet from which all action arises, O sacred crown that arises from the feet, O Jewel of the Sacred Dance.
commentary: All sacred expression flows from God and leads back to God in a complete circle. Perfect speech arises from the Veda (sacred scripture), which inspires music and praise, which in turn reveals the Lord. This divine reality is complete, encompassing both the feet from which all action begins and the crown where all things culminate.

translit: puraiyaṟu pukaḻē pukaḻpeṟu poruḷē poruḷatu muṭipē muṭivuṟu puṇarvē tiraiyaṟu kaṭalē kaṭaleḻu cutaiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē.
translation: O flawless glory, O reality that holds that glory, O culmination of that reality, O union that is the culmination, O waveless ocean, O ambrosia arising from the ocean, O Jewel of the Sacred Dance.
commentary: The ultimate state of being is a flawless, undisturbed peace. The metaphor of a "waveless ocean" suggests a reality that is perfectly still, infinite, and free from all agitation. This is the final union, the culmination of all existence, from which life-giving ambrosia arises.

translit: nikaḻnava nilaiyē nilaiyuyar nilaiyē niṟaiyaruḷ nitiyē nititaru patiyē tikaḻciva patamē civapata cukamē tirunaṭa maṇiyē tirunaṭa maṇiyē.
translation: O ever-new and manifest state, O state supreme above all states, O treasure of abundant grace, O Lord who bestows that treasure, O radiant realm of Sivam, O bliss of the realm of Sivam, O Jewel of the Sacred Dance.
commentary: The experience of God is described as an "ever-new and manifest state," always fresh and alive. This supreme state, called the state of Sivam (the ultimate, auspicious reality), is a treasure of grace. God is both the treasure and the one who gives it, the state of bliss and the bliss itself.

translit: nīṭiya vētam tēṭiya pātam nēṭiya kītam pāṭiya pātam āṭiya pōtam kūṭiya pātam āṭiya pātam āṭiya pātam.
translation: The feet sought by the enduring Vedas, the feet sung by loving hymns, the feet joined with the dancing consciousness, the dancing feet, the dancing feet.
commentary: All forms of spiritual seeking, from the ancient Vedas (scriptures) to heartfelt songs of devotion, are directed toward the Lord's sacred feet. These feet represent a physical form and also the very foundation of reality, the point of contact between the divine and the world. To unite with them is to unite with the dancing consciousness of God.

translit: cākkiya vētam tēkkiya pātam tākkiya ētam pōkkiya pātam cōkkiya vātam ākkiya pātam tūkkiya pātam tūkkiya pātam.
translation: The feet that contained the Buddhist doctrines, the feet that dispel attacking afflictions, the feet that create the doctrine of bliss, the lifted foot, the lifted foot.
commentary: This verse makes a powerful claim for inclusiveness, stating that even the Sākkia Vētam (Buddhist doctrines) are contained within the reality represented by the Lord's feet. This suggests that the ultimate truth is the source of all valid spiritual teachings. These same feet offer protection from suffering and establish the true "doctrine of bliss," which is direct experience, more than philosophy. The "lifted foot" is a classic image of Lord Siva as the cosmic dancer, symbolizing refuge and liberation.

translit: ēṉṟiya cūtam tōṉṟiya pātam īṉṟiya nātam āṉṟiya pātam ōṉṟiya pūtam ñāṉṟiya pātam ūṉṟiya pātam ūṉṟiya pātam.
translation: The feet that appeared under the sacred mango tree, the feet that are the fullness of creative sound, the feet on which the united elements depend, the planted foot, the planted foot.
commentary: The divine is the source of specific revelations, the origin of creation itself, and the foundation upon which the physical world rests. The "planted foot" of the cosmic dancer provides stability to the world, balancing the liberation offered by the lifted foot. This single divine presence is both the unmoving ground of being and the dynamic force of grace.

translit: cañcitam vīṭum neñcita pātam tañcita mākum cañcita pātam koñcita mēvum rañcita pātam kuñcita pātam kuñcita pātam.
translation: The feet, desired by the heart, that release one from accumulated karma, the graceful feet that become a dear refuge, the delightful feet, possessing charming beauty, the curved foot, the curved foot.
commentary: The divine feet are the ultimate refuge for the soul, offering release from the weight of past actions. Sanchita karma is the total accumulation of all our past deeds over many lifetimes; Vallalar says that turning to God with a sincere heart can wipe this slate clean. The "curved foot" is another name for the lifted foot of the dancing Siva, representing the highest grace.

translit: eṇṇiya nāṉē tiṇṇiyaṉ āṉēṉ eṇṇiya vāṟē naṇṇiya pēṟē puṇṇiyaṉ āṉēṉ aṇṇiyaṉ āṉēṉ puṇṇiya vāṉē puṇṇiya vāṉē.
translation: I, who meditated on you, became strong. The blessing I received is just as I imagined. I became meritorious; I became one who is near to you. O embodiment of all merit! O embodiment of all merit!
commentary: Here, the focus shifts from the divine to the devotee's transformation. Meditating on God is not a passive act; it makes the worshipper strong, worthy, and close to the divine presence. Vallalar is describing a direct, personal experience where the reward for seeking God is the very fulfillment one hoped for.

translit: tottiya cīrē pottiya pērē tuttiya pāvē pattiya nāvē cattiyam nāṉē nittiyaṉ āṉēṉ cattiya vāṉē cattiya vāṉē.
translation: O attained Glory! O treasured Name! O praised Song! O speech of the devout tongue! I myself am Truth; I have become eternal. O Heaven of Truth! O Heaven of Truth!
commentary: This is the peak of the devotional experience. After praising God through name, song, and speech, the separation between the worshipper and the worshipped dissolves. Vallalar declares a complete union: "I myself am Truth; I have become eternal." He is no longer just near to God; he has realized his own nature is identical to the divine reality he was praising.

translit: empulap pakaiyē empulat tuṟavē emkulat tavamē emkulac civamē ampiṉil kaṉalē antaṇark kiṟaiyē ampalat taracē ampalat taracē.
translation: O enemy to my senses! O renunciation of my senses! O spiritual discipline of my lineage! O Sivam of my lineage! O fire within the water! O Lord of the truly righteous! O King of the Ambalam! O King of the Ambalam!
commentary: God is addressed paradoxically as both the enemy of the distracting senses and the state of renunciation that overcomes them. This divine presence is also a personal inheritance, the Sivam (the ultimate reality) of one's own lineage. God is the hidden power, like fire within water, and the king of the Ambalam (the sacred expanse of consciousness).

translit: iṉpuṭaip poruḷē iṉcuvaik kaṉiyē eṇkuṇac cuṭarē intakat toḷiyē aṉpuṭaik kuruvē ampuyaṟ kiṟaiyē ampalat tamutē ampalat tamutē.
translation: O Substance of bliss! O Fruit of sweet flavor! O Flame of the eight qualities! O Light within the moon! O Guru who embodies love! O Lord even of Brahma, the lotus-born! O Nectar of the Ambalam! O Nectar of the Ambalam!
commentary: God is the very substance of bliss, experienced as sweet fruit, guiding light, and a loving teacher (guru). The "eight qualities" refer to God's perfect attributes, and as Lord of the lotus-born He is Lord even of Brahma, the creator. All these blissful aspects are found as nectar in the Ambalam, the vast inner space of consciousness.

translit: vēta cikāmaṇiyē pōta cukōtayamē mētaku māporuḷē ōtarum ōrnilaiyē nāta parāparamē cūta parāvamutē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O Crest-Jewel of the Vedas! O Dawn of Blissful Awareness! O Great, Exalted Reality! O Singular, Indescribable State! O Transcendent Sound, Supreme-Beyond-Supreme! O Supreme Nectar of Delight! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom!
commentary: God is the highest truth found in the Vedas (sacred scriptures) and the ultimate source of blissful awareness. This reality is singular and beyond description, the primal sound (nāda) from which all emerges, and the supreme nectar experienced in the Ñāṉa Capai (Hall of Wisdom).

translit: ēka catācivamē yōka cukākaramē ēma parānalamē kāma vimōcaṉamē nāka vikācaṉamē nāta cukōṭaṇamē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O One, Ever-Auspicious One! O Source of Yogic Bliss! O Supreme Golden Goodness! O Liberator from Desire! O Unfolder of the Serpent Power! O Blissful Sustenance of the Primal Sound! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom!
commentary: God is hailed as the source of yogic bliss and the power that liberates the soul from worldly desire. The verse references Sadasivam (the eternally auspicious form of God) and the "Unfolder of the Serpent Power," which refers to the awakening of spiritual energy (kuṇḍalinī) that leads to higher consciousness.

translit: tūya catākatiyē nēya catācivamē cōma cikāmaṇiyē vāma umāpatiyē ñāya parākaramē kāya purātaramē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O Pure, Eternal Refuge! O Beloved, Ever-Auspicious One! O Crest-Jewel wearing the Moon! O Lord of Uma on the left! O Supreme Source of Justice! O Ancient Support of the body! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom!
commentary: Vallalar uses traditional descriptions of the deity Siva to evoke a sense of loving intimacy with God. The moon in the hair symbolizes control over the mind and a cooling, blissful energy. The "Lord of Uma on the left" (Umāpati) depicts the divine as the perfect union of masculine and feminine principles. This is a God who is both a personal, beloved refuge and the cosmic foundation that supports our very bodies.

translit: āraṇa ñāpakamē pūraṇa cōpaṉamē ātia ṉātiyaṉē vētiya ṉātiyaṉē nāraṇa ṉātaramē kāraṇa mēparamē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O Essence of the Vedas! O Perfect Auspiciousness! O Beginning and the Beginningless One! O Primal One known to Vedic scholars! O Support of Narayana! O Supreme Cause! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom!
commentary: God is the single, ultimate source of all existence, including the scriptures and other divine beings. By calling God the "Support of Narayana" (a primary name for the deity Vishnu), Vallalar expresses a universal vision where one supreme reality underlies the various forms of God worshipped in different traditions. God is the first cause, the beginning of all beginnings.

translit: ākama pōtakamē yātara vētakamē āmaya mōcaṉamē āramu tākaramē nāka naṭōtayamē nāta purōtayamē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O Teacher of the Agamas! O Alchemist who transforms through love! O Liberator from affliction! O Source of precious Nectar! O Dawning of the Serpent's Dance! O Dawning of the Primal Sound! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom! O Lord of the Hall of Wisdom!
commentary: God is the supreme teacher, whose wisdom is found in the Agamas (sacred philosophical and ritual texts). Yet this teaching is not merely intellectual; God is an alchemist who transforms the soul through love, healing all affliction. This inner transformation awakens our own spiritual potential, experienced as the "Serpent's Dance" and the vibration of the "Primal Sound" within.

translit: āṭaka nīṭoḷiyē nēṭaka nāṭaḷiyē āti purātaṉaṉē vēti parāparaṉē nāṭaka nāyakaṉē nāṉava ṉāṉavaṉē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O vast light of pure gold! O you who grace those who seek you! O primordial and ancient one! O Creator, the supreme transcendent! O hero of the cosmic play! O you who have become one with me! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom!
commentary: The universe is a grand "cosmic play," and God is its hero and director. The final lines reveal the culmination of the spiritual path. The devotee's separate identity dissolves, and the great actor of the cosmos becomes one with the individual soul. The "Sabha of Wisdom" is the inner stage where this union of the human and the divine is realized.

translit: āriya ṉēcivaṉē āraṇa ṉēpavaṉē ālaya ṉēaraṉē ātara ṉēcuraṉē nāriya ṉēvaraṉē nāṭiya ṉēparaṉē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O noble one! O Sivan! O you who are the Vedas! O source of all being! O sacred temple! O Haran! O my support! O Lord of the celestials! O you who are one with the Woman! O bestower of boons! O one who is sought! O supreme one! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom!
commentary: By using many different names for God, including Sivan and Haran, Vallalar shows that all forms of divinity point to the same singular reality. The phrase "you who are one with the Woman" refers to the divine as a perfect union of masculine and feminine principles, a complete being who is our only true support.

translit: ātara vētiyaṉē āṭaka jōtiyaṉē āraṇi pātiyaṉē ātara vātiyaṉē nāta vipūtiyaṉē nāma vaṉātiyaṉē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O my support and creator! O Jothi of pure gold! O you whose half is the Goddess! O primal source of all support! O glorious power of Nada! O nameless and beginningless one! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom!
commentary: God is both a personal creator and the impersonal, nameless source of all that is. He is the divine light (Jothi) and the primal vibration of creation (Nada), yet he is also described as "nameless and beginningless," a mystery beyond all human categories.

translit: tēva kalānitiyē jīva tayānitiyē tīṉa cakānitiyē cēkara mānitiyē nāvala rōrpatiyē nāri umāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O treasure-house of divine arts! O treasure-house of compassion for all souls! O treasure-house of friendship for the destitute! O great and crowning treasure! O singular Lord of the learned! O Lord of Uma, the Woman! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom!
commentary: God's true greatness is found in compassion. While God is the source of all knowledge and art, Vallalar emphasizes that God's ultimate nature is a "treasure-house of compassion for all souls" and a friend to the most vulnerable.

translit: āṭiya nāṭakaṉē ālamar ātiyaṉē ākama mēlavaṉē āraṇa nālavaṉē nāṭiya kāraṇaṉē nīṭiya pūraṇaṉē ñāṉa capāpatiyē ñāṉa capāpatiyē.
translation: O you who danced the cosmic play! O primordial one seated under the banyan! O you who are supreme over the Agamas! O embodiment of the four Vedas! O the cause that is sought! O eternal, perfect fullness! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom! O Lord of the Sabha of Wisdom!
commentary: This verse unites different aspects of God: the dynamic creator dancing the cosmos into being, and the silent, primordial teacher. God is the living essence of the scriptures (Agamas and Vedas), the hidden cause behind everything, and the final, peaceful fullness that all souls are seeking.

translit: ampalattē tirunaṭañcey aṭimalareṉ muṭimēl aṇintukoṇṭēṉ aṉpoṭumeṉ āruyirkkum aṇintēṉ emparattē maṇakkumanta malarmaṇattait tōḻi eṉuraippēṉ uraikkaeṉṟāl eṉṉaḷavaṉ ṟatuvē vampicaittēṉ aṉṟaṭinī eṉarukē iruntuṉ maṇināci aṭaippataṉait tiṟantumukan taṟikāṇ nampuṟupār mutalnāta varaiyuḷanāṭ ṭavarum naṉkumukan taṉarviyantār naṉmaṇamī teṉavē.
translation: I have adorned my head with the flower-like feet of the one who performs the sacred dance in the Ambalam. With love, I have also adorned my very life-breath with them. O friend, what can I say about the fragrance of that flower that perfumes my entire being? To describe it is beyond my capacity. I am not speaking idly. Come, sit beside me, unblock your precious nostrils, and smell it to know for yourself. The inhabitants of all realms, from this trusted earth up to the realm of Natham, have smelled it well, were astonished, and declared, “This is a truly fine fragrance!”
commentary: Divine grace is a real, perceptible experience. Vallalar describes it as a beautiful fragrance from God's "flower-like feet" that fills his entire being. The experience is so powerful that he invites his friend to perceive it and declares that all beings in all worlds, from earth up to the level of Natham (primordial sound), can recognize its sublime nature.

translit: kaṇuṟaṅkēṉ uṟaṅkiṉumeṉ kaṇavaroṭu kalakkum kaṉavēkaṇ ṭuḷamakiḻvēṉ kaṉavoṉṟō naṉavum eṇaṭaṅkāp peruñjōti eṉiṟaivar eṉaiyē iṇaintiravu pakalkāṇā tiṉpuṟaccey kiṉṟār maṇuṟaṅkum malaiuṟaṅkum vaḷaikaṭalum uṟaṅkum maṟṟuḷael lāmuṟaṅkum mānilattē namatu peṇuṟaṅkāḷ eṉattāyar pēcimakiḻ kiṉṟār peṇkaḷelām kūcukiṉṟār peruntavañcey kilarē.
translation: I do not sleep. Even if I do sleep, I only see dreams of uniting with my husband, and my heart rejoices. And it is more than in dreams. In my waking life too, the immeasurable great Jothi, my Lord, unites with me, making me experience bliss, oblivious to night and day. The earth sleeps, the mountains sleep, the encircling sea sleeps, and all other things sleep. On this great earth, my mothers joyfully say, “Our girl does not sleep.” All the other women are abashed, for they have not performed such great penance.
commentary: The state of divine union transforms ordinary life, even transcending the need for sleep. While the rest of the world sleeps, unconscious, the soul remains awake in a constant state of blissful communion with God, the supreme Jothi (light). Most people would see sleeplessness as a problem, but here it is a sign of a higher state of awareness and joy, a state of being that sets the devotee apart.

translit: ellāñcey vallaturai eṉṉaimaṇam purintār evvulakil yāreṉakkiṅ kīṭurainī tōḻī nallāymīk kōḷuṭaiyār intirarmā muṉivar nāṉmukarnā raṇarellām vāṉmukarāy niṉṟē pallāril ivaḷpurinta peruntavattai nammāl pakarvariteṉ kiṉṟārciṟ patiyilnaṭam puriyum vallāṉai maṇantiṭavum peṟṟaṉaḷiṅ kivaḷē vallāḷeṉ ṟuraikkiṉṟār nallārkaḷ palarē.
translation: The Lord who can do all things has married me. In all the worlds, who is my equal? You tell me, friend. O good one, the highly praised Indra, the great sages, the four-faced Brahma, and Narayana all stand looking up at the sky and say, “Among the many, the great penance this woman has performed is too difficult for us to describe. She has attained the fortune of marrying the master who performs the dance in the domain of consciousness. She is a truly capable one.” This is what many good people are saying.
commentary: The soul that unites directly with the all-powerful Lord achieves a status beyond compare. Vallalar expresses this through the voice of the bride, who asks who could possibly be her equal now that she is "married" to God. The verse claims that even the great celestial beings like Indra, Brahma, and Narayana look on in astonishment at the good fortune of a soul that has achieved such an intimate union.

translit: iccaielām vallaturai eṉṉaimaṇam purintār yāṉceytavam yārceytār itukēḷeṉ tōḻi eccamayat tēvaraiyum ciṟṟurumpeṉ ṟēṉum eṇṇuvaṉō puṇṇiyarai eṇṇumaṉat tālē piccieṉa niṉaittālum niṉaiyaṭinī avaraip pirivēṉō piriveṉṟu pēcukiṉum tariyēṉ viccainaṭam kaṇṭēṉnāṉ naṭaṅkaṇṭāl pēyum viṭattuṇiyā teṉparkaḷeṉ viḷaivuraippa teṉṉē.
translation: The Lord who is master of all will has married me. Who has performed the penance that I have performed? Listen to this, my friend. Will I ever consider the gods of any other religion to be even as significant as a tiny ant? Even if you think I am a madwoman with a mind that thinks only of the holy one, will I ever leave him? I cannot even bear it if someone speaks of separation. I have seen the dance of divine knowledge. They say that even a ghost, if it sees that dance, would not dare to leave. What then is there to say about my state?
commentary: Union with the one true God leaves no room for any other allegiance. The bride will not count the gods of any religion as worth even a tiny ant: her Lord alone is real to her. Having seen the divine "dance of knowledge," she is utterly captivated; the very word separation is unbearable.

translit: vañcamilāt talaivarukkē mālaimakiḻn taṇintēṉ maṟaikaḷuṭaṉ ākamaṅkaḷ vakuttuvakut turaikkum eñcaluṟā vāḻvaṉaittum eṉṉuṭaiya vāḻvē eṟṟōnāṉ purintatavam caṟṟēnī uraiyāy añcumukam kāṭṭiyaeṉ tāyarelām eṉakkē āṟumukam kāṭṭimika vīṟupaṭaik kiṉṟār pañcaṭippā vaiyarellām viñcaṭippāl iruntē paravukiṉṟār tōḻieṉṟaṉ uṟavumika viḻaintē.
translation: I have joyfully placed the garland on the guileless Lord. All the unending life that the Vedas and Agamas describe in great detail is my life. What penance did I perform? Tell me, just a little. My mothers, who once showed me a fearful face, now show me a gracious one and take immense pride in me. All the women with feet as soft as cotton now stand at a distance and praise me, O friend, greatly desiring to be my kin.
commentary: Spiritual union transforms the inner self and one's entire world. The devotee claims the eternal life described in the scriptures (Vedas and Agamas, ancient sacred texts) as her own direct inheritance. This inner change is mirrored externally: family members who once feared for her now see her with pride, and her community now looks to her with reverence. Her connection to God has reordered her social reality.

translit: aṉṉamuṇa aḻaikkiṉṟāy tōḻiiṅkē nāṉtāṉ ampalattē āṭukiṉṟa aṇṇalaṭi malarttēṉ uṉṉainiṉait tuṇṭēṉeṉ uḷḷakattē vāḻum orutalaimaip peruntalaiva ruṭaiyaaruṭ pukaḻām iṉṉamutil eṉṉuṭaiaṉ peṉṉumnaṟuṅ kaṉiyiṉ iratamumeṉ taṉikkaṇavar urukkāṭci eṉumōr kaṉṉaluḷē taṉitteṭutta tēmpākum kalantē kaḷittuṇṭēṉ paciciṟitum kaṇṭilaṉuḷ ḷakattē.
translation: Friend, you call me to come eat, but I have already partaken of the flower-honey from the feet of the Lord who dances in the Hall. He is the one supreme Leader who lives within my heart. Into the sweet ambrosia of his grace-filled fame, I mixed the juice of the fragrant fruit of my love and the sweet syrup extracted from the sugarcane that is the vision of my unique husband's form. I ate it with delight, and I feel not the slightest hunger within.
commentary: The nourishment that comes from God is so complete that it replaces the need for physical food. The speaker describes a spiritual meal made of divine grace, her own love, and the vision of God's form. This experience of being completely filled with divine presence creates a state of total satisfaction where worldly appetites, like hunger, simply cease to exist.

translit: potunaṭañcey turaimukattē taḷataḷaeṉ ṟoḷirum puṉṉakaiyē orukōṭip poṉpeṟumeṉ ṟuraippār ituvaraiyō palakōṭi eṉṉiṉumōr aḷavō eṇiṟanta aṇṭavakai ettaṉaikō ṭikaḷum catumaṟaicol aṇṭavakai taṉittaṉiyē naṭattum cattarkaḷum cattikaḷum caṟṟēṉum peṟumō tutipeṟumat tiruvāḷar puṉṉakaiyai niṉaikkun tōṟummaṉam ūṟukiṉṟa cukaamutam peṟumē.
translation: People say the smile that shines brilliantly on the face of the one who performs the cosmic dance is worth ten million gold pieces. But even many tens of millions is no measure for it. Can the Saktars and Saktis, who individually govern the countless tens of millions of universal systems spoken of in the four Vedas, obtain even a little of it? Yet, whenever my mind thinks of the smile of that praiseworthy Lord, it receives the sweet ambrosia of bliss that wells up from within.
commentary: Even a momentary glimpse of divine reality is infinitely precious. The Lord's smile is a treasure beyond all wealth, something unobtainable even by the powerful cosmic beings (Saktars and Saktis) who govern the many universes. Yet, this priceless bliss is freely available to any devotee through the simple act of remembrance. The path to grace lies in the heart's loving attention.

translit: kaṇkalanta kaṇavareṉaik kaikalanta taruṇam kaṇṭaṟiyēṉ eṉṉaiyumeṉ karaṇaṅkaḷ taṉaiyum eṇkalanta pōkamelām civapōkam taṉilōr iṟaiaḷaveṉ ṟuraikkiṉṟa maṟaiaḷaviṉ ṟaṟintēṉ viṇkalanta tiruvāḷar uyirkalanta taruṇam viṉaittuyartīrn taṭaintacukam niṉaittiṭuntō ṟellām uṇkalanta āṉantap perumpōkam appō tuṟṟateṉa eṉaiviḻuṅkak kaṟṟatukāṇ tōḻi.
translation: When my husband, whose eyes had met mine, took my hand, I was not aware of the moment at all, nor of myself, nor of my inner faculties. I understood from the measure of the Vedas that all imaginable worldly pleasures are but a tiny fraction of the bliss of Siva. The glorious Lord who pervades the heavens mingled with my soul, and my karmic suffering ended. Now, every time I recall the bliss I attained at that moment, that great, all-pervading ecstasy has learned to swallow me whole, you see, friend.
commentary: The moment of mystical union with God is so absolute that it dissolves all sense of individual self and the outside world. In that state, all worldly pleasures are revealed as insignificant compared to the singular bliss of communion with the Divine. The experience is more than a past event; its memory is so powerful that it can re-ignite the original ecstasy, completely overwhelming the self once more.

translit: māṭamicai ōṅkunilā maṇṭapattē eṉatu maṇavāḷar koṭuttatiru aruḷamutam makiḻntē ēṭaviḻpūṅ kuḻalāynāṉ uṇṭatoru taruṇam eṉṉaiaṟin tilaṉulakam taṉṉaiyumnāṉ aṟiyēṉ tēṭaṟiya naṟumpālum tēmpākum neyyum tēṉumokkak kalantateṉac ceppiṉumcā lātē īṭaṟiyāc cuvaipukala eṉṉālē muṭiyā teṉṉaṭiyō avvamutam poṉṉaṭitāṉ nikarē.
translation: On the high terrace, in the moonlit hall, I delighted in drinking the sacred ambrosia of grace my bridegroom gave me. O friend with hair adorned with blossoming flowers, at the moment I consumed it, I knew not myself, nor did I know the world. Even to say it was like rare, fragrant milk, sweet syrup, ghee, and honey all mixed together is not adequate. It is impossible for me to describe its incomparable taste. What can I say, my dear? That ambrosia is equal only to His golden feet.
commentary: Divine grace is experienced as a drink, an ambrosia, that erases the distinction between self and world. This experience of bliss is so deep that it cannot be described with words or compared to any earthly taste. The only thing equal to this ambrosia is its source: the sacred feet of God, which symbolize the ultimate refuge and goal of the soul.

translit: kaṟpūram maṇakkiṉṟa teṉṉuṭampu muḻutum kaṇavartiru mēṉiyilē kalantamaṇam atutāṉ iṟpūta maṇampōlē maṟaivataṉṟu kaṇṭāy iyaṟkaimaṇam turiyaniṟai iṟaivaṭivat tuḷatē poṟpūvum naṟumaṇamum kaṇṭaṟiyār ulakar puṇṇiyaṉār tiruvaṭivil naṇṇiyavā ṟatuvē naṟpūti aṇintatiru vaṭivumuṟṟum tōḻi nāṉkaṇṭēṉ nāṉpuṇarntēṉ nāṉatuā ṉēṉē.
translation: My whole body smells of camphor. It is the fragrance from mingling with my husband's sacred form. See, it is not a fragrance that fades like the scents of this world. It is the natural fragrance inherent in the divine form, which is the fullness of the Turiya state. The people of the world have never known a golden flower and its sweet fragrance; that is how it exists on the sacred form of the Virtuous One. Friend, I saw that entire sacred form adorned with fine sacred ash, I united with it, I became it.
commentary: Union with God is a total transformation that leaves a lasting mark, like a divine fragrance permeating the devotee's body. This scent is eternal, unlike worldly perfumes, because it is the natural quality of pure divine consciousness, a state known as Turiya. The verse culminates in the ultimate mystic realization: the soul saw and united with God and became one with that divine reality.

translit: maṉṉutiruc capainaṭuvē vayaṅkunaṭam puriyum maṇavāḷar tirumēṉi vaṇṇaṅkaṇ ṭuvantēṉ eṉṉaṭiit tirumēṉi iruntavaṇṇam tōḻi eṉpukalvēṉ matiiravi ilaṅkumaṅki uṭaṉē miṉṉumoṉṟāyk kūṭiyavai eṇkaṭanta kōṭi viḷaṅkumvaṇṇam eṉṟuraikkō uraikkiṉumcā lātē aṉṉavaṇṇam maṟaimuṭivum aṟaivaritē anta arumperuñcō tiyiṉvaṇṇam yāruraippar antō.
translation: I saw the color of my Groom's divine form as he performs his radiant dance in the center of the eternal, sacred Sabhai, and I was overjoyed. Oh friend, what can I say about the nature of this divine form? Should I describe it as the brilliance of countless crores of moons, suns, blazing fires, and lightnings all gathered as one? Even saying that is not enough. The pinnacle of the Vedas finds it hard to describe such a color. Alas, who can describe the color of that rare, great Jothi?
commentary: The vision of God is an experience of overwhelming, indescribable light. Vallalar uses the metaphor of the cosmic dance happening in the sacred hall (Sabhai), a symbol for the heart or the center of consciousness. He struggles to find words for the "color" of the divine form, dismissing even the most dazzling cosmic imagery as inadequate. This ultimate reality, the great divine light or Jothi, transcends all scripture and human attempts to define it; it can be experienced, but never fully explained.

translit: kaḷḷuṇṭāḷ eṉappukaṉṟār kaṉakacapai naṭuvē kaṇṭatuṇṭu ciṟcapaiyil uṇṭatumuṇ ṭaṭināṉ eḷḷuṇṭa palaviṭayat tiṟaṅkuṅkaḷ aṉṟē eṉṟumiṟa vānilaiyil iruttuṅkaḷ ulakar uḷḷuṇṭa pōtumayak kuṟṟiṭuṅkaḷ alavē uḷḷamayak kaṉaittiṉaiyum oḻittiṭuṅkaḷ maṭavāy aḷḷuṇṭa piṟarumeṉai aṭuttaṭuttuk kaṇṭāl aṟivutarum avarkkumiṅkē yāṉuṇṭa kaḷḷē.
translation: They said I am like one who has drunk toddy. It is true, friend. I have seen in the center of the Kanaka Sabhai, and I have indeed drunk in the Chit Sabhai. This is not the drink that makes worldly people descend into despised sensual pleasures; rather, it places one in a state of eternal deathlessness. It is not a drink that brings confusion when consumed. Oh, innocent girl, it is the one that removes all inner confusion. If other people, consumed by worldly desires, see me again and again, this very toddy that I have drunk will give them wisdom too.
commentary: The speaker embraces the accusation that she is "drunk" but explains this is a divine intoxication, not a worldly one. This spiritual drink, found in the Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness), brings clarity and eternal life, unlike the toddy (kaḷ) that causes confusion. This state of bliss is so powerful that just being near her can grant wisdom to others lost in worldly desires.

translit: kārikainī eṉṉuṭaṉē kāṇavaru vāyō kaṉakacapai naṭuniṉṟa kaṇavarvaṭi vaḻakai ērikavāt tiruvaṭivai eṇṇamuṭi yātēl iyampamuṭin tiṭumōnām eḻutamuṭin tiṭumō pērikavā maṟaikaḷuṭaṉ ākamaṅkaḷ ellām piṉṉatumuṉ muṉṉatupiṉ piṉmuṉṉā mayaṅkip pārikavā tiṉṟaḷavum mikaeḻuti eḻutip pārkkiṉṟa muṭivoṉṟum pārttanilai ammā.
translation: Oh beautiful woman, will you come with me to see the beautiful form of our Master, who stands in the center of the Kanaka Sabhai? If we cannot even comprehend that immense, sacred form, can we ever describe it? Can we write of it? The voluminous Vedas and Agamas are all confused, putting what is last first and what is first last, jumbling the beginning and the end. To this day, they write and write at great length, yet, oh my, the conclusion they reach is not a state they have actually perceived.
commentary: Direct experience of God is superior to what can be learned from even the most sacred texts. The speaker says the divine form is impossible to fully comprehend or describe. She claims that the Vedas and Agamas (holy scriptures) are themselves confused, trying to write about a reality they have not directly perceived, unlike her.

translit: kaṇṇāṟupaṭumeṉanāṉ añcukiṉṟēṉ palakāl kaṇavartiru vaṭivaḻakaik kaṇṭukaṇṭu kaḷikkil eṇṇāeṉ ācaiveḷḷam eṉcolvaḻi kēḷā teṉaiīrttuk koṇṭucapaik kēkukiṉṟa tantō peṇṇācai periteṉpar viṇṇāḷum avarkkum peṇṇācai peritalakāṇ āṇācai peritē uṇṇāṭip paṟpalakāl kaṇṇāṟu kaḻikkal uṟukiṉṟēṉ tōḻiniṉṉāl peṟukiṉṟa paṭiyē.
translation: As I gaze and gaze upon the beauty of my Master's divine form and rejoice, I often fear that the evil eye will be cast. Alas, the immeasurable flood of my desire does not listen to my words, but drags me away to the Sabhai. They say desire for women is great. Even for those who rule the heavens, desire for women is not what is great. See here, desire for the Man is what is truly great. Oh friend, looking deep within, I find myself repeatedly performing the ritual to ward off the evil eye, just in the way I have learned from you.
commentary: The soul's desire for God is an overwhelming force that pulls her irresistibly toward the sacred Sabhai. She playfully declares that this "desire for the Man" is far greater than any earthly desire. Her love is so intense and protective that she feels the need to perform a ritual to ward off the evil eye (kaṇṇāṟu), worried that the sheer beauty of the divine form might attract harm.

translit: kaṟpūram koṇarntiṭuka taṉittōḻi eṉatu kaṇavarvaru taruṇamitu kaṇṇāṟu kaḻippām eṟpūta nilaiavartam tiruvaṭittā maraikkīḻ iruppataṭi kīḻiruppa teṉṟuniṉai yēlkāṇ paṟpūta nilaikaṭantu nātanilaik kappāl paranāta nilaiataṉmēl viḷaṅkukiṉṟa taṟinī iṟpūvai avvaṭikkuk kaṇṇāṟu kaḻittāl evvulakat tevvuyirkkum iṉitunalan tarumē.
translation: Bring camphor, my dear friend. This is the moment my Master will arrive; let us perform the ritual to ward off the evil eye. The elemental state I embody is beneath the lotus of his sacred feet, but do not think this means being in a low position. Know this: it shines above the state of Nada, which is beyond the states of the many elements, and even beyond the state of Para-Nada. If a woman of the house performs the evil eye ritual for those sacred feet, it will grant sweet well-being to every soul in every world.
commentary: A single act of pure devotion can bring grace to the entire cosmos. The speaker prepares to perform the evil eye ritual for her Master, an intimate act of love. The place beneath His lotus feet, she says, is not low: those feet shine above Para-Nada, beyond Nada (primordial sound) and beyond all the elements. So this loving gesture, offered at those feet, brings sweet good to every soul in every world.

translit: maṉaiaṇaintu malaraṇaimēl eṉaiaṇainta pōtu maṇavāḷar vaṭiveṉṟum eṉatuvaṭi veṉṟum taṉainiṉaintu pirittaṟinta tillaiyaṭi eṉaittāṉ caṟṟumaṟi yēṉeṉilyāṉ maṟṟaṟiva teṉṉē tiṉaiaḷavā yiṉumvikaṟpa uṇarccieṉpa tilaiyē tiruvāḷar kalantapaṭi ceppuvatep paṭiyō uṉaiaṇaintāl ivvāṟu nāṉkēṭpēṉ appō tuṉṉaṟivum eṉṉaṟivum ōraṟivām kāṇē.
translation: When he came to my house and embraced me on the flower bed, my friend, I had no separate thought of his form and my form. If I did not even know myself, what else could I know? There was not a millet-seed's worth of divisive perception. How can I describe the way the glorious Lord mingled with me? If he embraces you, I will ask you about it like this. At that time, you will see that your awareness and my awareness will become one.
commentary: In the ultimate moment of union with God, the distinction between "my form" and "his form" completely dissolves. The speaker explains that she lost all sense of her individual self, making it impossible to perceive anything as separate. This experience of non-separation is so complete that she tells her friend the only way to grasp it is to attain it herself, at which point their two minds will also become one awareness.

translit: tāḻkuḻalāy eṉaiccaṟṟē taṉikkaviṭṭāl ñāṉa capaittalaivar varukiṉṟa taruṇamitu nāṉtāṉ vāḻvaṭaipoṉ maṇṭapattē paḷikkaṟaiyi ṉūṭē malaraṇaiyai alaṅkarittu vaittiṭutal vēṇṭum cūḻuṟanāṉ alaṅkarippēṉ eṉkiṉṟāy tōḻi turaikkumaṉam illaiatu tuṇintaṟintēṉ palakāl ēḻkaṭalil peritaṉṟō nāṉaṭainta cukamiṅ kitaiviṭanāṉ ceypaṇivē ṟeppaṇinī iyampē.
translation: O you with flowing hair, if you would just leave me alone for a moment. This is the moment the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom is arriving. I must go and adorn the flower bed inside the crystal chamber in the golden hall of my abundant life. You say, "I will do all the decorating," my friend, but I have learned for certain many times that this is not my Master's wish. Is not the bliss I have attained here greater than the seven seas? Tell me, what service could I possibly perform other than this?
commentary: The soul's greatest joy is found in the personal, intimate act of preparing for the arrival of the divine Lord. The speaker gently refuses her friend's offer to help decorate the chamber for the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom (Gnana Sabai). This service is itself the source of her bliss, never to be handed to another, a happiness so immense that no other work could possibly compare.

translit: taṉittalaivar varukiṉṟa taruṇamitu tōḻi taṉikkaeṉai viṭunīyum taṉittorupāl irutti iṉittacuvait tiraḷkalanta tiruvārttai nīyum iṉpuṟakkēṭ ṭuḷaṅkaḷippāy itucālum niṉakkē maṉittarkaḷō vāṉavarō malarayaṉō mālō maṟṟaiyarō eṉpukalvēṉ makēcurarā tiyarum taṉittaoru tiruvārttai kēṭpataṟkē kōṭit tavañceytu niṟkiṉṟār navañceyta nilattē.
translation: Friend, this is the moment the singular Lord is arriving. Leave me alone. You too, sit apart by yourself. You can listen with pleasure to his sacred words, a blend of sweet essences, and rejoice in your heart. This will be enough for you. What can I say? Humans, celestials, flower-seated Brahma, Mal, or others… even Mahesvara and the rest are performing crores of penances on this hallowed ground just to hear a single sacred word from him.
commentary: Hearing a single word from God is a privilege of immeasurable value. The speaker tells her friend that even the highest celestial beings, including the creator-god Brahma and the preserver-god Vishnu (Mal), are performing immense penances just for the chance to hear what the soul is about to receive directly. For the friend, simply being allowed to listen from a distance is a great gift and blessing.

translit: maṇavāḷar varukiṉṟa taruṇamitu maṭavāy māḷikaiyiṉ vāyalelām vaḷampeṟanī puṉaika kuṇavāḷar aṇaiyummalar aṇaiakattai nāṉē kulavumaṇi viḷakkattāl alaṅkarikkap pukuvēṉ taṇavāta cukantarumeṉ taṉikkaṇavar varilō caṟṟumayal vātaṉaikaḷ uṟṟiṭutal ākā aṉavāta maṉattavaraip puṟappaṇikkē viṭuka aṉpuṭaiyār kaḷukkiṭuka akappaṇicey tiṭavē.
translation: O young woman, this is the moment the Bridegroom is arriving. You, adorn all the entrances of the mansion to make them beautiful. I myself will go and adorn the inner room containing the flower bed, where the Lord of virtues will recline, with radiant jeweled lamps. When my unique husband who gives unending bliss arrives, there must be no distracting influences at all. Assign those with unsteady minds to the outer tasks. Give the inner service to those who possess love.
commentary: Preparing for the arrival of the divine "Bridegroom" requires that tasks be assigned according to one's inner state.
