The speaker distinguishes between "outer work," like decorating the mansion entrances, and "inner service," like preparing the Lord's personal chamber. This reflects a spiritual principle: distracting, external duties are for those with unsteady minds, while the most sacred and intimate work is reserved for those whose hearts are filled with pure, steady love.

translit: arumpoṉaṉai yāreṉatu kaṇavarvaru taruṇam āyiḻaiī tātaliṉāl vāyalmukap pellām virumpuṟutō raṇamkoṭikaḷ paḻuttakulai vāḻai viraikkamuku teṅkiḷanīr eṉaippalavum puṉaika karumpunelliṉ muḷainiṟainīrk kuṭamiṇainta kayalum kaṇṇāṭi kavarimutal uṇṇāṭi iṭuka irumpoṭukal ottamaṉaṅ kaḷumkaṉiya urukkum iṟaivartiru varavetirkoṇ ṭēttuvataṟ kiṉitē.
translation: O woman of fine jewels, this is the moment my husband, who is like rare gold, is arriving. Therefore, adorn all the front entrances with lovely festoons, flags, bunches of ripe bananas, fragrant areca nut trees, tender coconuts, and many other things. Thoughtfully place sugarcane, pots full of water with rice sprouts, paired fish symbols, mirrors, ceremonial whisks, and more. It is sweet to welcome and praise the sacred arrival of the Lord who melts even hearts as hard as iron and stone until they are tender.
commentary: The preparations for the Lord's arrival use all the traditional symbols of a grand, auspicious welcome in Tamil culture: banana trees, coconuts, pots of water, mirrors, and more. This makes the divine event feel immediate and culturally rich, as if welcoming a beloved and highly honored guest home. The Lord's presence is described as so powerful it can soften even hearts as hard as iron and stone.

translit: pativarumōr taruṇamitu taruṇamitu tōḻī parākkaṭaiyēl maṇimāṭap pakkamelām puṉaika atikanalam peṟupaḷikku maṇimēṭai naṭuvē aṇaiyaialaṅ karittiṭanāṉ pukukiṉṟēṉ viraintē katitaruvār nalvaravu cattiyamcat tiyamnī kaḷippiṉoṭu maṇiviḷakkāl katirparava niraittē putiyanava maṇikuyiṉṟa ācaṉaṅkaḷ iṭuka puṇṇiyaṉār nalvaravai eṇṇieṇṇi iṉitē.
translation: Friend, this is the moment of my Lord's arrival, this is the moment! Do not be careless. Decorate all sides of the jeweled mansion. I am going in quickly to adorn the bed on the central crystal dais. His good arrival, which grants our ultimate state, is certain, certain. With joy, arrange rows of jeweled lamps so their rays spread out. Set out new seats inlaid with the nine gems, sweetly thinking and thinking of the holy one's good arrival.
commentary: The anticipation here is electric, with the speaker repeating that the moment of arrival is now and its blessing is absolutely certain. She directs her friend to fill the mansion with light from lamps while she herself prepares the innermost sanctuary. Her focus on decorating the central dais shows that the heart of the preparation is creating a place of pure, radiant beauty for the intimate union with God, which grants the soul its ultimate state (kathi).

translit: maṉṟāṭum kaṇavartiru varavainiṉaik kiṉṟēṉ makiḻntuniṉait tiṭuntōṟum maṉaṅkaṉivuṟ ṟuruki naṉṟāviṉ pāltiraḷiṉ naṟuneyyum tēṉum naṟkaruppañ cāṟeṭutta carkkaraiyum kūṭṭi iṉṟāra uṇṭateṉa iṉittiṉittup poṅki eḻunteṉaiyum viḻuṅkukiṉṟa teṉṟāleṉ tōḻi iṉṟāvi aṉṉavaraik kaṇṭukoḷum taruṇam eṉcaritam eppaṭiyō eṉpukalvēṉ antō.
translation: I am thinking of the arrival of my husband who dances in the cosmic hall. Every time I joyfully think of it, my heart ripens and melts. The feeling sweetens and sweetens, swells up, and swallows me whole, as if I have just feasted to my fill on fragrant ghee from the condensed milk of a fine cow, honey, and sugar from fresh sugarcane juice, all blended together. Friend, if this is so, then at the moment my soul beholds him today, what will my story be? What can I possibly say? Alas!
commentary: Even the mere thought of her husband's arrival is an experience of overwhelming ecstasy. Vallalar compares this feeling to being consumed by the richest, sweetest mixture imaginable: ghee, honey, and sugar from sugarcane. If just the anticipation can dissolve her sense of self in bliss, she wonders what the actual moment of union will be like, questioning if she can even contain it.

translit: kūṭiyaeṉ taṉikkaṇavar nalvarattai nāṉē kuṟikkiṉṟa tōṟumoḷi eṟikkiṉṟa maṉantāṉ nīṭiyapoṉ malaimuṭimēl vāḻvaṭainta tēvar nīḷmuṭimēl irukkiṉṟa teṉṟuraikkō aṉṟi āṭiyapoṟ capainaṭuvē ciṟcapaiyiṉ naṭuvē āṭukiṉṟa aṭiniḻaṟkīḻ irukkiṉṟa teṉkō ēṭaviḻpūṅ kuḻalāyeṉ iṟaivaraikkaṇ ṇuṟṟāl eṉmaṉattiṉ caritamatai yārpukalvār antō.
translation: Every time I contemplate the good arrival of my one husband who has already united with me, my mind radiates light. Shall I say my mind is now on the towering crowns of the Devas who have attained life on the high golden mountain peak? Or shall I say it is under the shade of the feet that dance in the middle of the golden hall, in the middle of the Hall of Consciousness? O friend with hair like unfolding blossoms, if I lay eyes on my Lord, who then could tell the story of my mind? Alas!
commentary: The act of thinking about God elevates the mind to a divine state. The speaker feels her consciousness transported, unsure if it now rests above the highest gods or at the very feet of the Lord dancing in the Cirsabai, the Hall of Consciousness. This shows that devotional focus is preparation for a future event and a transformation that happens now, lifting the mind into a sacred space. The experience of finally seeing God, she concludes, will be utterly beyond words.

translit: aruḷāḷar varukiṉṟa taruṇamitu tōḻi āyiramā yiraṅkōṭi aṇiviḷakkēṟ ṟiṭuka teruḷāya pacuneyyē viṭukamaṟṟai neyyēl tirumēṉik korumācu ceytālum ceyyum iruḷētu kālaiviḷak kēṟṟiṭavēṇ ṭuvatō eṉṉātē maṅkalamā ēṟṟutalāṅ kaṇṭāy maruḷēlaṅ kavarmēṉi viḷakkamateṇ kaṭanta matikatirceṅ kaṉalkūṭiṟ ṟeṉṉiṉumcā lātē.
translation: Friend, this is the moment the Gracious One arrives. Light billions upon billions of beautiful lamps. Use only pure cow's ghee. Other types of ghee might stain his sacred form. Do not ask, "Where is the darkness? Why must we light lamps in the morning?" You see, we are lighting them for auspiciousness. Do not be mistaken. The radiance of his form surpasses even the combined light of countless moons, suns, and red fires.
commentary: The preparations for God's arrival are symbolic acts of pure devotion. The soul asks for billions of lamps to be lit as an auspicious gesture of love. His own form is brighter than countless suns, so the lamps are an offering of reverence. The insistence on using only pure ghee shows that any act directed toward the divine must be of the highest purity.

translit: eṉṉirukaṇ maṇiaṉaiyār eṉṉuyirnā yakaṉār eṉuyiruk kamutāṉār ellāñcey vallār poṉaṇipoṟ capaiyāḷar ciṟcapaiyār eṉṉaip puṟampuṇarntār akampuṇarntār puṟattakattum puṇarntār aṉṉiyaral laṭiavarē eṉatukula teyvam aruntavattāl kiṭaittakuru vākumatu maṭṭō maṉṉuṟumeṉ taṉittāyum tantaiyumaṅ kavarē makkaḷporuḷ mikkatiru okkalumaṅ kavarē.
translation: He is the apple of my two eyes, my life's Lord, the ambrosia of my life, the all-powerful one who can do anything. The Lord of the beautiful Golden Hall, the Lord of the Hall of Consciousness, he united with me externally, he united with me internally, and he united with me in the space between the external and internal. Friend, he is no stranger. He is my clan deity, the guru I obtained through difficult penance. Is that all? He is also my one enduring mother and father. He is my children, my wealth, and all my treasured family.
commentary: The divine is the ultimate reality of every intimate human relationship. The soul identifies God as her husband, parent, child, teacher (guru), and family deity, showing that he contains and perfects every form of love we know. This union is total, occurring in the outer world, the inner self, and the subtle space between, transforming the relationship with God into one of absolute, all-encompassing intimacy.

translit: tantaieṉṟāy makaṉeṉṟāy maṇavāḷaṉ eṉṟāy takumōiṅ kitueṉṉa viṉavutiyō maṭavāy cintaiceytu kāṇaṭinī ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkum tiruvāḷar eṉaippuṇarnta tirukkaṇavar avartam antanaṭu mutalillā arumperuñcō tiyatē aṇṭacarā caraṅkaḷelām kaṇṭatuvē ṟilaiyē entavakai poypukalvēṉ maṟṟaiyarpōl ammā vīṟumavartirumēṉi nāṉumeṉa aṟiyē.
translation: O foolish girl, are you asking if it is proper for me to call him father, son, and husband? Think and see for yourself, my friend. The noble one who dances in the Hall of Consciousness is the sacred husband who united with me. His rare, great Jothi is without end, middle, or beginning. It is what created all the universes with their moving and unmoving things; there is nothing else. My dear, how can I speak lies like others do? I do not know his magnificent sacred body and myself to be separate.
commentary: The normal rules of human relationships do not apply to God because he is the one infinite source of all that exists. The soul explains that because the divine is an endless, great light (Jothi) that created everything, he naturally contains the essence of every possible relationship. Her seemingly confusing claims are a sign of a deeper truth: in the state of perfect union, she no longer experiences any separation between herself and God, and all logical distinctions dissolve.

translit: ellāmuñ ceyavalla taṉittalaivar potuvil iruntunaṭam purikiṉṟa arumperuñcō tiyiṉār nallāynal nāṭṭārkaḷ ellārum aṟiya naṇṇieṉai maṇampurintār puṇṇiyaṉār ataṉāl illāmai eṉakkillai ellārkkum taruvēṉ eṉṉuṭaiya peruñcelvam eṉpukalvēṉ ammā cellāta aṇṭamaṭṭō appuṟattap pālum civañāṉap peruñcelvam ciṟappatukaṇ ṭaṟiyē.
translation: The singular leader who is capable of doing everything, the rare, great Jothi who dances in the universal Hall, that virtuous one, O good friend, approached and married me with all the good people of the land as witnesses. Because of this, I have no lack. I will give to everyone. What can I say of my great wealth, my dear? It is not limited to the unreachable universes; even beyond that and further beyond, see and know that the great wealth of Siva-Jnanam flourishes.
commentary: Union with the divine brings an inexhaustible spiritual wealth that one is compelled to share with everyone. The soul, having been publicly "married" to the great Jothi, now possesses a treasure that knows no lack. This boundless wealth is Siva-Jnanam, the supreme wisdom of God. The immediate result of this union is an overflowing generosity, a desire to give to all from this infinite source.

translit: vāṉkaṇṭa piramarkaḷum nāraṇarum piṟarum mātavampaṉ ṉāṭpurintu varuntukiṉṟār antō nāṉkaṇṭa kāṭciyavar kaṇṭilarē ulakil nāṉorupeṇ ceytatavam ettavamō aṟiyēṉ kōṉkaṇṭa kuṭikkoṉṟum kuṟaivilaiyēl aṇṭa kōṭielām taṉipperuñceṅ kōlnaṭattum iṟaivar tāṉkaṇṭa kuṭiyāṉēṉ kuṟaikaḷelām tavirntēṉ taṉittavaḷa māṭamicai iṉittiruk kiṉṟēṉē.
translation: Alas, Brahmas, Narayanas, and others in the heavens perform great penance for many days and still suffer. They have not seen the vision I have seen in this world. I do not know what penance I, a lone woman, performed. The people acknowledged by a king lack nothing; in the same way, I have become one of the people acknowledged by the Lord who rules billions of universes with his singular, great, and just scepter. I am rid of all my failings. Now I reside blissfully upon a solitary, white, terraced palace.
commentary: True spiritual liberation comes directly from God's grace, surpassing even the achievements of celestial beings. The soul marvels that gods like Brahma and Vishnu still suffer despite their intense penance, while she, a simple human, has received the ultimate vision. Once acknowledged by the supreme Lord, all her failings are removed, and she lives in a state of perfect, unshakable peace.

translit: eṉkaṇavar peruntaṉmai āṟanta nilaikkē eṭṭiniṉṟu pārppavarkkum eṭṭātē tōḻi poṉkaṇavar kalaimaṭantai taṉkaṇavar mutalōr puṉainturaikkum kataipōla niṉainturaikkap paṭumō puṉkaṇavar aṟiyātē pulampukiṉṟār avarpōl pukalmaṟaiyum ākamamum pulampukiṉṟa tammā uṉkaṇavar tiṟampukaleṉ ṟuraikkiṉṟāy nītāṉ uttamaṉār aruṭcōti peṟṟiṭamuṉ virumpē.
translation: O friend, my husband's great nature is unreachable even for those who stand at the very end of the six paths and try to see. Can it be thought of and described like the fabricated stories told about the husband of the golden goddess, the husband of the goddess of learning, and others? The wretched, not knowing, lament. My dear, the very Vedas and Agamas that they proclaim also lament just like them. You ask me, "Describe your husband's nature." Instead, you should first desire to receive the grace-light of that perfect one.
commentary: God's true nature cannot be described by scriptures, philosophies, or myths; it can only be known through direct experience. The soul explains that the divine reality is beyond the reach of the six great philosophical paths and the stories told about other deities. She states that even the sacred Vedas and Agamas fail, "lamenting" their inability to capture the truth. The advice is clear: seek to receive his grace-light for yourself.

translit: īṅkucilar uṇṇukaeṉ ṟeṉṉaiaḻaik kiṉṟār eṉtōḻi nāṉivarkaṭ keṉpukalvēṉ ammā ōṅkunilā maṇṭapattē eṉkaṇava ruṭaṉē uvaṭṭāta teḷḷamutam uṇṭupaci tīrntēṉ tēṅkuḻaliṅ kiṉieṉakkup pacivarilap pōtu ceppukiṉṟēṉ ippōtu cilukiḻaittal vēṇṭā ēṅkalaṟa nīavarkkut teḷivippāy maṟṟai iruntavarum viruntavarum iṉitupucit tiṭaṟkē.
translation: Some people here are calling me to come and eat. My friend, what can I tell them, my dear? In the pavilion of bright moonlight, I was with my husband and partook of the clear, unsatiating ambrosia, and my hunger was quenched. O friend with honeyed hair, if I feel hunger again, I will tell you then. For now, there is no need to cause a fuss. You should explain this to them clearly so their concern may cease, and so that the others here, both residents and guests, may eat with pleasure.
commentary: Spiritual nourishment from God completely satisfies all worldly appetites, including physical hunger. When invited to eat, the soul explains that she has already been fed with a divine ambrosia while in union with the Lord. This spiritual food has so thoroughly quenched her hunger that she no longer needs physical sustenance. Her gentle response shows that one who has tasted divine bliss is freed from bodily demands, her only concern being that others may eat peacefully.

translit: aiyareṉai āḷuṭaiyār arumperuñcō tiyiṉār ampalattē naṭampuriyum āṉanta vaṭivar meyyareṉai maṇampurinta taṉikkaṇavar turiya veḷiyilnilā maṇṭapattē mēviamu taḷitteṉ kaiyakattē orupacumpoṟ kaṅkaṇamum puṉaintār kaṅkaṇattiṉ tarattaieṉṉāl kaṇṭuraikkap paṭumō vaiyakamum vāṉakamum koṭuttālum ataṟku māṟāka māṭṭātēl matipparitām atuvē.
translation: My master who rules me is the one of rare, great light. He is the form of bliss who dances in the hall. The True One, my sole husband, married me. In the moon pavilion in the expanse of Turiyam, he came, gave me ambrosia, and adorned my hand with a pure gold bracelet. Can I possibly describe the quality of that bracelet? Even if I were given the earthly world and the celestial world, they would not be a match for it; its value is beyond estimation.
commentary: The gifts received from God are infinitely more valuable than anything the material or celestial worlds can offer. The golden bracelet she receives is a symbol of her unbreakable bond with the divine, bestowed in a high state of consciousness called Turiyam. Its worth is immeasurable, far surpassing all the treasures of heaven and earth combined.

translit: taṉvaṭivam tāṉākum tirucciṟṟam palattē taṉinaṭañcey peruntalaivar poṟcapaieṅ kaṇavar poṉvaṭivam iruntavaṇṇam niṉaittiṭumpō tellām pukalarumpē rāṉanta pōkaveḷḷam tatumpi eṉvaṭivil poṅkukiṉṟa tammāeṉ uḷḷam iruntapaṭi eṉpukalvēṉ eṉaḷavaṉ ṟatutāṉ muṉvaṭivam karaintiṉiya carkkaraiyum tēṉum mukkaṉiyum kūṭṭiuṇṭa pakkamumcā lātē.
translation: In the sacred small hall where his own form becomes itself, my husband is the great leader who performs the unique dance in the Golden Hall. Whenever I think of his golden form just as it is, an indescribable flood of the bliss of union overflows and surges in my own form. Oh my, how can I describe the state of my heart? It is beyond my measure. Even the pleasure of eating sweet sugar candy, honey, and the three great fruits all mixed together does not compare.
commentary: The mere thought of God's true form can trigger an overwhelming experience of bliss that makes all worldly pleasures seem pale. This divine joy is a felt reality, a "flood of bliss" that surges through her entire being. She says that even the classic Tamil image of supreme sweetness, a mixture of sugar, honey, and the three great fruits, cannot compare to this spiritual ecstasy.

translit: ivvulakil eṉaippōlvār ōraṉantam kōṭi eṉṉiluyarn tirukkiṉṟār ettaṉaiyō kōṭi avvulakil ciṟantuniṉṟār aḷaviṟanta kōṭi attaṉaipēr kaḷumantō nittamvarun tiṭavum evvulakum uṇarvariya tirucciṟṟam palattē iṉitamarnta talaivariṅkē eṉṉaimaṇam purintār navviviḻi maṭamātē kīḻmēleṉ patutāṉ nātartiru aruṭcōti nāṭuvatoṉ ṟilaiyē.
translation: In this world, there are endless crores of people like me, and so many crores are more exalted than I am. In the other world, countless crores are preeminent. Alas, while all those people suffer daily, the Leader, who is blissfully seated in the sacred small hall which is hard for any world to comprehend, came here and married me. O young woman with eyes like a fawn, the Lord's sacred light of grace makes no distinction at all between high and low.
commentary: Divine grace is a gift of pure love, given without considering a person's merit or status. The speaker marvels that she was chosen for this union while countless others, who seem more worthy or spiritually advanced, are still suffering. The conclusion is that God's light of grace does not follow human logic of "high" and "low"; it is offered freely to all.

translit: tiruvāḷar poṟcapaiyil tirunaṭañcey taruḷvār ciṟcapaiyār eṉtaṉakkut tirumālai koṭuttār uruvāḷar aruvāki oḷiyāki veḷiyāy ōṅkukiṉṟār eṉṉuṭaiya uyirttuṇaivar avartam peruvāymait tiruvaruḷē peruvāḻveṉ ṟuṇarntōr pēciyamey vācakattiṉ perumaiyaiiṉ ṟuṇarntēṉ turuvāta eṉakkiṅkē aruḷniṉaikkum tōṟum collaḷaval lātacukam tōṉṟuvateṉ tōḻi.
translation: The glorious one graciously performs the sacred dance in the Golden Hall. The one from the Hall of Consciousnessgave me a sacred garland. The one who has form becomes formless, becomes light, becomes the expanse, and soars. He is the companion of my soul. Today I understood the greatness of the true words spoken by those who realized that His great, truthful, sacred grace is the greatest life. O my friend, whenever I think of the grace He has shown to me, who am so unrefined, a joy beyond words arises.
commentary: True spiritual life begins with the realization that God's grace is the only thing of lasting value. The speaker, who considers herself simple and "unrefined," is now filled with a joy beyond words whenever she remembers the grace she has received. This experience is a gift open to anyone, learned or not.

translit: aruḷāḷar poṟpotuvil āṉanta naṭañcey āṉanta vaṇṇareṉai āḷuṭaiyār nāṉtāṉ teruḷāta paruvattē teruṭṭimaṇam purinta tiruvāḷar avarperumait tiṟattaievar pukalvār maruḷāta ākamaṅkaḷ māmaṟaikaḷ ellām maruṇṭaṉavēl eṉṉaṭinam maṉavākkiṉ aḷavō iruḷāmai eṉṟuṟumō aṉṟuciṟi turaippām eṉṉavumnāṇ īrppatitaṟ keṉpurivēṉ tōḻi.
translation: The graceful one who performs the dance of bliss in the golden common space, the one whose very nature is bliss, rules me. He enlightened me and married me when I was still in an unenlightened state. Who can extol the power of the greatness of that glorious one? Even the unerring Agamas and the great Vedas were bewildered by him. If that is so, friend, what can our minds and words measure? I think, "When the day comes that I am free from darkness, then I will speak a little of it." But even to say that, shyness pulls at me. What can I do about this, my friend?
commentary: God's greatness is so immense that it leaves even the highest sacred texts, the Agamas and Vedas, bewildered. If these foundational scriptures cannot capture His reality, the speaker feels her own words are completely inadequate. This humility is so deep that she feels a sense of shyness even at the thought of someday being worthy enough to speak of Him.

translit: cempavaḷat tirumalaiyō māṇikka viḷakkō teyvamara katattiraḷō ceḻunīlap poruppō pampumaṇi oḷiyōnaṟ pacumpoṉṉiṉ cuṭarō paṭikavaṇṇap peruṅkāṭci tāṉōeṉ ṟuṇarntē emparamaṉ ṟemperumāṉ puṟavaṇṇam yātō eṉpārēl akavaṇṇam yāruraikka vallār tamparameṉ ṟeṉṉaiaṉṟu maṇampurintār ñāṉa capaittalaivar avarvaṇṇam cāṟṟuvateṉ tōḻi.
translation: Is he a crimson coral mountain, a ruby lamp, a divine cluster of emeralds, or a rich sapphire peak? Is he the light of gathered gems, the splendor of pure gold, or a grand vision of crystal? If people ask what my Supreme Lord’s outer form is, who could possibly describe his inner form? He is the Lord of the Hall of Wisdom who married me that day, claiming me as his own. What, my friend, can I say of his nature?
commentary: Language and comparison fail when trying to describe the Divine. The speaker lists a series of incomparably beautiful and powerful images, a coral mountain, a ruby lamp, a sapphire peak, only to find them all insufficient. If we cannot even describe God's outer form, she asks, how could we possibly describe His inner nature?

translit: tēvarkaḷō muṉivarkaḷō ciṟantamuttar tāmō tērntaciva yōkikaḷō cemporuḷ kaṇṭōrō mūvarkaḷō aivarkaḷō mutaṟparaiyō paramō muṉṉiyaeṉ taṉittalaivar tamiyalai uṇarntār yāvarkaḷum allaeṉṟāl yāṉuṇarntu moḻitaṟ kamaiyumō oruciṟitum amaiyātu kaṇṭāy āvaloṭum aṉpartoḻac ciṟcapaiyil naṭippār avarperumai avaraṟivar avarumaṟin tilarē.
translation: Was it the devas, the sages, the great liberated ones, the accomplished Siva Yogis, or those who have seen the True Reality? Was it the Three Gods, the Five, the primal Para Sakthi, or even the Supreme itself? No one has understood the nature of my unique Lord. If this is so, is it at all possible for me to understand and speak of it? It is not possible in the slightest, you see. He dances in the Hall of Consciousness, worshipped by devotees with great longing. He knows his own greatness; and yet, even he does not know it.
commentary: The ultimate nature of God is fundamentally unknowable. The speaker explains that not even the most enlightened beings, from gods (devas) to sages to the highest cosmic powers, have understood the Lord. The verse ends with a stunning paradox: God's greatness is an infinity that only He can know, and yet it is so boundless that even He does not fully measure or contain it.

translit: tirucciṟṟam palattiṉpat tiruvurukkoṇ ṭiṉpat tirunaṭañcey taruḷkiṉṟa tiruvaṭikkē toḻumpāy aruccikkum pēraṉpar aṟiviṉkaṇ aṟivāy avvaṟivil viḷaintacivā ṉantaamu tākip pariccikkumavvamutiṉ niṟaintacuvai yākip payaṉākip payattiṉaṉu pavamāki niṟaintē uruccikkum eṉamaṟaikaḷ ākamaṅkaḷ ellām ōtukiṉṟa eṉilavartam oḷiuraippa tevarē.
translation: For the great devotees who worship as servants at the sacred feet, which take on a blissful form in the sacred Hall of Consciousness and perform the blissful sacred dance, He becomes the awareness within their awareness. He becomes the blissful nectar of Siva that arises in that awareness, the full flavor of that experienced nectar, the benefit of it, and the experience of that benefit. If all the Vedas and Agamas proclaim this of Him, who then can speak of His radiance?
commentary: God is found within the very fabric of the devotee's consciousness. For those who worship with love, God is the awareness within their own awareness, the spiritual bliss that arises from it, and the very experience of that bliss. He is the path and the destination of the inner path, a reality so intimate that scriptures can only hint at His full radiance.

translit: veṭittaḷinta mukkaṉiyiṉ vaṭittaracan taṉilē virumpuṟa:uṭ piḻinteṭutta karumpiratam kalanta taṭittaceḻum pāṟpeytu kōṟṟēṉviṭ ṭataṉait taṉittapara amutattil tāṉkalantuṇ ṭāṟpōl iṭittiṭitteṉ uḷamuḻutum tittikkum vārttai iṉituraittu maṇampurinta eṉṉuyirnā yakarvāṉ poṭittirumē ṉiyaravaraip puṇaravallēṉ avartam pukaḻuraikka vallēṉō allēṉkāṇ tōḻī.
translation: My life's husband spoke words that, again and again, strike my entire being and fill it with sweetness, and with these sweet words, he married me. Those words were like drinking the pure essence of the three ripe, bursting fruits, mixed with the pressed juice of sugarcane, into which thick, rich milk was poured and hive honey added, and the whole blend then mixed into the unique supreme nectar itself. I was able to unite with him, whose celestial body is smeared with ash. But am I able to speak of his fame? I am not, you see, my friend.
commentary: The experience of God's presence is an overwhelming sweetness that defies description. Vallalar uses the vivid image of a divine nectar made from every sweet thing imaginable to hint at an experience that is deeply intimate and personal, yet too total to be explained in words. The soul has achieved union, but this very consummation renders it speechless.

translit: kaṉṉieṉai maṇantapati kaṉitaruciṟ capaikkē kalantataṉip pativayaṅku kaṉakacapā pativāṉ paṉṉiyaruk karuḷpurinta patiulaka mellām paṭaittapati kāttaruḷum pacupatiev vuyirkkum aṉṉiyamal lātakattum puṟattumakap puṟattum aruṭceṅkōl celuttukiṉṟa atipatiyām ataṉāl eṉṉiyalpōl piṟariyalai eṇṇiyiṭēl piṟarō eṉpatipāl aṉpatilār aṉpuḷarēl eṇṇē.
translation: The Lord who married me when I was a maiden is the one Lord of the fruitful Hall of Consciousness, the golden Lord of the Sabaï. He is the Lord who grants grace to the learned, the Lord who created all the worlds, the Pasupathi who protects them. For all life, he is not separate; he is within, without, and both within and without, ruling with his scepter of grace. Therefore, do not think that the nature of others is like mine. As for "others": they have no love for my Lord. If they do have love, then you may count them so.
commentary: Love for God becomes the single, defining quality of true spiritual kinship. The soul-bride declares her husband to be the supreme Lord (Pasupathi, the Lord of all souls) and states that only those who share her love for him can be considered her kin. This redefines family, moving it from blood ties to a shared orientation of the heart toward the divine.

translit: eṉṉiyalpōl piṟariyalai eṇṇēleṉ ṟuraittēṉ iṟumāppāl uraittaṉaṉeṉ ṟeṇṇiyiṭēl maṭavāy paṉṉiyanāṉ eṉpatiyiṉ paṟṟalatu vēṟōr paṟṟaṟiyēṉ uṟṟavarum maṟṟavarum poruḷum uṉṉiyaeṉ uyirumeṉa tuṭalumeṉa tuṇarvum uyiruṇarvāl aṭaicukamum tirucciṟṟam palattē maṉṉiyatā talilnāṉpeṇ makaḷumalēṉ varumāṇ makaṉumalēṉ aliyumalēṉ itukuṟitteṉ ṟaṟiyē.
translation: I told you, "Do not assume others' natures are like mine." Do not think I said this out of arrogance, you naive girl. I know no attachment other than to my Lord. My relatives, others, possessions, my very own life, my body, my consciousness, and the bliss attained through my soul's awareness, all of it belongs to the one who abides in the sacred hall of consciousness. Therefore, I am not a woman, nor a man, nor a neuter. Know that this is what I meant.
commentary: Complete union with the divine dissolves all limited, earthly identities, including gender. Because her entire being and consciousness now belong to God, who abides in the sacred hall of consciousness (Thiru Chitrambalam), the soul no longer identifies as a woman, a man, or anything in between. These categories have become meaningless in the face of total absorption into the absolute.

translit: pārmutalāp paranātap patikaṭantap pālum pāṅkuṭaiya taṉicceṅkōl ōṅkanaṭak kiṉṟa cīrterintār ēttutoṟum ēttutaṟkō eṉatu tiruvāḷar aruḷkiṉṟa taṉṟumaṉaṅ kaṉintē ārtarupē raṉpoṉṟē kuṟittaruḷu kiṉṟār ātaliṉāl avariṭattē aṉpuṭaiyār ellām ōrtarumeṉ uṟaviṉarām āṇaiitu nīyum uṟavāṉa tavaraṉpu maṟavāmai kuṟittē.
translation: Beyond the earth and all realms up to the supreme sound, and even further beyond, His unique, magnificent scepter reigns. My glorious Lord does not grant grace merely so that the wise who know His splendor can praise Him. With a melting heart, He bestows His grace aiming only for immense, overflowing love. Therefore, all who hold love for Him are my true kin. This is a command. You too have become my relative only by virtue of not forgetting your love for Him.
commentary: Divine grace is a direct response to a heart overflowing with love. God's grace seeks out pure, selfless love above all else. This makes love the one true basis for spiritual community, uniting all who feel it as a single family, regardless of any other distinction.

translit: nātānta varaiyumeṅkaḷ nāyakaṉār ceṅkōl naṭakkiṉṟa teṉkiṉṟār nātānta maṭṭō pōtānta nilaiyumuyar yōkānta nilaiyum puṉitakalān tappatiyum pukalkiṉṟār pukalum vētānta veḷiyummiku cittānta veḷiyum viḷaṅkumivaṟ ṟappālum ataṉmēlap pālum vātāntat tataṉmēlum ataṉmēlap pālum maṉṟāṭi aruṭceṅkōl ceṉṟāṭal aṟiyē.
translation: They say our Lord's scepter rules up to the limit of sound. But is it only up to there? They also speak of the state beyond consciousness, the high state beyond yoga, and the sacred realm beyond all principles. The proclaimed expanse of Vedanta and the vast expanse of Siddhantha shine, and beyond them, and further beyond that, and above the limits of doctrine and even beyond that: know that the Hall Dancer's scepter of grace goes forth and reigns.
commentary: The power and presence of God are infinite and beyond all human comprehension. The speaker lists the highest known spiritual planes, the limits of sound (Nathaantham), consciousness (Bothaantham), yoga, and even the vast conceptual spaces of philosophies like Vedanta and Siddhantha, only to say God's rule extends unimaginably further. The verse expresses a dizzying awe, acknowledging that no map of reality can chart the true expanse of the divine.

translit: puṇṇiyaṉār eṉuḷattē pukuntamarnta talaivar potuviḷaṅka naṭikkiṉṟa tirukkūttiṉ tiṟattai eṇṇiyanāṉ eṇṇutoṟum uṇṭupaci tīrntē irukkiṉṟēṉ aṭikkaṭinī eṉṉaiaḻaik kiṉṟāy paṇṇuṟumeṉ taṉikkaṇavar kūttaṭuñ capaiyaip pārttālum pacipōmē pārttiṭalaṉ ṟiyumē aṇṇuṟumat tiruccapaiyai niṉaikkiṉumvē cāṟal āṟumaṭi ūṟumaṭi āṉanta amutē.
translation: My Lord, the meritorious one who entered and resides in my heart, performs His sacred dance for all to see. Whenever I contemplate the nature of this dance, I am fed and my hunger is satisfied. You keep calling me, but just gazing upon the hall where my unique, melodious husband performs His dance makes hunger disappear. Beyond just seeing it, even thinking of that sacred hall makes all weariness cease and the nectar of bliss well up, my friend.
commentary: Contemplating God's divine dance is a form of spiritual nourishment so rich it satisfies all physical hunger and removes all weariness. The speaker, seeing God as her beloved husband, explains that her inner devotional life is completely self-sustaining. Just thinking of the sacred hall where He dances is enough to make worldly needs disappear and fill her with the nectar of bliss.

translit: kūcukiṉṟa teṉṉaṭināṉ ampalattē naṭikkum kūttāṭik kaṇavarukkē mālaiyiṭṭāy eṉavē ēcukiṉṟār āraṭiyō aṇṭapaki raṇṭat tirukkiṉṟa cattarkaḷum cattikaḷum piṟarum pēcukiṉṟa vārttaielām vaḷḷalaruṭ kūttiṉ perumaiyalāl vēṟoṉṟum pēcukiṉṟa tilaiyē vīcukiṉṟa peruñcōtit tirukkūttiṉ tiṟamē vētamuṭaṉ ākamaṅkaḷ viḷampukiṉṟa taṉṟē.
translation: Why should I feel shy, my friend? People taunt me, saying, "You garlanded the Dancer who performs in the hall!" But who are they? The Saktas and Saktis and all others who exist throughout this cosmos and beyond, all the words they utter speak only of the greatness of our benefactor's dance of grace; they speak of nothing else. Indeed, is it not the nature of the sacred dance of the great, effulgent Jothi that the Vedas and Agamas proclaim?
commentary: The world may mock personal devotion, but that devotion is actually the central theme of the entire cosmos. The speaker is taunted for her intense love for the divine Dancer, but she realizes that all beings, from the highest divine powers (Saktas and Saktis) down to the sacred scriptures (Vedas and Agamas), are constantly praising the very same thing. Her private act of love is a participation in a universal celebration of God's radiant grace.

translit: kulamaṟiyār pulamaṟiyār ampalattē naṭikkum kūttāṭi aiyarukkē mālaiyiṭṭāy eṉavē pulamaṟiyār pōlnīyum pukalutiyō tōḻi pulapulaeṉ ṟaḷappatelām pōkaviṭṭiṅ kitukēḷ alakaṟiyāt tirukkūtteṉ kaṇavarpuri yārēl ayaṉariyō ṭaraṉmutalām aivarkaḷum piṟarum vilakaṟiyā uyirpalavum nīyumiṅkē niṉṟu miṉukkuvatum kulukkuvatum veḷuttuviṭum kāṇē.
translation: "O friend, are you also speaking like someone without understanding, saying, 'You have garlanded a dancing master who performs in the Ambalam, one who knows neither lineage nor learning'? Stop all this prattling and listen to this. If my husband did not perform His immeasurable sacred dance, then Brahma, Vishnu, Siva, the other great gods, other beings, the countless inescapable lives, and even you standing here preening and posturing, all of it would pale into nothingness, you see.
commentary: The entire universe, including the highest gods and every living being, exists only because of God's continuous, creative dance. The speaker rebukes her friend's worldly criticism, pointing out that if the "dancing master with no lineage" were to stop his cosmic performance, everything and everyone, including the friend herself, would instantly vanish. Reality is a living act of God, and all existence depends on it moment by moment.

translit: koṭiiṭaippeṇ pētāynī ampalattē naṭikkum kūttāṭi eṉṟeṉatu koḻunartamaik kuṟittāy paṭiiṭattē vāṉiṭattē pātalattē aṇṭa pakiraṇṭa kōṭiyilē pativiḷakkam ellām aṭimalarkoṇ ṭaiyarceyyum tirukkūttiṉ viḷakkam ākumitu cattiyameṉ ṟarumaṟaiā kamaṅkaḷ keṭiyuṟavē paṟaiyaṭittut tirikiṉṟa avaṟṟaik kēṭṭaṟintu koḷvāyniṉ vāṭṭamelām tavirntē.
translation: O foolish girl with a waist like a vine, you called my husband a 'dancer who performs in the Ambalam'. All the radiant manifestations of the Divine on earth, in the heavens, in the netherworlds, and in the tens of millions of universes and macrocosms, are an expression of the sacred dance performed by the Master's flower-like feet. The rare Vedas and Agamas go about beating the drum, proclaiming this as the absolute truth. Listen to them and understand, and all your distress will vanish.
commentary: God's dance is the source of all divine light and presence throughout all worlds. Every form of God seen on earth, in the heavens, or in any other world is an expression of this one dance. The scriptures (Vedas and Agamas) loudly proclaim this, and realizing it is the key to ending all sorrow.

translit: iṉpavaṭi vantarutaṟ kiṟaivar varukiṉṟār ellāñcey vallacittar iṅkuvaru kiṉṟār aṉparuḷat tēiṉikkum amutarvaru kiṉṟār ampalattē naṭampuriyum aiyarvaru kiṉṟār eṉpuruppoṉ uruvākka eṇṇivaru kiṉṟār eṉṟutiru nātaoli icaikkiṉṟa tammā tuṉpamaṟat tirucciṉṉa oliataṉai nīyum cukampeṟavē kēḷaṭieṉ tōḻieṉaic cūḻntē.
translation: The sacred sound of the Natham resounds, "The Lord is coming to grant a form of bliss! The all-powerful Siddhar is coming here! The ambrosia that sweetens the hearts of devotees is coming! The Master who performs the dance in the Ambalam is coming! He is coming, intending to transform my bony form into gold!" O my friend, stay close to me and listen to the sound of that sacred chinnam (ceremonial trumpet) to end your suffering and receive bliss.
commentary: The inner world of the devotee is filled with a sacred sound, the Natham (primordial vibration), announcing God's arrival. This presence comforts and transforms: the Lord comes as a Siddhar (a perfected master) to turn the devotee's physical, perishable body into a radiant, immortal golden form. Hearing this inner sound is the way to receive this ultimate bliss.

translit: turiyapatam kaṭantaperuñ cōtivaru kiṉṟār cukavaṭivan tara:uyirkkut tuṇaivarvaru kiṉṟār periyapira mātiyarkkum ariyar varukiṉṟār pittareṉa maṟaipukalum cittarvaru kiṉṟār irivakalciṟ capainaṭañcey iṟaivarvaru kiṉṟār eṉṟutiru nātaoli icaikkiṉṟa tammā urimaipeṟum eṉtōḻi nīyumiṅkē ciṉṉa olikēṭṭuk kaḷittiṭuvāy uḷavāṭṭam aṟavē.
translation: The sacred sound of the Natham resounds, "The great Jothi who has transcended the state of Thuriyam is coming! The soul's companion is coming to grant a form of bliss! He who is rare even for the great Brahma and others is coming! The Siddhar, whom the Vedas call a 'madman', is coming! The Lord who dances in the imperishable Chit Sabhai is coming!" My dear friend, you too listen here to the sound of the chinnam and rejoice, so your heart's sorrow may vanish completely.
commentary: The inner sound continues its proclamation, describing God in a series of powerful ways. He is the great Light (Jothi) that exists beyond Thuriyam, the highest state of ordinary consciousness. He is the dancer in the eternal Hall of Consciousness (Chit Sabhai). Paradoxically, this supreme being is also the soul's intimate companion, a perfected Siddhar whose divine actions seem like "madness" to the unenlightened.

translit: īcareṉa tuyirttalaivar varukiṉṟār nīvir ellīrum puṟattirumiṉ eṉkiṉṟēṉ nītāṉ ēcaṟavē akattiruntāl eṉeṉakkēṭ kiṉṟāy eṉkaṇavar varilavartām iruntaruḷum muṉṉē ācaiveṭkam aṟiyātu nāṉavarait taḻuvi aṇaittumakiḻ vēṉatukaṇ ṭaticayittu noṭippār kūcaṟiyāḷ ivaḷeṉṟē pēcuvaraṅ kataṉāl kūṟiyatal latuvēṟu kuṟittatilai tōḻī.
translation: I say, "My Lord, the master of my soul, is coming; all of you please stay outside." You then ask, "What's the harm if I remain inside blamelessly?" When my husband arrives, before He even sits down, knowing neither desire nor shame, I will embrace Him, hold Him tight, and rejoice. Seeing this, others will be astonished and say, "This woman knows no shame!" That is the reason I said it, friend; I did not mean anything else.
commentary: The soul's love for God is so direct and passionate that it completely disregards social norms. She explains to her friend that upon the Lord's arrival, she will embrace him with a love that knows no shame or inhibition. This moment of union is too intimate for witnesses, as outsiders would only misunderstand and judge her ecstatic devotion.

translit: aracuvaru kiṉṟateṉṟē aṟaikiṉṟēṉ nītāṉ aiyamuṟēl uṟṟukkēḷ acaiyātu tōḻi muracucaṅku vīṇaimutal nātaoli mikavum muḻaṅkuvatu tirumēṉi vaḻaṅkuteyva maṇantāṉ viracaeṅkum vīcuvatu nāciuyirt taṟika vītielām aruṭcōti viḷaṅkuvatu kāṇka paracietir koḷḷutumnām kaṟpūra viḷakkup parinteṭutteṉ ṉuṭaṉvaruka terintaṭuttu makiḻntē.
translation: I declare that the King is coming. Do not doubt it. Friend, listen closely without moving. The sounds of the drum, conch, veena, and other instruments are resounding loudly. The divine fragrance from his sacred body is spreading everywhere; perceive it with your breath. See how the light of grace illuminates all the streets. Let us go forth to praise and receive him. Lovingly take up the camphor lamp and come with me, happily choosing to do so.
commentary: To her doubting friend, the soul presents concrete evidence of the Lord's approach. This is a belief and a sensory reality: the air resounds with celestial music from instruments like the veena, a divine fragrance spreads everywhere, and the light of grace visibly illuminates the world. She asks her friend to join her in the traditional act of welcome with a camphor lamp, participating in this real and present event.

translit: tāḻkuḻalnī āṇmakaṉpōl nāṇamaccam viṭuttē capaikkēṟu kiṉṟāyeṉ ṟuraikkiṉṟāy tōḻi vāḻvakaieṉ kaṇavartamaip puṟattaṇaintāḷ orutti māleṉumpēr uṭaiyāḷōr vaḷaiāḻip paṭaiyāḷ āḻkaṭalil tuyilkiṉṟāḷ māmaṇimaṇ ṭapattē āḷkiṉṟāḷ āṇmakaṉāy aṟintilaiyō avaraik kēḻvakaiyil akampuṇarntēṉ avarkaruṇai amutam kiṭaittatunāṉ āṇmakaṉā kiṉṟatati cayamō.
translation: Friend, you say to me, "You are ascending to the Assembly, having cast off shame and fear like a man." As for my state, a certain woman named Mal embraced my husband externally. She wields a discus as her weapon. She sleeps in the deep sea. In the great jeweled hall, she rules as a man. Did you not know him? I united with him inwardly in a fitting way. I received the nectar of his grace. Is it any wonder that I am becoming a man?
commentary: When her friend notes that she acts with the fearlessness "of a man," the soul gives a mystical explanation. The divine beloved transcends gender; the deity Mal (Vishnu) embraces him externally, yet rules "as a man." Having united with this same Lord inwardly and received his grace, the soul finds her own nature transformed. Becoming "like a man" signifies shedding conventional weakness and shame to embody a new, divine strength.

translit: tuṭiyēṟum iṭaiuṉakku vanta:iṟu māppeṉ coleṉṟāy aripiramar curarmuṉivar mutalōr poṭiēṟu vaṭivuṭaiyār eṉkaṇavar capaiyiṉ poṟpaṭikkīḻ niṟpatupeṟ ṟapparicu niṉaintē iṭiēṟu pōṉṟiṟumān tirukkiṉṟā raṭināṉ ellārum aticayikka īṇṭutiruc capaiyiṉ paṭiēṟit talaivartiru aṭiūṟum amutam parukukiṉṟēṉ iṟumākkum paricuraippa teṉṉē.
translation: You ask, "You with a waist like a small drum, what is this pride that has come over you?" Friend, Hari, Brahma, the celestials, sages, and others with ash-smeared forms stand below the beautiful steps of my husband's assembly. Just thinking of the gift of being there, they stand as proud as a thunderclap. But I, to everyone's amazement, have climbed the steps of this sacred assembly and am drinking the nectar that flows from my leader's sacred feet. So what is there to say about the nature of my pride?
commentary: The soul explains that her "pride" is nothing like worldly ego; it is the overwhelming wonder of her new state. Even great gods like Hari (Vishnu) and Brahma feel immense pride just to stand at the bottom of the steps to God's sacred assembly. She, however, has been invited to climb those very steps and drink the nectar of grace directly from the Lord's feet, a privilege that fills her with an astonishment far beyond ordinary pride.

translit: īṟṟaṟiyēṉ iruntiruntiṅ katicayippa teṉnī eṉkiṉṟāy nīeṉaiviṭ ṭēkutoṟum nāṉtāṉ kāṟṟaṟiyāt tīpampōl iruntiṭumat taruṇam kaṇṭapari ceṉpukalvēṉ aṇṭapaki raṇṭam tōṟṟaṟiyāp peruñcōti malaiparanā tattē tōṉṟiyatāṅ kataṉnaṭuvē tōṉṟiyatoṉ ṟatutāṉ māṟṟaṟiyāp poṉoḷiyō avvoḷikkuḷ āṭum vaḷḷalaruḷ oḷiyōī taticayikkum vakaiyē.
translation: You say, "I do not understand the end of it. Why do you just sit here, constantly amazed?" Whenever you leave me, I become like a lamp in a windless place. What can I say of the nature of what I see at that time? A great mountain of Jothi, which the universe and its outer shells have never seen, appears in the Paranātham. In its center, something else appears. Is it the light of pure, flawless gold? Or is it the light of grace of the great benefactor who dances within that light? This is the reason for my amazement.
commentary: The soul's constant amazement comes from a mystical vision she experiences in deep, still meditation. She sees a vast mountain of divine light (Jothi) appearing within the primal, creative sound (Paranātham). At the heart of this light is another, even more brilliant light: the grace of the dancing Lord. The vision is so overwhelming and beyond ordinary perception that it leaves her in a state of silent, unending wonder.

translit: naṭampurivār tirumēṉi vaṇṇamatai nāṉpōy naṉkaṟintu vantuṉakku navilvēṉeṉ kiṉṟāy iṭamvalamiṅ kaṟiyāyē nīyōeṉ kaṇavar eḻilvaṇṇam terinturaippāy icaimaṟaiyā kamaṅkaḷ tiṭampaṭanām teritumeṉac ceṉṟutaṉit taṉiyē tiruvaṇṇam kaṇṭaḷavē civacivaeṉ ṟāṅkē kaṭampeṟukaḷ uṇṭaveṉa mayaṅkukiṉṟa vāṟu kaṇṭilainī āṉālum kēṭṭilaiyō tōḻī.
translation: You say, "I will go, see the color of the Dancer's sacred body clearly, and return to tell you." You don't even know your left from your right here, yet you think you will discern my husband's beautiful color and describe it? The melodious Vedas and Agamas, determined to know for themselves, went separately to see his sacred form. The very moment they saw it, they stood there exclaiming, "Siva, Siva," utterly bewildered, as if they had drunk the intoxicating juice of the kadamba flower. Have you not seen this, friend? At the very least, have you not heard of it?
commentary: God's true form cannot be intellectually understood or described, not even by the most revered scriptures. The soul gently mocks her friend's confidence, pointing out that even the Vedas and Agamas (sacred scriptures) were struck speechless and bewildered when they tried to comprehend the divine. The direct vision of God is an intoxicating experience that overwhelms the mind, rendering all attempts at definition useless.

translit: poypiṭittār ellārum puṟattirukka nāṉpōyp potunaṭaṅkaṇ ṭuḷaṅkaḷikkum pōtumaṇa vāḷar meypiṭittāy vāḻiyanī camaracacaṉ mārkkam viḷaṅka:ula kattiṭaiyē viḷaṅkukaeṉ ṟeṉatu kaipiṭittār nāṉumavar kālpiṭittuk koṇṭēṉ kaḷittiṭuka iṉiyuṉainām kaiviṭōm eṉṟum maipiṭitta viḻiulakar ellārum kāṇa mālaiyiṭṭōm eṉṟeṉakku mālaiyaṇin tārē.
translation: While all who cling to falsehood remained outside, I went and watched the cosmic dance with a joyous heart. Just then, the Bridegroom took my hand, saying, “You have grasped the truth. May you live long! Shine forth in the world so the Samarasa Sanmarkkam may flourish.” I, in turn, grasped His feet. “Rejoice,” He said, “We will never abandon you from now on.” For all the people of the world with kohl-lined eyes to see, He declared, “We have placed this garland on you,” and adorned me with it.
commentary: The soul's sincerity grants her access to the divine vision of the cosmic dance (potu naṭam). In this intimate moment, God takes her hand, confirming her union and giving her a mission: to make the Samarasa Sanmarkkam, the path of universal harmony, shine in the world. This union is publicly solemnized with a garland, signifying a divine marriage and an unbreakable promise of grace.

translit: poruttamilār ellārum puṟattirukka nāṉpōyp potunaṭaṅkaṇ ṭuvantuniṟkum pōtutaṉit talaivar tiruttamuṟa arukaṇaintu kaipiṭittār nāṉum teyvamala raṭipiṭittuk koṇṭēṉcik keṉavē varuttamuṟēl iṉicciṟitum mayaṅkēlkāṇ aḻiyā vāḻvuvanta tuṉtaṉakkē ēḻulakum matikkak karuttalarntu vāḻiyaeṉ ṟāḻiaḷit teṉatu kaiyiṉilpoṟ kaṅkaṇamum kaṭṭiṉarkāṇ tōḻi.
translation: While all the unfit remained outside, I went and stood watching the cosmic dance with delight. At that moment, the peerless Leader approached me perfectly and took my hand. I, in turn, firmly grasped His divine, flower-like feet. “Do not grieve in the slightest from now on,” He said. “Do not be bewildered. An imperishable life has come to you. May you live with an expanded consciousness, esteemed by all seven worlds.” He gave me a ringand also tied a golden bracelet on my hand, O friend!
commentary: Continuing the theme of divine marriage, the soul receives God's ultimate assurance: an end to all grief and confusion. This union confers an imperishable life and an expanded state of awareness. The ring (āḻi) and golden bracelet are divine tokens of this eternal bond, symbolizing the soul's new status as one who is eternally united with God and protected by His grace.

translit: tamaiaṟiyār ellārum puṟattirukka nāṉpōyc capainaṭaṅkaṇ ṭuḷaṅkaḷikkum taruṇattē talaivar imaiaṟiyā viḻiuṭaiyār ellārum kāṇa iḷanakaimaṅ kaḷamukattē taḷataḷaeṉ ṟoḷira emaiaṟintāy eṉṟeṉatu kaipiṭittār nāṉum eṉṉaimaṟan teṉiṟaivar kālpiṭittuk koṇṭēṉ cumaiaṟiyāp pēraṟivē vaṭivāki aḻiyāc cukampeṟṟu vāḻkaeṉṟār kaṇṭāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: While all who do not know themselves remained outside, I went and watched the dance in the Hall. At the moment I was rejoicing, the Leader, with a gentle, auspicious smile shining radiantly on His blessed face for all the unblinking-eyed ones to see, took my hand, saying, “You have known Us.” Forgetting myself, I grasped my Lord's feet. “Become the very form of unburdened, vast wisdom and live, having attained undecaying bliss,” He said. See this, my friend!
commentary: The path to knowing God begins with knowing yourself. Those who lack self-knowledge are left outside the sacred dance hall (sabai). The reward for this inner knowing is bliss and a complete transformation of one's being into the very essence of pure, unburdened wisdom.

translit: aiyamuṟṟār ellārum puṟattirukka nāṉpōy ampalattē tirunaṭaṅkaṇ ṭakaṅkaḷikkum pōtu maiakattē poruntāta vaḷḷalaru kaṇaitteṉ maṭipiṭittār nāṉumavar aṭipiṭittuk koṇṭēṉ meyakattē nammaivaittu viḻittirukkiṉ ṟāynī viḷaṅkukacaṉ mārkkanilai viḷakkukaeṉ ṟeṉatu kaiakattē orupacumpoṟ kaṅkaṇamum puṉaintār karuṇaiyiṉil tāyaṉaiyār kaṇṭāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: While all who were filled with doubt remained outside, I went and rejoiced, watching the sacred dance in the great space. The Patron, in whose heart there is no darkness, came near and clasped my lap. I, in turn, grasped His feet. He said, “You keep Us within your true self and remain awake. Shine forth! Make the state of Sanmarkkam known.” And He, who is like a mother in His compassion, placed a pure golden bracelet on my hand. See this, my friend!
commentary: The key to this divine intimacy is to remain constantly aware of God's presence within your own true self. This inner wakefulness is what attracts the compassionate Lord, who is described as being like a mother. As in the other verses, this union comes with a sacred duty: to make the state of Sanmarkkam (universal harmony) known to others.

translit: kāmālaik kaṇṇarpalar pūmālai viḻaintār kaṇaṅkoṇṭa kaṇṇarpalar maṇaṅkoḷḷat tirintār kōmālai maṉaccerukkāl mayaṅkiuṭam pellām kuṟikoṇṭa kaṇṇarpalar veṟikoṇṭiṅ kalaintār āmālai avarellām kaṇṭuḷamnāṇ uṟavē arumperuñcō tiyareṉṉai virumpimaṇam purintār tēmālai aṇikuḻalāy nāṉceyta tavantāṉ tēvarkaḷō mūvarkaḷum ceytilarkaṇ ṭaṟiyē.
translation: Many with jaundiced eyes craved flower garlands. Many with a host of eyes wandered about, seeking to marry. Many, deluded by the arrogance of worldly power, had their bodies covered in eyes that were mere marks, and they roamed here in a frenzy. To make all of them see and feel shame in their hearts, the rare Great Jothi desired me and married me. O friend whose hair is adorned with sweet garlands! The penance I performed is something neither the gods nor even the great Trinity have ever done, you see.
commentary: The speaker's direct union with God is a unique achievement that puts all other spiritual ambitions to shame. Other powerful beings, including gods, are depicted as blind and frantic in their search for status and recognition. In contrast, the ultimate Divine Light (Jothi) itself desired and "married" the speaker, an attainment she says is beyond anything even the highest gods have accomplished.

translit: kāmālaik kaṇṇareṉṟum kaṇakkaṇṇar eṉṟum karutupala kuṟikoṇṭa kaṇṇareṉṟum pukaṉṟēṉ āmālum avvayaṉum intiraṉum ivarkaḷ aṉṟimaṟṟait tēvarkaḷum acaiaṇukkaḷ āṉa tāmālaic ciṟumāyā cattikaḷām ivarkaḷ tāmōmā māyaivaru cattikaḷōṅ kārat tēmālaic cattikaḷum viḻittirukka eṉakkē tirumālai aṇintārciṟ capaiyuṭaiyār tōḻi.
translation: I called them those with jaundiced eyes, those with a thousand eyes, and those with eyes showing various signs. But really, Mal, Brahma, Indra, and the other gods are merely powers of lesser māyā, like chains of moving atoms. While they, the powers originating from Mahā Māyā, and the sweet-garlanded powers of Omkara all watched with eyes wide open, the Lord of the Chit Sabhai adorned me alone with the sacred garland, O friend.
commentary: The great gods of the traditional pantheon are themselves products of māyā (cosmic illusion). Vallalar makes a bold claim: while these celestial beings, from Brahma and Indra to the powers of Omkara (the primordial sound), could only stand and watch, the supreme Lord of the Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness) chose to unite with the devoted human soul alone.

translit: mātēkēḷ ampalattē tirunaṭañcey pāta malaraṇinta pātukaiyiṉ puṟatteḻunta aṇukkaḷ mātēvar uruttirarkaḷ orukōṭi kōṭi vaḷaipiṭitta nāraṇarkaḷ orukōṭi kōṭi pōtēyum nāṉmukarkaḷ orukōṭi kōṭi purantararkaḷ palakōṭi āka:urup puṉaintē ātēyar ākiiṅkē toḻilpurivār eṉṟāl aiyartiru vaṭipperumai yāruraippār tōḻi.
translation: O lady, listen! The particles that rise from the outside of the sacred sandals adorning the flower-like feet that perform the sacred dance in the hall, if these particles take form as tens of millions upon tens of millions of Mahadevas and Rudras, tens of millions upon tens of millions of conch-wielding Narayanas, tens of millions upon tens of millions of four-faced Brahmas, and many tens of millions of Purandaras, and if, as these subordinate gods, they perform their duties here, then who can express the greatness of our Master's sacred feet, O friend?
commentary: The heroine speaks of the greatness of the sacred feet. Mere particles of dust from the sandals on those feet take form as countless Rudras, Narayanas, Brahmas and Indras, who then do their work as servants. If the dust of the sandals is this, who can speak the greatness of the feet themselves?

translit: uruttirarkaḷ orukōṭi nāraṇarpal kōṭi uṟupiramar palakōṭi intirarpal kōṭi peruttamaṟṟait tēvarkaḷum muṉivarkaḷum piṟarum pēcilaṉan taṅkōṭi āṅkāṅkē kūṭit tiruttamuṟu tiruccapaiyiṉ paṭippuṟattē niṉṟu tiyaṅkukiṉṟār naṭaṅkāṇum cintaiyarāy antō varuttamoṉṟum kāṇātē nāṉorutti ēṟi mānaṭaṅkāṇ kiṉṟēṉeṉ mātavantāṉ peritē.
translation: Tens of millions of Rudras, many tens of millions of Narayanas, numerous Brahmas, many tens of millions of Indras, and, if one were to speak of them, infinite tens of millions of other great gods, sages, and others gather in various places. They stand outside the steps of the perfect, sacred hall, bewildered, their minds set on seeing the dance. Alas! Yet I, alone and without any hardship, have ascended and am witnessing the great dance. The great penance I performed must be immense indeed!
commentary: Countless gods, sages and others gather outside the steps of the sacred Hall, bewildered, longing to see the dance. Vallalar, speaking as the bride, has gone up without hardship and sees it. Those whom the world calls highest stand outside; the one who loves is let in.

translit: pārulakā tiparpuvaṉā tiparaṇṭā tiparkaḷ pakiraṇṭā tiparviyōmā tiparmutalām atipar ērulavāt tiruppaṭikkīḻ niṉṟuviḻit tirukka eṉaimēlē ēṟṟiṉarnāṉ pōṟṟiaṅku niṉṟēṉ cīrulavā yōkānta naṭamtirukka lāntat tirunaṭamnā tāntattē ceyumnaṭampō tāntap pērulavā naṭaṅkaṇṭēṉ tiruamutam uṇavum peṟṟēṉnāṉ ceytatavam pērulakil peritē.
translation: The rulers of the earth-world, the rulers of the realms, the rulers of the universes, the rulers of the outer-universes, the rulers of space, and other such masters all stood wide-eyed below the beautiful, eternal steps. He lifted me upwards; I stood there offering praise. I saw the glorious, unending dance of Yogānta (the end of yoga), the sacred dance of Kalānta (the end of arts), the dance performed at Nādānta (the end of sound), and the renowned, eternal dance of Bodhānta (the end of consciousness). I also received the sacred ambrosia to consume. The penance I performed in this great world is immense.
commentary: Rulers of the earth, of worlds, of universes and of space stand wide-eyed below the steps. God lifts Vallalar up, and he sees the dances at the ends of yoga, of art, of sound and of knowing (Yogānta, Kalānta, Nādānta, Bodhānta), and receives the sacred nectar. The vision passes through every summit the traditions name.

translit: eṉpukalvēṉ tōḻināṉ piṉṉarkaṇṭa kāṭci icaippataṟkum niṉaippataṟkum eṭṭātu kaṇṭāy aṉpuṟucit tāntanaṭam vētānta naṭamum ātinaṭu antamilāc cōtimaṉṟil kaṇṭēṉ iṉpamaya māyoṉṟāy iraṇṭāyoṉ ṟiraṇṭum illatuvāy ellāñcey vallatuvāy viḷaṅkit taṉparamām paraṅkaṭanta camaracappē rantat taṉinaṭamum kaṇṇuṟṟēṉ taṉittacukap potuvē.
translation: What can I say, friend, about the vision I saw after that? It is beyond both description and thought. In the Jothi Maṉṟam (hall of light) which has no beginning, middle, or end, I saw the beloved dance of Siddhānta and the dance of Vedānta. Becoming one with bliss, I also beheld that unique dance of great, harmonious Samarasam. It shines as one, as two, and as that which is neither one nor two; as the all-accomplishing power that transcends even its own supreme transcendent state. I witnessed this in the unique common space of bliss.
commentary: What he saw next is beyond word and thought. In the Hall of Light, without beginning, middle or end, he saw the dances of Siddhanta and Vedanta, and then the unique dance of Samarasam, the great harmony beyond both. It is one, it is two, it is neither, and it can do all things.

translit: tūṅkukanī eṉkiṉṟāy tūṅkuvaṉō eṉatu turaivarumōr taruṇamitil tūkkamuntāṉ varumō īṅkiṉināṉ taṉittirukka vēṇṭuvatā taliṉāl eṉṉuṭaiya tūkkamelām niṉṉuṭaiya tākki ēṅkalaṟap puṟattēpōyt tūṅkukanī tōḻi eṉṉirukaṇ maṇiaṉaiyār eṉaiaṇainta uṭaṉē ōṅkuṟavē nāṉavaraik kalantavarum nāṉum oṉṟāṉa piṉṉaruṉai eḻuppukiṉṟēṉ uvantē.
translation: You tell me to sleep, but how can I? This is the moment my lord will arrive. Will sleep even come at a time like this? Since I must now be alone here, take all my sleepiness upon yourself and go sleep outside without pining, my friend. As soon as the one who is like the pupils of my eyes embraces me, and I merge sublimely with him, and we two become one, I will joyfully wake you.
commentary: The bride cannot sleep: this is the moment her Lord will come. She asks her friend to take her sleepiness and go and rest outside. When her Beloved embraces her and the two become one, she will wake her friend with joy. The soul's longing for God is told in the language of a bride awaiting her husband.

translit: aiyamuṟēl kālaiyilyām varukiṉṟōm itunam āṇaieṉṟār avarāṇai aruḷāṇai kaṇṭāy veyyaruḷat tēpukutap pōṉatiruḷ iravu viṭintatunal cuṭarutayam mēvukiṉṟa taruṇam taiyaliṉi nāṉtaṉikka vēṇṭuvatā taliṉāl caṟṟēap puṟattirunī talaivarvanta uṭaṉē uyya:iṅkē nāṉavaraik kalantavarum nāṉum oṉṟāṉa piṉṉaruṉai aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ uvantē.
translation: "Do not doubt, I will come in the morning. This is my command," he said. His command, you see, is a command of grace. The dark night that enters the hearts of the cruel is over; it is the moment the good light is dawning. My friend, since I must be alone now, stay just outside for a little while. As soon as my leader arrives and, for my salvation, I merge with him here, and we two become one, I will joyfully call for you.
commentary: The Lord has promised to come in the morning, and His word is a command of grace. The dark night that dwells in cruel hearts is over; the good light is dawning. The bride asks to be alone for a little while. When she and her Lord have become one, she will call her friend with joy.

translit: maṉṟuṭaiyār eṉkaṇavar eṉuyirnā yakaṉār vāymalarnta maṇivārttai malaiilakkām tōḻi tuṉṟiyapē riruḷellām tolaintatupaṉ māyait tukaḷoḷimā māyaimati oḷiyoṭupō yiṉavāl iṉṟaruḷām peruñcōti utayamuṟṟa tataṉāl iṉicciṟitu puṟattirunī iṟaivarvanta uṭaṉē oṉṟuṭaiyēṉ nāṉavaraik kalantavarum nāṉum oṉṟāṉa piṉṉaruṉai aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ uvantē.
translation: The Lord of the Hall is my husband, my very life-master. His jewel-like words are an inscription on a mountain, my friend. All the dense, great darkness has been destroyed. The dust-like light of many illusions and the moonlight of the great illusion are gone. Today, the great Jothi that is grace has dawned. Therefore, stay outside for a little while now. As soon as the Lord arrives and I, who possess only him, merge with him, and we two become one, I will joyfully call for you.
commentary: The Lord's words stand like an inscription carved on a mountain: certain and lasting. The great darkness is gone, and the lesser lights of māyai, its dust-light and moonlight, have faded with it. The great Jothi of grace has risen. The bride, who has nothing but Him, waits to become one with Him.

translit: vaikaṟaiī taruḷutayam tōṉṟukiṉṟa teṉatu vaḷḷalvaru taruṇamiṉi vārttaioṉṟā ṉālum caikaraiyēl iṅṅaṉamnāṉ taṉittiruttal vēṇṭum tāṟkuḻalnī āṅkēpōyt tattuvappeṇ kuḻuvil poykaraiyā tuḷḷapaṭi pukaḻpēci irunī puttamutam aḷittaaruṭ cittarvanta uṭaṉē uykaraivāy nāṉavaraik kalantavarum nāṉum oṉṟāṉa piṉṉaruṉai aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ uvantē.
translation: This is the dawn; the sunrise of grace is appearing. It is the moment my benefactor will arrive. Do not utter even a single word now. I must be alone like this. You, with your flowing hair, go join the group of women who understand the truths, and speak his praise just as it is, without falsehood. As soon as the gracious Siddhar who gave me fresh ambrosia arrives, and I merge with him on the shore of salvation, and we two become one, I will joyfully call for you.
commentary: Dawn has come, and grace is rising like the sun. The bride asks for silence, not one word now. She sends her friend to the women who understand the truths, to praise the Lord as He truly is, without falsehood. When the gracious Siddhar who gave her fresh nectar arrives, they will become one.

translit: kālaiyilē varukuvareṉ kaṇavareṉṟē niṉakkuk kaḻaṟiṉaṉnāṉ eṉṉalatu kātiluṟṟa tilaiyō vēlaiilā tavaḷpōlē vampaḷakkiṉ ṟāynī viṭintatunāṉ taṉittirukka vēṇṭuvatā taliṉāl cōlaiyilē malarkoytu toṭuttuvantē puṟattil cūḻntiruppāy tōḻieṉṟaṉ tuṇaivarvanta uṭaṉē ōlaiuṟā tiyāṉavaraik kalantavarum nāṉum oṉṟāṉa piṉṉaruṉai aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ uvantē.
translation: I already told you that my husband will come in the morning. Did my words not reach your ears? You are chattering idly like someone with nothing to do. It has dawned, and because I must be alone, go to the grove, pick flowers, string them into a garland, and wait nearby outside, my friend. As soon as my companion arrives, and I merge with him directly, without any message between us, and we two become one, I will joyfully call for you.
commentary: The bride grows impatient with her chattering friend: she has already said her husband comes in the morning, and it is dawn. She sends the friend to the grove to gather flowers for a garland and wait outside. The union she awaits needs no messenger between them. When they are one, she will call her friend with joy.

translit: viṭintatupēr āṇavamām kāriruḷnīṅ kiyatu veyyaviṉait tiraḷellām ventatukāṇ māyai oṭintatumā māyaioḻin tatutiraitīrn tatupē roḷiutayam ceytatiṉit talaivarvaru taruṇam tiṭampeṟanāṉ taṉittirukka vēṇṭuvatā taliṉāl tēmoḻinī puṟattirumā tēvarvanta uṭaṉē uṭampuṟavē nāṉavaraik kalantavarum nāṉum oṉṟāṉa piṉṉaruṉai aḻaikkiṉṟēṉ uvantē.
translation: Dawn has broken; the deep darkness of great āṇavam has departed. See how the entire mass of harsh karma is burned away. Māyai is broken, Māmāyai is gone, and the veil has been removed. The great light has dawned. Now is the moment my Master will arrive. Since I must be steadfastly alone for this, you, my honey-tongued friend, please stay outside. As soon as the great God arrives, after I have embraced him and we have become one, I will call for you with joy.
commentary: The speaker, representing the soul, announces that the inner obstacles to spiritual union have been overcome. The darkness of ego (āṇavam), the burden of past actions (karma), and the veils of illusion (māyai) have all been cleared away. Now, in this state of purity and solitude, the soul is ready to merge completely with God, an event she frames as the arrival of her divine husband.

translit: mālaiyilē ulakiyalār makiḻnaroṭu kalattal vaḻakkamatu kaṇṭaṉamnī maṇavāḷa ruṭaṉē kālaiyilē kalappataṟkiṅ keṉaippuṟampō eṉṟāy kaṇṭilaṉī taticayameṉ ṟuraiyēleṉ tōḻi ōlaiyilē poṟittatainī uṉṉuḷattē karuti uḻalkiṉṟāy ātaliliv vuḷavaṟiyāy tarumac cālaiyilē camaracacaṉ mārkkacaṅkan taṉilē caṟṟiruntāy eṉilitaṉai uṟṟuṇarvāy kāṇē.
translation: My friend, do not say, “It is the custom for worldly people to unite with their husbands in the evening, we have seen that. But you tell me to go outside so you can unite with your bridegroom in the morning. I have never witnessed such a marvel!” You are distressed because you only consider what is written on palm leaves, and so you do not know this secret. If you had spent just a little time in the hall of charity, in the assembly of the Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam, you would perceive this clearly, you see.
commentary: The friend is confused, since worldly lovers unite at night, but the speaker prepares for union in the morning. Vallalar uses this to contrast two kinds of knowledge. The friend's view is based on custom and scripture ("what is written on palm leaves"). The speaker's knowledge comes from the direct experience of the Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam, a path that teaches that true spiritual union happens not in the darkness of worldly passion (night), but in the bright clarity of a purified soul (day).

translit: iravakattē kaṇavaroṭu kalakkiṉṟār ulakar iyalaṟiyār uyalaṟiyār mayaloṉṟē aṟivār karavakattē kaḷuṇṭu mayaṅkiniṟkum taruṇam kaṉikoṭuttāl uṇṭucuvai kaṇṭukaḷip pārō turavakattē viḻuntārpōṉ ṟivarkūṭum kalappil cukamoṉṟum illaiyaṭi tuṉpamatē kaṇṭār uravakattē eṉkaṇavar kālaiyileṉ ṉuṭaṉē uṟukalappāl uṟucukantāṉ uraipparitām tōḻi.
translation: Worldly people unite with their husbands at night. They do not know reality, they do not know salvation; they only know infatuation. When people are dazed from secretly drinking toddy, if you give them a ripe fruit, will they eat it, perceive its taste, and rejoice? In the union they engage in, which is like falling into a well, there is no pleasure at all, friend; they find only suffering. By contrast, the pleasure arising from the profound union my powerful husband has with me in the morning is impossible to describe, O friend.
commentary: Worldly sexual union, pursued at night, is compared to a drunken, confused act that yields only suffering, not true pleasure. In stark contrast, the "morning" union with the divine is an experience of pure, conscious bliss that is beyond all description. Vallalar uses this powerful imagery to separate fleeting sensory gratification from lasting spiritual fulfillment.

translit: eṉṉuṭaiya taṉittōḻi itukēḷnī mayaṅkēl ellāñcey vallavareṉ iṉṉuyirnā yakaṉār taṉṉuṭaiya tiruttōḷai nāṉtaḻuvum taruṇam taṉittaciva cākkirameṉ ṟiṉittanilai kaṇṭāy paṉṉuminta nilaiparacāk kiramāka uṇarēl pakarparacāk kiramaṭaṅkum patiyākum puṇarntu maṉṉunilai maṟṟiraṇṭum kaṭantakuru turiya mānilaieṉ ṟuṇarkaoḷir mēṉilaiyil iruntē.
translation: My own dear friend, listen to this and do not be confused. The moment I embrace the sacred shoulder of my sweet life-lord, who has the power to do all things, is a delightful state called taṉi Sivan̄āṉa cākkiram, you see. Do not perceive this oft-mentioned state as para-cākkiram. It is the foundation in which the said para-cākkiram is absorbed. Abiding in that radiant higher plane, know that this enduring state of union transcends the other two and is the great state of guru-turīyam.
commentary: This union is a feeling and a specific, supreme state of consciousness called taṉi Sivan̄āṉa cākkiram (the distinct wakeful state of Siva-consciousness). The speaker clarifies that this state is even higher than the para-cākkiram (transcendent wakeful state) known to other mystics. It is a unique plane of awareness she calls guru-turīyam, the Master's "fourth state," indicating it is an ultimate realization beyond ordinary spiritual categories.

translit: nāṉpukalum moḻiitukēḷ eṉṉuṭaiya tōḻi nāyakaṉār taṉiuruvam nāṉtaḻuvum taruṇam vāṉpukaḻum cuttaciva cākkirameṉ ṟuṇarntōr vaḻuttunilai ākumuruc cuvaikalantē atuvāyt tēṉkalanta cuvaiyoṭunaṉ maṇikalanta oḷiyāyt tiripiṉṟi iyaṟkaiiṉpac civaṅkalanta nilaiyē tāṉpukalmaṟ ṟaiyamūṉṟum kaṭantappāl irunta cākkirā tītameṉat taṉittuṇarntu koḷḷē.
translation: Listen to these words I speak, my friend. The moment I embrace the unique form of my Lord is the state that the wise praise as the heaven-acclaimed suddha-Siva-cākkiram. It is a state where form and flavor merge and become that itself; a taste blended with honey, a light infused in a fine gem; a state of unswervingly mingling with Sivam, which is natural bliss. Know that it transcends the other three spoken-of states and uniquely understand it to be cākkirātītam.
commentary: This state of union, also called suddha-Siva-cākkiram (the pure Siva-wakeful state), is a total fusion of the soul with the divine. It is experiencing God and becoming one with God's very nature, which is described as pure, natural bliss. This ultimate state, cākkirātītam (that which is beyond the wakeful state), transcends all other levels of consciousness.

translit: ivvulakōr iravakattē puṇarkiṉṟār ataṉai eṅṅaṉamnāṉ icaippatuvō eṉṉiṉummaṟ ṟitukēḷ evvamuṟum iruṭpoḻutil iruṭṭaṟaiyil aṟivōr eḷḷaḷavum kāṇātē kaḷḷaḷaviṉ ṟaruntik kavvaipeṟak kaṇkaḷaiyum kaṭṭimaṟait tammā kalakkiṉṟār kaṇaccukamum kaṇṭaṟiyār kaṇṭāy cevvaiyuṟak kālaiyileṉ kaṇavaroṭu nāṉtāṉ cērtaruṇac cukampukala yārtaruṇat tavarē.
translation: The people of this world unite at night. How can I possibly describe it? Yet, listen to this. In the miserable darkness, in a dark room where the wise cannot see a thing, they drink limitless toddy. My goodness! They even tie up and cover their eyes in confusion. They unite, but they do not know even a moment of pleasure, you see. Who is capable of describing the bliss of the moment when I unite properly with my Husband in the morning?
commentary: Vallalar again contrasts the conscious, blissful union with God against worldly passion. He portrays worldly sexual union as a blind, ignorant act, performed in darkness with one's senses clouded, yielding no true happiness. The spiritual union, however, is an experience of such profound joy in the full light of awareness that no one on earth has the capacity to describe it.

translit: poṉpaṟiyāp pukalvārpōl maṟaippateṉṉai maṭavāy pūvaiyarkā laiyilpuṇara nāṇuvarkāṇ eṉṟāy aṉpaṟiyāp peṇkaḷukkē niṉuraicam matamām ācaiveṭkam aṟiyāteṉ ṟaṟintilaiyō tōḻi iṉpaṟiyāy ātaliṉāl iṅṅaṉamnī icaittāy iṟaivartiru vaṭivatukaṇ ṭiṭṭataru ṇantāṉ tuṉpaṟiyāk kālaieṉṟum mālaieṉṟum oṉṟum tōṉṟātu cukamoṉṟē tōṉṟuvateṉ ṟaṟiyē.
translation: "Why are you being so evasive, foolish girl? You said, 'You see, women would be shy to unite in the morning.'" Your words are only fit for women who do not know love. O friend, have you not realized that desire knows no shame? You speak this way because you have not known true bliss. Know this: the very moment I saw the Lord's sacred feet, distinctions like 'sorrow-free morning' or 'evening' vanish completely. Only bliss appears.
commentary: Her friend's objection is based on social rules about shame and propriety. The soul dismisses this, stating that true love and desire for God operate beyond all human conventions. In the state of divine bliss, even fundamental concepts like time, morning and evening, dissolve, leaving only the unbroken experience of joy itself.

translit: aruḷuṭaiyār eṉaiyuṭaiyār ampalattē naṭikkum aḻakarelām vallavartām aṇaintaruḷum kālam iruḷuṭaiya iravakattē eytātu kaṇṭāy etaṉāleṉ ṟeṇṇutiyēl iyampuvaṉkēḷ maṭavāy teruḷuṭaieṉ taṉittalaivar tirumēṉic cōti ceppuṟupār mutalnāta pariyantam kaṭantē aruḷuṟumōr paranāta veḷikaṭantap pālum appālum viḷaṅkumaṭi akampuṟattum niṟaintē.
translation: The one full of grace, who possesses me, the beautiful one who dances in the Ampalam, the all-powerful one, the time He comes to embrace me with grace is not in the darkness of night, you see. If you wonder why, foolish girl, I will tell you, so listen. The Jothi of my unique Lord's sacred form transcends everything from the manifest earth up to the realm of Natham, and goes beyond the expanse of Para Natham, shining even beyond that, filling all that is within and without.
commentary: God does not come in the "darkness of night," which symbolizes a state of spiritual ignorance. The reason is simple: God is pure, infinite light (Jothi). This light is so immense that it fills the entire cosmos, from the physical earth to the subtlest realms of divine sound (Natham), leaving no room for darkness. This experience of overwhelming light happens within the Ampalam, the sacred space of one's own consciousness.

translit: ammānāṉ coṉmālai toṭukkiṉṟēṉ nītāṉ ārkkaṇiya eṉkiṉṟāy aṟiyāyō tōḻi immālai ampalattē emmāṉuk kaṉṟi yārkkaṇivēṉ itaiaṇivār yāṇṭaiuḷār pukalnī cemmāppil uraittaṉaiic ciṟumoḻieṉ cevikkē tīnuḻaintāl pōṉṟatuniṉ cintaiyumniṉ nāvum paṉmālait tattuvattāl aṉṟirumpoṉ ṟālē paṭaittatuṉaip paḻakkattāl poṟuttaṉaṉeṉ ṟaṟiyē.
translation: My goodness, I am weaving a garland of words, and you ask, "For whom are you adorning it?" Do you not know, O friend? For whom would I adorn this garland, if not for my Master in the Ampalam? You tell me, where is anyone else who could wear this? You spoke this trivial word out of pride, and it was like fire entering my ears. It seems you, your mind, and your tongue were created not from the many-stranded Tattvas but from iron alone. Know that I have tolerated you only because of our long friendship.
commentary: The "garland of words" is this very poetry, an offering to God. The soul is shocked that her friend would think her creative energy could be directed anywhere else. She describes her friend's question as coming from a coarse, unfeeling nature, like being made of "iron" instead of the subtle Tattvas (principles of reality) that constitute a spiritually sensitive person.

translit: nāṭukiṉṟa palakōṭi aṇṭapaki raṇṭa nāṭṭārkaḷ yāvaruman nāṭṭāṇmai vēṇṭi nīṭukiṉṟa tēvareṉṟum mūrttikaḷtām eṉṟum nittiyarkaḷ eṉṟumaṅkē nilaittatelām maṉṟil āṭukiṉṟa tiruvaṭikkē taṅkaḷtaṅkaḷ tarattuk kāṉavakai colmālai aṇintataṉāl aṉṟō pāṭukiṉṟa eṉṉuṭaiya pāṭṭellām poṉṉam palappāṭṭē tirucciṟṟam palappāṭṭē tōḻi.
translation: Is it not true that all the inhabitants of many millions of sought-after universes and outer universes, and all the great Devas, the Murtis, and the Nityas who desire dominion over those realms, attained their status only by adorning the sacred feet that dance in the Manram with garlands of words, each according to their own capacity? That is why, O friend, every song I sing is a song of Ponnampalam, a song of Thiru-chittram-palam.
commentary: Praise is presented as a universal path to greatness. Even the highest celestial beings (Devas, Murtis) attained their status by offering "garlands of words" to God's dancing feet. This is why the soul's every song is dedicated to the divine dance in the Thiru-chittram-palam (the sacred hall of consciousness), the ultimate source of all power and being.

translit: toṭukkiṉṟēṉ mālaiitu maṇimaṉṟil naṭikkum turaiavarkkē avaruṭaiya tūkkiyakāl malarkkē aṭukkiṉṟōrk karuḷaḷikkum ūṉṟiyacē vaṭikkē avvaṭikaḷ aṇintatiru alaṅkārak kaḻaṟkē koṭukkiṉṟēṉ maṟṟavarkkuk koṭuppēṉō avartām kuṟittitaṉai vāṅkuvarō aṇitaramtām uḷarō eṭukkiṉṟēṉ kaiyilmaḻuc ciṟcapaipoṟ capaivāḻ iṟaivaralāl eṉmālaik kiṟaivarilai eṉavē.
translation: I am weaving this garland for the Master who dances in the Gem Hall; for his lifted flower-foot; for the planted sacred foot that gives grace to those who draw near; for the beautiful, decorated ankle-ring he wears on those feet. I am giving it to him. Would I give it to others? Would they accept it with purpose? Do they have the stature to wear it? I take the red-hot axe in my hand to swear it: besides the Lord who lives in the Hall of Consciousness and the Golden Hall, there is no other master for my garland.
commentary: The offering of praise is reserved exclusively for the supreme dancer in the Maṇimaṉṟam (Gem Hall). The soul declares that no other being, human or divine, possesses the necessary stature to receive such a total offering. This absolute focus is directed to the Lord of the Chit Sabhai (Hall of Consciousness) and Por-Sabai (Golden Hall), locating the ultimate object of worship in the innermost sanctum of awareness.

translit: nāṉtoṭukkum mālaiitu pūmālai eṉavē nāṭṭārkaḷ muṭimēlē nāṭṭārkaḷ kaṇṭāy vāṉtoṭukkum maṟaitoṭukkum ākamaṅkaḷ toṭukkum maṟṟavaiyai aṇivārkaḷ matatturimai yālē tāṉtoṭutta mālaielām parattaiyartōḷ mālai taṉittiṭumeṉ mālaiaruṭ capainaṭuvē naṭikkum ūṉṟeṭutta malarkaḷaṉṟi vēṟukuṟi yātē ōṅkuvatā talilavaikkē urittākum tōḻi.
translation: O friend, do not think this garland I weave is a flower garland that worldly people place on their heads. The heavens weave garlands, the Vedas weave them, the Agamas weave them; those other garlands people wear by right of their religion. All the garlands they have woven are garlands for the shoulders of harlots. My garland stands alone; it rises high because it seeks nothing other than the planted and lifted flower-feet of Him who dances in the center of the Hall of Grace. Therefore, it belongs only to those feet.
commentary: This "garland of words" is no ordinary garland. The heavens, the Vedas and the Agamas weave garlands of their own, and people wear them by right of their religion; Vallalar calls all such garlands "garlands for the shoulders of harlots", passed to whoever claims them. His own garland stands alone: it seeks nothing but the planted and lifted feet of the Lord who dances in the Aruṭ Sabai (Hall of Grace), and belongs to them alone.

translit: vāṉkoṭutta maṇimaṉṟil tirunaṭaṉam puriyum vaḷḷalelām vallavarnaṉ malareṭutteṉ uḷattē tāṉkoṭukka nāṉvāṅkit toṭukkiṉṟēṉ itaṉait talaivarpiṟar aṇikuvarō aṇitarantām uḷarō tēṉkoṭutta cuvaipōlē tittitteṉ uḷattē tirukkūttuk kāṭṭukiṉṟa tiruvaṭikkē urittām yāṉkoṭukkum paricinta mālaimaṭṭō tōḻi eṉāvi uṭalporuḷum koṭuttaṉaṉuḷ icaintē.
translation: The generous and all-powerful one, who performs the sacred dance in the Gem Hall gifted by the heavens, himself picked fine flowers and placed them in my heart. I received them and am weaving this garland. Would other leaders wear it? Do they have the stature to wear it? It belongs only to the sacred feet that, sweet like honey, reveal the sacred dance within my heart. O friend, is this garland the only gift I am giving? I have also willingly given my very life, body, and possessions with my heart's full consent.
commentary: The very inspiration for this poetry is a gift from God. The soul is a weaver, arranging the "flowers" that the Lord himself placed within the heart. This divine origin means the work can only be offered back to its source. The offering goes beyond the poem, to a total surrender of the poet's life, body, and possessions to the sweet, dancing presence felt within.

translit: eṉmālai māttiramō yārmālai eṉiṉum iṟaivaraiyē ilakkiyamāy icaippateṉil avaitām naṉmālai ākumantac coṉmālai taṉakkē nāṉaṭimai tantaṉaṉpal vantaṉamcey kiṉṟēṉ puṉmālai palapalavāp pukalkiṉṟār ammā poypukuntāṟ pōlceviyil pukuntōṟum taṉittē vaṉmālai nōyceyumē kēṭṭiṭavum paṭumō maṉṟāṭi patampāṭi niṉṟāṭum avarkkē.
translation: my garland and any garland of verse composed with the Lord as its sole subject is a good garland. I am a slave to such a garland of words; I surrender myself and offer it many salutations. But alas, people compose so many wretched poems! Each time they enter my ears, like falsehood itself, they inflict a severe, malignant sickness. How can one even bear to hear them? To those who stand and dance singing of the feet of the Hall's Dancer, they are a harsh affliction.
commentary: Any poem written for God is a sacred work, worthy of reverence. In sharp contrast, poetry about worldly subjects is toxic. He describes hearing such verses as a "malignant sickness," a spiritual poison that is physically painful to a person attuned to the divine. For one who is focused on God, any art that is not god-centered is an unbearable affliction.

translit: uriyaperun taṉittalaivar ōṅkucaṭān tattiṉ uṭpuṟattum appuṟattum oruceṅkōl celuttum turiyarturi yaṅkaṭanta cukacorupar potuvil cuttanaṭam purikiṉṟa cittaraṭik kaḻalē periyapatat talaivarelām niṟkunilai ituōr peṇuraieṉ ṟeḷḷutiyō koḷḷutiyō tōḻi ariyaperum poruḷmaṟaikaḷ ākamaṅkaḷ uraikkum āṇaiyumiṅ kītitaṟkōr aiyamilai aṟiyē.
translation: He is the rightful, great, singular Head, who rules with a single scepter both within and beyond the lofty Six Antas.
