He is the one in the turīya state, the embodiment of bliss who has transcended even turīya. He is the siddha who performs the pure dance in the common space. His ankleted feet are the very ground upon which all who have attained great positions stand. O friend, will you dismiss this as the word of a mere woman, or will you accept it? This is the rare, great truth spoken by the Vedas and the Agamas, and this is my oath. Know this: there is no doubt about it.
commentary: God is the supreme reality, a being who dances in a state beyond even the highest levels of consciousness like turīya (the fourth state). He is a siddha (a perfected being), and his feet are the very ground upon which all other great souls stand. Speaking as a woman, the poet challenges the listener to recognize this as the essential, authoritative truth of the Vedas and Agamas (India's most sacred scriptures), not simply a personal feeling.

translit: matameṉumpēy piṭittāṭṭa āṭukiṉṟōr ellām maṉṟiṭattē vaḷḷalceyum mānaṭamkāṇ kuvarō catameṉavē irukkiṉṟār paṭuvataṟin tilarē cākāta kalvikaṟkum taramivarkkum uḷatō patamaṟiyā intamatavātikaḷō ciṟṟam palanaṭaṅkaṇ ṭuyntēṉaic cilapukaṉṟār eṉṟāy cutaimoḻinī aṉṟucoṉṉa vārttaiaṉṟō iṉṟu tōttirañcey tāṅkāṅkē toḻukiṉṟār kāṇē.
translation: Will those who are possessed and made to dance by the demon called religion ever see the great dance the Patron performs in the sacred hall? They live as though they were permanent and do not know that they will die. Do they even have the capacity to learn the deathless education? You said that these religious fanatics, who do not know the divine state, were criticizing me, who was saved by seeing the dance in the small hall. O you with nectar-sweet words, isn't that what you said the other day? Now look! They are singing praises and bowing down everywhere.
commentary: Vallalar names religion itself a demon (matam eṉum pēy) that seizes people and makes them dance. Those it holds cannot see the great dance in the Hall, nor learn the deathless education (cākāta kalvi); they live as if they were permanent and do not know they will die. The very partisans of religion who once spoke ill of the bride are now seen singing praise and bowing everywhere.

translit: evvulakil evvaurkkum arumperuñcō tiyarē iṟaivareṉpa taṟiyātē immatavā tikaḷtām kavvaipeṟu kuruṭarkari kaṇṭakatai pōlē kataikkiṉṟār cākāta kalvinilai aṟiyār navviviḻi yāyivarō cilapukaṉṟār eṉṟāy ñāṉanaṭam kaṇṭēṉmeyt tēṉamutam uṇṭēṉ cevvaipeṟu camaracacaṉ mārkkacaṅkan taṉilē cērntēṉat tīmoḻiyum tēmoḻiā yiṉavē.
translation: Not knowing that the great rare Jothi is the Lord for everyone in every world, these religious fanatics tell tales like the story of the blind men and the elephant. They are ignorant of the state of deathless education. O you with doe-like eyes, you said they were speaking ill of me. I have seen the dance of wisdom, I have consumed the true honey-nectar, and I have joined the perfect association of the Samarasa Sanmarkkam. Those foul words have now become sweet words.
commentary: The experience of divine union renders all worldly criticism irrelevant. By seeing the "dance of wisdom" and joining the Samarasa Sanmarkkam (the path of universal harmony and truth), the devotee transcends the petty conflicts of religious division. The insults of her critics, once painful, are now heard as "sweet words," showing an inner transformation. The "great rare Jothi" (divine light) is for everyone, a truth missed by those lost in sectarianism.

translit: perukiyapē raruḷuṭaiyār ampalattē naṭikkum peruntakaieṉ kaṇavartirup pērpukaleṉ kiṉṟāy arukarputta rātieṉpēṉ ayaṉeṉpēṉ nārā yaṇaṉeṉpēṉ araṉeṉpēṉ āticivaṉ eṉpēṉ parukucatā civameṉpēṉ catticivam eṉpēṉ paramameṉpēṉ piramameṉpēṉ parappiramam eṉpēṉ turuvucuttap piramameṉpēṉ turiyaniṟai veṉpēṉ cuttacivam eṉpaṉivai cittuviḷai yāṭṭē.
translation: You ask me to state the sacred name of my husband, the great personage of overflowing grace who dances in the hall. I will say Arhat, Buddha, and the others. I will say Ayan. I will say Narayanan. I will say Aran. I will say the Primal Siva. I will say the delectable Sadasivam. I will say Sakthi-Sivam. I will say the Supreme. I will say Brahman. I will say Para-Brahman. I will say the sought-after Pure Brahman. I will say the fullness of the Turiya state. I will say Pure Sivam. These are the playful acts of consciousness.
commentary: God is one, but has infinite names. When asked for God's name, the poet joyfully lists titles from across different religions and philosophies: Arhat, Buddha, Vishnu, Siva, Brahman, and many more. The point is that all these names, which people often fight over, are simply different facets of the same, single divine reality. They are the "playful acts of consciousness," not rigid, separate identities.

translit: ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkiṉṟa nāyakaṉār tamakkuc cērntapuṟac camayappēr poruntuvatō eṉṟāy piṟcamayat tārpeyarum avarpeyarē kaṇṭāy pittareṉṟē peyarpaṭaittārk keppeyarov vātō accamayat tēvarmaṭṭō niṉpeyareṉ peyarum avarpeyarē evvuyiriṉ peyarumavar peyarē ciṟcapaiyil eṉkaṇavar ceyyumoru ñāṉat tirukkūttuk kaṇṭaḷavē teḷiyumitu tōḻi.
translation: You ask if names from other, external religions are suitable for the Lord who dances in the hall of consciousness. Understand this: the names from those other religions are also his names. For one who has earned the name 'Madman', what name is not fitting? Is it only the names of the gods of those religions? Your name and my name are his names. The name of every living being is his name. My friend, this will all become clear the moment you see the sacred dance of wisdom my husband performs in the hall of consciousness.
commentary: The divine is present in all religions and in all of existence, including every single living being. When his companion questions using names from "outside" traditions, Vallalar explains that God's identity is so vast that every name, including your name and my name, is His. This truth, he says, becomes self-evident upon witnessing the divine dance of wisdom in the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness), the inner space of pure awareness.

translit: epporuṭkum evvuyirkkum uḷḷakattum puṟattum iyaluṇmai aṟiviṉpa vaṭivāki naṭikkum meypporuḷām civamoṉṟē eṉṟaṟintēṉ uṉakkum viḷampukiṉṟēṉ maṭavāynī kiḷampukiṉṟāymīṭṭum ipporuḷap poruḷeṉṟē icaippateṉṉē potuvil iṟaivarceyum niraticaya iṉpanaṭan taṉainī paippaṟavē kāṇutiyēl attaruṇat tellām paṭṭanaṭup pakalpōla veṭṭaveḷi yāmē.
translation: I have realized that Sivam is the one true reality, which dances as the very form of natural truth, consciousness, and bliss, within and without all things and all beings. I am explaining this to you, but you, foolish girl, are starting to argue again. Why do you keep talking about 'this entity' and 'that entity'? If you could only see, without any confusion, the dance of unsurpassed bliss the Lord performs in the universal space, at that very moment it would all become as open and clear as broad daylight.
commentary: Intellectual arguments about God are a distraction from the path; true clarity comes only from direct experience. The speaker has realized that Sivam, the ultimate reality of truth, consciousness, and bliss, is the single substance of all that exists. He gently chides his companion for getting caught in mental distinctions ("this entity" versus "that entity"), saying that if she could just witness the Lord's dance, all her confusion would vanish like shadows in broad daylight.

translit: kāṇāta kāṭciyelām kāṇkiṉṟēṉ potuvil karuṇainaṭam purikiṉṟa kaṇavaraiuṭ kalantēṉ kōṇāta mēlnilaimēl iṉpaaṉu pavattil kuṟaiyāta vāḻvaṭaintēṉ tāḻvaṉaittum tavirntēṉ nāṇāḷum tiruppotuvil naṭampāṭip pāṭi nayakkiṉṟēṉ naṟṟavarum viyakkiṉṟa paṭiyē māṇākam poṉākam ākavaram peṟṟēṉ vaḷḷalaruḷ nōkkaṭaintēṉ kaṇṭāyeṉ tōḻi.
translation: I see sights never before seen. I have merged internally with my Husband who performs the dance of compassion in the common space. In the blissful experience of the supreme, unswerving state, I have attained an undiminishing life. All my lowliness has vanished. Day by day, I delight, dancing and singing in the sacred common space in a way that makes even great ascetics marvel. I received the boon for my great body to become a golden body. I have received the grace-filled gaze of the Benefactor, you see, my friend.
commentary: Spiritual realization is a complete transformation that brings immortal life and perfects the physical body itself. Vallalar describes a state of ecstatic union where he has merged with the divine and attained an "undiminishing life," free from all limitation. Most importantly, he received the boon for his physical body to become a "golden body," a deathless, luminous form made of grace. This is literal: the entire being is perfected.

translit: cāticama yaṅkaḷilē vītipala vakutta cāttirakkup paikaḷellām pāttiramaṉ ṟeṉavē ātiyileṉ uḷattiruntē aṟivitta paṭiyē aṉpāliṉ ṟuṇmainilai aṟivikka aṟintēṉ ōtiuṇarn tōrpukaḻum camaracacaṉ mārkkam uṟṟēṉciṟ capaikāṇap peṟṟēṉmeyp poruḷām cōtinaṭat taracaieṉṟaṉ uyirkkuyirām patiyaic cuttaciva niṟaivaiuḷḷē peṟṟumakiḻn tēṉē.
translation: Just as He declared from within my mind at the beginning that the heaps of trash that are the scriptures, which lay out many paths within castes and religions, are unworthy vessels, today I have come to know the true state that He has revealed through love. I have attained the Samarasa Sanmarkkam, praised by those who have studied and realized it. I have been blessed to see the hall of consciousness. I have received within me and rejoice in the King of the Jothi dance, who is the true substance, the Master who is the life of my life, the fullness of pure Sivam.
commentary: True spirituality is found not in external scriptures or religious divisions, but in an inner state of love and direct realization. Vallalar makes a powerful statement, recalling how God revealed to him that scriptures creating divisions of caste and religion are "heaps of trash." The true path, the Samarasa Sanmarkkam (path of universal harmony), is attained through love, which opens the way to realizing the divine Jothi (light) as the very life of one's own life.

translit: cariyainilai nāṉkumoru kiriyainilai nāṉkum taṉiyōka nilaināṉkum taṉittaṉikaṇ ṭaṟintēṉ uriyaciva ñāṉanilai nāṉkumaruḷ oḷiyāl oṉṟoṉṟā aṟintēṉmēl uṇmainilai peṟṟēṉ ariyaciva cittānta vētānta mutalām āṟanta nilaiaṟintēṉ appālniṉ ṟōṅkum periyaciva aṉupavattāl camaracacaṉ mārkkam peṟṟēṉiṅ kiṟavāmai uṟṟēṉkāṇ tōḻi.
translation: I saw and knew, one by one, the four stages of chariyai, the four stages of kiriyai, and the four unique stages of yōkam. Through the light of grace, I knew, one by one, the four stages of the rightful Siva jñānam and attained the supreme true state. I came to know the states of the six antas, such as the rare Siva Siddhanta and Vedanta. Through the great experience of Sivam that stands and soars beyond them, I obtained the Samarasa Sanmarkkam. Here, I have attained deathlessness, see, my friend.
commentary: Vallalar describes his spiritual path as a progression through and beyond traditional paths. He mastered the four established stages of religious life: chariyai (selfless service), kiriyai (devotional worship), yōkam (meditative union), and jñānam (wisdom). He then went further, moving beyond the conclusions of major philosophies (antas) like Vedanta and Saiva Siddhanta. His final attainment, the Samarasa Sanmarkkam, is presented as a higher truth that grants the ultimate prize: a deathless physical existence.

translit: nāṉpacitta pōtellām tāṉpacittār āki nallatiru amutaḷittē allalpaci tavirttē ūṉpatitta eṉṉuṭaiya uḷattētam muṭaiya upayapatam patittaruḷi apayameṉak kaḷittār vāṉpatikkum kiṭaippariyār ciṟcapaiyil naṭikkum maṇavāḷar eṉaippuṇarnta puṟappuṇarccit taruṇam tāṉpatitta poṉvaṭivam taṉaiaṭaintu kaḷittēṉ cāṟṟumakap puṇarcciyiṉām ēṟṟamuraip patuvē.
translation: Whenever I was hungry, He Himself became hungry. Giving me good, sacred ambrosia, He ended my painful hunger. In my mind, which was fixated on the flesh, He graciously impressed His twin feet and gave me refuge. The Bridegroom who dances in the chit sabai, so difficult for even the lords of heaven to attain, joined with me in an outer union. At that moment, I attained the golden form He established and rejoiced. How, then, can I even speak of the sublimity of the acclaimed inner union?
commentary: God's compassion is so intimate that He feels the devotee's hunger as His own, providing spiritual nourishment that ends all suffering. This divine love brings total refuge (abhayam, freedom from fear) and transforms the devotee's physical body into a radiant golden form. This "outer union" is a tangible, physical experience of grace, which itself is only a prelude to an even deeper inner union that is too sublime to describe.

translit: turuvupara cākkirattaik kaṇṭukoṇṭēṉ parama coppaṉaṅkaṇ ṭēṉparama cuḻuttiyuṅkaṇ ṭuṇarntēṉ kurupirama cākkirattaik kaṇṭēṉpiṉ piramam kulaviyacop paṉaṅkaṇṭēṉ civacuḻutti kaṇṭēṉ kuruturiyam kāṇkiṉṟēṉ camaracacaṉ mārkkam kūṭiṉēṉ potuvilaruṭ kūttāṭum kaṇavar maruviṭappeṟ ṟavarvaṭivam nāṉāṉēṉ kaḷittu vāḻkiṉṟēṉ etiraṟṟa vāḻkkaiyileṉ tōḻi.
translation: I saw and comprehended the investigative supreme waking state. I saw the supreme dream state. I saw and realized the supreme deep sleep state. I saw the Guru-Brahman waking state, then I saw the dream state where Brahman flourishes, and I saw the Siva deep sleep state. I am now seeing the Guru turīyam. I have joined the Samarasa Sanmarkkam. Having been blessed with union with my Husband who performs the grace-dance in the common space, I have become His very form. I live rejoicing in an unequaled life, my friend.
commentary: This verse maps an ascent through extraordinary states of consciousness far beyond our ordinary waking, dreaming, and deep sleep. Vallalar describes seeing and realizing a series of supreme states (para-jāgrat, para-svapna, para-suṣupti) and then even more advanced states associated with the Guru and Sivam. The ascent culminates in seeing turīyam, the transcendent fourth state of pure awareness, where he becomes one with God's form and lives a life without equal.

translit: taṉippaṭumōr cuttaciva cākkiranal nilaiyil taṉittiruntēṉ cuttaciva coppaṉattē cārntēṉ kaṉippaṭumeyc cuttaciva cuḻuttiyilē kaḷittēṉ kalantukoṇṭēṉ cuttaciva turiyanilai atuvāyc ceṉippilatāy ellāmāy allatuvām cutta civaturiyā tītattē civamayamāy niṟaintēṉ iṉippuṟuciṟ capaiiṟaiyaip peṟṟapari cataṉāl ittaṉaiyum peṟṟiṅkē irukkiṉṟēṉ tōḻi.
translation: I was alone in the good state of suddha siva jākkiram; I reached suddha siva soppanam; I rejoiced in the ripe, true suddha siva suḻutti; I mingled with and became the state of suddha siva turiyam; in the birthless suddha siva turiyātītam, which is everything and yet not, I became filled, all-pervading as Siva. Because of the grace by which I obtained the Lord of the sweet Chit Sabhai, I have received all this and am here now, O friend.
commentary: The progression through higher states of consciousness continues into an even more refined level, which he calls the "pure Siva" states. After experiencing pure Siva-awareness in waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, he enters suddha siva turiyam (the pure Siva fourth state) and finally suddha siva turiyātītam, the state beyond the fourth. In this final state, he experiences himself as one with Siva, birthless and all-pervading. He attributes this entire attainment to the grace of the Lord of the Chit Sabhai, the hall of pure consciousness.

translit: aruṭcōtit talaivareṉak kaṉpuṭaiya kaṇavar aḻakiyapoṉ mēṉiyaināṉ taḻuviniṉṟa taruṇam iruṭcātit tattuvaṅkaḷ ellāmpō yiṉavāl eṅkaṇumpē roḷimayamāy iruntaṉaāṅ kavartām maruṭcāti nīkkieṉaip puṇarntaoru taruṇam maṉṉucivā ṉantamayam ākiniṟai vuṟṟēṉ teruṭcārpil iruntōṅku camaracacaṉ mārkkat tiruccapaikkaṇ uṟṟēṉeṉ tirukkaṇava ruṭaṉē.
translation: The Lord of the Grace-Jothi is my loving husband. The moment I stood embracing his beautiful golden body, all the tribes of darkness, the tattuvams, vanished. Everywhere became a great expanse of light. The moment he removed the tribes of delusion and united with me, I became filled with enduring Siva-bliss. Together with my sacred husband, I have reached the holy assembly of the Samarasa Sanmarkkam, which thrives in the realm of clarity.
commentary: The union with God, the Lord of the Grace-Jothi (light of grace), has a powerful, purifying effect. This embrace dissolves the tattuvams, the fundamental principles or building blocks of the cosmos and the human body. In their place, there is only a vast expanse of light and enduring bliss. This ultimate clarity is the experience of the Samarasa Sanmarkkam, the path of universal harmony.

translit: puṟappuṇarcci eṉkaṇavar purintataru ṇantāṉ puttamutam nāṉuṇṭu pūritta taruṇam ciṟappuṇarcci mayamāki akappuṇarcci avartām ceytataru ṇaccukattaic ceppuvatep paṭiyō piṟappuṇarcci viṭayamilai cuttacivā ṉantap perumpōkap peruñcukantāṉ perukieṅkum niṟaintē maṟappuṇarcci illātē nāṉatuvāy atueṉ mayamāycciṉ mayamāyttaṉ mayamāṉa nilaiyē.
translation: The moment my husband performed the outer union was the moment I drank the fresh ambrosia and swelled with fullness. How can I possibly describe the bliss of the moment he performed the inner union, which was made of supreme consciousness? It is not a matter related to the consciousness of birth. It is the great bliss of the great enjoyment of pure Siva-bliss, which overflowed and filled everything. It is a state without any consciousness of forgetting, where I became That, That became my very being, became pure consciousness, and became its own being.
commentary: Vallalar returns to the distinction between the "outer" and "inner" union. While the outer union was a moment of ecstatic fullness, the inner union is something else entirely: a state of pure, blissful consciousness. This experience has nothing to do with ordinary life or the cycle of birth and death. It is a complete merging where the distinction between self and God dissolves, leaving only a single, all-encompassing, self-aware existence.

translit: tāyiṉumpē raruḷuṭaiyār eṉṉuyiril kalanta taṉittalaivar nāṉceytaperun tavattālē kiṭaittār vāyiṉumōr maṉattiṉummā matiyiṉumet tiṟattum matittaḷattaṟ karunturiya maṉṟilnaṭam purivār āyiṉumeṉ aḷaviṉmika eḷiyareṉa eṉṉai akampuṇarntār puṟampuṇarntār puṟappuṇarccit taruṇam tūyaoḷi peṟṟaḻiyā tōṅkuvaṭi vāṉēṉ cukamayamām akappuṇarcci colluvatep paṭiyō.
translation: He who possesses greater grace than a mother, the singular Lord who has mingled in my soul, I obtained him through the great austerities I performed. He performs the dance in the hall of turiyam, a state difficult to measure by mouth, mind, great intellect, or any other means. Yet, to my measure, he is utterly simple. Thus he united with me inwardly and united with me outwardly. The moment of the outer union, I received a pure light and became an imperishable, elevated form. How can I speak of the inner union, which is made of pure bliss?
commentary: God's grace is greater than a mother's love. Though the Divine dances in turiyam, a state beyond the grasp of the mind, it can make itself simple and accessible to the seeker. Vallalar emphasizes that this union has two results. The "outer union" granted him an imperishable body of pure light. The "inner union" brought a state of pure bliss that remains beyond description. The path is a combination of sincere effort and overwhelming grace.

translit: aṟiyāta paruvattē eṉṉaivalin taḻaittē āṭalceyum tiruvaṭikkē pāṭalceyap paṇittār ceṟiyāta maṉacciṟiyēṉ ceytapiḻai ellām tiruviḷaiyāṭ ṭeṉakkoṇṭē tirumālai aṇintār piṟiyāmal eṉṉuyiril kalantukalan tiṉikkum peruntalaivar naṭarāyar eṉaippuṇarntār aruḷām aṟivāḷar puṟappuṇarcci eṉaiaḻiyā tōṅka aruḷiyatīṇ ṭakappuṇarcci aḷavuraikka lāmē.
translation: In my unknowing age, he forcefully called to me and commanded me to sing songs to his sacred feet that perform the dance. Taking all the mistakes made by me, a small one with an unconcentrated mind, as his sacred play, he wore the sacred garland for me. The great Lord, Natarajar, who inseparably mingles and sweetens my soul, united with me. The outer union of the Knower, who is Grace itself, was a touch that graced me to rise imperishably. Can the inner union even be measured and described?
commentary: Grace is a gift freely given. God, the cosmic dancer Natarajar (Siva as King of Dance), sought out the soul in its "unknowing age," treating its flaws and scattered mind as part of a divine game. This initiated union bestows an immortal body and leads to an inner communion that is beyond all description.

நவநி றைந்தபேர் இறைவர்கள் இயற்றிட ஞானமா மணிமன்றில்
தவநி றைந்தவர் போற்றிட ஆனந்தத் தனிநடம் புரிகின்றான்
எவன்அ வன்திரு வாணைஈ திசைத்தனன் இனித்துய ரடையேனே.
translit: civame ṉumpeyark kilakkiyam ākiec ceyalumtaṉ camukattē navani ṟaintapēr iṟaivarkaḷ iyaṟṟiṭa ñāṉamā maṇimaṉṟil tavani ṟaintavar pōṟṟiṭa āṉantat taṉinaṭam purikiṉṟāṉ evaṉa vaṉtiru vāṇaiī ticaittaṉaṉ iṉittuya raṭaiyēṉē.
translation: He is the very definition of the name Sivam. In His presence, great and graceful deities perform all actions. In the great jeweled hall of wisdom, He performs the singular dance of bliss as those perfected in spiritual disciplinepraise Him. By the sacred command of that One, I have declared this. I will suffer no more.
commentary: The ultimate reality, Sivam (the auspicious divine principle), is the cosmic dancer whose presence empowers all other gods. The words of this poem are presented as a direct command from that supreme being, a revealed truth that has personally liberated Vallalar from all suffering. Those who have perfected themselves through tavam, or intense spiritual discipline, are the ones who witness this divine dance.

translit: aiyaṉaruḷ varukiṉṟa taruṇamitu kaṇṭīr aiyamilai aiyamilai aiyaṉaṭi āṇai meyyaṉeṉai āṭkoṇṭa vittakaṉciṟ capaiyil viḷaṅkukiṉṟa cittaṉelām vallaoru vimalaṉ tuyyaṉaruṭ peruñcōti turiyanaṭa nātaṉ cukaamutaṉ eṉṉuṭayai turaiamarntiṅ kirukka vaiyamicait tirukkōyil alaṅkarimiṉ viraintē maṇiyālum poṉṉālum malarālum viyantē.
translation: The moment of the Lord's grace is arriving, you see! There is no doubt, no doubt; I swear on the Lord's feet. The True One, the master-magician who enslaved me, is the Siddha shining in the Chit Sabhai, the one immaculate being who is all-powerful. The Pure One, the ArutPerunJothi, the Lord of the Turīya dance, the nectar of bliss, my master, is now taking his seat here. Therefore, quickly and wondrously adorn the sacred temple on this earth with gems, gold, and flowers.
commentary: This verse is an urgent announcement: the Lord's arrival is happening right now. Vallalar describes God as the ArutPerunJothi (Great Grace-Light) and the master of the Turīya dance, a dance that occurs in a state of pure consciousness beyond waking or sleeping. This divine being, he says, is taking his seat on earth, in the Chit Sabhai (hall of consciousness). The call to adorn a temple is a literal instruction to prepare for this imminent, physical manifestation.

translit: taṉittalaimaip perumpatieṉ tantaivaru kiṉṟa taruṇamitu cattiyamkāṇ cakatalattīr kēṇmiṉ iṉittanaṟuṅ kaṉipōṉṟē eṉṉuḷamtit tikka iṉṉamutam aḷitteṉṉai ēḻulakum pōṟṟa maṉitta:uṭam pitaiaḻiyā vāymaiuṭam pākki maṉṉiyacit tellāmcey vallapamum koṭuttē kaṉittacivā ṉantameṉum perumpōkam taṉilē kaḷittiṭavait tiṭukiṉṟa kālaiyumiṅ kituvē.
translation: This is the moment my Father, the great Lord of unique supremacy, is arriving. This is the truth; people of the world, listen! To make all seven worlds praise me, he gave me sweet nectar that sweetens my heart like a ripe, fragrant fruit. He transformed this human body into an imperishable body of truth and gave me the power to perform all the established Siddhis. This is also the very time he has caused me to rejoice in the great experience known as ripened Sivananda.
commentary: The evidence for the Lord's imminent arrival is the change that has already occurred within Vallalar himself. He declares that God has already transformed his physical human body into an immortal one, granted him Siddhis (supernatural powers), and immersed him in Sivananda (the bliss of the divine). His personal, radical transformation serves as the first sign and proof of the universal change that is about to unfold for all.

translit: cattiyavāṉ vārttaiitu tāṉuraittēṉ kaṇṭāy cantēkam ilaiitaṉil cantōṭam uṟuvāy ittiṉamē aruṭcōti eytukiṉṟa tiṉamām iṉivarumat tiṉaṅkaḷelām iṉpamuṟu tiṉaṅkaḷ cuttaciva caṉmārkkam tulaṅkumelā ulakum tūymaiuṟum nīuraitta colaṉaittum palikkum cettavarkaḷ eḻuntulakil tirintumakiḻn tiruppār tiruvaruṭceṅ kōleṅkum cellukiṉṟa tāmē.
translation: I have spoken this word of the True One, you see. There is no doubt in this; be joyful. This very day is the day the Grace-Light is attained. All the days that follow are days of bliss. The Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam will shine throughout all the worlds. The world will become pure. All the words you have spoken will come true. The dead will rise and wander the world, living in joy. The righteous scepter of divine grace will indeed hold sway everywhere.
commentary: The consequences of this divine arrival will be global. Vallalar makes a series of staggering prophecies: his path of pure truth, the Suddha Siva Sanmarkkam, will spread everywhere, the world will be purified, and even the dead will be resurrected to live joyfully again. This is personal salvation and the dawn of a new, blissful age for all humanity, governed directly by divine grace.

translit: eṉcāmi eṉatuturai eṉuyirnā yakaṉār iṉṟuvantu nāṉirukkum iṭattilamar kiṉṟār piṉcārum iraṇṭarainā ḻikaikkuḷḷē eṉatu pēruṭampil kalantuḷattē piriyāmal iruppār taṉcāti uṭaiyaperun tavattālē nāṉtāṉ cāṟṟukiṉṟēṉ aṟintitutāṉ cattiyamcat tiyamē miṉcārum iṭaimaṭavāy eṉmoḻiniṉ taṉakkē veḷiyākum iraṇṭarainā ḻikaikaṭanta pōtē.
translation: My God, my master, the Lord of my life, is coming today and will take his seat in the place where I am. Within the next two and a half nāḻikai, he will merge with my glorious body and remain within my heart, never to part. By the great penance that is his very nature, I declare this. Know that this is the truth, the absolute truth. O maiden with a waist like a flash of lightning, my words will become clear to you once these two and a half nāḻikai have passed.
commentary: The announcement becomes intensely immediate and personal, with a specific timeline. Within the next hour (two and a half nāḻikai), God will permanently merge with Vallalar's physical body. He presents this as an absolute, verifiable fact. This is the moment of complete union, where the divine presence will inhabit his human form without separation.
NOTES
Note 374

tamil: இத்திருப்பாட்டின் கீழ் "சத்திய அறிவிப்பு, சத்திய வார்த்தை" என அடிகளால்எழுதப்பெற்றுள்ளது.
translit: ittiruppāṭṭiṉ kīḻ "cattiya aṟivippu, cattiya vārttai" eṉa aṭikaḷāleḻutappeṟṟuḷḷatu.
translation: Beneath this verse, "cattiya aṟivippu, cattiya vārttai" (true proclamation, true word) is written in the Aṭikaḷ's own hand.
Note 375

tamil: இத்திருப்பாட்டின் கீழ் "இங்ஙனம் எல்லாம் வல்லவர் ஓதுக என்றபடி உரைத்துளேன்"என அடிகளால் எழுதப்பெற்றுள்ளது.
translit: ittiruppāṭṭiṉ kīḻ "iṅṅaṉam ellām vallavar ōtuka eṉṟapaṭi uraittuḷēṉ"eṉa aṭikaḷāl eḻutappeṟṟuḷḷatu.
translation: Beneath this verse, "iṅṅaṉam ellām vallavar ōtuka eṉṟapaṭi uraittuḷēṉ" ("Thus have I uttered it, as the All-Powerful One bade me recite") is written in the Aṭikaḷ's own hand.

translit: jōti jōti jōti cuyañ jōti jōti jōti parañ jōti jōti jōti yaruṭ jōti jōti jōti civam.
translation: Jothi, Jothi, Jothi, self-manifest Jothi. Jothi, Jothi, Jothi, supreme Jothi. Jothi, Jothi, Jothi, Jothi of Grace. Jothi, Jothi, Jothi, Sivam.
commentary: The poem begins with a powerful, rhythmic chant, using repetition as a form of meditation. By repeating Jothi (Divine Light), the mind is filled with the presence of God as Light. This Light is described as self-created, the highest reality, the source of all grace, and finally as Sivam, the auspicious and absolute Being.

translit: vāmajōti cōmajōti vāṉajōti ñāṉajōti mākajōti yōkajōti vātajōti nātajōti ēmajōti viyōmajōti ēṟujōti vīṟujōti ēkajōti ēkajōti ēkajōti ēkajōti.
translation: Beautiful Jothi, moon Jothi, heavenly Jothi, wisdom Jothi, great Jothi, yoga Jothi, Jothi of principle, Jothi of sound, golden Jothi, spatial Jothi, ascending Jothi, excellent Jothi, the one Jothi, the one Jothi.
commentary: This verse expands the vision of God as Light, showing that this single Jothi manifests in every beautiful and powerful form. It is the cool light of the moon, the vastness of the heavens, the inner light of wisdom (jñāna), the goal of spiritual practice (yoga), and the primal sound of creation (nāda). All these different lights are expressions of one, single, all-encompassing Light.

translit: ātinīti vētaṉē āṭalnīṭu pātaṉē vātiñāṉa pōtaṉē vāḻkavāḻka nātaṉē.
translation: O embodiment of primal justice and the Vedas! O you of the great dancing feet! O teacher of wisdom through discourse! Hail, hail, O Lord!
commentary: After the ecstatic chant of "Jothi," the poem concludes with a personal cry of praise. The Divine is hailed as the source of cosmic justice and the wisdom of the Vedas (ancient sacred texts). The "great dancing feet" is a classic image of God's dynamic, creative energy, while "teacher of wisdom" portrays the divine as a guide who actively leads souls to truth.

glossary.def: The five divine functions: creation, preservation, dissolution, veiling and grace. Vallalar says these are done by deities under God, and that God granted them to him.
The Agamas, scriptures of temple worship and doctrine. Vallalar says their truth is known by grace, not by reading.
A Tamil verse form of long, flowing lines. The ArutPerunJothi Agaval, Vallalar's hymn of 1,596 lines, belongs to the Sixth Thirumurai and is published as a separate volume.
Ambalam: the hall or open stage where God dances. It is the hall at Chidambaram and, within, the space of consciousness where God is known.
Nectar, ambrosia. Vallalar's word for the sweetness of grace, tasted within, which brings deathless life.
Bliss, Ananda. The joy of union with God.
The root impurity of the ego, the "I-ness" that veils the soul. The first of the three impurities (malam).
Anma Neya Orumaipadu: the unity of all souls in love. Every living being shares the same essence, so every being is to be seen as one's own.
The universe, the macrocosm. Vallalar sees the same Light filling the countless universes (aṇṭam) and the human body (piṇṭam).
Traditionally a name for Brahmins. Vallalar gives it its root meaning: the gracious ones whose nature is coolness and compassion toward all life, whatever their birth.
Refuge. The cry "apayam, apayam" ("refuge, refuge") runs through the pathigam Apayam Iṭutal, the soul's plea to be held by God.
Virtue, righteous action. For Vallalar its heart is compassion: feeding the hungry and relieving the suffering of every living being.
A name for the Vedas.
The six "ends" (antam) or culminations of the philosophical traditions: Vedanta, Siddhanta, Bodhanta, Nadanta, Yoganta and Kalanta. Vallalar says God is beyond all six.
Grace. The living, compassionate power of God that frees the soul and transforms it. For Vallalar grace is received through compassion for all life.
ArutJothi, the Grace-Light: God as the Light of grace, seen and received within.

ArutPerunJothi, the Vast Grace-Light: Vallalar's name for God in the Sixth Thirumurai. The one infinite Light of grace from which everything comes and in which everything is held, open to every living being.
The deathless education: the knowledge, given by grace, of the life that does not end in death.
The waking state, the first of the states of consciousness. Vallalar speaks of a higher waking beyond the usual states.
Salai, the hall or house. Here the Sathya Dharma Salai, the free kitchen at Vadalur.
Samarasam: perfect harmony, equality of all. Part of the full name of Vallalar's path, Samarasa Suddha Sanmarkkam.
Religion as an organized creed. In the Sixth Thirumurai Vallalar declares the religions, creeds and sects false, and calls people beyond them to the true path.
The conch, blown to announce victory and arrival. Vallalar has it blown to proclaim the coming of God.
Sanmarkkam, the true path. Vallalar's name for the way of grace, compassion and direct knowledge of God, open to every living being.
Satguru, the true teacher. Vallalar's name for God, who taught him directly from within.
Caste. Vallalar declares caste false, a darkness to be thrown away, and calls all people one family.
Sathya Gnana Sabai, the Hall of True Wisdom that Vallalar consecrated at Vadalur in 1872, a hall of light open to all, built for no religion.
Sathya Dharma Salai, the free kitchen Vallalar opened at Vadalur in 1867 so that no one would go hungry. Its fire has not been put out since.
Crest-jewel, the jewel worn at the top of a crown. Used for God as the highest of all.
Chit Sabhai, the Hall of Consciousness, where God dances. Both the hall at Chidambaram and the inner space of awareness.
Chitrambalam, the "small" or subtle hall: the hall of the dance at Chidambaram and the hall of consciousness within. Thiru Chitrambalam is "the sacred Chitrambalam".
Siddhanta, the Saiva philosophical tradition. One of the six "ends" (āṟantam) that Vallalar says God transcends.
Siddhar, a perfected one. Vallalar calls God the Siddhar who can do all things.
Siddhi, attainment or perfect power. Vallalar speaks above all of the Siddhi that can do all things, given by grace.
Sivakami, the Divine Mother, consort of the Lord who dances at Chidambaram.
Sivam, the Auspicious: the supreme Reality. In the Sixth Thirumurai Vallalar says that Sivam alone is the true substance.
Bliss, lasting well-being.
The bliss of simply being: the stillness beyond all effort and thought that Vallalar longs for in the second verse of the Sixth Thirumurai.
Suddha Sanmarkkam, the pure true path that Vallalar names and teaches in the Sixth Thirumurai: compassion for all life, the end of caste and creed, and union with ArutPerunJothi.
The seven levels. In the pathigam on the Hall of Pure Gold, the seven stages of the inner vision, each marked by a change of jewel and color.
Jeeva Karunyam, compassion for all living beings. For Vallalar the foundation of all spiritual life and the key to God's grace.
Jothi, Light. Vallalar's central name for God.
Husband. In the bridal songs the soul is the bride and God the husband, the closest union a human life knows.
Karma: the accumulated effect of one's actions. One of the three impurities (malam).
The evil eye: harm believed to come from an envious look.
The inner faculties: mind, intellect, will and ego. Vallalar asks that they be purified and ruled by grace.
Compassion, mercy. God's compassion toward all, and the compassion the soul must have for every living being.
Kollāmai, non-killing. For Vallalar the condition of the true path: those who kill and eat flesh stand outside it until they give up killing.
Death, personified as Yama, the god of death.
Mahamayai, the great māyai: the subtle, primal form of illusion.
Malam, impurity. The three impurities, ego (āṇavam), karma (kaṉmam) and illusion (māyai), veil the soul until grace removes them.
Manimanram, the Hall of Gems, where God dances.
Creed or doctrine; also pride or madness. Vallalar uses the double meaning: attachment to creed is a kind of madness.
Māyai, illusion: the power that makes the passing world seem the whole of reality. One of the three impurities.
Mettukuppam, the village near Vadalur where Vallalar lived his last years and where, on 30 January 1874, he entered his room and was not seen again.
Silence, the stillness beyond all words.
Mutti, liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
A unit of time of twenty-four minutes.
Gnana Sabai, the Hall of Wisdom: the hall of God's dance, and Vallalar's hall at Vadalur.
Gnanam, wisdom: direct knowledge of God, given by grace and not by study.
The medicine of wisdom: God as the remedy for every ill, above all for birth and death.
Dance. God's dance in the hall is the movement of grace that sustains all things.
Nadam, the primordial sound from which manifestation arises.
Nadanta, "the end of sound": the state beyond primordial sound. One of the six "ends" (āṟantam).
Nataraja, the King of Dance: God as the Dancer in the hall at Chidambaram and in the hall of consciousness.
The central channel, the subtle path at the center of the body in which, Vallalar says, God dances.
Justice. Vallalar speaks of the compassionate justice that rules in God's hall.
The sacred sound Om.
Parai, the supreme Power of God, worshipped as the Divine Mother.
Pati, Lord. God as the sovereign of all souls, as in Sivapati, "the Lord who is Siva".
Pathigam, a hymn, usually of ten verses. The Sixth Thirumurai is arranged in pathigams.
The body, the microcosm, set against aṇṭam, the universe.
Enjoyment. In the Sixth Thirumurai, the bliss of union with God.
The Golden Hall (Pon Sabhai) at Chidambaram, where God dances.
The common space, open to all. God dances in the common space so that all may see.
The heroine of the love songs. In Vallalar's bridal songs she is the soul, and her beloved is God.
Tandavam, the cosmic dance of God.
Tattva, a principle of existence. The tattvas are the levels from the elements to the subtlest powers. God is in them all and beyond them.
Tapas, spiritual discipline or penance.
Thillai, the old name of Chidambaram, the town of the Golden Hall where God dances.
Thirumurai, "sacred book". The Thiru Arutpa is arranged in six Thirumurai; this is the sixth and last.
Thiru Arutpa, "the Divine Songs of Grace": the collected poetry of Vallalar.
The sacred feet of God, the place of refuge and of grace.
The heroine's friend and confidant in the love songs, to whom the soul tells her experience of God.
The evil path, the way of cruelty and falsehood, as opposed to Sanmarkkam.
Turiyam, the "fourth" state of consciousness beyond waking, dreaming and deep sleep.
Turiyatitam, the state beyond the fourth.
The refrain of a traditional Tamil girls' game-song, also used by Manikkavasagar. Vallalar uses it to sing God's deeds as joyful play.
Latent tendencies left in the mind by past experience, which bind the soul until grace frees it.
"Come!" The refrain of the pathigam Ampalavāṇar Varukai, calling God to come.
Vadalur, the town in Tamil Nadu where Vallalar founded the Sathya Dharma Salai and the Sathya Gnana Sabai.
Space, the expanse. Vallalar speaks of many spaces, up to the Space of Siva (Siva veḷi).
Vedanta, the philosophy of the Upanishads. One of the six "ends" (āṟantam) that Vallalar says God transcends.
Open space, the boundless expanse of pure consciousness in which all things are seen to resolve.
Karma: the effect of past actions that binds the soul to birth.
